   178: 
   179: ## C input phase selection
   180: 
   181: A `.c` input and any path under `-x c` begin as raw C source and run the full
   182: preprocessor. In automatic language mode, `.i` begins as preprocessed C;
   183: `-x cpp-output` selects that same phase for any suffix, including an
   184: extensionless path. `-x c` deliberately overrides a `.i` suffix, while
   185: `-x none` restores suffix inference.
   186: 
   187: Preprocessed C still runs the normal lexer, identifier interning, source-map
   188: publication, numeric/`#line` marker handling, pragma state and C23 keyword
   189: normalization. It does not replay command-line `-D`/`-U` operations, includes,
   190: conditional or definition directives, diagnostics directives, or macro
   191: expansion in ordinary text. `-E` on preprocessed C serializes that retained
   192: token stream with the normal output spacing; it is not a second preprocessing
   193: pass and need not preserve the input bytes verbatim. This is a starting-phase
   194: distinction, not a new C dialect or backend.
   195: `COMPILER_DRIVER_LANGUAGE_CPP_OUTPUT` exposes the same contract to invocation
   196: API callers; a future per-input `-x` snapshot can carry that language value
   197: without changing the frontend contract.
   198: 
   199: A `.s` input, or any input under `-x assembler`, is an assembly translation
   200: unit rather than a C one. `assembly_unit_encode` (`assembly_unit.c`) is the
   201: layer above `assembly_encode`: it interprets the directive vocabulary, tracks
   202: one offset per section, resolves labels, and hands each instruction line to
   203: the instruction layer beneath, and the driver turns its sections, symbols and
   204: relocations into an `ObjectFile` like any other. The vocabulary is `.text`,
   205: `.data`, `.bss`, `.rodata` and `.section`; `.globl`/`.global`, `.weak`,
   206: `.hidden`, `.type` and `.size`; `.align`, `.balign` and `.p2align`; `.byte`,
   207: `.short`/`.word`/`.hword`/`.value`, `.long`/`.int`, `.quad`, `.ascii`,
   208: `.asciz`/`.string`, and `.zero`/`.skip`/`.space`; `.intel_syntax noprefix` and
   209: `.att_syntax prefix`; and the `.cfi_*` family, accepted and dropped because it
   210: describes unwinding rather than bytes. Anything else -- a directive the table
   211: does not claim, or an operand form one of these does not cover -- is a
   212: diagnostic naming the directive and its line, the way every other unsupported
   213: construct here is reported rather than silently dropped.
   214: 
   215: Text alignment without an explicit fill uses x86-64 NOP bytes or complete
   216: little-endian AArch64 NOP instructions. A partial AArch64 instruction boundary
   217: is zero-filled before the NOPs; explicit fills remain repeated bytes on both
   218: targets. Data alignment defaults to zero fill.
   219: 
   220: Three things that layer owns rather than the instruction layer. Local numeric
   221: labels: `1:` becomes a generated name and `1f`/`1b` resolve to the nearest
   222: following or preceding definition in source order, and those names leave the
   223: symbol table again once every reference to one is folded, the way GNU as drops
   224: its own `.L` locals. A repeat or lock prefix alone on a line joins the
   225: instruction on the next one. And a same-section PC-relative reference to a
   226: label defined in the file is written into the bytes; only a cross-section or
   227: undefined name becomes a relocation. `@PLT` is dropped: a static link resolves
   228: such a call the same way it resolves a plain one. Sections keep their own
   229: names -- `.init` and `.fini` are neither `.text` nor absent -- and a
   230: hand-written section gets alignment 1, because `crti.o` and `crtn.o`
   231: contribute one and two bytes to `.init` and any padding between them would
   232: run as code.

   150: - **An atomic aggregate is loaded and stored as one integer access of its
   151:   promoted width**, which is what the promotion above exists for: a three-byte
   152:   record is read and written through four bytes, and the padding the promotion
   153:   added is written as zero, because Clang copies the value through a zeroed
   154:   temporary and that is the oracle. The frontend represents widths one, two,
   155:   four and eight bytes on both targets, plus sixteen on x86-64 and on AArch64.
   156:   A sixteen-byte x86-64 aggregate uses native canonical atomic operations when
   157:   `cx16` admits `CMPXCHG16B`. On baseline x86-64 without `cx16`, the C frontend
   158:   instead emits the fixed type-specific libatomic ABI calls
   159:   (`__atomic_load_16`, `__atomic_store_16`, the fetch/exchange family, and
   160:   `__atomic_compare_exchange_16`) so canonical code generation never receives
   161:   an operation the selected CPU cannot implement. The object format retains
   162:   those imports; a hosted final link must supply libatomic, as the registered
   163:   contention fixture does. AArch64 lowers sixteen-byte accesses through
   164:   exclusive-pair loops -- the sequences `_Atomic __int128` already uses, which
   165:   also take aggregates promoted into that width. The
   166:   AArch64 selector now handles the promoted aggregate loads/stores through
   167:   sixteen bytes as well as full-width integer exchange/RMW/CAS. Its pair
   168:   update rows consume the integer images described below; they do not widen
   169:   arbitrary smaller frame objects. Any other target-specific selection miss
   170:   remains visible in fallback statistics pending native-backend retirement.

   175:   *finished* body rather than where the access is built, because an operand is

   184: - **GNU generic atomics use an integer view of the caller's exact object
   185:   representation.** `__atomic_load`, `__atomic_store`, `__atomic_exchange`
   186:   and `__atomic_compare_exchange` lower 1-, 2-, 4- and 8-byte objects through

    72:   range; all frames share one query-sized scratch allocation, released on
    73:   success and failure. Constructed types remain in the translation-unit arena.

    75:   delimiter index to skip nested ranges. Consecutive unary tasks inherit a
    76:   completed operator scan until removing a parenthesis exposes a new range.

    78:   top-level unqualification); bare `typeof` operands retain their original type.

    82: - **A failed call blames the call, not the declaration.** A direct call's
    83:   callee token is not an identifier *use*: it resolves through the
    84:   call-target index, so the parser records no binding for it and
    85:   `c_ir_identifier_entity` misses. The lowering failure in
    86:   `c_ir_lower_expression_core_step` looks the name up before reporting, and
    87:   keeps the identifier's own token index rather than the one the call arm
    88:   advanced to the closing parenthesis, so an object called as a function is
    89:   reported as one instead of as an unbound identifier. A name nothing
    90:   declares still reports as unbound, which is what a SIMD builtin missing
    91:   from `c_symbol_predefined` looks like.
    92: - **A call to a function declared `()` supplies the parameters itself.**
    93:   Before C23 an empty parameter list is no prototype at all, so the arguments
    94:   take the default argument promotions and the *call site* is the signature.
    95:   `IrType.is_unprototyped` marks such a declaration's type, and
    96:   `c_ir_unprototyped_call_type` in `c_gen.c` gives the `IR_OPCODE_FUNCTION`
    97:   reference the call's own parameter types plus a trailing `...` -- Clang's
    98:   model, which declares `void die()` as `void (...)` and types each call site
    99:   `void (i32, ...)`. The `...` reaches only System V x86-64, where it sets the
   100:   AL vector count that a callee which really is variadic reads;
   101:   `int printf(); printf("%f", x);` is that program. Every argument stays
   102:   *named*, so Darwin AArch64 passes them in registers rather than on its
   103:   variadic stack, and a definition is untouched: `int main()` is still an
   104:   ordinary zero-parameter body with no register save area.
   105:   `ir_validate_instruction` therefore lets a function reference disagree with
   106:   its symbol's type when that type is the unprototyped one and the return
   107:   types agree, and Wasm64 refuses such a call, because it types every call by
   108:   the callee's declared signature. C23 made `()` mean `(void)`, so the marker
   109:   is never set in that dialect and the call is refused as an arity error --
   110:   which every dialect now reports by naming the callee and its parameter
   111:   count rather than as "could not prepare C calls" (issue #666).
   112: - **A callable parameter type is separate from its local object's type.**
   113:   `c_ir_parameter_value_type` strips only top-level `volatile` from fixed
   114:   parameter values in declaration and expression-built function types. It
   115:   retains the existing atomic ABI shape and never strips pointee or member
   116:   qualifiers. `c_ir_emit_parameter` receives both types: its `ARGUMENT` matches
   117:   the callable signature exactly, while its local copy keeps the definition's
   118:   qualifiers, alignment and volatile accesses. Array/function/va_list
   119:   adjustments remain intact. The strict call-signature validator is unchanged;
   120:   `c_test_qualified_parameter_values` checks the producer, parameter object and
   121:   a deliberately mismatched call before shared promotion. The minimal fixture
   122:   and the existing native differential corpus cover execution and compatible
   123:   function pointers (GitHub #361).
   124:   Compound assignments likewise compute with the unqualified value type,
   125:   including when a narrower right operand needs promotion. Their original
   126:   place retains volatile load/store effects and the separate atomic update
   127:   path; `c_test_qualified_compound_values` checks both frontend forms.
   128: - A by-value parameter's local copy retains its type's natural alignment.
   129:   `c_ir_emit_parameter` must pass the resolved layout alignment to
   130:   `c_ir_emit_local`, just as an ordinary declaration does. Rounding a slot's
   131:   frame-relative offset alone cannot honor alignment greater than the frame
   132:   pointer guarantee; the canonical native emitter uses the place's alignment
   133:   to reserve and materialize dynamically aligned storage. The parameter
   134:   alignment tests inspect IR on all six native targets and use an opaque,
   135:   separately host-compiled observer for native x86-64 callee addresses.
   136: - The generic JIT loads already-produced host-native objects and resolves
   137:   explicit bindings. It is not a second source-language compiler and must stay
   138:   independent of frontend semantic structures.
   139: - The command-line driver accepts C source/preprocessed C plus native
   140:   objects/archives where the selected action permits them. Unknown languages,
   141:   retired module-root options, and unsupported source extensions must fail
   142:   explicitly rather than being forwarded or guessed.
   143: 
   144: - `__builtin_va_list` is a builtin type spelling, never a `void *` macro.
   145:   Both primitive-type scanners preserve its identity, and arbitrary typedef
   146:   aliases share the unqualified `C_TYPE_VA_LIST`. Typedef names alone do not
   147:   confer that identity. `va_start` and `va_copy` lower their destination through
   148:   the existing place continuation and retain it while evaluating the copy
   149:   source. List members, subscripts and dereferences follow the same address
   150:   conversion as named objects; every operand is evaluated once. Invalid list

    35:   parse and `c_lower_to_ir` in `c_gen.c` builds the `IrType`. They disagreed
    36:   about `#pragma pack` before this: the fold packed and the IR did not, so a
    37:   folded size contradicted the object it sized.
    38:   A packed bit-field takes the next bit rather than the next storage unit of
    39:   its declared type, which is what Clang and GCC do and what makes
    40:   `struct __attribute__((packed)) { int a : 3; int b : 30; }` five bytes. The
    41:   unit such a field is *read* through is chosen after the aggregate's size is
    42:   known, by sliding it back until it lies inside the object -- a
    43:   read-modify-write through a unit hanging off the end would clobber the next
    44:   object -- and where the object is too small for the declared type to sit
    45:   anywhere, by narrowing the unit to the smallest power of two that covers the
    46:   field: `struct __attribute__((packed)) { char c; int b : 5; char t; }` is
    47:   three bytes, so `b` is read through the byte at offset one, which is again
    48:   what Clang and GCC do. **The narrowed width lives on `IrField.access_size`**,
    49:   zero meaning the declared type's size, and `ir_field_access_size` is what
    50:   every reader asks: the load and the read-modify-write in `c_gen.c`, the four
    51:   constant-initializer folds there, the `IR_OPCODE_AGGREGATE` selectors in
    52:   `machine_x86_64.c` and `machine_aarch64.c`, and the two canonical emitters in
    53:   `codegen.c`. It is also the one place a `LOAD` or `STORE` may disagree with
    54:   its place's type, which `ir_place_narrow_bit_field_access` is what validation
    55:   admits it through. **A field whose bits cross every unit that fits has no
    56:   single-unit access even then**, which is every width whose byte count is not
    57:   a power of two: `union __attribute__((packed)) { long long b : 40; }` is five
    58:   bytes and there is no five-byte load. `access_size` then carries the *span*
    59:   rather than a unit, and `ir_field_access_pieces` decomposes it into the
    60:   descending powers of two that cover it -- five is four plus one, seven is
    61:   four plus two plus one, and nine, the widest span there is, is eight plus
    62:   one. Clang writes the same access as `i40` and lowers it to the same
    63:   sequence. Every reader walks the pieces: the frontend assembles a load out of
    64:   them and read-modify-writes each one in turn, reaching the bytes past the
    65:   first through a `unsigned char*` taken from the member place, and the
    66:   constant folds deposit the bits one byte at a time because no integer is nine
    67:   bytes wide. Both native `IR_OPCODE_AGGREGATE` selectors walk the same pieces,
    68:   merging only each field's intersection with the current piece. Siblings
    69:   sharing the complete storage unit accumulate together; zero-width separators
    70:   emit no stores. Keep the packed, anonymous and unnamed initializer fixtures
    71:   in the strict MIR corpus. **A `_Bool` bit-field is extracted
    72:   like any other**: its declared type is not an integer, so it used to skip the
    73:   extraction and hand back the whole `_Bool` unit -- every neighbour's bits with
    74:   it, normalized to one, which is why a `_Bool` that was the only set bit still
    75:   read correctly -- and the write clobbered them. The unit it is read and
    76:   written through is the unsigned integer of the same width, because the shift
    77:   has to see the raw byte. A zero-width bit-field keeps aligning to its declared
    78:   type even inside a packed aggregate, which is also what Clang and GCC do.
    79:   **A zero width belongs to the *unnamed* bit-field alone**: C requires a named
    80:   one to be at least one bit wide (C23 6.7.3.2p4) and both reference compilers
    81:   refuse `int b : 0;`, where accepting it laid out a member that occupies no
    82:   bits and can still be assigned and read back (issue #710). The width is
    83:   checked in `c_lower_to_ir` where the constant expression is folded, so the
    84:   expression spelling `int b : 1 - 1;` is refused with the literal one rather
    85:   than only the spelling the parse fast path folds. The report shares the
    86:   one-diagnostic-per-type budget with the rejected alignment specifier -- they
    87:   are one `definition_rejection` slot whose kind travels with the message --
    88:   and the definition still lays out, the way a rejected alignment specifier
    89:   still hands back an alignment, so the program hears about the member it wrote
    90:   rather than about a type that never got a layout.
    91:   On AArch64 the accesses this reaches land at whatever byte offset packing
    92:   chose, and the scaled unsigned-immediate load/store addresses only multiples
    93:   of its own width, so `codegen_canonical_a64_memory_operation_base` falls back
    94:   to the unscaled form -- `LDUR`/`STUR`, any byte offset in a nine-bit field --
    95:   and materializes the address beyond that. It used to fail the whole
    96:   compilation instead, which `struct __attribute__((packed)) { char a; int v :
    97:   32; }` already reached before any of this.
    98:   **A bit-field is not a field for System V's unaligned-field rule.** Its
    99:   declared type is not what it occupies -- `int value : 20` at bit eight of a
   100:   packed record occupies twenty bits inside the first eightbyte, not four
   101:   bytes at an offset no `int` would sit at -- so
   102:   `ir_system_v_abi_classify_bit_field` merges INTEGER into each eightbyte the
   103:   field's *bits* fall in and leaves the declared type out of it, which is what
   104:   the psABI writes and what clang and GCC compile. Asking the declared type
   105:   instead sent every such record to memory, so the five bytes of
   106:   `struct __attribute__((packed)) { char lead; int value : 20; char tail; }`
   107:   came back through a hidden pointer where System V returns them in `rax`
   108:   (issue #721); a program agreed with itself and disagreed with the object
   109:   next to it. An *unnamed* nonzero-width field has a versioned interoperability
   110:   boundary (GitHub #391): measured Clang 18.1.3 treats it as padding, while
   111:   GCC 13.3 merges INTEGER. For `struct { float f; int : 20; }`, that changes
   112:   an argument from `xmm0` to `rdi` and a result from `xmm0` to `rax`.
   113:   Buster preserves its historical padding default and exposes
   114:   `-fsysv-unnamed-bitfields=integer|padding` for explicit selection. Zero-width
   115:   fields remain padding. [LLVM #216777](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/216777)
   116:   adopted GCC's behavior, and [LLVM #220788](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/220788)
   117:   added `-fclang-abi-compat=23` to restore the older behavior; a compiler's major
   118:   version alone is therefore not proof of the selected convention. These are
   119:   upstream implementation records, not a claim that every Clang release has
   120:   the change. The class is always INTEGER, since C admits no bit-field of
   121:   floating type. AArch64 never asked: its aggregates up to sixteen bytes take
   122:   INTEGER parts by size once `ir_homogeneous_float_abi` declines them.
   123:   **A union member starts at bit zero whichever kind it is**, so a union sizes
   124:   to the bits its widest member *occupies* rather than to that member's
   125:   declared type: `union __attribute__((packed)) { char c; int b : 5; }` is one

     1: # `_Float16`, long double, assembly, and Wasm boundaries
     2: 
     3: [Agent instructions](../../../AGENTS.md) · Paths and commands below are relative to the repository root.
     4: 
     5: `signbit` reads the original float representation through canonical memory
     6: operations: bit 31 for binary32, bit 63 for binary64, byte-eight bit 15 for
     7: x87 and byte-eight bit 63 for binary128. It does not widen or narrow a value
     8: before observing the sign. This preserves signaling NaNs, signed zero and
     9: floating exception state. `basic_c_signbit_images.c` and its independent host
    10: observer cover those images across the native target/mode/frontend/PIC matrix.
    11: AArch64 binary128 widening uses ordinary MIR frame images; see the machine
    12: guide for its exact conversion and native floating-environment checks. This
    13: does not claim binary128 scalar ABI or arithmetic support.
    14: The host FENV fixture in `tests/host_aarch64_float_to_f128.c` uses ordinary
    15: GNU inline asm for `mrs`/`msr` reads and writes of `fpsr`/`fpcr`; the baseline
    16: AArch64 inline-assembly vocabulary selects these checked system-register rows
    17: as closed MIR transactions, with strict no-fallback compilation retaining
    18: their source/debug locations.

    20: Read the matching sections; [the frontend index](../frontend.md) lists these notes in their original order. Cross-references such as “above” and “below” follow that order.
    21: 
    22: - **`_Float16` is IEEE-754 binary16, and it is a real type rather than a
    23:   storage alias.** Two naturally aligned bytes on every supported target
    24:   (`TargetDataLayout.float16_type`, `C_TYPE_FLOAT16`), its own rank below
    25:   `float` in the usual arithmetic conversions, its own place in the
    26:   `vector_size` element ladder, and `_Float16 _Complex` beside it as clang's
    27:   extension (`C_TYPE_FLOAT16_COMPLEX`, two contiguous halves). The C23
    28:   `f16`/`F16` constant suffix and the `__FLT16_*__` prelude macros carry it,
    29:   and every constant rounds through one encoder pair,
    30:   `c_ir_float16_bits_from_f64` / `c_ir_float16_to_f64` in `c_gen.c`: no host
    31:   half type is used, because the compiler builds under four C compilers and
    32:   cross-compiles. Every static-initializer writer routes its 16-bit case
    33:   through that pair; the byte strings in `c_test_float16_type` were taken
    34:   from clang 18 compiling the same spellings.
    35: 
    36:   **Native code generation implements the binary16 runtime vocabulary.**
    37:   Scalar arguments and results use the ABI's real floating position: the low
    38:   sixteen bits of an XMM register on System V and Win64 x86-64, and the H/V
    39:   register position on AArch64. The direct emitter and the MIR value-shape
    40:   tables agree on that classification, so `none`, `mir-stack`, `fast` and
    41:   `quality` compile the same signatures without machine fallback. Baseline
    42:   targets need no F16C or AVX512-FP16 feature. On x86-64, lowering widens each half through
    43:   `__extendhfsf2`, performs arithmetic in binary32, and rounds immediately back
    44:   through `__truncsfhf2`; a binary64 source uses `__truncdfhf2`. Darwin x86-64's
    45:   compiler-runtime entry points carry the half bits in the integer ABI even
    46:   though ordinary `_Float16` still uses XMM, so lowering bridges those symbols
    47:   through an internal `unsigned short` view. AArch64 uses baseline scalar `FCVT`
    48:   instructions for the same half/wider conversions, without runtime imports.
    49:   Apple AArch64 packs named stack-only scalar arguments at their natural
    50:   alignment; unnamed variadic arguments retain eightbyte-aligned slots;
    51:   the canonical and MIR call layouts share that rule. Comparisons and truth
    52:   conversion widen exactly, negation flips the binary16 sign bit without
    53:   quieting a NaN, and vector arithmetic/comparisons scalarize through the same
    54:   per-lane operations. Hosted x86-64 links therefore need the compiler-runtime/libgcc
    55:   builtins, just as complex multiply/divide links do. The Wasm, eBPF and LLVM
    56:   bitcode backends retain their own structured ABI/instruction checks; this is
    57:   a native x86-64/AArch64 contract, not a claim that those formats gained a
    58:   binary16 ABI.
    59: - **`__bf16` has a distinct bfloat16 representation.** Its own
    60:   `C_TYPE_BFLOAT16`, `TargetDataLayout.bfloat16_type` (two naturally aligned
    61:   bytes), and `IrType.float_format` discriminating `IR_FLOAT_FORMAT_BFLOAT16`
    62:   from `IR_FLOAT_FORMAT_IEEE` at the same 16-bit width; an equal-width
    63:   identity conversion between the two formats is invalid. Scalar constants
    64:   round once from the binary64 carrier through
    65:   `c_ir_bfloat16_bits_from_f64`, and integer-to-bfloat16 conversion uses
    66:   precision 8. No backend implements bfloat16 runtime operations, so a
    67:   `__bf16` value needed at run time is still refused by the structured codegen
    68:   diagnostic; unlike binary16, it has no compiler-runtime lowering. Mixed
    69:   `_Float16`/`__bf16` arithmetic selects
    70:   `_Float16`: bfloat16 carries the lower conversion rank
    71:   (`c_ir_float_conversion_rank` ranks it below binary16 despite equal storage
    72:   width), so the usual arithmetic conversions convert `__bf16` to `_Float16`
    73:   numerically, never as an identity. This can reduce exponent range.
    74: 
    75:   Wide-source constants retain their target x87/binary128 payload in the two
    76:   integer limbs of `CIrConstantValue`; `c_ir_constant_float_literal` rounds a
    77:   literal in its source format first, and `c_ir_constant_wide_float_cast`
    78:   rounds directly to the destination through the existing rational machinery.
    79:   Neither casts nor arithmetic/comparison/truth/integer consumers may read a
    80:   wide value through the binary64 carrier. Scalar, array, aggregate and local
    81:   static BF16 initializers use this path. An explicit cast to `double` still
    82:   deliberately rounds to binary64. The binary128 rational converter uses a
    83:   two-limb quotient, not a host extended type or a new numeric dependency.
    84:   This does not add native BF16 arithmetic/ABI or binary128 scalar ABI support.
    85: 
    86:   `c_parse_bfloat16_builtin` carries the LLVM18 BF16/AVX-NE-CONVERT signatures
    87:   and the select/FMA dependencies used by the pristine resource headers.
    88:   Identifier binding and type queries record their uses in a sparse worklist;
    89:   `c_parse_validate_bfloat16_builtin_calls` checks arity and operand types
    90:   before unused definitions are omitted. Nested, unreachable and unevaluated
    91:   calls are still checked. Same-sized GNU arithmetic vectors are convertible
    92:   by value; pointer pointees retain format/size identity, with ordinary C
    93:   null/void-pointer conversions. This signature checking is not a claim of
    94:   native intrinsic lowering. `c_test_bfloat16_semantic_acceptance` covers
    95:   source-format rounding on six layouts in both frontend forms, mixed-format
    96:   identity, positive/negative builtin operands, and deep nested calls.
    97: - **`long double` is 80-bit x87 on System V x86-64, and it is memory-only.**
    98:   Transport, the four arithmetic operators, negation, the six comparisons,
    99:   truth conversion, and the conversions to and from the narrower floats and
   100:   integers through 64 bits all lower, and a variadic argument takes the sixteen-
   101:   byte, sixteen-aligned overflow slot the ABI requires. Every one of those is
   102:   a *closed* x87 transaction: it loads its operands from frame slots, operates,
   103:   stores the result back, and leaves the x87 stack as empty as it found it, so
   104:   no value is ever live in an ST register across a machine instruction and the
   105:   register allocators need no x87 class. Machine selection carries resolved
   106:   SysV f80 values in sixteen-byte frame slots and selects arithmetic, negate,
   107:   unordered-aware comparisons, f32/f64 conversion, signed integers through
   108:   64 bits and unsigned integers through 64 bits. The six `MACHINE_X64_F80_*`
   109:   rows have explicit frame operands and memory/barrier effects. Only the ABI
   110:   bridges leave ST(0), or ST(0)/ST(1) for complex results, live beside a call or
   111:   return. Single-f80 wrappers use the same ABI-proven bridge. SSA joins use
   112:   two ordinary integer limbs and restore the frame value at block entry.
   113:   Unsigned-64 conversion composes signed conversion, comparison, scalar masks
   114:   and an exact zero/2^63 correction at extended precision; it preserves all
   115:   four rounding modes and restores the complete control word after truncation.
   116:   The direct implementation is `codegen_canonical_x64_emit_f80_*` in
   117:   `codegen.c`; f80/i128 conversions remain unsupported by both backends.
   118:   Preserve the caller's
   119:   x87 control word: canonical truncate helpers and the MIR conversion row
   120:   may temporarily change only rounding control for a C integer cast, then
   121:   restore the exact saved word. `tests/basic_c_f80_machine.c` checks this
   122:   subset under strict MIR; its HOST/LIBRARY/FENV modes support independent
   123:   Clang callers and callees. `tests/basic_c_f80_u64.c` covers unsigned
   124:   thresholds, fractions and positive zero, with CLIENT/LIBRARY/FENV modes
   125:   for Clang boundary checks across all four rounding-control modes.
   126:   An **aggregate** carrying an f80 payload takes one of two paths, and which
   127:   one is the ABI classification's answer, never a walk of the fields. System
   128:   V's merger algorithm orders its rules equal, NO_CLASS, MEMORY, INTEGER, x87,
   129:   SSE — **INTEGER beats x87** — so musl's `union ldshape`, an f80 overlaid
   130:   with `struct { uint64_t m; uint16_t se; }`, classifies as two INTEGER
   131:   eightbytes and rides two general-purpose registers, which is what clang
   132:   compiles it to (`{ i64, i64 }`) and is not what a literal "an x87 class
   133:   makes the value MEMORY" reading produces. A shape the merger cannot
   134:   reconcile — `union { long double; unsigned long; }`, whose X87_UP tail is
   135:   then unaccompanied, or `union { long double; double; }`, or anything past
   136:   two eightbytes — goes to memory whole, byval in and sret out. Neither asks
   137:   anything of the x87 stack: their bytes are copied. Only a classification
   138:   that really carries an X87/X87_UP part needs the x87 vocabulary, and
   139:   `ir_abi_value_has_x87_part` is the predicate every gate asks. Objects of
   140:   more than one `long double` — `long double v[2]`, local or global — lower
   141:   the same way, because the array is memory-class and its elements are reached
   142:   one f80 at a time. `tests/basic_c_long_double_aggregate.c` covers the
   143:   semantics under all four allocators; the ABI itself is only pinned by
   144:   `tests/basic_c_long_double_aggregate_{caller,callee}.c`, linked against the
   145:   host compiler in both directions, because a caller and a callee this
   146:   compiler produced agree with each other whatever they agree on.
   147:   Reading one back out of a `va_list` admits exactly the two shapes the
   148:   argument side does, and for the same reason. The X87/X87_UP pair classifies
   149:   into memory, so a variadic `long double` is never in the register save area
   150:   whatever the argument counters hold: `va_arg` realigns the overflow cursor
   151:   to sixteen, takes the slot, and advances past all sixteen bytes. Canonical
   152:   emission copies through x87 and clears padding; MIR copies the ten payload
   153:   bytes directly, preserving payload/sign and making no padding promise.
   154:   An opaque aggregate reads back through the ordinary eightbyte path.
   155:   `tests/basic_c_va_arg_long_double.c` pins both under all four
   156:   allocators, including a read through a `va_list *` and one past a `va_copy`
   157:   — the spellings musl's `pop_arg` uses. Strict MIR selection, allocation and
   158:   execution are also registered for this fixture.
   159:   A *static* x87 initializer is folded rather than emitted:
   160:   `c_ir_ext80_fold_initializer` in `c_gen.c` evaluates a constant expression
   161:   over numeric literals — `+ - * /`, unary sign, parentheses — straight into
   162:   the 64-bit significand and sign/exponent pair the object writer stores, for a
   163:   scalar global, a function-local static, and each x87 element of an aggregate.
   164:   Every leaf rounds in its own declared type and every operation rounds in the
   165:   common real type the usual arithmetic conversions pick, which is what
   166:   reproduces C's per-operation rounding and makes the bytes Clang-identical; a
   167:   decimal fold would not, because `1/LDBL_EPSILON` is exactly 2^63 only once
   168:   musl's spelling of the epsilon has rounded to 2^-63 first. Overflow becomes
   169:   an infinity, underflow a signed zero, and the invalid operations — infinity
   170:   minus infinity, infinity times zero, infinity over infinity, zero over zero —
   171:   the default *positive* quiet NaN whatever the operand signs were, which is
   172:   the answer Clang's own folder gives and the one
   173:   `c_ir_fold_float_invalid_operation` gives the same expression inside a
   174:   function; the two have to stay together, because a disagreement prints `nan`
   175:   from one and `-nan` from the other. Those last two matter because musl spells
   176:   `INFINITY` as `1e5000f` and `NAN` as `(0.0f/0.0f)` for a compiler that does
   177:   not advertise the GNU builtins, so they are what a `long double` table in
   178:   libc-test is made of. An operation between two *integer* operands is refused
   179:   on purpose: it does not round at all, and `1/3` would need integer division
   180:   semantics (zero), rather than floating-point division — which is also why
   181:   `0/0` between two integer literals is a diagnostic here rather than the NaN
   182:   its floating spellings fold to, Clang rejecting that initializer outright.
   183:   So is an addition that aligns a genuine subnormal against a near-maximum
   184:   operand, which spans more of the
   185:   x87 exponent range than the folder's bignum holds — a zero operand is taken
   186:   as the exact identity instead of aligned, so only a real subnormal reaches
   187:   that edge. `tests/basic_c_long_double_static_initializer.c` pins the finite
   188:   arithmetic and `tests/basic_c_long_double_static_special.c` everything from
   189:   the infinities out, both against bytes read out of Clang's own object.
   190:   The canonical emitter still refuses a fixed wide-float parameter of a
   191:   variadic *definition* (the SysV `va_start`
   192:   register-save area does not account for it), an aggregate whose
   193:   classification carries an X87 class without being the ABI-proven single-f80
   194:   or complex shape, and every wide float on a target whose `long double` is
   195:   not this format.
   196: - **A module-level `__asm__` block emits into the module's text through
   197:   `codegen_emit_global_assembly` in `codegen.c`.** It interprets the
   198:   directives itself — `.text`, `.byte`, `.p2align`, and the symbol directives
   199:   `.globl`/`.global`, `.weak`, `.hidden`, `.type` and `.size` — and hands
   200:   every instruction it does not have a fixed encoding for to `assembly_encode`,
   201:   the same assembler the inline-assembly path uses, one line at a time. That
   202:   is where relocation support comes from: a `call sym` or a
   203:   `lea sym(%rip),%reg` against a name the block does not define becomes a
   204:   `CodegenModuleRelocation`. The assembler's PC-relative addend already carries
   205:   the distance from the relocated field to the end of its instruction, and the
   206:   module vocabulary's does not — the object writer subtracts four on the way
   207:   out — so the emitter adds those four back rather than restricting the shapes
   208:   it accepts. A symbol the block names does not need a C declaration: the
   209:   emitter adds one to `IrProgram.symbols` when the search misses, which is what
   210:   lets a startup object define `_start`. Two things follow from the AT&T/Intel

   697:   sites. Absolute inline pointer literals in executable text are rejected by
   698:   Apple's linker. Direct calls retain CALL26; ELF/PE address and TLS forms
   699:   retain their existing target contracts. The qualified-aggregate differential
   700:   corpus checks native Apple linking and execution across allocator modes.
   701: - `-fPIC` is a code model, not an accepted flag. It reaches code generation as
   702:   `CodegenModuleOptions.position_independent`, and generation resolves it for
   703:   the target: x86-64 ELF, where the relocations it changes are the ones `ld`
   704:   refuses in a shared object. A symbol another object could interpose --
   705:   `ir_symbol_is_interposable`, which is external or imported linkage without
   706:   hidden visibility -- has its address loaded out of its GOT slot
   707:   (`R_X86_64_GOTPCREL`) instead of computed rip-relative, and a direct call to
   708:   one is relocated `R_X86_64_PLT32` so the linker may route it through a
   709:   procedure linkage entry. Internal and hidden symbols keep the rip-relative
   710:   form, and a thread-local address is the thread-local model's to pick --
   711:   `codegen_thread_local_model` reads the same flag and answers general-dynamic
   712:   under it. The canonical emitter and the machine path make
   713:   the same decision from the same predicate: the selector writes a
   714:   `MachineSymbolReference` beside each call-target row and the module
   715:   relocation is derived from it, so the four allocators cannot disagree. One
   716:   object-writer decision follows from the model rather than from a relocation:
   717:   an unwind record's function pointer is relocated against a local text symbol
   718:   with the function's own offset, because an FDE naming a preemptible function
   719:   is the same PC-relative reference to an interposable symbol that `ld`
   720:   refuses in the body.
   721: - `-fPIE`/`-fpie` stay accepted and inert, and that is a statement rather than
   722:   an omission: every reference this compiler emits is already rip-relative, an
   723:   executable's own definitions are not interposable, its references to another
   724:   image's data are what the linker's copy relocation is for, and its own
   725:   thread-local block is still the initial one -- so the
   726:   position-independent-executable model asks for no code this compiler does not
   727:   already produce. `-fno-pic` clears the model; `-fno-pie` clears nothing
   728:   because nothing was set.
   729: - The built-in linker resolves both forms for the image it writes, which binds
   730:   every name in it: `PLT32` patches the same rel32 `PC32` does, and a GOT load
   731:   is relaxed back into the `lea` it would have been (`link_x86_relax_got_load`),
   732:   the same relaxation `ld` performs for a `GOTPCRELX` it can resolve. The ELF
   733:   reader takes `R_X86_64_GOTPCREL`, `GOTPCRELX` and `REX_GOTPCRELX` as one
   734:   kind for that reason, so a `-fPIC` object -- this compiler's or clang's --
   735:   links here. An instruction shape the relaxation does not recognize fails the
   736:   link by name rather than being rewritten. It relaxes the two indirect
   737:   thread-local models back to local-exec for the same reason
   738:   (`link_elf_relax_thread_local`).

   740: ## Wide integer conversion rounding
   741: 
   742: - AArch64 i128-to-f32/f64 casts normalize the magnitude as two scalar MIR
   743:   limbs and retain round/sticky/parity bits before one nearest-even rounding
   744:   at the destination precision. A zero high limb selects the ordinary u64
   745:   conversion; a nonzero high limb scales the rounded significand by an exact
   746:   power of two. Suppress the modulo-64 cross shift when CLZ(high) is zero.
   747:   Signed results restore the floating sign only after forming the magnitude.
   748:   The registered fixture constructs expected IEEE images in integer code,
   749:   checks even/odd ties and significand carries across the limb boundary, and
   750:   requires all desktop AArch64 targets and allocator/frontend combinations.
   751: 
   752: ## Incoming argument reads
   753: 
   754: Both `MACHINE_X64_LOAD_INCOMING` and `MACHINE_A64_LOAD_INCOMING` declare
   755: `MACHINE_MEMORY_EFFECT_READ`. Their implicit frame-relative address has no
   756: fixed stack-slot identity, so the scheduler treats them as unknown memory and
   757: chains them against every pending slot access. No architecture-specific
   758: scheduler exception is needed. The stack-alias tests explicitly recognize
   759: incoming reads independently of that metadata; otherwise a missing descriptor
   760: bit could disappear from both the scheduler and its test oracle.
   761: 
   762: ## AArch64 large aggregate copies
   763: 
   764: The three frame/pointer copy rows emit a bounded eight-byte loop at 256 bytes
   765: and above, followed by exact 4/2/1-byte tails. X9/X10 are declared cursor clobbers;
   766: reserved X16/X17 carry the count and data. CBNZ preserves flags. Pointer operands
   767: are captured before either cursor is overwritten, and the encoder reserves a
   768: constant 128-byte capacity for this form. Smaller copies retain inline accesses.
   769: The same memory effects and source/destination ownership apply in every allocator.

   197: ## Configured external compiler fixtures
   198: 
   199: The registered driver PIC fixture uses `BUSTER_HOST_C_COMPILER_ID`, supplied
   200: from CMake's configured compiler identity, rather than assuming that the host
   201: compiler accepts Clang flags. Clang/AppleClang use `-target`; native GCC does
   202: not. The executable path and optional `BUSTER_HOST_C_COMPILER_ARG1` remain
   203: separate arguments, including `zig` with `cc`. An unknown family fails the
   204: fixture with an explicit diagnostic instead of inheriting Clang's options.
   205: The argument-policy regression runs on every test host; real ELF fixture
   206: compilation, relocation inspection, linking and execution are native Linux
   207: x86-64 checks. They preserve signed absolute `R_X86_64_32S` and GOTPCREL
   208: coverage; the indexed fixture makes both GCC and Clang produce those forms.
   209: The fixture is compiled `-O2`, because that is where both narrow an address to
   210: 32 bits and emit a GOT load with no REX prefix -- the `R_X86_64_GOTPCRELX`
   211: shapes the linker converts to an absolute immediate rather than to an address
   212: computation.
   213: For x86-64 Linux, the native linker removes an undefined
   214: `_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_` marker only when no relocation or explicit entry request
   215: uses it. It copies the symbol/relocation view before remapping indices, preserving
   216: the input object. Real GOT-base references and ordinary unresolved imports keep
   217: their errors. The registered link tests cover these boundaries and byte-identical
   218: output relative to an object without the unused marker.
   219: 
   220: The native driver's `compiler_discovery_self_test` runs before every combination
   221: matrix and covers real Clang identity, platform/override selection, and failed
   222: GCC requests preserving existing configurations. The GCC row selects Homebrew
   223: `gcc-15` on macOS; see [build policy](build.md) for `BUSTER_GCC` overrides and
   224: the logged compiler provenance.
   225: 
   226: For the user-level GCC workflow, with the selected build directory idle:
   227: 
   228: ```sh
   229: ./build.sh generate --cc gcc --ci --linker DEFAULT
   230: BUSTER_TEST_JOBS=1 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=1 ./build.sh build --config Debug -t test_all
   231: ```
   232: 
   233: Repeat with `--cc clang` on an idle tree. `generate` recreates the tree; do not
   234: run the two configurations concurrently in it. The ordinary combination
   235: matrix's GCC row is compile-only, so a green row alone does not certify this
   236: runtime workflow. Run the full registered suite explicitly; unrelated test
   237: failures remain failures and must not be hidden by this fixture repair.
   238: 
   239: ## Native differential matrix
   240: 
   241: `build.c` exposes `test_differential` (implementation: `tools/differential.c`).
   242: Use a fresh output directory and a built native `ide`; run `--self-test` before
   243: matrix execution. The driver and runner share `codegen_configurations.h` for
   244: allocator/optimization discovery. See [differential-testing.md](../differential-testing.md)
   245: for ABI fixtures, diagnostics, opt-in IR/MIR validation, sanitizer controls,
   246: reduction limits and evidence format. This supplements all existing gates;
   247: it does not replace target-matrix execution or the seeded differential corpus.
   248: 
   249: ## Source-equivalence campaigns
   250: 
   251: `ide test` also runs a bounded source-equivalence smoke campaign under all native
   252: allocator modes. `ide metamorphic` exposes the wider native/LLVM/Wasm64/eBPF
   253: matrix, optional engine discovery, explicit unexecuted rows, and grammar-aware
   254: failure reduction. See [metamorphic testing](../metamorphic-testing.md) for the
   255: transformation preconditions, reproducible seeds, strict execution mode and
   256: failure bundles. Cross-target compilation is not a behavioral pass.
   257: 
   258: ## External GPU consumers
   259: 
   260: `./build.sh test_gpu_toolchains` exposes explicit optional status; each selected
   261: `--profile` is required and fails on missing tools, version drift, compiler or
   262: consumer errors. See [GPU toolchain acceptance](../gpu-toolchain-validation.md).
   263: Its native `--self-test` checks the evidence machinery without vendor tools;
   264: registered GPU planner tests remain fast and deterministic.
   265: 
   266: ## Fixture arena ownership and memory reports
   267: 
   268: `ide test --verbose=1 --ci=1` emits `TEST_ARENA_V1` records; either verbose
   269: or CI mode enables them. Ordinary quiet tests retain the same fixture lifetimes.
   270: Records have stable module names, static fixture names, and invocation indices.
   271: `arena_slot=0` is the supplied fixture arena; slots 1 and 2 are the selected
   272: thread context's scratch arenas. Parallel modules buffer complete records and
   273: failure text separately, then replay in descriptor order after the lane barrier.

    43: session — always pass a body file. Write the body as a file rather than a
    44: shell string: backticks inside `$(cat <<EOF)` get command-substituted by zsh,
    45: which has mangled a commit message before.
    46: 
    47: `fj` supersedes the older workarounds. `tea`'s login for this host has no
    48: token, and the raw-`curl` recipe that went with it needed a browser
    49: `User-Agent` to get past Cloudflare's `403 error code: 1010`; `fj` is not
    50: subject to either problem.
    51: 
    52: **Issues are the task queue.** Work that is real but not being done right now
    53: becomes an issue, not a paragraph in an audit that nobody will find — a chip
    54: filed against a memory is invisible to the next agent, while an issue is
    55: something a fresh session can pick up cold. Write the body as a **prompt**: what
    56: is wrong and how it was diagnosed, the file and symbol names to start from,
    57: the constraints and do-not-retries that earlier work already paid for, how to
    58: validate the fix (which oracle, which harness, which counters), and a
    59: definition of done. State what was measured and when, so a stale claim is
    60: recognisable as stale; the tree moves fast enough that a count quoted without
    61: a date is a trap. Issues #537-#549 are examples of the form.
    62: 
    63: **Push a rebase before you re-verify it.** A rebase onto a moved `main` is
    64: followed by a full local pass — `test_all`, `test_self_host`, whichever compat
    65: harness the change touches — and that pass takes longer than CI takes to start.
    66: Push the rebased branch first, as long as the runners are not already saturated
    67: with other work, so the matrix runs while the local pass runs; the two agree
    68: almost always, and when they disagree you have both answers sooner. Force-push
    69: with `--force-with-lease`, never a bare `--force`, so a branch someone else
    70: advanced is not overwritten. This is a rebase rule, not a general one: a branch
    71: whose content is still changing waits for the local pass, because a red CI run
    72: on a commit you already know is incomplete tells nobody anything.

    31: ## 2. New findings
    32: 
    33: Priority here is audit triage, not a formal project severity label: P1 means a directly demonstrated correctness failure; P2 means demonstrated scaling trouble that still needs workload-level prioritization.
    34: 
    35: ### N1 — P1: eBPF comparisons and Boolean-not skip their true result
    36: 
    37: **Location:** `src/buster/lib/compiler/ebpf/ebpf.c`, `ebpf_fe_emit_comparison` and the Boolean-not arm of `ebpf_fe_emit_unary`.
    38: 
    39: The comparison helper emits this structure:
    40: 
    41: ```text
    42: 0: result = 0
    43: 1: if comparison is true, jump +2
    44: 2: unconditional jump +1
    45: 3: result = 1
    46: 4: subsequent code
    47: ```
    48: 
    49: Offsets are relative to the next instruction. A taken conditional branch at instruction 1 therefore reaches instruction 4, not instruction 3. The false branch also reaches instruction 4. `result = 1` is unreachable, so every comparison handled by this helper returns false. Boolean-not uses the same faulty layout, making `!false` return false as well. The current source is visible [here](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b/src/buster/lib/compiler/ebpf/ebpf.c#L1364-L1473).
    50: 
    51: The probe calls the actual backend emitter, then executes its output in a small host interpreter for the emitted instruction subset. It covers fourteen comparison operations, including signed/unsigned boundary values, pointer equality/inequality, and Boolean equality/inequality. **220/440 comparison cases passed before the fix; all 220 true cases failed. Boolean-not passed only 1/2.**
    52: 
    53: **Fix:** change the two affected conditional offsets from `2` to `1`; keep their unconditional offsets unchanged. The unrelated Boolean-normalization sequence has a different layout, so its `+2` must not be changed mechanically.
    54: 
    55: This is not a kernel-verifier or end-to-end C-program execution result. It is a direct semantic test of emitted instructions, reinforced by the backend's own relative-jump patching convention.
    56: 
    57: Ready issue: [ebpf-boolean.md](issues/ebpf-boolean.md). Fix: patchset 01.
    58: 
    59: ### N2 — P1: eBPF signed bitwise-not loses sign extension
    60: 
    61: **Location:** `ebpf_fe_emit_unary`, `IR_UNARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_NOT`.

    27: 
    28: ```sh
    29: python3 publish.py
    30: python3 publish.py --checkout /path/to/buster --publish
    31: ```
    32: 
    33: On publication, the helper fetches GitHub main, checks exact production preimages, applies/tests each patch in a separate temporary worktree, and only then creates issues, pushes new branches, and opens **draft** PRs. It does not use or modify the checkout's working files or push archived history, and never force-pushes. It detects existing reports using audit markers or exact titles, and existing PRs using their audit branch/marker. A closed matching item or an unexpected existing branch stops the run for review. Exact-title matching is not semantic duplicate detection: review current issues/PRs before invoking publication.
    34: 
    35: Live GitHub publication has not been tested here. GitHub writes cannot be atomic across issues/branches/PRs; successful URLs are saved incrementally in publication-result.json if a later step fails. Full CI/self-host and platform-specific gates remain required before merging the drafts. No issues are auto-closed by this script; closing keywords take effect only upon a later merge.
    36: 
    37: ## Symbol growth probe
    38: 
    39: The probe includes the actual eBPF source and needs the repository include directory. From a repository root, replace /path/to/bundle with this extracted bundle:
    40: 
    41: ```sh
    42: clang -O2 -g -fwrapv -funsigned-char -Wno-unused-function -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Isrc /path/to/bundle/evidence/ebpf_symbols.c -Wl,--gc-sections -pthread -lm -o /tmp/buster-ebpf-symbols && /tmp/buster-ebpf-symbols
    43: ```
    44: 
    45: The counts printed as key_comparisons follow N(N-1)/2 analytically. The timings are illustrative, not a benchmark acceptance gate.

===== docs/audits/2026-09-06/issues/ebpf-boolean.md =====
--- lines 1-34 ---
     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-06:ebpf-boolean -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-06 against GitHub `main` at `ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b`. The affected implementation was authenticated by Git blob hash, then tested in a recovered checkout at `6d2bdbf9d19e15be93cb2f09fe0c467ba2fa70d2`. This is focused implementation testing, not a successful full build of current `main`.
     4: 
     5: 
     6: ## What is wrong
     7: 
     8: `ebpf_fe_emit_comparison` emits `MOV result,0; Jcc +2; JA +1; MOV result,1`. A branch offset is relative to the next instruction; taken `Jcc +2` lands after `MOV result,1`, and the false path's `JA +1` also lands there. Consequently every supported comparison lowered through this helper returns false, including true integer, pointer, and Boolean comparisons.
     9: 
    10: `IR_UNARY_BOOLEAN_NOT` in `ebpf_fe_emit_unary` repeats the same four-instruction pattern, so `!false` also returns false.
    11: 
    12: Start in [ebpf.c](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b/src/buster/lib/compiler/ebpf/ebpf.c#L1364-L1473). The file's own `ebpf_patch_jump` computes `target - instruction - 1`, independently confirming the offset convention.
    13: 
    14: ## Reproduction and measured evidence
    15: 
    16: The supplied `tests/ebpf_scalar_regression.c` emits real backend bytecode and executes the relevant instruction subset in a small host-side interpreter. It tests all fourteen comparison operations (including signed boundary values) and both Boolean-not inputs. This does not load any code into the Linux kernel.
    17: 
    18: Before the fix, comparison cases pass 220/440 and Boolean-not passes 1/2. Every true comparison case fails. Example: integer equality of zero and zero yields zero instead of one. Both false and true arms are exercised; this is not just an opcode-byte assertion.
    19: 
    20: ## Required fix
    21: 
    22: Change the two affected conditional-branch offsets from `2` to `1`. Keep the following unconditional branch at `1`. Do not blanket-replace all offsets: the separate Boolean-normalization sequence has a different layout and its conditional `+2` is correct.
    23: 
    24: ## Validation / definition of done
    25: 
    26: Apply the eBPF scalar patchset and run `python3 tests/ebpf_scalar_regression.py`. The combined suite (including the separate signed bitwise-not issue) improves from 244/474 to 474/474. Each fix must preserve signed/unsigned predicates, Boolean values, and distinct input/result registers.
    27: 
    28: The focused suite passed with Clang at -O0 and -O2, Clang -O2 with ASan/UBSan, and GCC -O2. Run the eBPF module suite, `test_all`, and Release self-host in the full current tree; add an emitted-program integration test or kernel/independent VM check before treating the target as comprehensively validated.
    29: 
    30: ## Existing work / scope
    31: 
    32: This is separate from #102 (verifier-stack slot reuse), #43 (vector/intrinsic semantics), and the native-machine performance PRs. No matching report was found in the current issue search or open-PR inventory. The small correctness patch is in `01-ebpf-scalar-correctness.patch`.
    33: 
    34: The standalone tests compile the repository's actual implementation. They are not mocks of the emitter, but they do not replace full `test_all`, Release self-host, or target integration tests. The audit host could not bootstrap self-host because TCC was missing. Current GitHub source was readable, but a full current checkout and remote publishing were unavailable.
===== docs/audits/2026-09-06/issues/ebpf-signed-not.md =====
--- lines 1-34 ---
     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-06:ebpf-signed-not -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-06 against GitHub `main` at `ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b`. The affected implementation was authenticated by Git blob hash, then tested in a recovered checkout at `6d2bdbf9d19e15be93cb2f09fe0c467ba2fa70d2`. This is focused implementation testing, not a successful full build of current `main`.
     4: 
     5: 
     6: ## What is wrong
     7: 
     8: `IR_UNARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_NOT` emits XOR with -1, then calls `ebpf_fe_store_result(..., true, false)`. The last argument forces unsigned normalization even for signed integer result types. The adjacent integer-negation case already uses the result type's signedness correctly.
     9: 
    10: For a signed 32-bit zero operand the actual emitted sequence leaves `0x00000000ffffffff`, while the backend's normalized signed representation should be `0xffffffffffffffff` (-1). The same mistake affects negative results at widths 8 and 16. The low-width bits are correct, but the high bits are wrong for later 64-bit operations and signed use. The cast emitter normalizes to the destination width, so a wider destination is not a substitute for establishing the source's signed representation.
    11: 
    12: Start in [ebpf_fe_emit_unary](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b/src/buster/lib/compiler/ebpf/ebpf.c#L1449-L1464) and compare its negate case, `ebpf_fe_normalize`, `ebpf_fe_store_result`, and `ebpf_fe_emit_cast`.
    13: 
    14: ## Reproduction
    15: 
    16: The supplied real-emitter bytecode test checks bitwise-not for 8/16/32/64-bit integers, signed and unsigned, on four inputs per combination. Before the fix 23/32 cases pass and 9 fail. The signed-32 zero input produces 4294967295, not the 64-bit representation of -1.
    17: 
    18: The witness is at the canonical-IR/emitter boundary. It is not a claim that an end-to-end C translation unit was compiled and executed on a kernel eBPF target during this audit.
    19: 
    20: ## Required fix
    21: 
    22: Pass `type && type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER && type->is_signed` to result normalization, matching integer negate. Preserve unsigned and 64-bit behavior.
    23: 
    24: ## Validation / definition of done
    25: 
    26: `python3 tests/ebpf_scalar_regression.py` includes these 32 cases plus comparison and logical-not cases. The combined suite passes 474/474 after the two independent correctness fixes, on Clang -O0/-O2, Clang -O2 with ASan/UBSan, and GCC -O2.
    27: 
    28: Add integration coverage for storing/reloading the narrow result, signed comparisons, and widening, then run the normal eBPF tests, `test_all`, and Release self-host. Preserve enum/type normalization contracts rather than guessing additional signedness rules.
    29: 
    30: ## Existing work / scope
    31: 
    32: Separate from #102 and from the comparison-branch issue. Both simple fixes share `01-ebpf-scalar-correctness.patch`; this issue describes only signed result normalization.
    33: 
    34: The standalone tests compile the repository's actual implementation. They are not mocks of the emitter, but they do not replace full `test_all`, Release self-host, or target integration tests. The audit host could not bootstrap self-host because TCC was missing. Current GitHub source was readable, but a full current checkout and remote publishing were unavailable.
===== docs/audits/2026-09-06/issues/ebpf-symbol-growth.md =====
--- lines 1-37 ---
     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-06:ebpf-symbol-growth -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-06 against GitHub `main` at `ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b`. The affected implementation was authenticated by Git blob hash, then tested in a recovered checkout at `6d2bdbf9d19e15be93cb2f09fe0c467ba2fa70d2`. This is focused implementation testing, not a successful full build of current `main`.
     4: 
     5: 
     6: ## What is wrong
     7: 
     8: Every `ebpf_add_symbol_record` calls `ebpf_symbol_by_key`, which linearly searches all existing records even when inserting a fresh key. Building N unique symbols performs N(N-1)/2 unsuccessful key comparisons. Numeric symbol keys are already available; scanning the growing record array discards that advantage.
     9: 
    10: Start at [ebpf_symbol_by_key and ebpf_add_symbol_record](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b/src/buster/lib/compiler/ebpf/ebpf.c#L570-L594). Also inspect `ir_symbol_keys`, synthetic string symbols, duplicate references, relocation resolution, and final ELF index assignment.
    11: 
    12: ## Reproduction / measurement
    13: 
    14: The supplied `evidence/ebpf_symbols.c` invokes the actual insertion helper on fresh contexts. On this virtualized Linux host, one illustrative run produced:
    15: 
    16: | Unique keys | Comparisons implied by source | Helper elapsed microseconds |
    17: |---:|---:|---:|
    18: | 2,048 | 2,096,128 | 3,658 |
    19: | 4,096 | 8,386,560 | 5,966 |
    20: | 8,192 | 33,550,336 | 16,765 |
    21: | 16,384 | 134,209,536 | 63,632 |
    22: 
    23: The comparison counts are derived from the control flow, not PMU counters or an instrumented count. The elapsed values are one unpinned microbenchmark run, not a reliable speedup estimate, not an end-to-end compiler result, and not Zen 5 evidence. The exact asymptotic defect does not depend on those timings.
    24: 
    25: ## Requested work
    26: 
    27: Use a key-to-record-index projection or a compact map, with a clear ownership and invalidation contract. Store indices rather than raw pointers when the record vector can reallocate. Preserve idempotent insertion for repeated keys, stable ELF symbol ordering, and synthetic-symbol handling.
    28: 
    29: Measure the whole eBPF object-emission workload as well as symbol-heavy cases. Do not replace this with a SIMD full-table scan: deleting the repeated work is the first experiment.
    30: 
    31: ## Definition of done
    32: 
    33: Insertion cost is linear or expected-linear for unique keys. Duplicate keys reuse the correct record. Symbol and relocation outputs remain byte-identical where ordering is unchanged. Tests cover empty tables, growth, many globals/functions, synthetic strings, and repeated references. Report compiler elapsed time, memory, and index-building overhead; run eBPF tests, `test_all`, and Release self-host.
    34: 
    35: ## Existing work / scope
    36: 
    37: This concerns eBPF symbol-record construction, not #102's stack-slot allocation and not #117's ELF dynamic-object data lookup. No matching eBPF symbol-growth report appeared in the issue search. No performance patch is proposed here because a correct data-structure migration and an end-to-end benchmark exceed a two-line fix.
===== docs/audits/2026-09-06/issues/wasm-alignment.md =====
--- lines 1-38 ---
     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-06:wasm-alignment -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-06 against GitHub `main` at `ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b`. The affected implementation was authenticated by Git blob hash, then tested in a recovered checkout at `6d2bdbf9d19e15be93cb2f09fe0c467ba2fa70d2`. This is focused implementation testing, not a successful full build of current `main`.
     4: 
     5: 
     6: ## What is wrong
     7: 
     8: `wasm64_fe_load` and `wasm64_fe_store` write `log2(type->layout.alignment)` into the memory instruction without limiting the hint to the instruction's natural access width. A stronger object alignment can therefore make otherwise ordinary scalar bytecode invalid.
     9: 
    10: For an i32 with size 4 and alignment 16, the backend emits `28 04 00` for load and `36 04 00` for store: alignment exponent 4 where the opcode permits at most 2. Node/V8 rejects the resulting memory64 modules:
    11: 
    12: ```text
    13: invalid alignment; expected maximum alignment is 2, actual alignment is 4
    14: ```
    15: 
    16: Start in [wasm.c](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/ee3b5c5022bdddef07840b9d787e76dfb6fe6e8b/src/buster/lib/compiler/wasm/wasm.c#L1483-L1534).
    17: 
    18: ## Reproduction and oracle
    19: 
    20: `tests/wasm_memory_alignment_regression.c` calls the actual load/store helpers for eight scalar type shapes, seven alignments (1 through 64), and both memory directions. The Python runner embeds their exact bytes in 112 minimal memory64 modules and validates each using `new WebAssembly.Module` in Node v22.16.0, with `--experimental-wasm-memory64`.
    21: 
    22: Original implementation: 44/112 modules validate; 68 fail. Patched implementation: 112/112 validate. This is a real independent engine validator, not just a handwritten decoder. It validates modules, rather than executing a full C-produced program.
    23: 
    24: ## Required fix
    25: 
    26: Clamp the alignment hint to the scalar access width (at most 8 bytes for these supported scalar instructions). Preserve weaker/unaligned hints and do not change object allocation or layout alignment. Keep unsupported type handling separate.
    27: 
    28: ## Validation / definition of done
    29: 
    30: Apply `02-wasm-memory-alignment.patch`, then run `python3 tests/wasm_memory_alignment_regression.py` with a memory64-capable Node. `NODE` and `AUDIT_NODE_FLAGS` can select a different engine executable/flag spelling.
    31: 
    32: All 112 cases passed with emitted helpers built using Clang -O0/-O2, Clang -O2 with ASan/UBSan, and GCC -O2. Run the standard Wasm suite, `test_all`, and Release self-host. Integrate an over-aligned frontend-to-Wasm witness when a complete current checkout is available.
    33: 
    34: ## Existing work / scope
    35: 
    36: This is separate from #97 (Wasm shadow-stack reservation/placement). A search for `repo:buster14a/buster wasm alignment` returned no matching issue. None of the nine open PR descriptions covered this path.
    37: 
    38: The standalone tests compile the repository's actual implementation. They are not mocks of the emitter, but they do not replace full `test_all`, Release self-host, or target integration tests. The audit host could not bootstrap self-host because TCC was missing. Current GitHub source was readable, but a full current checkout and remote publishing were unavailable.
