===== docs/audits/2026-09-07/AUDIT_REPORT.md =====
--- lines 1-282 ---
     1: # buster — codebase audit, 6 September 2026
     2: 
     3: Revision audited: `d0ecad0d` (`tests: integrate runtime boundary regressions on desktop hosts`), cloned from `github.com/buster14a/buster`.
     4: 
     5: **Rebased 2026-09-07 onto `44a936a8`** (10 commits later). Four cited files had changed; the tree was rebuilt and every runnable reproducer re-run at that revision. All of them still reproduce — none of these defects were fixed by the intervening commits. Line numbers in this report and in `issues/` refer to `44a936a8`.
     6: 
     7: Baseline: Debug and Release both build clean with clang 18. `ide test` is green — **322668/322668 unit tests, 39/39 module tests**. Every defect below is therefore in territory the existing suite does not reach.
     8: 
     9: Scope note: the `2026-09-06` bundle already in `docs/audits/` covered the eBPF emitter, Wasm alignment, and runtime file/string boundaries. Those were excluded here.
    10: 
    11: **23 findings. 17 reproduced first-hand against the built compiler**, marked ✅. The rest come from subsystem passes and are marked accordingly. Ranked by severity.
    12: 
    13: ---
    14: 
    15: ## S1 — Silent miscompilation of valid C
    16: 
    17: The worst class in a compiler: correct C in, wrong answer out, no diagnostic. All seven were reproduced by differential test against clang 18 on the default target and allocator.
    18: 
    19: ### 1. ✅ Enums are always `int` — every enumerator outside 32-bit range is corrupted
    20: 
    21: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:42391` (`c_lower_to_ir`), same hardcode at `:24173` (`c_ir_emit_integer_value`).
    22: 
    23: An enum without a C23 fixed underlying type is unconditionally mapped to `s32_type`, instead of picking the type from the enumerator range.
    24: 
    25: ```c
    26: enum Flags { F_NONE = 0, F_HIGH = 0x80000000 };
    27: enum B { BB = 4294967296LL };
    28: printf("%d %lld %zu\n", F_HIGH > 0, (long long)BB, sizeof(enum B));
    29: ```
    30: 
    31: | | `F_HIGH > 0` | `BB` | `sizeof(enum B)` |
    32: |---|---|---|---|
    33: | clang | 1 | 4294967296 | 8 |
    34: | **ide** | **0** | **0** | **4** |
    35: 
    36: `BB` collapses to zero. Any enum used as a bit-flag set with bit 31 set — a very common pattern — silently compares as negative.
    37: 
    38: **Fix:** derive the underlying type from the enumerator range (`unsigned int` / `long` / `unsigned long long`). The rule is already written down for enum bit-fields at `c_gen.c:42751`; reuse it.
    39: 
    40: ### 2. ✅ Signed `__int128` division and remainder are wrong for every negative dividend
    41: 
    42: `src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/codegen.c:15088` (`codegen_generate_canonical_module_attempt`).
    43: 
    44: The `sign_xor` row (`XOR R9, R8`, emitted at `:15133`) overwrites R9 — which holds the **divisor's** sign mask — with the combined result sign, *before* the divisor-magnitude rows at `:15139–15142` read R9. So the divisor is negated iff the two signs differ, rather than iff the divisor is negative.
    45: 
    46: ```c
    47: volatile long long a = -100, b = 7;
    48: __int128 x = a, y = b;
    49: printf("q=%lld r=%lld\n", (long long)(x/y), (long long)(x%y));
    50: ```
    51: 
    52: clang: `q=-14 r=-2` — **ide: `q=0 r=-100`**. Divisor 7 becomes 2^128−7, the restoring loop terminates immediately, quotient is 0 and remainder is the whole dividend.
    53: 
    54: `tests/basic_c_int128.c:66-70` misses it because its only assertion is `q*37 + r == n`, which `q=0, r=n` satisfies trivially. The AArch64 sibling `codegen_canonical_a64_i128_divide` (`codegen.c:8104`) is correct — it keeps the divisor sign in x16 and the combined sign in x17.
    55: 
    56: **Fix:** emit `sign_xor`/`save_sign` *after* `divisor_high_sbb`. Pure reordering — R9 then still carries the divisor's own sign mask through the negation. Worth strengthening that test to compare against exact expected values.
    57: 
    58: ### 3. ✅ Every negative floating constant converted to an integer folds to −1
    59: 
    60: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:39410` (`c_ir_constant_cast`).
    61: 
    62: `(u64)source.floating` is undefined behaviour for a negative value. Clang lowers it to `vcvttsd2usi`, which returns `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`.
    63: 
    64: ```c
    65: static const long long L = (long long)(-2147483648.0);
    66: static const int T[3] = {(int)-1.5, (int)-2.5, (int)2.5};
    67: ```
    68: 
    69: | | `L` | `T` |
    70: |---|---|---|
    71: | clang | −2147483648 | `-1, -2, 2` |
    72: | **ide** | **−1** | **`-1, -1, 2`** |
    73: 
    74: The same line also drops the high limb for `__int128` targets: `static __int128 F = (__int128)1.5e30;` yields `0x…00000000FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`.
    75: 
    76: **Fix:** convert through `s64` when the value is negative, range-check against the target type, and populate `integer_high` for 128-bit targets.
    77: 
    78: ### 4. ✅ `_Bool` in an aggregate initializer keeps only bit 0 — and Debug rejects valid C outright
    79: 
    80: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:37855` (`c_ir_constant_initializer_store_integer_leaf`).
    81: 
    82: The literal fast path masks the value to the member's `bit_width` instead of comparing against zero. `_Bool` has `bit_width == 1`, so every **even** nonzero constant becomes `false`.
    83: 
    84: ```c
    85: struct S { _Bool b; };
    86: struct S s = { 2 };
    87: _Bool a[3] = {2, 256, 1};
    88: ```
    89: 
    90: clang: `b=1 a=1,1,1` — **Release ide: `b=0 a=0,0,1`**.
    91: 
    92: Two different failure modes from one bug: the Debug build instead **aborts the compiler** on this valid C — `assertion failed at c_gen.c:37995 in c_ir_constant_initializer_check_literal_leaf`. That differential gate is `#if !BUSTER_OPTIMIZE`, so Release is silent and wrong while Debug refuses to compile.
    93: 
    94: **Fix:** store `value != 0` when `child->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN` (C 6.3.1.2), or exclude boolean children from `c_ir_constant_initializer_leaf_class`.
    95: 
    96: ### 5. ✅ Unsigned constants ≥ 2^63 initializing a float member become negative
    97: 
    98: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:37903` (`c_ir_constant_initializer_fold_integer_leaf`).
    99: 
   100: The INTEGER_TO_FLOAT arm converts through `c_ir_integer_signed_value` — an `s64` — regardless of the literal's signedness.
   101: 
   102: ```c
   103: struct F { double d; };
   104: struct F f = { 18446744073709551615ULL };
   105: ```
   106: 
   107: clang: `1.8446744073709552e+19` — **ide: `-1`**. Same for `float` members and for `9223372036854775808ULL`. Debug aborts at `c_gen.c:37995` instead.
   108: 
   109: **Fix:** route this arm through `c_ir_constant_integer_to_float`, which already handles unsigned values and rounds at the destination precision.
   110: 
   111: ### 6. ✅ A `char[]` member initialized by a string literal gets one garbage byte, when the initializer also has a nested brace
   112: 
   113: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:20848` (`c_ir_lower_nested_compound_literal_step`).
   114: 
   115: The unbraced string literal is brace-elided into element 0 instead of being recognised as a whole-array string initializer.
   116: 
   117: ```c
   118: struct Point { int x, y; };
   119: struct Cfg { struct Point origin; char name[16]; int flags; };
   120: struct Cfg c = { .origin = {3,4}, .name = "widget", .flags = 7 };
   121: ```
   122: 
   123: clang: `name='widget' len=6` — **ide: `name='\xef' len=1`**.
   124: 
   125: The trigger is narrow but the shape is ordinary: it fires only when the initializer contains a nested brace or designator that routes it to the nested walker. `{ .name = "widget" }` on its own is correct, and the `static` version is correct — which is exactly why the tests miss it. The positional form `{ {1,2}, "cd" }` fails identically.
   126: 
   127: **Fix:** take the string branch before the aggregate-descent `while` loop — `c_ir_tokens_are_string_literals(...)` + `c_ir_emit_string_range_typed` + `c_ir_emit_store_place` — as the task-level branch at `c_gen.c:20605` already does for a braced string.
   128: 
   129: ### 7. ✅ `__int128` array/struct static initializers drop the high 64 bits
   130: 
   131: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:35234` and `:35503` (`c_ir_constant_initializer_bytes_legacy_core`).
   132: 
   133: `c_ir_constant_store_bits(..., bits, sign_extend)` takes a single `u64`, so a 128-bit member is written as its low 64 bits sign-extended and `converted.integer_high` is discarded.
   134: 
   135: ```c
   136: __int128 g4[2] = { ((__int128)1<<100), (__int128)0xffffffffffffffffULL };
   137: ```
   138: 
   139: `.data` via `objdump -s`:
   140: 
   141: ```
   142: clang:  00000000 00000000 00000000 10000000     <- 2^100
   143:         ffffffff ffffffff 00000000 00000000     <- 2^64-1
   144: ide:    00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000     <- 0
   145:         ffffffff ffffffff ffffffff ffffffff     <- -1
   146: ```
   147: 
   148: Both elements wrong: one loses its value entirely, the other is sign-extended into a different number. The scalar form `__int128 g1 = ((__int128)1<<100);` is correct — it takes the `IR_GLOBAL_INITIALIZER_BYTES` path — so only aggregate members are affected.
   149: 
   150: **Fix:** give the aggregate leaf writer a 128-bit path that stores `converted.integer` and `converted.integer_high` when `type->layout.size == 16`.
   151: 
   152: ---
   153: 
   154: ## S2 — The assembler emits wrong machine code
   155: 
   156: Verified by assembling with `ide cc -c` and disassembling the output with `objdump`. These are on APX / AVX-512 paths — directly on the Zen 5 target line.
   157: 
   158: ### 8. ✅ APX EVEX hardcodes `pp = 0` and `vvvv = 0` — instructions collide and decode as invalid
   159: 
   160: `src/buster/lib/compiler/assembly/x86_64_metadata.c:6984` (in `buster_x86_metadata_emit_form_to_scratch`).
   161: 
   162: `p1 |= apx_evex_fixed_width_no_w ? (0x7c | pp) : 0x7c;` pins `vvvv=1111` and `pp=00` for every APX EVEX form that is not SCC and not ND, discarding both the mandatory prefix and the NDS source register. `p2` at `:6991` likewise pins `V'=1`, and the ND branch at `:6982` also omits `| pp`.
   163: 
   164: ```asm
   165: g: adcx %rax, %rcx
   166: h: adox %rax, %rcx
   167: ```
   168: 
   169: ```
   170: clang:  66 48 0f 38 f6 c8    adcx %rax,%rcx
   171:         f3 48 0f 38 f6 c8    adox %rax,%rcx
   172: ide:    62 f4 fc 08 66 c8    wrssq %rcx,(bad)     <- both
   173:         62 f4 fc 08 66 c8    wrssq %rcx,(bad)     <- identical bytes
   174: ```
   175: 
   176: `adcx` and `adox` assemble to *the same bytes*, and those bytes are not a valid instruction. This needs no extended register — plain `%rax`/`%rcx` on any APX target. The same defect collides `shlx`/`sarx`/`shrx`, `pdep`/`pext`, and corrupts `andn`, `blsi`, `mulx`, `rorx` whenever an r16–r31 operand forces EVEX promotion.
   177: 
   178: **Fix:** OR `pp` into `p1` in all three branches, and encode `vvvv`/`V'` from `vvvv_index` whenever the pattern has a vvvv-bound operand — not only when `pattern.has_nd`.
   179: 
   180: ### 9. ✅ EVEX broadcast operands use the wrong disp8 scale — wrong memory address
   181: 
   182: `src/buster/lib/compiler/assembly/x86_64_metadata.c:5860` (`buster_x86_metadata_emit_tuple_scale`, used at `:6021`/`:6026`).
   183: 
   184: The compressed-disp8 scale N is derived from `form->tuple_kind` and vector length only; the broadcast state (`query.attributes.broadcast_elements`) is never passed into `buster_x86_metadata_emit_address`. A Full-tuple broadcast therefore scales by 64/32/16 instead of the element size 4/8.
   185: 
   186: ```asm
   187: vaddps 64(%rax){1to16}, %zmm1, %zmm2
   188: ```
   189: 
   190: ```
   191: clang:  62 f1 74 58 58 50 10    vaddps 0x40(%rax){1to16},%zmm1,%zmm2
   192: ide:    62 f1 74 58 58 50 01    vaddps 0x4(%rax){1to16},%zmm1,%zmm2
   193: ```
   194: 
   195: The load comes from the wrong address — off by a factor of 16 here. Any displacement that is a nonzero multiple of the vector byte width is affected; non-multiples fall back to disp32 and are correct, which is why the tests pass.
   196: 
   197: **Fix:** pass the broadcast flag into `buster_x86_metadata_emit_address` and return the element size from `emit_tuple_scale` when EVEX.b is set.
   198: 
   199: ### 10. ✅ REX2 forms lose `W` when the width comes only from the memory operand — 64-bit ops become 32-bit
   200: 
   201: `src/buster/lib/compiler/assembly/x86_64_metadata.c:6729-6730` (`scalar_memory_width_rex_w`).
   202: 
   203: The rule "a folded memory width is a REX.W authority" is gated on `PREFIX_LEGACY || PREFIX_REX` and omits `PREFIX_REX2` — which is exactly what an r16–r31 base or index forces.
   204: 
   205: ```asm
   206: addq $1, (%r16)
   207: ```
   208: 
   209: ```
   210: clang:  d5 18 83 00 01    addq $0x1,(%r16)
   211: ide:    d5 10 83 00 01    addl $0x1,(%r16)
   212: ```
   213: 
   214: A 4-byte read-modify-write where an 8-byte one was written; the upper half of the target is left stale. The same applies to `adcq sbbq subq andq orq xorq cmpq testq incq decq negq notq mulq divq idivq shlq shrq sarq rolq rorq rclq rcrq btq btsq btrq btcq` with any EGPR memory operand, and to `lock addq`. Two ad-hoc patches already exist for exactly IMUL `F7 /5` and MOV at `:6708-6716`, which is why only those two are right.
   215: 
   216: **Fix:** add `|| form.prefix_kind == BUSTER_X86_METADATA_PREFIX_REX2` to `scalar_memory_width_rex_w`, and drop the two per-iclass workarounds.
   217: 
   218: ### 11. AT&T `s` suffix treated as a generic 32-bit size suffix — `bts` assembles as `bt`
   219: 
   220: `src/buster/lib/compiler/assembly/assembly.c:11154-11158` (`assembly_x86_metadata_suffix_alias`). *Subsystem pass; bytes disassembled there, not re-run by me.*
   221: 
   222: `suffix == 's' ? 32` maps any mnemonic ending in `s` to base+32-bit. When the exact `bts` form is rejected (memory operand of unspecified width), the fallback strips the `s`, resolves `bt`, and emits BT's `/4` extension instead of BTS's `/5`:
   223: 
   224: ```
   225: ide:    d5 90 ba 27 03    btl  $0x3,(%r23)     <- reads the bit, never sets it
   226: gas:    d5 90 ba 2f 03    btsl $0x3,(%r23)
   227: ```
   228: 
   229: The alias also makes the assembler accept non-instructions as 32-bit ops (`adds`, `cmps`, `movs` with immediate operands), which gas rejects.
   230: 
   231: **Fix:** gate the `s`/`t` suffix widths on the x87 alias table rather than applying them to every mnemonic.
   232: 
   233: ### 12. x86-64 rejects `__int128` ↔ float casts and 16-byte `_Atomic` structs
   234: 
   235: `codegen.c:11604` and `codegen.c:12764`. *Subsystem pass.*
   236: 
   237: `double d = (double)someI128;` fails with `cc: error: C code generation failed with error 2 … opcode 27` — valid C rejected outright. AArch64 has `codegen_canonical_a64_i128_to_float` / `..._float_to_i128` (`codegen.c:8202`/`8381`); x86-64 has no counterpart. Separately, a 16-byte `_Atomic` *struct* is rejected by the CMPXCHG16B path's `IR_TYPE_INTEGER` test even though the identical-layout `_Atomic unsigned __int128` compiles and runs.
   238: 
   239: These are hard errors rather than silent wrong answers, which is why they rank below the S1 set.
   240: 
   241: ---
   242: 
   243: ## S3 — Memory safety and robustness in the compiler
   244: 
   245: ### 13. ✅ Systemic: `BUSTER_CHECK` is `__builtin_unreachable()` in Release, so validation guards are not guards
   246: 
   247: `src/buster/lib/os.h:288-292`:
   248: 
   249: ```c
   250: #if BUSTER_OPTIMIZE
   251: #define BUSTER_CHECK(ok) ((void)(BUSTER_UNLIKELY(!(ok)) ? (BUSTER_UNREACHABLE(), 0) : 0))
   252: #else
   253: #define BUSTER_CHECK(ok) ((void)(BUSTER_UNLIKELY(!(ok)) ? (os_fail_message(S8("assertion failed")), 0) : 0))
   254: #endif
   255: ```
   256: 
   257: That is the correct semantic for an *invariant* the code has already established. It is the wrong one wherever `BUSTER_CHECK` is currently doing duty as a **bounds or error check on data the program does not control** — there, the shipping build does not merely skip the check, it grants the optimizer permission to assume the bad case cannot happen and delete the surrounding handling.
   258: 
   259: This is the common root of findings 14, 16 and 17 below, and of the capacity pre-checks in the object readers. It is worth a deliberate sweep separating the two uses — an invariant assertion from a validating check — rather than fixing each site as it is found.
   260: 
   261: ### 14. ✅ 18 bytes of malformed C hang the compiler forever
   262: 
   263: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c:4967`, with the pop at `:4884-4890` (`c_parse_infer_initializer_array_count_core`).
   264: 
   265: ```c
   266: struct i e[]={>};
   267: ```
   268: 
   269: Both Debug and Release spin indefinitely (killed at 20s and 120s). The brace-elision branch advances the parent to `frame->cursor = value_end`, then pushes a `borrowed` child at `.cursor = designator.value_start`; when the child is immediately popped as exhausted, the pop copies the child's **unadvanced** cursor back into the parent, undoing the advance. `struct i` is incomplete, so `c_parse_initializer_type_slots` returns 0, the child pops on the first iteration, and the loop oscillates between frame counts 1 and 2 with the cursor pinned at 7. Same for `struct s e[]={()};` and `struct i e[]={<};`.
   270: 
   271: A build that touches an unlucky generated file never terminates.
   272: 
   273: **Fix:** on popping a `borrowed` frame, propagate its cursor only when it advanced (`if (cursor > frames[frame_count-1].cursor)`); or refuse to push a borrowed frame whose type has zero slots.
   274: 
   275: ### 15. ✅ Out-of-bounds arena write from repeated typedef-name statements
   276: 
   277: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c:11722` (`c_parse_bind_identifier_entity`).
   278: 
   279: A typedef name at statement start is bound twice — once as a declaration-specifier at `:13996`, again as a plain identifier use at `:14058` when the declaration parse falls through — but `identifier_use_capacity` is sized `identifier_count + 1` at `:15420`.
   280: 
   281: ```c
   282: typedef int B; void n(void){ B{}B{}B{}B{}B{}B{}B{}B{} }
--- lines 349-405 ---
   349: ```
   350: 
   351: `main`'s code is at 0x401030; its DIE claims 0x802030. Every subprogram, lexical block and inline site is unreachable by address in gdb and lldb. A single unlinked `.o` verifies clean, which is why this survived. `.debug_loc` lists at `:1143-1156` have the identical defect.
   352: 
   353: **Fix:** emit the CU's `DW_AT_low_pc` as a literal 0 with no address relocation (LLVM's convention when children use `DW_AT_ranges`), or keep the range entries CU-relative.
   354: 
   355: ### 21. CodeView: `LF_FIELDLIST` length overflows `u16` at ~2500 members
   356: 
   357: `src/buster/lib/compiler/codeview/codeview.c:238` (`codeview_type_record_end`). *Subsystem pass.* The record length is `(u16)(count - offset - 2)` with no overflow check, and `LF_FIELDLIST` (`:541-565`) accumulates every member into one record with no `LF_INDEX` continuation split. A struct with 2500 `int` members produces a ~135 KB payload whose length field reads 3930 (135010 mod 65536); `llvm-readobj --codeview-merged-types` reports "The CodeView record is corrupted" and every subsequent type record is parsed out of member-name text. 2400 members is fine.
   358: 
   359: **Fix:** split field lists at ~64 KB into continuation records chained with `LF_INDEX`; fail the build rather than truncate if a single record still exceeds `UINT16_MAX`.
   360: 
   361: ### 22. CodeView: `S_GPROC32` `pEnd` offsets are wrong after the PDB split, and the scope stack is quadratic
   362: 
   363: `codeview.c:734` and `codeview.c:369` (`codeview_build_legacy`). *Subsystem pass.*
   364: 
   365: `pEnd` is patched with an offset into the whole `.debug$S` blob, but `pdb_split_codeview` (`pdb.c:252-256`) puts only the concatenated `DEBUG_S_SYMBOLS` payloads into the module stream — so every `pEnd` is too large by the stripped signature and subsection headers, and a DIA/MSVC reader following it walks into the C13 line-table region. Separately, `codeview_emit_scope_tree` allocates its frame stack `arena_allocate(..., scope_count + 1)` on **every call**, once per function, giving O(function_count × scope_count) of never-released arena; the DWARF path allocates once at `dwarf.c:1531`.
   366: 
   367: **Fix:** patch `pEnd`/`pParent` with the running module-symbol offset; hoist the frame stack to one allocation per `codeview_build_legacy`.
   368: 
   369: ### 23. ✅ `-c` without `-o` writes the object next to the source, not into the working directory
   370: 
   371: `src/buster/lib/compiler/driver/driver.c:3401` (`compiler_driver_default_object_path`), duplicated at `:3765`.
   372: 
   373: The default object path replaces the extension of the *full input path* instead of taking its basename:
   374: 
   375: ```
   376: $ cd outdir && ide cc -c ../srcdir/a1.c
   377:    srcdir/a1.o exists? YES     outdir/a1.o exists? no
   378: ```
   379: 
   380: gcc and clang both write `./a1.o`. Out-of-tree builds deposit objects into the source tree, two configurations of the same tree overwrite each other's objects, and compiling from a read-only checkout fails outright.
   381: 
   382: **Fix:** strip the directory prefix as well as the extension.
   383: 
   384: ---
   385: 
   386: ## Areas examined and found clean
   387: 
   388: Worth recording, since it is a real result and tells you where not to spend effort next:
   389: 
   390: - **`object.c` / `link.c` / `jit.c` — genuinely hardened.** Every on-disk count, offset and size in the ELF, COFF, Mach-O and archive readers is validated against `bytes.length` before use; string-table reads are bounds-scanned; relocation values are range-checked before truncation (PC32/PLT32/GOTPCREL against `INT32` bounds, AArch64 CALL26/JUMP26/ADRP through validity-flagged helpers); addend arithmetic uses overflow-safe helpers; REL vs RELA is handled correctly; the JIT enforces W^X. ~2900 mutated objects and archives plus ~4000 crafted malformed archives across all six targets produced zero crashes and zero ASan reports. This is the strongest code in the repo.
   391: - **The AVX-512 compaction lexer.** 1.2M randomized inputs through a `c_lex` vs `c_lex_reference` differential harness — tokens, shapes, metrics, checkpoints, diagnostics — produced zero mismatches, and the tail/lookahead bounds hold by hand-check.
   392: - **Register allocation under pressure.** ~800 generated programs across three generators × four allocators, plus hand-written swap/parallel-copy, 40-live-value and deep-expression cases: clean. Also clean: 64-byte ZMM values live across calls, SysV struct/float/mixed argument and return ABI, varargs including aggregates and `va_copy`, over-aligned locals, VLAs, >300 KB frames with page probing, computed goto, TLS, `-fPIC`, long double.
   393: - **AArch64 encoding.** 3230 instructions checked against clang, zero mismatches; branch and PC-relative range checks are properly bounded.
   394: - **Bitfields and layout.** Packing and access including 32/64-bit-wide and packed fields, struct/union/over-aligned/FAM/VLA layout and `offsetof`, integer promotions and usual arithmetic conversions, runtime float↔int conversions, float constant folding: all clean.
   395: - **`string.c`, `integer.c`, `hash.c`, `simd.h` fallbacks** under ASan+UBSan with adversarial inputs: clean.
   396: 
   397: ## Two structural observations
   398: 
   399: **The Debug/Release divergence is a liability.** Findings 4 and 5 abort the Debug compiler on valid C while Release silently miscompiles it; findings 15, 17 and 18 are contained in Debug and are memory-unsafe in Release. The `#if !BUSTER_OPTIMIZE` differential gates are doing real work — they caught these — but they gate *aborts*, not *corrections*, so the configuration you ship is the one with no defence. Finding 13 is the root.
   400: 
   401: **Self-hosting cannot catch any of the S1 defects.** `test_self_host` requires stage-1 and stage-2 to be byte-identical, and a compiler that miscompiles enums identically in both generations still reaches a fixed point. Byte-identity proves determinism, not correctness. Every S1 finding above passes self-host by construction — differential testing against a reference compiler is the gate that would have caught them, and there is currently no such gate in CI.
   402: 
   403: ---
   404: 
   405: *Reproducers for every ✅ finding are one-file C or `.s` inputs quoted inline above; each was run against `build/Debug/ide` and `build/Release/ide` at `d0ecad0d` and compared with clang 18.*

    67: ## Suggested order
    68: 
    69: 1. **`release-check-macro-is-unreachable` first**, or at least decide its policy first — four P1s below are instances of it, and fixing them individually without settling the macro question invites a fifth.
    70: 2. **S1 as one batch.** Five of the seven are in `c_gen.c` constant/initializer handling and share test scaffolding. `x64-i128-signed-divide` is a two-row reorder with a correct AArch64 reference to copy.
    71: 3. **S2 next** — `x86-apx-evex-prefix-fields` is the worst of them (invalid instructions, silently) and is on the Zen 5 target line.
    72: 4. **S3 memory safety**, then **S4**, which affects debuggability rather than generated code.
    73: 
    74: ## Publishing to GitHub
    75: 
    76: `publish.py` reaches GitHub one of two ways, chosen automatically: an authenticated **`gh` CLI** when one is on PATH — preferred, because the issues are then authored by you — or the **REST API** with `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` from the environment, which is what an agent sandbox provides. No token is accepted on the command line or stored. The default run touches the network not at all.
    77: 
    78: If the REST path reports 403 on the repository, the session running it does not have that repository attached. Repository access is fixed when a session starts, so authorizing access to a *running* session does not help — start a fresh one with the repository attached, or run this from a machine with `gh`.
    79: 
    80: ```sh
    81: python3 publish.py                    # offline plan, no network
    82: python3 publish.py --check            # online preflight: drift + duplicates, still no writes
    83: python3 publish.py --publish          # file the issues
    84: python3 publish.py --link-references  # second pass: rewrite key references as #numbers
    85: ```
    86: 
    87: Three things it refuses to do, each because getting it wrong is expensive:
    88: 
    89: **File a stale line number.** Every issue records the git blob SHA of each production file it cites. Before any write, those are compared against `--ref` (default `main`). If a cited file has changed since `d0ecad0d`, the run stops and names the issues involved — the defect may well still be there, but the line numbers are no longer trustworthy. `--allow-drift` files anyway and appends an explicit drift notice to the body; `--skip KEY` leaves those out instead.
    90: 
    91: **File a duplicate.** Each body carries a `<!-- buster-audit-2026-09-07:key -->` marker. Existing issues are matched on that marker or on exact title, across all states; a closed match stops the run for review. This is not semantic duplicate detection — read the open issues yourself before a first publication.
    92: 
    93: **Publish a body you did not review.** Bodies are checked against the `sha256` in the manifest and the run aborts if one was edited without the manifest being updated deliberately.
    94: 
    95: GitHub writes cannot be atomic across 26 issues, so each creation is recorded in `publication-results.json` the moment it succeeds. A run interrupted halfway is resumed by re-running the same command: filed issues are skipped, not re-filed. `--only KEY` files a single issue.
    96: 
    97: Both transports are tested offline against stubs covering the whole flow — plan, preflight, drift refusal, `--allow-drift`, closed-match abort, duplicate reuse, mid-run failure and resume, cross-reference linking, and the 403 case. **Neither has been exercised against live GitHub.** Do a `--check` first, then `--publish --only <one key>`, and look at the result before filing the rest.
    98: 
    99: ## Two structural notes
   100: 
   101: Both are argued in `AUDIT_REPORT.md` and worth reading before picking up any individual issue.
   102: 
   103: **Debug and Release disagree about what is a bug.** Two findings abort the Debug compiler on valid C while Release silently miscompiles it; three more are contained in Debug and memory-unsafe in Release. The `#if !BUSTER_OPTIMIZE` differential gates are doing real work — they caught both miscompiles — but they gate *aborts*, not *corrections*, so the shipped configuration has no defence.
   104: 
   105: **Self-hosting cannot catch any S1 defect.** `test_self_host` requires stage 1 and stage 2 to be byte-identical, and a compiler that miscompiles enums identically in both generations still reaches a fixed point. Byte-identity proves determinism, not correctness. Every S1 finding passes self-host by construction; a differential gate against a reference compiler is what would have caught them, and CI has none.
===== docs/audits/2026-09-07/issues/c-enum-underlying-type.md =====
--- lines 1-50 ---
     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-07:c-enum-underlying-type -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-07 against a full clone of `main` at [`d0ecad0d`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/commit/d0ecad0ddd6ecc676e20fda5694d33176880a90b) ("tests: integrate runtime boundary regressions on desktop hosts"). The tree was built with clang 18 in Debug and Release using the documented hosted-CI bootstrap exception (`clang -Isrc -Wall -Werror ... build.c`), because TCC is unavailable on the audit host. `ide test` was green at 322668/322668 unit tests and 39/39 module tests before auditing, so nothing here is caught by the existing suite. Release self-host was not run: it needs TCC for the trusted bootstrap. **Rebased onto [`44a936a8`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/commit/44a936a8):** the line numbers below are current as of that commit, and the reproduction was re-run there — the defect still occurs.
     4: 
     5: **Priority:** P1 - demonstrated miscompilation of valid C, no diagnostic.
     6: **Evidence:** reproduced first-hand in this audit against `build/Debug/ide` and `build/Release/ide`, differentially against clang 18.
     7: 
     8: ## What is wrong
     9: 
    10: `c_lower_to_ir` maps an enumeration without a C23 fixed underlying type unconditionally to `s32_type` instead of selecting the type from the enumerator range. `c_ir_emit_integer_value` (`c_gen.c:24192`) hardcodes the same choice on the value path, and `c_ir_constant_identifier` on the constant path.
    11: 
    12: C requires the implementation to choose an underlying type capable of representing every enumerator. Any enumerator outside `int` range is therefore truncated or sign-extended, and `sizeof` reports the wrong size.
    13: 
    14: **Source locations**
    15: 
    16: - src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:42413 (`c_lower_to_ir`)
    17: - src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:24192 (`c_ir_emit_integer_value`)
    18: 
    19: ## Reproduction and measured evidence
    20: 
    21: ```c
    22: #include <stdio.h>
    23: enum Flags { F_NONE = 0, F_HIGH = 0x80000000 };
    24: enum B { BB = 4294967296LL };
    25: int main(void) {
    26:     printf("high_gt0=%d bb=%lld sz=%zu\n", F_HIGH > 0, (long long)BB, sizeof(enum B));
    27:     return 0;
    28: }
    29: ```
    30: 
    31: ```
    32: clang 18 : high_gt0=1 bb=4294967296 sz=8
    33: ide      : high_gt0=0 bb=0          sz=4
    34: ```
    35: 
    36: `BB` collapses to zero. `F_HIGH` compares as negative, so any enum used as a bit-flag set with bit 31 set is silently wrong at every comparison and every widening use. Both Debug and Release agree, on the default target and allocator.
    37: 
    38: ## Required fix
    39: 
    40: Derive the underlying type from the enumerator range: `unsigned int` when no enumerator is negative and the maximum exceeds `INT_MAX`, `long`/`long long` when a value exceeds 32 bits, `unsigned long long` when an unsigned value exceeds `LLONG_MAX`. The rule is already written down for enum bit-fields at `c_gen.c:42773` - reuse it rather than inventing a second one. Fix all three sites (`c_lower_to_ir`, `c_ir_emit_integer_value`, `c_ir_constant_identifier`) together; fixing one leaves the constant and value paths disagreeing.
    41: 
    42: ## Validation / definition of done
    43: 
    44: Add a frontend test covering: an enumerator at `0x80000000`, one at `2^32`, one negative alongside a large positive, and `sizeof` for each. Assert against the values in the reproduction above, not against self-consistency.
    45: 
    46: Run the C frontend module suite and `test_all`. Note that Release self-host cannot catch this class of defect: it requires stage 1 and stage 2 to be byte-identical, and a compiler that miscompiles enums identically in both generations still reaches a fixed point. A differential run against clang or gcc is the gate that catches it.
    47: 
    48: ## Existing work / scope
    49: 
    50: One of seven silent-miscompilation findings in the 2026-09-07 audit; see `AUDIT_REPORT.md` section S1. Independent of the eBPF/Wasm/runtime work in the 2026-09-06 bundle.
===== docs/audits/2026-09-07/issues/c-float-to-integer-constant-fold.md =====
--- lines 1-48 ---
     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-07:c-float-to-integer-constant-fold -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-07 against a full clone of `main` at [`d0ecad0d`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/commit/d0ecad0ddd6ecc676e20fda5694d33176880a90b) ("tests: integrate runtime boundary regressions on desktop hosts"). The tree was built with clang 18 in Debug and Release using the documented hosted-CI bootstrap exception (`clang -Isrc -Wall -Werror ... build.c`), because TCC is unavailable on the audit host. `ide test` was green at 322668/322668 unit tests and 39/39 module tests before auditing, so nothing here is caught by the existing suite. Release self-host was not run: it needs TCC for the trusted bootstrap. **Rebased onto [`44a936a8`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/commit/44a936a8):** the line numbers below are current as of that commit, and the reproduction was re-run there — the defect still occurs.
     4: 
     5: **Priority:** P1 - demonstrated miscompilation of valid C, no diagnostic.
     6: **Evidence:** reproduced first-hand in this audit against `build/Debug/ide` and `build/Release/ide`, differentially against clang 18.
     7: 
     8: ## What is wrong
     9: 
    10: `c_ir_constant_cast` converts a floating constant to its integer representation with a bare `(u64)source.floating`. That is undefined behaviour in C whenever the value is negative or at least 2^64. Clang lowers the expression to `vcvttsd2usi`, whose out-of-range result is `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`, so every negative floating constant converted to an integer type folds to -1.
    11: 
    12: The same line also drops the high limb for 128-bit targets: `integer_high` is never populated.
    13: 
    14: **Source locations**
    15: 
    16: - src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:39429 (`c_ir_constant_cast`)
    17: 
    18: ## Reproduction and measured evidence
    19: 
    20: ```c
    21: #include <stdio.h>
    22: static const long long L = (long long)(-2147483648.0);
    23: static const int T[3] = {(int)-1.5, (int)-2.5, (int)2.5};
    24: int main(void) { printf("L=%lld T=%d,%d,%d\n", L, T[0], T[1], T[2]); return 0; }
    25: ```
    26: 
    27: ```
    28: clang 18 : L=-2147483648 T=-1,-2,2
    29: ide      : L=-1          T=-1,-1,2
    30: ```
    31: 
    32: Note `T[0]` is coincidentally right - truncation of -1.5 really is -1 - which is exactly the kind of accident that hides this in a spot check. `T[1]` is wrong.
    33: 
    34: 128-bit form: `static __int128 F = (__int128)1.5e30;` yields `0x00000000000000000FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` instead of the correct value. Confirmed under gdb: `converted.integer == UINT64_MAX` from a `C_IR_CONSTANT_FLOAT` of -10.
    35: 
    36: ## Required fix
    37: 
    38: Convert through `s64` when the value is negative (`source.floating < 0 ? (u64)(s64)source.floating : (u64)source.floating`), range-check the result against the destination type before storing, and populate `integer_high` when the target is 128-bit. Out-of-range conversions are UB in the source program too, but the compiler must not itself execute UB while folding - pick a defined result and be consistent with the runtime conversion path.
    39: 
    40: ## Validation / definition of done
    41: 
    42: Add constant-folding tests for negative and positive floats into every integer width, signed and unsigned, plus the 128-bit destination, plus values beyond the destination range. Cross-check each against the runtime conversion path in the same compiler - the two must agree.
    43:

     1: <!-- buster-audit-2026-09-07:x64-i128-signed-divide -->
     2: 
     3: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first. Audited on 2026-09-07 against a full clone of `main` at [`d0ecad0d`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/commit/d0ecad0ddd6ecc676e20fda5694d33176880a90b) ("tests: integrate runtime boundary regressions on desktop hosts"). The tree was built with clang 18 in Debug and Release using the documented hosted-CI bootstrap exception (`clang -Isrc -Wall -Werror ... build.c`), because TCC is unavailable on the audit host. `ide test` was green at 322668/322668 unit tests and 39/39 module tests before auditing, so nothing here is caught by the existing suite. Release self-host was not run: it needs TCC for the trusted bootstrap. **Rebased onto [`44a936a8`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/commit/44a936a8):** the line numbers below are current as of that commit, and the reproduction was re-run there — the defect still occurs.
     4: 
     5: **Priority:** P1 - demonstrated miscompilation of valid C, no diagnostic.
     6: **Evidence:** reproduced first-hand in this audit against `build/Debug/ide` and `build/Release/ide`, differentially against clang 18.
     7: 
     8: ## What is wrong
     9: 
    10: In the x86-64 128-bit divide lowering, R9 holds the divisor's sign mask and R8 the dividend's. The `sign_xor` row (`XOR R9, R8`, emitted at `codegen.c:15137`) overwrites R9 with the combined result sign **before** the divisor-magnitude rows at `codegen.c:15143-15146` read it:
    11: 
    12: ```
    13: XOR RCX, R9
    14: XOR RSI, R9
    15: SUB RCX, R9
    16: SBB RSI, R9
    17: ```
    18: 
    19: So the divisor is negated iff the two operand signs *differ*, rather than iff the divisor is negative. With a negative dividend and a positive divisor, the divisor is turned into its two's complement (2^128 - d); the restoring division loop then terminates immediately, yielding quotient 0 and remainder = dividend.
    20: 
    21: The AArch64 sibling `codegen_canonical_a64_i128_divide` (`codegen.c:8104`) is correct - it keeps the divisor's own sign in x16 and the combined sign in x17.
    22: 
    23: **Source locations**
    24: 
    25: - src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/codegen.c:15092 (`codegen_generate_canonical_module_attempt`, signed_division block at :15070-15149)
    26: 
    27: ## Reproduction and measured evidence
    28: 
    29: ```c
    30: #include <stdio.h>
    31: int main(void) {
    32:     volatile long long a = -100, b = 7;
    33:     __int128 x = a, y = b;
    34:     printf("q=%lld r=%lld\n", (long long)(x / y), (long long)(x % y));
    35:     return 0;
    36: }
    37: ```
    38: 
    39: ```
    40: clang 18 : q=-14 r=-2
    41: ide      : q=0   r=-100
    42: ```
    43: 
    44: `(-100)/(-7)` returns 0 as well. All four allocators are affected - the machine selectors leave i128 divide to this canonical lowering. Disassembly of the emitted object shows `xor %r8,%r9` at 0x7e feeding `xor %r9,%rcx` at 0x91, which is the bug directly.
    45: 
    46: Unsigned 128-bit divide is correct, and so is the constant-folded static-initializer path, so only the emitted signed sequence is at fault.
    47: 
    48: ## Required fix
    49: 
    50: Emit `sign_xor`/`save_sign` **after** `divisor_high_sbb`. This is a pure reordering: R9 then still carries the divisor's own sign mask through the divisor negation, and the combined sign is computed once the magnitude rows no longer need R9.
    51: 
    52: ## Validation / definition of done
    53: 
    54: `tests/basic_c_int128.c:66-70` currently misses this because its only assertion is `q*37 + r == n`, which `q=0, r=n` satisfies trivially. Strengthen it to compare against exact expected quotients and remainders, and cover all four sign combinations plus `INT128_MIN / -1`.
    55: 
    56: Run the codegen module suite, `test_all`, and Release self-host across all four allocators.
    57: 
    58: ## Existing work / scope
    59: 
    60: Section S1 of the 2026-09-07 audit. The AArch64 path is correct and can serve as the reference for the fix.

===== docs/byte-writer.md =====
--- lines 1-46 ---
     1: # Bounded CodeView and PDB writing
     2: 
     3: `src/buster/lib/byte_writer.h` defines a non-owning writer over a pre-reserved
     4: span. CodeView and PDB retain their existing arena allocations and capacity
     5: estimates; the shared layer neither grows nor frees storage. No callback or
     6: function-pointer dispatch is involved. Object and machine-code writers remain
     7: outside this experiment.
     8: 
     9: `byte_writer_make` starts at count zero. Each append, zero fill, patch or
    10: four-byte alignment operation either writes its entire requested range or
    11: leaves bytes and count unchanged. Failure sets the sticky `overflow` flag;
    12: subsequent operations cannot change the buffer. Format-specific record-length
    13: checks may set that same flag. Alignment uses a single bounded zero fill, so
    14: insufficient capacity cannot strand PDB emission in an alignment loop.
    15: 
    16: The primitive checks use subtraction after validating the offset. Patches can
    17: only address the written prefix, including an empty patch at its end; spare
    18: capacity is not initialized output. Zero-length writes accept null data and do
    19: not perform pointer arithmetic or call `memcpy`/`memset`. Nonempty copy spans
    20: must not overlap. Integer writes and patches explicitly encode little-endian
    21: bytes and require no alignment.
    22: 
    23: `byte_writer_commit` publishes a borrowed `ByteSlice` only when the writer is
    24: valid; on failure it leaves the supplied output unchanged. It does not seal the
    25: writer or transfer ownership, so the view keeps the backing storage's lifetime
    26: and may observe subsequent successful writes. CodeView publishes its symbol
    27: and type slices together after both streams succeed. PDB checks every stream's
    28: failure state before constructing the MSF container and only publishes a valid
    29: container after directory emission succeeds. Failed format results remain
    30: invalid; no partial artifact becomes a successful result.
    31: 
    32: The registered `byte_writer_tests` exercise exact endian bytes, guard regions,
    33: empty operations, all small alignment tails, patch ranges, huge lengths,
    34: sticky errors and publication. Existing CodeView/PDB tests continue to decode
    35: records, field-list continuations, source tables, scopes, contributions and MSF
    36: page maps independently. For a full run:
    37: 
    38: ```sh
    39: ./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all
    40: ./build.sh test_self_host --config Release
    41: ```
    42: 
    43: Performance admission for other consumers requires separate evidence. Measure
    44: compiler-build cost and emitted writer code size alongside complete debug
    45: compilation/linking workloads; a primitive append microbenchmark alone does not
    46: establish a compiler-throughput gain.
===== docs/canonical-cfg-publication.md =====
--- lines 1-81 ---
     1: # Canonical CFG publication
     2: 
     3: `ir_prepare_canonical_module` publishes `IrFunction.published_cfg` after
     4: canonical transforms and their validation boundaries. `ir_function_publish_cfg`
     5: is the only topology/edge-argument producer. It consumes validated input or an
     6: explicit trusted producer/pass contract; the const publication pointer does not
     7: extend an input semantic certificate to arbitrary later mutations.
     8: 
     9: Publication checks exact construction-list extents, tails, incoming order/types,
    10: topology agreement and bounded IDs/counts. It proves instruction ownership while
    11: building one instruction permutation, then publishes these immutable slices:
    12: 
    13: - Instructions occupy one contiguous span per block, in block ID order.
    14: - Successor edges are grouped by source, retaining first terminator-target order.
    15: - Predecessor slices contain edge indices sorted by source block ID.
    16: - Parameters are grouped by block; argument `i` on an edge supplies parameter
    17:   `i` of its destination.
    18: - Variable operands, targets and immediates occupy shared pools. Already
    19:   contiguous pools are reused, including shared promotion's operand pool.
    20: 
    21: Repeated conditional/switch/computed-goto destinations collapse to one edge.
    22: Parameter-free destinations are included even if their builder omitted its
    23: optional predecessor list. `ir_function_cfg_edge` searches a destination's
    24: sorted predecessor slice without searching parameter incoming lists.
    25: Construction transposes ordered builder incoming columns once, with linear
    26: work in blocks, terminator targets, parameters and incoming values.
    27: 
    28: When instruction order changes, `instruction_remap` is the one explicit map
    29: from prepublication IDs to published IDs. The row permutation is in place;
    30: canonical source rows move with it, value definitions are remapped, and sparse
    31: instruction extras are remapped and sorted again. Block, value, local, symbol
    32: and label IDs remain stable. Computed-goto address identity and relocation
    33: ownership therefore do not change. The declared entry remains independent of
    34: numeric block order, and backend layout still emits it first where required.
    35: The authoritative instruction row remains 64 bytes.
    36: 
    37: Native selectors, native canonical emission, Wasm, eBPF and LLVM consume the
    38: same instruction spans and dense parameter/argument arrays. Both selectors'
    39: private row-order reconstruction and their canonical edge reconstruction are
    40: removed. Selected machine IR still owns its graph: AArch64 legalization can
    41: split canonical blocks and i128 joins expand a value into two registers. That
    42: is a target lowering result, not a duplicate canonical CFG.
    43: 
    44: Publication clears every per-instruction `next` and every builder
    45: parameter/predecessor first/last pointer. The linked construction graph is no
    46: longer retained as a second authoritative representation. Its arena allocations
    47: become unreachable; arena high-water memory is reclaimed when the translation
    48: unit is released, not by freeing individual nodes at publication. This cost
    49: must be included in peak-memory measurements.
    50: 
    51: `ir_function_invalidate_cfg` explicitly reopens construction: it reconstructs
    52: mutable links from the published slices, then clears the publication pointer.
    53: Call it **before** mutating published rows or CFG/value identities, and reacquire
    54: builder pointers afterward. Old construction-node pointers are stale. Builder
    55: appends and shared-promotion entry perform this transition automatically.
    56: Uncertified preparation validates the current representation; passing false is
    57: not a replacement for reopening construction before a topology mutation.
    58: Repeated unchanged preparation reuses its publication without reconstruction.
    59: 
    60: The canonical verifier reads either mutable construction lists or published
    61: slices. Published shape checks verify dense coverage and topology agreement;
    62: parameter type/label-provenance checks share the same semantic rules through
    63: an indexed incoming-value view. Bootstrap tracing similarly reads published
    64: slices after finalization and preserves its construction path beforehand.
    65: 
    66: `allocated_bytes` reports new persistent allocation performed by this
    67: publication, excluding reused pools, original builder storage, arena padding
    68: and temporary scratch. Pool counts and instruction-remap presence describe the
    69: additional retained data. The existing optional `CFG_*` counters describe
    70: publication work; `CFG_COPY_SOURCES` counts actual machine copy translation.
    71: These counts are not compiler throughput results.
    72: 
    73: `ir_cfg_publication_tests` checks complete edge/argument streams for degrees
    74: 0/1/2/17/4096 and parameter widths 0/1/2/32/33, reversed builder order,
    75: duplicate destinations, optional predecessor lists, invalid IDs,
    76: truncated/overlong/cyclic lists and wrong tails. Instruction-span tests cover
    77: interleaving, explicit remaps, source/extras/value-definition preservation,
    78: nonzero entry identity, link discard and reconstruction. Existing native/mode,
    79: Wasm, eBPF and bitcode tests cover downstream behavior. Performance acceptance
    80: requires paired measurements and must account for finalization cost and peak
    81: arena memory as well as saved backend traversal.
===== docs/canonical-fast-pipeline.md =====
--- lines 22-117 ---
    22: ## Order and ownership
    23: 
    24: `ir_prepare_canonical_module` receives the frontend's completed CFG. It checks
    25: uncertified input, runs the existing shared local-promotion oracle when needed,
    26: then runs selected FAST transforms on each lowered function in this order:
    27: 
    28: | Stage | Algorithm and preserved boundary |
    29: | --- | --- |
    30: | Local promotion / frontend SSA | Existing frontend construction and `ir_promote_function`; the existing `-fno-frontend-ssa` and `-fno-canonical-local-promotion` controls remain independent. |
    31: | `fold` | One forward scan; path-compressed value replacements; integer constants up to 64 bits, integer identities, same-type pure casts, integer truncation/extension. No floating-point folding, division/remainder folding, branch deletion or iterative global propagation. |
    32: | `address` | One scan collapses `&*pointer` and `*&place` only when type, category, alignment and all value qualifier facts agree. Shared selector address facts in #44 own deeper offset/index analysis. |
    33: | `dce` | Count surviving instruction and edge-argument uses; queue unused pure definitions, decrement their operands transitively. Each row enters the queue at most once. No CSR use index. |
    34: | `parameters` | Remove a block parameter when all resolved non-self incoming values agree. Up to four full sweeps; remaining nontrivial/cyclic parameters stay valid. No edge order or CFG topology change. |
    35: | Compact | One `ir_rewrite_compact` map shared with local promotion updates values, instruction links, operands, parameters/incomings, source ranges, extras and builder-local maps. Shared input operand slices are copied once into a single new pool. |
    36: | Certify | Any changed FAST result is checked for uncertified callers and Debug/test/sanitizer/explicit transform-check builds. Optimized production trusts the transform's contract under the same policy as promotion; input certification is not extended to changed rows. |
    37: 
    38: The compaction helper is extracted from existing promotion without changing its
    39: remapping algorithm. Its parameter cleanup remains separate, so counters added
    40: by #371 retain their meaning. FAST counters do not include that cleanup.
    41: Functions with computed-label instructions or sparse label provenance are
    42: conservatively skipped; their ID/provenance relation is left intact.
    43: 
    44: `fast_complete` records one completed optional transformation run, not a
    45: certificate. Mutating a prepared module requires clearing the relevant
    46: preparation markers and revoking the caller's input certificate. Repeated
    47: untrusted preparation still validates. Published CFG/address facts must be
    48: invalidated before mutation and rebuilt after these transforms (#38/#44).
    49: Producer-certified modules that do not yet satisfy the stricter canonical
    50: validator are left unchanged as a unit and increment `validation_skips`.
    51: Optional transformation must never turn an otherwise accepted legacy source
    52: shape into a new diagnostic.
    53: 
    54: When preparation has already run that validator over the module in exactly
    55: its current state -- the promotion-output scan of a Debug/test/sanitizer/
    56: explicit transform-check build, or the input scan of an uncertified caller --
    57: the FAST input guard reuses that result instead of scanning the unchanged
    58: module a second time. Any mutation between the two points clears the reuse,
    59: and the guard still scans whenever nothing has proven the current
    60: representation. In the default tests-enabled Release `ide`, a translation
    61: unit in which promotion changes any function therefore pays one strict scan
    62: before FAST, not two.
    63: 
    64: ## Purity contract
    65: 
    66: `ir_instruction_is_pure` is the shared canonical DCE authority. Scalar integer
    67: arithmetic, integer/pointer conversions and address construction may be removed
    68: when their results have no instruction or incoming-edge uses. Place-producing
    69: FIELD/INDEX rows may be removed; value projections are conservative. Calls,
    70: loads (including nonvolatile loads), stores, atomics, fences, inline assembly,
    71: stack operations, traps, all exact SIMD operations, division/remainder and
    72: floating arithmetic/conversions remain observable. This preserves both their
    73: effects and deliberate backend refusal. New opcode classes are impure until
    74: this contract explicitly classifies and tests them.
    75: 
    76: ## Controls and measurement
    77: 
    78: ```sh
    79: # Independently disable one default pass (last flag wins).
    80: build/Release/ide cc source.c -fno-canonical-fast-dce -o output
    81: # Select only folding; do not collect timing during throughput observations.
    82: build/Release/ide cc source.c -fcanonical-fast-fold -o output
    83: # Diagnostic replay only: clocks and per-pass work counts, plus compaction.
    84: build/Release/ide cc source.c -fcanonical-fast -ftime-canonical-fast -v -o output
    85: ```
    86: 
    87: All four names accept `-fcanonical-fast-NAME` and
    88: `-fno-canonical-fast-NAME`. `-fno-canonical-fast` clears the whole selection.
    89: Timing selection does not enable transformations. Per-pass `IR_FAST_PASS` records
    90: report the enable/timing bits, nanoseconds, row/operand/incoming visits and
    91: changes. `IR_FAST` records instruction counts, validation/budget/provenance
    92: skips, parameter-cap hits,
    93: compaction time and memory upper bounds. Multi-input sums additive counters;
    94: the scratch bound is the maximum, not a sum.
    95: 
    96: The explicit incremental limits per function are:
    97: 
    98: - 16 MiB maximum scratch payload bound: `16*values + 16*instructions + 256`.
    99:   This covers replacement/use/value maps, removal bytes, deletion queue,
   100:   compaction instruction/link maps and allocation alignment.
   101: - 8 MiB maximum new retained payload bound:
   102:   `4*original_operands + 8*original_instructions`. This includes the compacted
   103:   operand pool and the worst case of one new integer immediate per input row.
   104:   When CFG data is already published, admission also includes reopening its
   105:   builder arrays: `sizeof(IrBlockParameter)*parameters + sizeof(IrIncoming)*arguments
   106:   + sizeof(IrPredecessor)*edges`, plus up to `alignof(T)-1` padding for each of
   107:   those three allocations. Reopening is recorded even when no pass changes a row.
   108: - 4,194,304 maximum work population: instructions + values + operands + blocks
   109:   + parameters + incoming arguments. Each selected folding/address pass scans
   110:   once, DCE is linear, and parameter cleanup has at most four sweeps. Budget
   111:   accumulation saturates before any unsafe multiplication.
   112: 
   113: An exceeded guard skips all optional passes for that function and increments
   114: `budget_skips`. It does not reject source. Memory records are conservative
   115: payload **bounds**, not measured arena capacity or peak process RSS. They cover
   116: these new passes; frontend construction, existing local promotion, mandatory
   117: validation and backend storage retain their existing costs. Explicitly enabling

   117: The `.forgejo/workflows/github-hosted.yml` workflow runs only for pushes to

   121: `GH_HOSTED_RUNNERS_ENABLED` unset keeps current CI unchanged. After a
   122: successful trial, make the bridge job's exact status context required in the

   124: `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` as defense in depth.

   126: ## Per-run credential lifecycle
   127: 
   128: 1. The dispatcher revokes any `github-bridge-*` deploy key older than two
   129:    hours (leftovers of a crashed run), reading every deploy-key page before
   130:    deleting keys so pagination cannot skip shifted entries, then waits until no broker run is
   131:    active, because the single secret name serializes runs.
   132: 2. It generates a fresh ed25519 keypair under `/dev/shm`, registers the
   133:    public half as a **read-only** Forgejo deploy key titled
   134:    `github-bridge-<nonce>`, and seals the private half into the broker
   135:    secret `FORGEJO_DEPLOY_KEY`.
   136: 3. It dispatches the broker workflow with only the nonce and the exact
   137:    commit ID, discovers the run by its `forgejo-<nonce>` run name (the
   138:    dispatch API returns no run ID), and polls it to completion, requesting
   139:    cancellation on timeout or interruption.
   140: 4. Whatever happened, it deletes the GitHub secret and revokes the Forgejo
   141:    deploy key. Either half alone is useless; both deletions failing at once
   142:    still leaves a read-only, single-repository key that the next dispatch's
   143:    stale-key sweep revokes.
   144: 
   145: Each hosted platform compiles the build driver with the Clang already
   146: present on the hosted image, configures the Clang CI tree, and runs the
   147: Release `test_all` target inside the memory workspace. This narrow
   148: bootstrap exception avoids downloading an unpinned compiler before the
   149: source fetch and avoids modern macOS's lack of a working TCC package. It is
   150: supplementary portable coverage, not a replacement for
   151: `test_all_combinations_ci`: the controlled Forgejo matrix retains the exact
   152: Clang/GCC/Zig versions, sanitizers, fuzzing, self-hosting, Android, and iOS
   153: coverage required by this repository.
   154: 
   155: ## Trust rules
   156: 
   157: - Keep automatic dispatch restricted to protected branches. Never add a
   158:   secret-bearing bridge job to a fork pull-request trigger.
   159: - Require review for changes to `.forgejo/workflows/github-hosted.yml`,
   160:   `.forgejo/scripts/github_runner_bridge.py`, and the installed broker
   161:   workflow. A trusted main commit can deliberately exfiltrate its own
   162:   source; this architecture cannot prevent that.
   163: - Keep the Forgejo checkout action pinned to its reviewed commit rather
   164:   than a mutable major-version tag, because it prepares the dispatcher that
   165:   receives both API tokens in the next step.
   166: - Scope `GH_BRIDGE_FORGEJO_TOKEN` to deploy-key management on this one
   167:   repository if the Forgejo token model allows it, and rotate it like any
   168:   administrative credential. It never leaves the Forgejo runner.
   169: - Do not add `actions/cache`, `upload-artifact`, verbose failure-log
   170:   printing, source mirroring, or package-manager toolchain installation to
   171:   the broker. Those features create persistent copies or introduce code
   172:   that can run before or beside the credentialed fetch.
   173: - Do not weaken the memory-workspace step: everything derived from the
   174:   source (objects, binaries, fixture output, logs, `TMPDIR`) must stay
   175:   under the RAM root on Linux and macOS.
   176: - If the Forgejo server refuses fetches of unadvertised objects, set
   177:   `uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant` server-side rather than teaching the
   178:   broker to fetch a branch: the broker must only ever fetch the exact
   179:   commit it was told.
   180: - Mobile tests remain on the existing controlled Forgejo runners. The
   181:   current Android and iOS workflows depend on KVM/emulator and simulator
   182:   behavior that this desktop broker does not claim to reproduce.
   183: 
   184: ## Reading a run's logs
   185: 
   186: Forgejo is the index and GitHub holds the (deliberately thin) detail. Each
   187: push to `main` produces a "GitHub hosted desktop matrix" run whose
   188: "Privacy bridge" job log is the audit trail:
   189:

    38: Previously, modes ran only after combinations finished, even though modes
    39: already deleted and regenerated the build tree before compiling its own
    40: Release compiler. Moving that independent work onto another runner removes an
    41: ordering dependency without adding another expensive compiler producer.
    42: Modes and differential stay together: separating those two would either

    46: `734 + 141 + 1430 = 2305` seconds to `max(734, 141 + 1430) = 1571` seconds.
    47: The potential removed serial work is 734 seconds, not an observed speedup.
    48: New runner queues, checkout and evidence uploads affect the actual result.
    49: 
    50: ## Ownership and required checks
    51: 
    52: | Job group | Lanes | Work |
    53: | --- | ---: | --- |
    54: | `test` | 6 | Unchanged complete `test_all_combinations_ci` |
    55: | `native` | 4 Unix | Unchanged modes and native differential, sequential within each lane |
    56: | `mobile` | 3 | Unchanged Android and iOS `--all` suites |
    57: | `lint` | 1 | Workflow lint and approved action references |
    58: | `complete` | 1 | Fail-closed aggregation of all four groups |
    59: 
    60: The native check names append ` native` to Linux x86-64, Linux AArch64,
    61: macOS x86-64 and macOS AArch64. Their runner labels are unchanged from the
    62: corresponding combination lanes. Native and mobile jobs have no `needs`
    63: dependency on combinations. Every matrix retains `fail-fast: false`.
    64: `CI complete` requires all fifteen jobs including itself, not just the six
    65: legacy desktop names. Failure, cancellation, skips and missing results fail.
    66: The separate `Linux x86-64 bootstrap evidence` check remains separate.
    67:

    70: mobile execution policy changes. `build.c` still owns all native build/test
    71: policy. The combination lanes still install verified Zig and Linux mold.
    72: Native lanes need neither: they keep Clang and `--linker DEFAULT` with the

     1: # GitHub workflow audit — 2026-09-07
     2: 
     3: > Historical suite-level design/evidence. The subsequent internal desktop
     4: > partition and current 23-job completion contract are documented in
     5: > [Desktop combination shards](ci-combination-shards.md). Historical timings
     6: > below are not matched before/after evidence for #333.
     7: 
     8: Base: `66bf321936ccb2b4f0df42cb6f65ed197f8652b5`. The three workflow blobs
     9: are unchanged from the measured revision `9834a4253c61934a8a253641a84741a25d3717e3`.
    10: This change concerns the public repository's GitHub workflows, **not** the
    11: source-free broker under `.forgejo/github-bridge/`. Broker cache/artifact and
    12: credential restrictions remain untouched.
    13: 
    14: ## Coverage contract and scheduling
    15: 
    16: The six existing desktop names and runner labels remain. Every desktop lane
    17: invokes the entire `test_all_combinations_ci` command; build.c still owns the
    18: compiler/configuration cross product, CPU budget, sanitizer/fuzz policy,
    19: static-analysis lane, table audits, and supported self-host fixed points.
    20: There is no additional sanitizer-only build duplicating those configurations.
    21: The four Unix lanes also invoke the complete `test_mode_matrix --config Release`
    22: with the same explicit Clang/Release/default-linker generation. A failed
    23: combination no longer suppresses that independent check. Neither a step nor a
    24: job uses `continue-on-error`, and both matrix strategies disable fail-fast.
    25: 
    26: Mobile work is sharded by suite, not by arbitrary test-name prefixes:
    27: 
    28: | Shard | Existing coverage retained |
    29: | --- | --- |
    30: | Android x86-64 / ubuntu-26.04 | Fixed API-35 x86-64 image; `android/test_ci.sh --all` (Debug and Release) |
    31: | iOS x86-64 / macos-26-intel | `ios/test_ci.sh --all`: existing Debug/Release compile, link and bundle validation |
    32: | iOS AArch64 / macos-26 | `ios/test_ci.sh --all`: Debug/Release simulator execution |
    33: 
    34: The Intel iOS compile-only exception already exists in `ios/test_ci.sh`; this
    35: PR neither introduces nor expands it. Both mobile entry points configure their
    36: own build trees, use the default linker, and disable developer targets. They
    37: do not consume the desktop build driver or desktop compiler outputs. Thus
    38: separating them removes a dependency without duplicating desktop test work.
    39: This is **suite-level sharding**, not a new per-case shard protocol.
    40: 
    41: **Require `CI complete` for merging.** It waits for workflow lint, all six
    42: desktop lanes, and all three mobile lanes. A skipped, cancelled, or failed
    43: prerequisite fails the gate. Requiring only the old six desktop names no longer
    44: covers mobile results. This PR does not change repository branch protection.
    45: The independent, path-filtered mobile lifecycle workflow retains its Linux and
    46: macOS fake-tool tests; its filter now includes Android/iOS-specific test files
    47: and the main workflow, not just files containing `mobile` in their names.
    48: 
    49: Desktop and mobile jobs retain the existing 300-minute outer timeout. Existing
    50: per-command self-host/emulator/simulator deadlines are unchanged. Reducing the
    51: outer deadline without a broader runtime distribution would be speculative.
    52: 
    53: ## Cache and artifact trust boundaries
    54: 
    55: Only Zig's **upstream compressed archive** is cached. The exact key includes a
    56: schema version, runner OS/architecture, Zig target, and the hash of `.github/zig.json` (version and all SHA-256 pins). There
    57: are no fallback restore keys and no cached build trees or compiler outputs.
    58: Every restore, including an exact hit, is SHA-256 checked before extraction and
    59: PATH publication. Only successful default-branch push setup writes a cache,
    60: and it writes immediately after verification, before repository tests run.
    61: Other branches and manual runs are read-only cache consumers. A corrupt
    62: archive fails setup rather than executing unverified bytes.
    63: 
    64: Mutable Android SDK packages, AVD state, and Homebrew prefixes are deliberately not cached. Their present installation commands
    65: do not provide immutable per-package revisions/checksums suitable for portable
    66: cache keys. Caching those directories by a coarse OS key would create stale or
    67: cross-toolchain state. Unused Vulkan SDK setup is removed because these jobs
    68: leave renderer/shader options disabled; mobile SDK coverage remains.
    69: 
    70: Actions are pinned to full commit IDs. Checkout credentials are not persisted.
    71: Workflow tokens request `contents: read` only; no job consumes repository
    72: secrets or uses `pull_request_target`. No broad environment dump is uploaded.
    73: Desktop, mobile, lifecycle, and lint transcripts are retained for seven days,
    74: with unique lane/run/attempt names. They live outside `build/`, because `generate`
    75: deletes that tree. There is no compiler artifact promoted for downstream use.
    76: 
    77: The issue-33 recovery workflow remains scoped to its original branch and keeps
    78: its one-day source archive. It now has pinned actions, shallow checkout,
    79: non-persisted credentials, a GitHub-only guard, and cancellation of obsolete
    80: snapshots. `git archive` includes tracked source only. Its gzip file is uploaded without redundant ZIP compression.
    81: 
    82: ## Cancellation and duplicate work
    83: 
    84: PR revisions and merge groups supersede their own obsolete runs. Main and tag
    85: pushes and explicit manual runs have unique run-ID groups so pending-run
    86: replacement cannot discard measurements. PR triggers include forks with read-only
    87: permissions; feature pushes do not create duplicate matrices. Mobile lifecycle
    88: PR updates cancel only their own stale runs; main lifecycle results are retained.
    89: 
    90: Android INT/TERM handlers retain nonzero cancellation status and use the
    91: existing bounded lifecycle stop command through the EXIT cleanup handler.
    92: Cleanup failure after otherwise successful tests still fails the shard.
    93: Bounded summaries use `always()`; uploads use `!cancelled()` and do not start
    94: after cancellation. Required-suite summaries fail closed through `ci_summary.py`.
    95: 
    96: ## Reproduction
    97: 
    98: Match the platform/architecture, Zig version/checksum, image toolchains and SDK
    99: settings in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Run from the repository root, with no
   100: other process using the selected build directory. Local entry points retain
   101: the trusted TCC bootstrap:
   102: 
   103: - Compiler/configuration matrix: `./build.sh test_all_combinations_ci --verbose=1`; Windows: `./build.ps1 test_all_combinations_ci --verbose=1`.
   104: - Unix modes: `./build.sh generate --cc clang --config Release --linker DEFAULT && ./build.sh test_mode_matrix --config Release`.
   105: - iOS: `BUSTER_IOS_ARCH=arm64 ./ios/test_ci.sh --all` (use `x86_64` on Intel).
   106: - Android: start with `bash ./android/start_emulator_ci.sh start`, run `./android/test_ci.sh --all`, and always call `bash ./android/start_emulator_ci.sh stop`, preserving the first failure.
   107: - Lifecycle: `bash tests/mobile_ci_scripts_test.sh` with coreutils and modern Bash available on macOS.
   108: - Workflows: `go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@03d0035246f3e81f36aed592ffb4bebf33a03106 .github/workflows/*.yml`.
   109: 
   110: To reproduce the hosted bootstrap on Unix, run `mkdir -p build && clang -Isrc -Wall -Werror -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable -g build.c -o build/build && ./build/build test_all_combinations_ci --verbose=1`.
   111: For the hosted mode gate, keep the second Clang-built driver outside `build/`
   112: and retain its `CFLAGS=-Wno-invalid-feature-combination`, as spelled out in the
   113: workflow. Windows reproduction must enter the architecture-specific VS shell
   114: and then put standalone LLVM first; the workflow contains the complete command.
   115: Each job summary records the commit, suite outcome, and relevant entry points.
   116:

   134: runner labels and coverage. Record per-run elapsed time (run start to last
   135: job completion), summed job seconds, queue delay, step durations, run attempt,
   136: and cache-hit state. Report cold and warm cache cohorts separately. Compute

   141:
