     1: # Desktop Zig configure evidence
     2: 
     3: [Build guidance](agents/build.md) · [Desktop combination shards](ci-combination-shards.md) ·
     4: [CI reproduction](ci-github-actions.md) ·
     5: [Investigation #707](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/issues/707)
     6: 
     7: This is diagnostic infrastructure, not a configure optimization or a speedup
     8: claim. The native `test_all_combinations_ci` command still owns compiler
     9: selection, graph generation, probes, scheduling, coverage, and failure policy.
    10: No compiler-works result is preseeded and no Zig compilation cache is restored.
    11: 
    12: ## Retained evidence
    13: 
    14: Each `release` or `checks` desktop shard copies a fixed allowlist from the
    15: native driver's `build/build-<release|checks>-ci_on-cc_*` trees after its
    16: combination step into that shard's existing
    17: `desktop-<os>-<arch>-<release|checks>-<run>-<attempt>` artifact, under
    18: `configure/`. The unsharded local `BUSTER_MATRIX_SHARD=all` path retains the
    19: legacy `build/build-ci_on-cc_*` names; the collector recognizes those names too
    20: without admitting either shard's separate superbuild directory.
    21: 
    22: - `CMakeCache.txt` and `CMakeFiles/CMakeConfigureLog.yaml`;
    23: - legacy `CMakeFiles/CMakeOutput.log` and `CMakeFiles/CMakeError.log`, when present;
    24: - `cmake-profile.json`, when native profiling was enabled.
    25: 
    26: Zig belongs to the `checks` partition, so the primary #707 evidence is in the
    27: Windows x86-64 checks and macOS x86-64 checks artifacts. Keep both shards when
    28: reconstructing a complete desktop lane: each artifact contains only the trees
    29: owned by that partition.
    30: 
    31: `configure/manifest.json` records every allowlisted path as captured, missing,
    32: or error, with byte length and SHA-256 for captured bytes. It includes only an
    33: explicit allowlist of run/runner identifiers, not a copy of the environment.
    34: The source, driver, compiler, target, and coverage identities remain in the
    35: adjacent authoritative `coverage.json`; exact commands and native timings remain
    36: in `combinations.log`. The manifest is diagnostic-only: it neither certifies
    37: successful compiler probes nor replaces the coverage/result consumers.
    38: 
    39: The collector performs no build or toolchain subprocesses and does not parse or
    40: sum profile events. It examines at most 4,096 build-root entries and 32 matching
    41: trees, retains at most 32 MiB per file and 128 MiB total, refuses links and
    42: Windows reparse points below the selected root, and requires a fresh output
    43: directory outside the build tree. Collection and size errors are retained in
    44: the manifest and fail the collection step. Missing optional diagnostics are
    45: explicit, including a profile absent from a failed configure. Raw files are not
    46: truncated or normalized. Run collection only after the shard's matrix has
    47: stopped; it is not an atomic snapshot of changing trees.
    48: 
    49: Raw CMake diagnostics may contain absolute toolchain/SDK paths and command-line
    50: options. Do not pass credentials through CMake options or place secrets in these
    51: files. The artifact is never restored as a build or test cache.
    52: 
    53: ## Diagnostic run
    54: 
    55: The normal PR, push, tag, and merge-group paths keep profiling disabled. A
    56: manual **Buster CI** dispatch also remains uninstrumented unless its boolean
    57: `cmake_profile` input is enabled. That value is captured in the dispatch event
    58: and is therefore immutable for every delayed or retried job in the run; no
    59: repository setting needs to be changed or cleared. The workflow maps the input
    60: to the existing native `BUSTER_CMAKE_PROFILE=1` switch only for
    61: `workflow_dispatch` events.
    62: 
    63: This control changes instrumentation only. It does not merge the `release` and
    64: `checks` partitions, remove a row, or create a configure-only workflow. The
    65: native driver writes one `cmake-profile.json` per configured tree and emits its
    66: existing profile summary.
    67: 
    68: For an already prepared hosted-equivalent checkout, reproduce a shard directly:
    69: 
    70: ```sh
    71: BUSTER_MATRIX_SHARD=checks BUSTER_CMAKE_PROFILE=1 \
    72:     ./build/build test_all_combinations_ci --verbose=1
    73: ```
    74: 
    75: On Windows, use the same Visual Studio/LLVM environment and verified Zig setup
    76: as `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
    77: 
    78: ```powershell
    79: $env:BUSTER_MATRIX_SHARD = 'checks'
    80: $env:BUSTER_CMAKE_PROFILE = '1'
    81: .\build\build.exe test_all_combinations_ci --verbose=1
    82: ```
    83: 
    84: These snippets do not install tools or replace the workflow bootstrap. Do not
    85: move the hosted driver from `build/build[.exe]`: coverage pins that location.
    86: After completion, collect into a fresh directory outside `build/`:
    87: 
    88: ```sh
    89: python3 tools/ci_configure_evidence.py \
    90:     --build-root build --output /path/outside/build/configure \
    91:     --profile-requested 1
    92: ```
    93: 
    94: Use `python` on the hosted Windows lane. An existing Zig profile can be
    95: summarized with the native driver:
    96: 
    97: ```sh
    98: ./build/build cmake_profile_summary \
    99:     build/build-checks-ci_on-cc_zig-sanitize_off-fuzz_available_off-configs_Debug/cmake-profile.json \
   100:     --limit 30
   101: ```
   102: 
   103: CMake's profile describes time inside CMake commands, including time waiting for
   104: children. It is not process CPU, RSS, or filesystem attribution. Nested commands
   105: must not be summed as independent wall time. Use the raw configure log and exact
   106: subprocess commands to decide whether OS-level tracing of a compiler, ABI, or
   107: runtime-cache operation is needed. Do not transfer Windows attribution to Intel
   108: macOS without separate evidence.
   109: 
   110: ## Performance experiment remains separate
   111: 
   112: Use profiling only to locate work. For timed repetitions set
   113: `BUSTER_CMAKE_PROFILE=0`. Independently prepare and document cold and warm **Zig
   114: compilation/runtime-cache** cases; a hit on the verified download-archive cache
   115: does not establish either state. Do not reuse Buster objects, compiler artifacts,
   116: or passing test verdicts. Keep cache preparation outside measured configuration
   117: and retain its cost separately.
   118: 
   119: Before comparing a candidate, retain exact source/driver, CMake/Ninja/Zig,
   120: compiler/SDK, runner-image, CPU budget, shard, and cache identities, including
   121: effective Zig cache paths and how they were prepared. Match the authoritative
   122: expected, detected, and executed coverage identities across both partitions.
   123: Record at least three successful comparable uninstrumented full runs per arm,
   124: preserving failed and cancelled attempts separately. Report configure, build,
   125: full-job, queue, and aggregate runner time, plus CPU/RSS and transfer or
   126: verification cost where available. Do not report the historical configure

   274: ### Execution waves
   275: 
   276: Work can proceed in parallel inside a wave; a later wave begins for an issue
   277: only after its own hard dependencies are complete.
   278: 
   279: 1. **Semantic foundations and inventories:** #32, #33, #37, #38, #39, #42,
   280:    #43, #44 and #45. Preserve conservative scheduling classification in #126 /
   281:    PR #127 while #41 remains blocked.

   283:    their hard dependencies.
   284: 3. **Retirement:** #36, after the machine verifier and fallback corpus prove the
   285:    machine path is authoritative.
   286: 
   287: ## Change gates
   288: 
   289: Every child PR records the base commit, corpus, target, allocator mode, command,
   290: result and before/after measurement. A count without a date and revision is not
   291: an architectural fact.
   292: 
   293: The minimum local gates are selected by change class:
   294: 
   295: - `ide test` for focused unit, verifier, selector, allocator, encoder and driver
   296:   coverage;
   297: - `./build.sh test_mode_matrix --config Release` for allocator/target/object
   298:   format width;
   299: - `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` for deep native fixed-point
   300:   coverage;
   301: - `test_all` plus the relevant Wasm64, eBPF and LLVM-bitcode assertions when a
   302:   shared canonical contract changes;
   303: - differential execution or byte/relocation inspection against the direct
   304:   emitter and external compilers where they are valid oracles.
   305: 
   306: Tests that cannot execute a cross-target image still inspect the strongest
   307: available structural property. A missing execution avenue is reported, not
   308: silently counted as a pass.
   309: 
   310: ## Completion rule
   311: 
   312: Issue #31 is the architecture and coordination parent. It is complete when:
   313: 
   314: 1. this contract is in the repository and contradicting code changes update it;
   315: 2. #32 through #45 have explicit owners;
   316: 3. the dependency order and coordination edges above are the queue of record;
   317: 4. every child has a correctness oracle and compile-time/code-quality
   318:    measurement contract;
   319: 5. fallback observability and non-native consumer duties remain mandatory
   320:    through the migration.
   321: 
   322: Closing #31 does **not** claim that #32 through #45 are implemented. Each child
   323: remains the independently reviewable implementation and closure unit for its
   324: exception. The destination architecture is reached when those child issues,
   325: not the coordination parent, are closed with their recorded evidence.

     1: # Native configuration differential testing
     2: 
     3: `build.c` owns `test_differential`; its implementation is in
     4: `tools/differential.c`. It complements, rather than replaces, the existing
     5: seeded Python differential corpus, `test_all`, and `test_mode_matrix`.
     6: There is no new runtime dependency or shell-based process orchestration.
     7: 
     8: ## Run
     9: 
    10: From the repository root, build `ide` normally and use a **new** output directory:
    11: 
    12: ```sh
    13: ./build.sh test_differential --ide build/Release/ide --cc clang --out build/differential-release --sanitize-oracle
    14: ```
    15: 
    16: The defaults use thirteen permanent cases and four generated cases, seed 1, a
    17: 10-second deadline per child, and at most 64 reduction trials for the first
    18: runtime mismatch in each case. A reference compiler must be available; its
    19: absence is a failure, not a skip. `--cc` accepts a Clang/GCC-style executable,
    20: not a shell command containing flags. On Windows specify the `.exe` path.
    21: 
    22: Desktop SysV x86-64 hosts additionally run `sysv-sseup`: an independently
    23: compiled observer checks sixteen-byte vector wrappers, nested wrappers, union
    24: class merging, stack/register exhaustion, copied variadic lists and calls in
    25: both directions. Every MIR leg is strict; NONE is a separately checked direct
    26: oracle. This case checks actual payloads against the host compiler, so matching
    27: Buster outputs cannot conceal a shared ABI-classification defect.
    28: 
    29: Desktop SysV x86-64 also runs `sysv-va-list`. Actual public 24-byte,
    30: eight-aligned lists cross the Clang/GCC boundary in both directions, including
    31: native-owned destinations, independent copies, named and unnamed GP/FP pool
    32: exhaustion, and guarded member/array/dereference destinations. A native source
    33: ends at an inaccessible page to detect oversized reads as well as writes.
    34: Every MIR leg is strict; the registered driver suite additionally checks all
    35: four allocators and both frontend forms on Linux/macOS/Android/iOS objects,
    36: executing the matching desktop ABI with its configured host compiler.
    37: Cross-generated mobile objects are not native mobile execution evidence.
    38: 
    39: The native variadic case also exercises ELF AArch64's independent integer
    40: and floating-point argument files. Its ten-float call exhausts the floating
    41: registers, and its mixed named parameters check the anonymous integer cursor.
    42: Both directions cross compiler boundaries, with copied lists and stack
    43: canaries. Homogeneous floating aggregates cover two- and four-element reads,
    44: including a spill that closes the floating register file before a smaller
    45: following argument. Machine unit tests select and verify the fixture for ELF
    46: AArch64 as well as x86-64 and execute it when the host ABI matches.
    47: 
    48: The registered driver suite runs strict MIR platform variadic tests on native
    49: Darwin and Windows AArch64, outside the direct-emitter comparison matrix.
    50: Its separately compiled callers and callees cover named floating arguments,
    51: mixed anonymous integer/floating arguments, integer register exhaustion,
    52: Darwin's packed narrow named stack arguments, copied lists, and scalar,
    53: homogeneous-floating and integer aggregates up to sixteen bytes. Public
    54: `va_list` objects cross the compiler boundary in both directions: copying a
    55: by-value list preserves the producer's cursor, while advancing through a
    56: pointer changes it. The standalone source also serves the cross-target driver
    57: checks; writing a Darwin or Windows object on another host is not native
    58: execution evidence. The former direct emitter has independently reproduced
    59: public-list and Darwin named-stack ABI defects, so agreement with it does not
    60: serve as the oracle for these new public-ABI cases.
    61: 
    62: On ELF AArch64, twenty-two additional relations exchange actual public `va_list`
    63: objects, rather than only calling variadic functions compiled by the other
    64: compiler. Independent producers and consumers check the three-pointer/two-offset
    65: layout, pointer and by-value list parameters, original-versus-copy independence,
    66: canaries, mixed named register/stack arguments, i128 register/stack alignment,
    67: HFA overflow and independent GP/FP exhaustion. By-value calls pass a separate
    68: `va_copy`, end that consumed copy before any further use, and continue through
    69: an independent original list. The consumer checks distinct caller/callee storage;
    70: no check relies on reusing the consumed by-value list. The extended caller/reader cases cover 24/32-byte
    71: HFAs, 17-byte and over-aligned indirect composites, 64/128-bit short vectors,
    72: and two/four-part HVAs, including mixed vector lane types. They exhaust both
    73: register files and check sixteen-byte overflow alignment after a double-sized
    74: stack slot, including named vector/HVA parameters before the anonymous tail.
    75: Direct V-register staging retains preceding X arguments in every
    76: allocator mode. Quad-precision floats and vectors wider than sixteen bytes
    77: remain outside these read fixtures. The existing native configuration matrix
    78: runs them on Linux AArch64; other hosts do not count the guarded relations as
    79: executed. QEMU cross-compiler checks are separate emulator evidence.
    80: 
    81: The native aggregate case covers Windows indirect arguments in both call
    82: directions, including 3/5/7-byte values, 12/16/24/32-byte values, aligned
    83: objects, hidden return pointers and function-pointer calls. Volatile writes

    86: also verify that distinct calls reuse one aligned outgoing copy area. The
    87: fixture has a validated Linux x86-64 and AArch64 baseline. Calls to locally
    88: defined functions with qualified aggregate parameters under strict verification

    90:

    92: ./build.sh test_differential --self-test

   102: This also accepts saved C cases from `tools/differential_c_harness.py`.
   103: `--host` and `--reject` cannot be combined. The original subject's directory

   105: `--timeout N`, and `--minimize N` are validated bounded integers; zero reduction

   109: default mode, retaining NONE and its alias as direct controls. It is recorded in
   110: the manifest and exact child arguments. The built-in `sysv-sseup` and
   111: `sysv-va-list` cases always require this strict policy, including reductions,

   124: 
   125: ## forgejo#537 — c frontend: fix the conditional-type prediction that miscompiles mask64_prefix
   126: 
   127: Closed 2026-08-24. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/537
   128: 
   129: **Task for an agent.** Read `AGENTS.md` first; it holds the house rules this change has to satisfy (one return per function, orientation headers, no unverified comments).
   130: 
   131: ## What is wrong
   132: 
   133: `ide cc` miscompiles a conditional whose arms are a 64-bit constant and a 64-bit shift expression. Five-line repro, no SIMD involved:
   134: 
   135: ```c
   136: volatile u32 opaque; opaque = 32; u32 lane = opaque;
   137: u64 v = lane >= 64 ? ~(u64)0 : (((u64)1 << lane) - 1);
   138: /* clang: 0x00000000ffffffff   ide cc: 0xffffffffffffffff */
   139: ```
   140: 
   141: That is `mask64_prefix` from `src/buster/lib/simd.h` expanded, so **every `mask64_prefix(n)` with a runtime `n` in [32,64) returns `~0` in self-hosted stages**.
   142: 
   143: ## Cause (already diagnosed, verify before fixing)
   144: 
   145: From `ide cc -emit-llvm`: the conditional's result slot is allocated **i32**. Both arms are computed correctly in i64, then `trunc`ed into the slot and `sext`ed back on reload. The slot is sized by the *predicted* type — `c_ir_predict_expression_type_attempt` → `c_ir_query_conditional_type` (`src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:1906`, with `c_ir_conditional_result_type_attempt` at `c_gen.c:19437`) — which returns invalid here and falls back to `builder->s32_type`, not by the resolved type.
   146: 
   147: It needs **both** arms to be what they are: `cond ? ~(u64)0 : x` alone is fine, `cond ? y : ((u64)1 << lane) - 1` alone is fine, the shift outside a conditional is fine. All four allocator modes (`fast`, `quality`, `mir-stack`, `-fno-register-allocator`) fail identically, so this is upstream of codegen. The same prediction machinery has produced wrong answers before (see the sizeof/array-bound history in `PERFORMANCE_AUDITS.md`).
   148: 
   149: ## Blast radius
   150: 
   151: Self-hosted stages only — clang builds the compiler correctly; this is about what `ide cc` *emits*. The live caller is `ir_source_search_vector` (`src/buster/lib/compiler/ir/ir.c:92-93`): `mask64_prefix(lanes * 4)` covers [32,64) for 8..15 lanes, so the wrong mask over-reads the loaded vector. The extra lanes are masked out of `covered` immediately afterwards, so it is latent — but it is a real over-read.
   152: 
   153: Coverage missed it because `simd_test.c` and `tests/basic_c_simd.c` only ask for `mask64_prefix(0)`, `(1)` and `(64)`, all compile-time constants.
   154: 
   155: ## Definition of done
   156: 
   157: 1. The prediction returns the correct 64-bit type for this shape (fix the prediction, do not special-case `mask64_prefix`).
   158: 2. The five-line case is registered as a driver fixture under `tests/`.
   159: 3. `simd_test.c` and `tests/basic_c_simd.c` gain a **runtime-count sweep** over `mask64_prefix` (every n in 0..64 through a volatile), not just constants.
   160: 4. `c_parse.c:11490`'s workaround macro `c_parse_census_lanes_below` is reverted to a plain `mask64_prefix` call (it exists only to dodge this bug).
   161: 5. Four-mode self-host reaches a byte-identical stage 2, and `test_all_combinations_ci` is green.
   162: 
   163: ---
   164: 
   165: ## forgejo#538 — parser: write a kind|punctuator sidecar from the preprocessor's token emitter
   166: 
   167: Closed 2026-08-24. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/538
   168: 
   169: **Task for an agent.** Performance work: read the newest entry of `PERFORMANCE_AUDITS.md` for the reference numbers before measuring anything, and record the result as a new audit file under `docs/performance-audits/` (mint the id with `tools/new_audit.py`).
   170: 
   171: ## The finding
   172: 
   173: The parser-side SIMD census (audit `2026-08-22T220912Z`, PR 532) found the layout fact underneath every ranked parser lever: **`CToken` is a 12-byte AoS row, and every parser pass reads exactly two of those bytes** — `kind` and `punctuator`, at offsets 10 and 11 — to ask what shape a token is. That is four full strided walks of the token stream per parse, each touching 12 bytes to use 2.
   174: 
   175: `lcm(12,64) = 192`, so today's kernels must gather fields with fixed `vpermt2b` index vectors across three chunks per sixteen tokens (see `c_parse_token_census` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` for the working example).
   176: 
   177: ## The task
   178: 
   179: Have the **preprocessor's token emitter** write a parallel `kind|punctuator` sidecar array as it fills the token rows, and switch the parser's shape queries to read it. This turns all four strided parser walks into contiguous byte scans, and lets the census kernel drop its projection step entirely.
   180: 
   181: Constraints and prior art:
   182: 
   183: - The window emitter already writes the final 12-byte `CToken` row format directly into the preprocessor's final slots (see the preprocessor token-stream work, PR 500) — the sidecar has to be written on that same path, in the same private-arena scheme, without adding a second pass over the stream.
   184: - The reference (non-compact) lexer path must produce an identical sidecar; the differential gate compares the two implementations and is the thing that proves the change.
   185: - Budget the memory: one byte per token against ~570 K identifiers-plus-everything-else per stage-1 compile. Say in the audit what the sidecar costs in bytes and in the emitter's instruction count, not just what it saves.
   186: 
   187: ## Definition of done
   188: 
   189: - Sidecar written by the emitter, consumed by `c_parse_token_census`, and by the other three shape walks it can serve.
   190: - Outputs byte-identical, self-host fixed point holds, `-march=x86-64` clean.
   191: - Pinned A/B pairs (11 is the house standard) with per-run instruction and branch deltas, recorded in a new audit; report the emitter-side cost separately from the parser-side win.

   316: 
   317: Oracle against **clang**, not against buster's canonical emitter:
   318: 
   319: ```
   320: clang -target aarch64-linux-gnu -nostdlib -static -fuse-ld=lld
   321: ```
   322: 
   323: `_start` plus `svc #0` exit, run under `qemu-aarch64`. For the c_abi lane, compile the three TUs together with a local no-op `write()` stub TU, or the link goes dynamic and qemu has no aarch64 interpreter.
   324:

   367: ## forgejo#544 — codegen: alias single-chunk machine streams instead of flattening them
   368: 
   369: Closed 2026-08-24. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/544
   370: 
   371: **Task for an agent.** Performance work, from the copy cluster in audit `2026-08-22T195419Z` (PR 521). Read the newest `PERFORMANCE_AUDITS.md` entry for current reference numbers before measuring; record a new audit at the end.
   372: 
   373: ## The lead
   374: 
   375: `machine_stream_flatten` (`src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/machine.c:1381`) is **3.17% of DRAM samples** — the largest single member of the ranked copy cluster. It copies each builder stream's chunks into one flat array.
   376: 
   377: The observation that makes it addressable: **chunks and flattened arrays share one arena**, and `MACHINE_BUILDER_CHUNK_BYTES` is 16 KB = 682 instruction rows, so **most functions are single-chunk**.    378:

   380: 
   381: ## Constraints
   382:

   385: - Measure how often single-chunk actually holds on stage 1 before writing the fix; the whole lead rests on that fraction, and it is cheap to count.
   386: - A DRAM-sample ranking predicts which fix pays **badly** — that has bitten this codebase before. Instructions first: take the change if instructions drop, and treat a miss-count improvement without an instruction win as unproven.

   389: 
   390: - Single-chunk streams alias; multi-chunk streams keep flattening.

   423:

   429:

   431: 
   432: It already did. On 2026-08-24 the canonical emitter was found to have never captured incoming argument registers at entry: it read each parameter's argument register at its `IR_OPCODE_ARGUMENT` instruction, which is only sound if the entry block is a contiguous run of parameter homes. A parameter written with **array syntax** breaks that — the C frontend emits the bound's element-count × element-size multiply between the homes, and that multiply's scratch is RAX and **RCX**, the fourth System V argument. The defect reproduced as far back as `45f8c133` (2026-07-30), when canonical was the *only* emitter, and went unnoticed for a month because no function in `ide.c` had the triggering shape until `d3311023` (2026-08-18).
   433: 
   434: The by-hand recipe that would have caught it — all four modes must reach the same byte-identical stage 2:
   435: 
   436: ```
   437: for m in none mir-stack fast quality; do
   438:   build/Release/ide cc -Isrc -Ibuild/generated -DBUSTER_UNITY_BUILD=1 \
   439:     -DBUSTER_INCLUDE_TESTS=0 -fregister-allocator=$m \
   440:     src/buster/apps/ide/ide.c -o build/s1-$m
   441:   ./build/s1-$m cc -Isrc -Ibuild/generated -DBUSTER_UNITY_BUILD=1 \
   442:     -DBUSTER_INCLUDE_TESTS=0 src/buster/apps/ide/ide.c -o build/s2-$m
   443:   sha256sum build/s2-$m
   444: done
   445: ```
   446: 
   447: ## The task
   448: 
   449: Wire that four-mode chain into the self-host gate so `none` and `quality` are covered, not just default and `mir-stack`.
   450: 
   451: Judgement to make and to justify in the change: a full four-mode self-host is not free, and CI wall time is already gated by the 4-CPU Windows runner. Options worth pricing before picking one — run all four only on the fastest Linux lane, run `none` on a reduced translation unit, or run the extra modes on a schedule rather than per push. Whatever you choose, **`none` must be gated somewhere that fails a PR**, not only nightly, and the reasoning belongs in `AGENTS.md`'s Tests section.
   452: 
   453: ## Definition of done
   454: 
   455: - `-fregister-allocator=none` self-host is gated and demonstrably fails when the canonical emitter is broken (revert `93d4d85a` locally to prove it).
   456: - Added CI wall-time cost measured and stated.
   457: - `AGENTS.md` records which modes are gated where.

   511: ## forgejo#549 — codegen: materialize block addresses for label addresses and computed goto
   512: 
   513: Closed 2026-08-24. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/549
   514: 
   515: **Task for an agent.** Cross-target design work. Larger than the other open tasks — expect a design pass before any code, and expect to split it into more than one PR.
   516: 
   517: ## What is missing
   518: 
   519: Taking the address of a label, and everything that follows from it, is unsupported on **both** machine paths. From the AArch64 census (audit `2026-08-22T205418Z`, verified per class, not assumed):
   520: 
   521: - label addresses: 8 fixture functions
   522: - `INDIRECT_BRANCH`: 1
   523: - computed-goto `ARGUMENT`: 1
   524: - inline assembly: 10 (separate concern, not this task)
   525: 
   526: The label/indirect-branch group was measured **equally unsupported on the x86-64 machine path**, which is what makes this cross-target design work rather than an AArch64 catch-up item. Functions using it fall back whole to the canonical emitter.
   527: 
   528: ## What the design has to answer
   529: 
   530: 1. **Block-address materialization** — a label's address is a code address that is only known after layout and relaxation, so it needs its own **relaxer fixup class**, on both targets, plus whatever the object writers need to emit for it (and for PIC, a relative form).
   531: 2. **Allocator edge contracts across indirect edges.** An `INDIRECT_BRANCH` has an edge set that is not derivable from the terminator alone. Live-range splitting, the frequency weighting in the fast allocator, and the spill placement all assume a known successor list. Decide how the edge set is declared and what the allocators are allowed to assume at an indirect edge — this is the part that will decide whether the change is small or large.
   532: 3. Interaction with the existing switch lowering, which already carries a side-table terminator on a64 (`switch_opcode` in the description) and a compare chain — a computed goto is close enough to that shape that it may reuse the machinery.
   533: 
   534: ## Suggested shape of the work
   535: 
   536: - A written design first (an audit-style document or a PR description), naming the fixup class, the edge-declaration mechanism, and what each allocator mode must do.
   537: - Then x86-64, then AArch64, each with the census re-measured — the census corpus changes underneath you (it tripled in one day when the c_abi port merged), so **re-measure, never quote a stale count**.
   538: 
   539: ## Definition of done
   540: 
   541: - The ten-or-so label/indirect fixture functions select on both targets in all four allocator modes.

   547: ## forgejo#555 — c frontend: an identifier in an array parameter's bound is unbound at lowering
   548: 
   549: Closed 2026-08-24. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/555
   550: 
   551: ## What is wrong
   552: 
   553: An identifier in an array parameter's bound that is **not** a call is rejected
   554: on valid C:
   555: 
   556: ```c
   557: static long extra = 1;
   558: static int head(long n, int a[extra + n]) { return a[0]; }
   559: int main(void) { int v[4] = {13, 1, 2, 3}; return head(2, v); }
   560: ```
   561: 
   562: ```
   563: cc: error: t.c:2:31: in function 'head': could not lower variable-length array parameter bounds
   564: ```
   565: 
   566: The inner failure (visible by not overwriting `builder.failure_message` in the
   567: parameter loop of `c_lower_to_ir`) is `could not lower unbound identifier
   568: 'extra'`, from `c_gen.c` around the "unbound identifier" diagnostic in
   569: `c_ir_lower_expression_core_step`.
   570: 
   571: Same shape, same cause, all rejected:
   572: 
   573: ```c
   574: static int object = 1;
   575: static int head(long n, int a[(long)&object - (long)&object + n]) { return a[0]; }
   576: 
   577: static int helper(void) { return 5; }
   578: static int head2(long n, int a[(long)&helper - (long)&helper + n]) { return a[0]; }
   579: ```
   580: 
   581: The identical expressions work in a **body** VLA bound (`int a[extra + n];`
   582: inside a function compiles and runs), so this is specific to the declarator.
   583: 
   584: ## How it was diagnosed
   585: 
   586: `c_parse_array_suffixes` (`c_parse.c`) records a parameter's bound as a token
   587: range and never binds the identifiers inside it, so
   588: `parse.identifier_uses` -- and therefore `token_entities`, which is derived
--- lines 600-691 ---
   600: - a **global object or function designator** has no such fallback --
   601:   `c_ir_emit_global_place` and the `C_ENTITY_FUNCTION` arm both need the entity
   602:   from `c_ir_identifier_entity`, which returns invalid, so `value` stays
   603:   invalid and the "unbound identifier" diagnostic fires.
   604: 
   605: ## Where to start
   606: 
   607: - `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c`, `c_ir_lower_expression_core_step`,
   608:   the `CEntityId entity = c_ir_identifier_entity(builder, index);` that opens
   609:   the identifier arm. `c_ir_identifier_entity_or_lookup` right next to it
   610:   already does the file-scope fallback that would resolve these; the question
   611:   is whether widening that arm is safe for body identifiers, where an unbound
   612:   name currently *is* an error.
   613: - `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c`, `c_parse_array_suffixes` and
   614:   `c_parse_bind_identifier`, for the root-cause alternative: bind a parameter
   615:   bound's identifiers at parse time. That is the honest fix and it would also
   616:   retire the parameter-bound reachability pass PR #554 added, but
   617:   `c_parse_array_suffixes` is shared with every other declarator (binding there
   618:   would double-bind local ones), it takes no scope, and
   619:   `c_parse_bind_identifier` asserts on `identifier_use_capacity` -- so the
   620:   capacity accounting and the scope plumbing both have to be worked out first.
   621: 
   622: ## Constraints and do-not-retries
   623: 
   624: - PR #554 already handled the call case and the three capacities it needed;
   625:   do not re-derive those. Its parameter-bound reachability pass exists only
   626:   because the parser records no identifier use here -- if the parser fix lands,
   627:   delete the pass and re-measure.
   628: - Widening the capacity scan over the declarator **unconditionally** costs
   629:   0,05% of a self-compile's instructions; PR #554 gates it on the definition
   630:   having an array parameter for half that. Keep the gate.
   631: 
   632: ## How to validate
   633: 
   634: Differential against clang with the exit code carrying the answer (binaries
   635: built by `ide cc` swallow `printf` output, so `return` the value):
   636: 
   637: ```sh
   638: clang -O0 -o a t.c && ./a; echo $?
   639: build/Release/ide cc -o b t.c && ./b; echo $?
   640: ```
   641: 
   642: Cover: a global object in the bound, a function designator's address in the
   643: bound, both in the second dimension of a two-dimensional parameter, and an
   644: enumerator. Then extend `tests/basic_c_vla.c` (it already carries
   645: `check_call_bound_parameter`), and run `./build.sh test_all_combinations_ci`
   646: plus `./build.sh test_self_host`. Report the self-compile instruction delta
   647: measured with both compilers over one fixed baseline tree.
   648: 
   649: ## Definition of done
   650: 
   651: The four shapes above compile, run, and agree with clang; `tests/basic_c_vla.c`
   652: covers them; the local matrix is green; the instruction delta is reported.

  1028:   declarator's function-name token. With no parameter-list declarator there is
  1029:   no such token, so the declaration is filed `C_DECLARATION_OBJECT` even
  1030:   though its type is `C_TYPE_FUNCTION`.

  1033:   `c_ir_find_function_for_call` additionally checks arity against
  1034:   `builder->signatures[declaration_index]`, which `c_ir_function_signature`
  1035:   fills from `declaration.parameter_start/parameter_count` -- empty for this
  1036:   shape. The parameter list lives in the `CType`, not in the declaration.
  1037: - The diagnostic is also misleading: the identifier branch in
  1038:   `c_ir_lower_expression_core_step` reports "could not lower unbound
  1039:   identifier" when the entity *is* bound and it is the function lookup that

  1055: ## forgejo#644 — codegen: an x87 aggregate object rejects the whole function
  1056: 
  1057: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/644
  1058: 
  1059: The canonical emitter refuses any function one of whose values has a canonical
  1060: type that *contains* f80 without *being* the scalar x87 shape. That gate is now
  1061: the sole blocker for the seventeen `src/math` units named in issue 583, whose
  1062: static initializers PR 643 taught the frontend to fold.
  1063: 
  1064: ## Reproduce
  1065: 
  1066: ```sh
  1067: ./build.sh build --config Release -t ide
  1068: printf 'static long double a[2];\nlong double f(void){return a[1];}\n' > /tmp/a.c
  1069: ./build/Release/ide cc -c /tmp/a.c -o /dev/null
  1070: # cc: error: C code generation failed with error 3 (CODEGEN_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_ABI),
  1071: # function 0 ('f', ...), instruction 0, opcode 0, operation 73
  1072: ```
  1073: 
  1074: No initializer is involved: an uninitialized array reproduces it, and it
  1075: reproduced identically on the binary from before PR 643. These all fail the
  1076: same way, while the scalar and pointer forms beside them succeed:
  1077: 
  1078: | shape | verdict |
  1079: | --- | --- |
  1080: | `long double q(long double *p){return p[1];}` | ok |
  1081: | `static long double s; long double q(void){return s;}` | ok |
  1082: | `static struct S{long double x;} s; long double q(void){return s.x;}` | ok |
  1083: | `static long double a[2]; long double *q(void){return &a[1];}` | ok |
  1084: | `static long double a[2]; long double q(void){return a[1];}` | **error 3** |
  1085: | `static long double a[2]; long double q(void){long double *p=a; return p[1];}` | **error 3** |
  1086: | `long double q(void){long double a[2]; a[0]=1.0L; return a[1];}` | **error 3** |
  1087: | `static long double a[2]; ... (const unsigned char*)a` inside a function, `-fregister-allocator=none` | **error 3** |
  1088: 
  1089: Note the last row: reading the array's *bytes* is refused too, under the NONE
  1090: allocator only, because that is the allocator whose path is the canonical
  1091: emitter. `tests/basic_c_long_double_static_initializer.c` works around it by
  1092: reaching each object through a file-scope pointer; that workaround should be
  1093: removable once this is fixed.
  1094: 
  1095: ## Where it is
  1096: 
  1097: `codegen_generate_canonical_module_attempt` in
  1098: `src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/codegen.c`, in the block that opens with the
  1099: comment "The recursive contains query is broader than the x87 payload we can
  1100: interpret" (around line 7985 as of `dfc07bb2`). For each of the function's
  1101: values it asks `codegen_canonical_x64_type_contains_f80_cached`, and if the
  1102: answer is yes it demands `codegen_canonical_x64_type_is_f80_x87_shape_cached`,
  1103: which requires `layout.size == 16 && layout.alignment == 16` plus an ABI class
  1104: of x87. A `[2 x long double]` is 32 bytes, so it fails that and the whole
  1105: function is rejected.
  1106: 
  1107: The gate is deliberate — its comment says it exists so that "an
  1108: instruction-specific path" cannot "mistake their bytes for scalar f80 data".
  1109: The work is to let an x87 *object* through as memory while keeping every
  1110: x87 *ABI value* on the narrow shape it has today: an array or struct of long
  1111: doubles is addressable storage that only ever moves through loads, stores and
  1112: `memcpy`, never through a return-class or argument-class decision.
  1113: 
  1114: ## Validate
  1115: 
  1116: - The four shapes in the table above compile, and their generated code loads
  1117:   and stores the right ten bytes.
  1118: - `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  1119:   `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`.
  1120: - `./build/build test_musl --config Release ~/dev/musl-v1.2.6`: the seventeen
  1121:   units of issue 583 — `floorl`, `ceill`, `roundl`, `truncl`, `rintl`, `modfl`,
  1122:   `__rem_pio2l`, `atanl`, `expl`, `logl`, `log2l`, `log10l`, `log1pl`, `powl`,
  1123:   `tgammal`, `erfl`, `exp10l` — should compile. Rebaseline
  1124:   `MUSL_EXPECTED_COMPILED_UNITS` and `MUSL_EXPECTED_FAILURE_HASH` in `build.c`
  1125:   from the `MUSL_INVENTORY` line and update the class counts in AGENTS.md's
  1126:   musl section (currently 66 code-generation failures, of which these are part).
  1127: - Oracle the emitted code against Clang for the same source, by object bytes.
  1128:   `~/dev/musl-v1.2.6` is pinned at tag v1.2.6, commit
  1129:   `9fa28ece75d8a2191de7c5bb53bed224c5947417`; never modify it.
  1130: 
  1131: ## Do not retry
  1132: 
  1133: Loosening `codegen_canonical_x64_type_is_f80_x87_shape_cached` itself is the
  1134: wrong lever: that predicate answers an ABI question — "is this type returned
  1135: and passed in x87?" — and an array of long doubles is not. The gate that needs
  1136: to change is the per-value scan, which currently conflates "this function
  1137: touches x87 storage" with "this function passes x87 across a boundary".

  1141: ## forgejo#646 — link: an undefined weak symbol must resolve to zero, not become a dynamic import
  1142: 
  1143: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/646
  1144: 
  1145: ## What is wrong
  1146: 
  1147: An undefined *weak* symbol must resolve to address zero when nothing in the
  1148: link defines it. Buster's linker instead turns it into a dynamic import, so the
  1149: program builds and then dies at load.
  1150: 
  1151: Reproduce with the compiler as of PR #645, which is what made weak symbols
  1152: reachable from C source in the first place (`.weak` in a module-level
  1153: `__asm__` block):
  1154: 
  1155: ```c
  1156: typedef unsigned long word;
  1157: int c(word* absent);
  1158: __asm__(".text\n"
  1159:         ".globl e\n"
  1160:         ".type e, @function\n"
  1161:         "e:\n"
  1162:         "xorl %ebp, %ebp\n"
  1163:         ".weak absent_symbol\n"
  1164:         ".hidden absent_symbol\n"
--- lines 1181-1523 ---
  1181: The object itself is right. `readelf -sW` shows `absent_symbol` as
  1182: `OBJECT WEAK HIDDEN UND`, matching Clang byte for byte in binding and
  1183: visibility, and `ld -static` on the same object resolves the `lea` to address
  1184: zero and produces a program that runs. Only Buster's own link is wrong.
  1185: 
  1186: ## Why it matters
  1187: 
  1188: This is exactly musl's `_DYNAMIC` in `arch/x86_64/crt_arch.h`: a static
  1189: program's startup code takes the address of `_DYNAMIC` and reads zero to learn
  1190: it is static. Any startup object Buster produces is therefore linkable by GNU
  1191: `ld` but not by Buster's own linker. Measured 2026-08-28.
  1192: 
  1193: ## Where to start
  1194: 
  1195: `link_objects` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/link/link.c` already arbitrates
  1196: `ObjectSymbol.weak` for duplicate *definitions* (around
  1197: `link.c:826-838`); nothing consults it for an undefined one. The driver links
  1198: with `allow_undefined_symbols = true`, so the undefined symbol survives into
  1199: `link_native_executable_elf64_x86_64` / `..._dynamic`, which decides at
  1200: `link.c:2396` and `link.c:2667` whether an undefined symbol becomes a dynamic
  1201: import. A weak undefined that no input object and no shared library defines
  1202: should instead resolve to zero and its relocations be applied against that,
  1203: rather than joining the dynamic symbol table.
  1204: 
  1205: Take care not to change the existing case: a weak undefined that a shared
  1206: library *does* define must still bind to the library, which is what the
  1207: present code effectively gets right for the hosted link.
  1208: 
  1209: ## Adjacent, and probably worth doing in the same change
  1210: 
  1211: `__attribute__((weak))` on a C declaration is still parsed and ignored, so a
  1212: weak symbol can only be spelled from assembly today. musl declares `_init` and
  1213: `_fini` weak in `crt/crt1.c`, and Buster's `crt1.o` emits both as strong
  1214: undefined for that reason. `IrSymbol.is_weak` and `ObjectSymbol.weak` already
  1215: carry the bit end to end (PR #645); the frontend just has to set it. The
  1216: sibling `__attribute__((alias))` work is tracked separately.
  1217: 
  1218: ## Definition of done
  1219: 
  1220: - The repro above exits 0 under Buster's own link, on every register allocator.
  1221: - A hosted program that references a weak symbol a shared library defines still
  1222:   binds to the library.
  1223: - `__attribute__((weak))` on a C declaration produces `STB_WEAK`, checked in a
  1224:   fixture the way `tests/basic_c_global_asm_weak.c` checks the assembly
  1225:   spelling.
  1226: - `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  1227:   `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` green.
  1228: 
  1229: ---
  1230: 
  1231: ## forgejo#651 — c: __attribute__((packed)) and __attribute__((aligned)) are parsed and then ignored
  1232: 
  1233: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/651
  1234: 
  1235: `__attribute__((packed))` and `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` are accepted and
  1236: then ignored: the declaration compiles, no diagnostic is printed, and the
  1237: object gets the layout it would have had without the attribute. `_Alignas`,
  1238: which asks the same question in standard C, is honoured, so this is an
  1239: attribute-plumbing gap rather than a layout-engine one.
  1240: 
  1241: Measured 2026-08-29 on `3206be61`, Release `ide`.
  1242: 
  1243: ## Reproduce
  1244: 
  1245: ```sh
  1246: ./build.sh build --config Release -t ide
  1247: cat > /tmp/al.c <<'EOF'
  1248: #include <stdio.h>
  1249: struct A { _Alignas(32) int i; };
  1250: struct __attribute__((packed)) P { char c; int i; };
  1251: static char buf[8] __attribute__((aligned(64)));
  1252: int main(void){ printf("%d %d %d %d %d\n", (int)sizeof(struct A), (int)_Alignof(struct A),
  1253:                         (int)sizeof(struct P), (int)_Alignof(struct P),
  1254:                         (int)((unsigned long)buf % 64 == 0)); return 0; }
  1255: EOF
  1256: clang -o /tmp/al-clang /tmp/al.c && /tmp/al-clang     # 32 32 5 1 1
  1257: ./build/Release/ide cc -Wall -o /tmp/al-buster /tmp/al.c && /tmp/al-buster   # 32 32 8 4 0
  1258: ```
  1259: 
  1260: `_Alignas` agrees (32/32). `packed` does not (`sizeof` 8 vs 5, `_Alignof` 4 vs
  1261: 1) and neither does `aligned(64)` on a file-scope object, which lands
  1262: unaligned. `-Wall` says nothing in either case.
  1263: 
  1264: A member-level `__attribute__((packed))` is ignored the same way:
  1265: `struct C { char c; int i __attribute__((packed)); }` is 8 bytes rather than 5.
  1266: 
  1267: ## Why it matters
  1268: 
  1269: A silently different layout is an ABI divergence that no fixture can trip over
  1270: by accident, because both halves of a Buster-only program agree with each
  1271: other. It shows up when Buster-compiled code meets code another compiler
  1272: built, or when a program computes an offset by hand. Live users in the pinned
  1273: compatibility corpora:
  1274: 
  1275: - QuickJS `cutils.h` declares `struct __attribute__((packed)) packed_u64` /
  1276:   `packed_u32` / `packed_u16` and reads unaligned memory through them. The
  1277:   single member sits at offset 0, so the idiom happens to work anyway, which is
  1278:   exactly the kind of accident that keeps this hidden.
  1279: - QuickJS `quickjs.c` uses `__attribute__((aligned(JS_MALLOC_ALIGN)))` on
  1280:   flexible array members of its allocator headers.
  1281: - SQLite's `vdbeapi.c` uses `__attribute__((aligned(8)))` on a buffer it then
  1282:   casts.
  1283: - libc-test's `src/functional/tls_local_exec.c` uses `aligned(64)` and
  1284:   `aligned(4096)` on `__thread` objects, and the test checks the addresses.
  1285: 
  1286: ## Where to start
  1287: 
  1288: `_Alignas` already reaches the layout engine, so the alignment path exists and
  1289: the work is to route the attributes into it and to teach the struct layout an
  1290: alignment of one per member. Grep for the attribute parser in
  1291: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` and for `_Alignas` in
  1292: `c_parse.c`/`c_gen.c` to find both ends. `IrTypeLayout` carries `size` and
  1293: `alignment`; a packed aggregate needs its member offsets computed without
  1294: member alignment padding as well as its own alignment reduced.
  1295: 
  1296: ## Validate
  1297: 
  1298: - The reproducer above prints Clang's five numbers under `ide cc`.
  1299: - A fixture under `tests/` that a host compiler and Buster both compile,
  1300:   linked in both directions the way
  1301:   `tests/basic_c_long_double_aggregate_{caller,callee}.c` are, so a layout
  1302:   disagreement fails rather than being agreed on privately.
  1303: - `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  1304:   `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`.
  1305: - The QuickJS and SQLite harnesses (`test_quickjs`, `test_sqlite`), whose
  1306:   sources contain the uses listed above.
  1307: 
  1308: ## Do not retry
  1309: 
  1310: Do not make an unknown or unimplemented attribute a hard error as part of this:
  1311: the corpora carry many attributes Buster deliberately ignores, and turning the
  1312: whole class fatal fails units that are correct today. The change is to
  1313: implement these two, not to reject the rest.
  1314:

  1317: ## forgejo#653 — c: compose an unprototyped function declaration with a later prototype
  1318: 
  1319: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/653
  1320: 
  1321: ## What is wrong
  1322: 
  1323: A function declared with an empty parameter list -- `long f();`, which in C99
  1324: declares a function taking an *unspecified* number of arguments rather than
  1325: none -- conflicts with a later prototype for the same name:
  1326: 
  1327: ```c
  1328: long cp_c();
  1329: long cp_c(long nr, long u) { return nr + u; }
  1330: // cc: error: conflicting declaration of 'cp_c' (previous type 2, new type 4)
  1331: ```
  1332: 
  1333: Clang and GCC compose the two: C11 6.7.6.3p15 says a function type with a
  1334: parameter type list is compatible with an unprototyped one when the return
  1335: types are compatible and the parameters are unaffected by the default
  1336: argument promotions. `c_parse_types_compatible` in
  1337: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` compares
  1338: `left_type.parameter_count != right_type.parameter_count` first and rejects
  1339: the pair, so the entity search in `c_analyze_semantics` finds no compatible
  1340: candidate and falls through to `C_DIAGNOSTIC_CONFLICTING_DECLARATION`.
  1341: 
  1342: ## Why it matters
  1343: 
  1344: It is two of the 100 remaining `MUSL_UNSUPPORTED` units, and the two are the
  1345: whole "conflicting declarations" class of the inventory:
  1346: 
  1347: - `src/thread/__syscall_cp` -- `hidden long __syscall_cp_c();` at the top,
  1348:   then `weak_alias(sccp, __syscall_cp_c)` whose `__typeof(sccp)` is a
  1349:   prototype.
  1350: - `src/thread/pthread_cancel` -- `hidden long __cancel(), __syscall_cp_asm(),
  1351:   __syscall_cp_c();` at the top, then full prototypes for two of the three
  1352:   further down the same file.
  1353: 
  1354: Both are pre-existing: they fail identically on `3206be61`, before the
  1355: issue #641 fix that made a type-name declaration a function declaration.
  1356: 
  1357: ## Where to start
  1358: 
  1359: - `c_parse_types_compatible` (`c_parse.c`), the `C_TYPE_FUNCTION` case. An
  1360:   unprototyped function type has `parameter_count == 0` and is not variadic --
  1361:   which is also what `long f(void)` has, and *that* one must keep conflicting
  1362:   with `long f(long)`. The two therefore have to be told apart on the type
  1363:   before the compatibility rule can be written; a `void` parameter list and an
  1364:   empty one are the same `CType` shape today, so this needs a bit on `CType`
  1365:   (or a parameter record) set where the declarator is parsed, not a new scan.
  1366: - Composition matters as much as compatibility: after the two are accepted as
  1367:   one entity, the entity's type has to become the *prototyped* one, or the
  1368:   call site resolves against a signature with no parameters. The array-bound
  1369:   composite in `c_analyze_semantics` (`existing->type = declaration->type`
  1370:   when a redeclaration completes an unbounded array) is the existing precedent
  1371:   for adopting the more complete type.
  1372: - The default-argument-promotion caveat is real: `f()` is *not* compatible
  1373:   with `f(char)` or `f(float)`. Clang warns rather than errors on those, but a
  1374:   conservative reading -- accept the composite only when every parameter type
  1375:   is unaffected by the promotions -- keeps the two musl units and refuses the
  1376:   shapes the standard refuses.
  1377: 
  1378: ## How to validate
  1379: 
  1380: - A fixture under `tests/` covering: the accepted composition, a call through
  1381:   it resolving to the prototype's arity, `f(void)` still conflicting with
  1382:   `f(long)`, and a promotion-affected parameter still refused.
  1383: - `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  1384:   `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` stay green.
  1385: - `./build/build test_musl --config Release ~/dev/musl-v1.2.6` should reach
  1386:   `compiled=1251` with a new failure hash; the gate is
  1387:   `compiled=1249 failure_hash=0x4a0fec5b97536fd8` as of 2026-08-29, and both
  1388:   numbers move on purpose. The two units named above should leave the
  1389:   `MUSL_UNSUPPORTED` list and nothing else should join it.
  1390: 
  1391: ---
  1392: 
  1393: ## forgejo#656 — link: a default-visibility undefined weak symbol no library defines must also resolve to zero
  1394: 
  1395: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/656
  1396: 
  1397: ## What is wrong
  1398: 
  1399: An undefined weak symbol with **default visibility** that no shared library
  1400: actually defines still comes out non-zero. Issue #646 fixed the hidden case --
  1401: a reference nothing can preempt is relocated against zero at link time -- but
  1402: left the default-visibility one to the dynamic loader, because buster does not
  1403: know what a shared library exports on ELF. The loader is then asked for a
  1404: symbol nothing has, and buster's own representation of the import is what
  1405: answers instead of zero: a function gets its PLT thunk's address and an object
  1406: gets the copy slot the writer reserved for it, both non-zero.
  1407: 
  1408: Measured 2026-08-29, on the tree with the #646 fix in it:
  1409: 
  1410: ```c
  1411: extern __attribute__((weak)) unsigned long absent_object;
  1412: __attribute__((weak)) void absent_function(void);
  1413: int main(void) { return (&absent_object == 0 && absent_function == 0) ? 0 : 7; }
  1414: ```
  1415: 
  1416: ```sh
  1417: ./build/Release/ide cc -o /tmp/wu /tmp/wu.c && /tmp/wu ; echo $?   # 7
  1418: clang -no-pie -o /tmp/wuc /tmp/wu.c && /tmp/wuc ; echo $?          # 0
  1419: ```
  1420: 
  1421: The program loads and runs -- before #646 it died at load with `symbol lookup
  1422: error` -- so this is the remaining half, not a regression.
  1423: 
  1424: ## Why it matters
  1425: 
  1426: musl's `crt/crt1.c` declares `_init` and `_fini` weak, and nothing else in a
  1427: link that has no `crti.o` defines them. Buster compiles that startup object
  1428: correctly (`readelf -sW` shows both as `FUNC WEAK UND`), but linking it with
  1429: buster's own linker gives both a PLT thunk, so `__libc_start_main` sees them
  1430: as present and calls into a null GOT slot. `ld -static` resolves both to zero.
  1431: Reproduced by hand on 2026-08-29 against a local `musl-v1.2.6` checkout, with a
  1432: stub `__libc_start_main` reporting which of the two came back non-null:
  1433: 
  1434: ```sh
  1435: ./build/Release/ide cc -std=c99 -nostdinc -fno-builtin -fno-strict-aliasing \
  1436:   -fno-stack-protector -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700 -I<musl arch/generated includes> \
  1437:   -O2 -g0 -c -o /tmp/crt1.o <musl>/crt/crt1.c
  1438: ./build/Release/ide cc -e _start -o /tmp/crtprog /tmp/crt1.o /tmp/startmain.c
  1439: ```
  1440: 
  1441: `crtprog` exits 9, the status the stub returns for a non-null `_fini`.
  1442: 
  1443: ## Where to start
  1444: 
  1445: The decision is `link_elf_symbol_resolves_to_zero` in
  1446: `src/buster/lib/compiler/link/link.c`, just above the first ELF writer. It
  1447: answers `hidden || !dynamic_image` today because that is all the information
  1448: there is. The information it wants is `NativeDynamicLibrary.exported_symbols`
  1449: and `exports_known`, which `link.h` already carries and which
  1450: `compiler_driver_pe_library_exports` in `driver.c` already fills in **for PE
  1451: only** -- it maps the DLL and reads its export directory. The ELF equivalent
  1452: is the same shape: map the `.so`, read `.dynsym`/`.dynstr`, record the names.
  1453: Then the rule becomes the correct one -- a weak undefined that no library in
  1454: the link is known to export resolves to zero, and one that is exported stays
  1455: an import -- and it subsumes the visibility test rather than replacing it.
  1456: 
  1457: Two things to settle before writing it:
  1458: 
  1459: - **Finding the libraries.** The ELF writers name `libc.so.6` in `DT_NEEDED`
  1460:   themselves; it is not in `options.dynamic_libraries` at all, and no path for
  1461:   it is ever resolved. A search list (`-L` paths, the sysroot,
  1462:   `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`, `/usr/lib`, `/lib64`) is host-dependent, so decide
  1463:   what a link does when the file is not found: falling back to today's import
  1464:   makes the answer differ between machines, which a fixture cannot assert.
  1465:   Keeping the visibility rule as the floor and using exports only to *promote*
  1466:   a reference to an import is the conservative shape.
  1467: - **Cross links.** A `-target` link has no host libc to read. The same
  1468:   fallback question applies, and the sysroot is the only honest source.
  1469: 
  1470: ## Definition of done
  1471: 
  1472: - The repro above exits 0 under buster's own link, on every register allocator.
  1473: - A weak reference to a symbol libc does define still binds to it, which
  1474:   `tests/basic_c_weak_undefined.c` checks through `puts`.
  1475: - musl's `crt1.o`, linked by buster's own linker, reports `_init` and `_fini`
  1476:   as null.
  1477: - `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  1478:   `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` green.
  1479: 
  1480: ---
  1481: 
  1482: ## forgejo#659 — link: AArch64 copy relocations keep the x86-64 relocation type
  1483: 
  1484: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/659
  1485: 
  1486: The AArch64 dynamic ELF writer leaves copy relocations at the x86-64
  1487: relocation type. An imported data symbol in an `aarch64-linux-gnu`
  1488: executable comes out as type 5, which on AArch64 is not `R_AARCH64_COPY`
  1489: (1024) but a nonsense relocation the loader would apply as a 16-bit
  1490: absolute move.
  1491: 
  1492: ## Reproduction
  1493: 
  1494: ```c
  1495: extern int optind;
  1496: int main(void) { return optind; }
  1497: ```
  1498: 
  1499: ```
  1500: $ build/Release/ide cc -target aarch64-linux-gnu a64.c -o a64
  1501: $ readelf -W --relocs a64
  1502: 0000000000401018  0000000100000402 R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT    0000000000401110 optind + 0
  1503: 0000000000401020  0000000200000402 R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT    0000000000000000 exit + 0
  1504: 0000000000401110  0000000100000005 R_AARCH64_P32_MOVW_UABS_G0 0000000000401110 optind + 0
  1505: ```
  1506: 
  1507: The last entry should read `R_AARCH64_COPY`. Measured 2026-08-29 at
  1508: `178c78f6`.
  1509: 
  1510: ## Why it happens
  1511: 
  1512: `link_native_executable_elf64_aarch64_dynamic` in
  1513: `src/buster/lib/compiler/link/link.c` does not lay out its own image: it
  1514: calls the x86-64 dynamic writer and then patches the result. Its
  1515: relocation fix-up loop walks exactly `import_count` entries — the PLT
  1516: range — and rewrites each `Info` word to `R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT` (1026):
  1517: 
  1518: ```c
  1519: for (u32 import_index = 0; import_index < import_count; import_index += 1)
  1520: {
  1521:     u64 relocation = relocation_offset + (u64)import_index * ELF_RELOCATION_SIZE;
  1522:     link_write_u64(bytes, relocation + 8, ((u64)(import_index + 1) << 32) | 1026);
  1523: ```
--- lines 1728-2120 ---
  1728: 
  1729: ```sh
  1730: ./build.sh build --config Release -t ide
  1731: build/Release/ide cc -c x.c -o x.o && objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn x.o
  1732: ```
  1733: 
  1734: `ud2` immediately after the `call` means buster saw the `noreturn`. `mov $0x0,%eax` before the `ud2` means it did not — that trailing `ud2` is the ordinary falls-off-the-end terminator, not the noreturn one. Cross-check with `clang -c -Wreturn-type`: no `-Wreturn-type` warning means clang treats the callee as noreturn.
  1735: 
  1736: ## Done when
  1737: 
  1738: `tests/basic_c_noreturn_call.c` (registered at `src/buster/tests/compiler/driver/driver_test.c:5288`) covers the multi-declarator shape — running to a normal exit rather than trapping — and both redeclaration shapes, and the driver suite is green.
  1739: 
  1740: ## Verified as working, do not regress
  1741: 
  1742: `_Noreturn` in any specifier position, leading and trailing `__attribute__((noreturn))` and `((__noreturn__))`, attribute lists carrying other attributes (`((cold, noreturn))`), `__declspec(noreturn)`, `<stdnoreturn.h>`'s `noreturn` macro, the name fallback for `abort`/`__assert_fail`/`__assert_perror_fail`, and the resumes-after-call exemption in `c_gen.c:9652` that keeps `?:`, `&&`/`||`, loop and `if` conditions and statement expressions working.

  1746: ## forgejo#662 — c: a statement expression containing control flow yields 0 instead of its value
  1747: 
  1748: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/662
  1749: 
  1750: A GNU statement expression whose body contains a branching statement (`if`, `while`) evaluates to 0 instead of the value of its final expression statement. Silent — no diagnostic. Found 2026-08-29 at `40a87bd4`.
  1751: 
  1752: ```c
  1753: #include <stdio.h>
  1754: int a(int x) { return ({ if (x > 100) { x = 1; } 7; }); }
  1755: int b(int x) { int v = 0; v = ({ if (x > 100) { x = 1; } 7; }); return v; }
  1756: int c(int x) { return ({ if (x > 100) { x = 1; } 7; }) + 1; }
  1757: int d(int x) { printf("d=%d\n", ({ if (x > 100) { x = 1; } 7; })); return 0; }
  1758: int e(int x) { return ({ if (x > 100) { x = 1; } x + 6; }); }
  1759: int n(int x) { return ({ while (x > 100) { x = 1; } 7; }); }
  1760: int main(void) { printf("a=%d b=%d c=%d e=%d n=%d\n", a(1), b(1), c(1), e(1), n(1)); d(1); return 0; }
  1761: ```
  1762: 
  1763: buster prints `a=0 b=0 c=1 e=0 n=0` and `d=0`; clang prints `a=7 b=7 c=8 e=7 n=7` and `d=7`. Every context is affected: initializer, `return`, assignment, arithmetic operand, call argument.
  1764: 
  1765: A statement expression with no branching statement in it is correct — `({ x = x + 1; 7; })` yields 7 — so the value is being lost once the body's control flow opens new blocks: the result is read from the wrong block, or never wired to the block the final expression statement ends up in. Lowering is in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c`; start from the `C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_STATEMENT_EXPRESSION` frame and `statement_expression_mode` on the body frame.
  1766: 
  1767: ## Why it survived
  1768: 
  1769: The existing coverage, `c_test_statement_expression_control_call` and `c_test_statement_expression_nested_call` at `src/buster/tests/compiler/frontend/c/c_test.c:7248`, only exercises `(void)({ ... })`. The value is discarded in both, so a lost value is invisible.
  1770: 
  1771: ## Done when
  1772: 
  1773: The shapes above match clang, coverage exists for the value-producing case in each context (a runtime fixture diffed against clang is the strongest form), and `test_all` is green.
  1774: 
  1775: ## Related
  1776: 
  1777: A declaration inside a value-producing statement expression (`int v = ({ int t = x + 1; t; });`) fails with "use of undeclared identifier"; filed separately. The two may share a root cause — if this fix covers it, say so on that issue.
  1778:

  1809: ## forgejo#664 — c: the C23 [[...]] attribute syntax is not parsed at all
  1810: 
  1811: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/664
  1812: 
  1813: The C frontend does not support the C23 `[[...]]` attribute syntax at all. A declaration carrying one does not register, so the failure surfaces as an unrelated "undeclared identifier" later. Every `-std` mode behaves the same — `c17`, `c23`, `c2x`, `gnu23`. Found 2026-08-29 at `40a87bd4`.
  1814: 
  1815: ```c
  1816: [[noreturn]] void die(int);
  1817: int f(int x) { die(x); }
  1818: /* cc: error: use of undeclared identifier 'die'  -- the declaration never registered */
  1819: 
  1820: [[deprecated]] void die(int);                         /* same failure */
  1821: 
  1822: [[noreturn]] void die(int x) { while (1) { (void)x; } }
  1823: /* cc: error: use of undeclared identifier 'x'    -- on a definition too */
  1824: 
  1825: int f(int x) { [[maybe_unused]] int y = x; return y; }
  1826: /* cc: error: use of undeclared identifier 'maybe_unused'  -- statement position too */
  1827: ```
  1828: 
  1829: clang accepts all of these.
  1830: 
  1831: ## Scope
  1832: 
  1833: Parse and skip `[[...]]` attribute lists everywhere the standard allows them — declarations, declarators, statements — including the scoped `[[vendor::attr]]` form and the balanced-token argument form `[[attr(...)]]`. Honor at minimum `[[noreturn]]`: `c_ir_noreturn_marker_in_range` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:1043` already has a `[[` branch, which is dead code today because parsing fails before it can ever see one. Wire it up and prove it fires.
  1834: 
  1835: Attributes buster chooses not to act on should be skipped silently rather than rejected, matching how unknown names inside GNU `__attribute__` are already treated.
  1836: 
  1837: ## Oracle for `[[noreturn]]`
  1838: 
  1839: ```sh
  1840: ./build.sh build --config Release -t ide
  1841: build/Release/ide cc -c x.c -o x.o && objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn x.o
  1842: ```
  1843: 
  1844: `ud2` immediately after the `call` means the marker was seen; `mov $0x0,%eax` before the `ud2` means it was not (that trailing `ud2` is the ordinary falls-off-the-end terminator).
  1845: 
  1846: ## Done when

  1854: ## forgejo#665 — c: noreturn on a function pointer type or typedef is ignored
  1855: 
  1856: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/665
  1857: 
  1858: `noreturn` written on a function pointer type or typedef is ignored: only declarations are consulted, so a call through the pointer does not end control flow. Found 2026-08-29 at `40a87bd4`.
  1859: 
  1860: ```c
  1861: typedef __attribute__((noreturn)) void (*die_fn)(int);
  1862: int f(int x, die_fn p) { p(x); }
  1863: ```
  1864: 
  1865: buster emits `mov $0x0,%eax` then the falls-off-the-end `ud2`, i.e. the call is treated as returning. clang treats it as noreturn — `clang -c -Wreturn-type` does not warn on this function.
  1866: 
  1867: `c_ir_declaration_is_noreturn` (`src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:1116`) reads a `CDeclaration`; nothing carries the marker on a type, so the indirect call site at `c_ir_emit_call_target` (`c_gen.c:9743`) has nothing to consult. Carrying it would mean a bit on the function type rather than on the declaration.
  1868: 
  1869: Impact is dead code only — no wrong answers — which is why this is filed separately from the `noreturn` defects that do drop live code. A plain pointer type is correctly *not* treated as noreturn even when it is initialized from a noreturn function, which matches clang; only the spelled-on-the-type case is missing.
  1870: 
  1871: ## Done when
  1872: 
  1873: The shape above ends control flow at the indirect call, a fixture covers it alongside `tests/basic_c_noreturn_call.c` (registered at `src/buster/tests/compiler/driver/driver_test.c:5288`), and `test_all` is green.
  1874:
