  1878: 
  1879: ## forgejo#666 — c: calling an unprototyped function with arguments is refused as 'could not prepare C calls'
  1880: 
  1881: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/666
  1882: 
  1883: Calling an unprototyped function with at least one argument is refused when the translation unit has no definition to supply the parameters. Found 2026-08-29 at `40a87bd4`.
  1884: 
  1885: ```c
  1886: void die();
  1887: int f(int x) { die(x); return 0; }
  1888: /* cc: error: in function 'f': could not prepare C calls */
  1889: 
  1890: int die();
  1891: int f(int x) { return die(x); }        /* same */
  1892: 
  1893: void die();
  1894: int f(int x) { die(x, 2); return 0; }  /* same */
  1895: ```
  1896: 
  1897: clang compiles all three. Two neighbouring shapes already work, which brackets the gap:
  1898: 
  1899: ```c
  1900: void die(); int f(void) { die(); return 0; }                      /* ok: zero arguments */
  1901: void die(); void die(int x) { (void)x; } int f(int x){ die(x); return 0; }  /* ok: a later definition supplies the prototype */
  1902: ```
  1903: 
  1904: The second is the documented unprototyped-to-prototyped candidate replacement at `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c:7678`; the missing case is the one where no prototyped declaration ever appears, so the call must be lowered from the argument types alone (default argument promotions). The refusal is raised by call preparation in `c_gen.c`; `c_ir_signature_call_supported` and the arity check in `c_ir_emit_call_target` (`c_gen.c:9701`) are the places to start.
  1905: 
  1906: Note the dialect split: `()` means "unspecified parameters" through C17 and these must compile, but C23 makes `()` equivalent to `(void)`, where a call with arguments is a constraint violation. If the C23 behaviour is deliberate, the fix is still worth making — the diagnostic should then name the real problem instead of "could not prepare C calls", and the pre-C23 dialects should accept the call.
  1907: 
  1908: ## Done when
  1909: 
  1910: The three shapes above compile in the pre-C23 dialects and run correctly against clang's answers, C23 either accepts them or refuses them with an accurate diagnostic, coverage lands in `src/buster/tests/compiler/frontend/c/c_test.c`, and `test_all` is green.
  1911: 
  1912: ---
  1913: 
  1914: ## forgejo#673 — c: noreturn on a struct member declarator is ignored
  1915: 
  1916: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/673
  1917: 
  1918: `noreturn` written on a struct or union member declarator is ignored: a call
  1919: through the member does not end control flow. Found 2026-08-29 while fixing
  1920: #665, which covered the same marker on a typedef, a plain function-pointer
  1921: declarator, and a parameter declarator.
  1922: 
  1923: ```c
  1924: extern int sink;
  1925: struct ops { __attribute__((noreturn)) void (*fail)(int); };
  1926: void member_case(int x, struct ops* o) { o->fail(x); sink = 5; }
  1927: ```
  1928: 
  1929: buster emits the store to `sink`; clang does not, and `clang -c -Wreturn-type`
  1930: does not warn on the non-void spelling `int member_case(int x, struct ops* o)
  1931: { o->fail(x); }`.
  1932: 
  1933: Impact is dead code only — no wrong answers — the same as #665.
  1934: 
  1935: ## Where the mechanism already is
  1936: 
  1937: PR 672 carries the marker on the function type: the parser notes the function
  1938: type ids a declarator spelled it on into
  1939: `CParseResult.noreturn_function_types`, `c_parse_type_is_noreturn` answers for
  1940: one id, the C-to-IR type mapping copies the answer onto `IrType.is_noreturn`,
  1941: and `c_ir_emit_prepared_call_step` reads it through the signature it builds
  1942: from the pointed-to function type. Adding members means one more note site;
  1943: nothing downstream changes.
  1944: 
  1945: The three existing sites are `c_parse_declaration_type` (the wrapper around
  1946: `c_parse_declaration_type_derive`), the declarator segment loop in
  1947: `c_parse_local_declarations`, and `c_parse_parameter_segment`. Each captures
  1948: `result->type_count` before its declarator runs, calls
  1949: `c_parse_noreturn_candidate_function_type`, and only then scans tokens for the
  1950: marker.
  1951: 
  1952: Members are built instead inside the type-parse machine's member frame, around
  1953: `result->members[result->member_count++] = (CMember){...}` in `c_parse.c`,
  1954: which is why they were left out rather than grown into that change.
  1955: 
  1956: ## Constraints paid for already
  1957: 
  1958: - **Only a type the declarator itself built may be noted.** A declarator that
  1959:   merely names an existing function type — `__attribute__((noreturn)) handler
  1960:   fail;` over a shared `typedef void handler(int);` — must not mark the
  1961:   typedef, or every other call written with it ends control flow and the live
  1962:   code after those calls is deleted. The member frame's `frame->checkpoint`
  1963:   is taken per member *declaration*, so `frame->checkpoint.type_count` is a
  1964:   sound lower bound for this guard; a per-declarator bound would be tighter
  1965:   but is not required for correctness.
  1966: - **The marker's token range must not span sibling declarators.** Scan the
  1967:   shared specifiers and this declarator separately, never the span between
  1968:   them, or a preceding declarator's own trailing attribute is read as this
  1969:   one's. `c_ir_declaration_is_noreturn` and the block-scope site both do this.
  1970: - Do **not** treat a plain member pointer initialized or assigned from a
  1971:   noreturn function as noreturn; clang does not, and #665 says so explicitly.
  1972: 
  1973: ## Done when
  1974: 
  1975: The shape above ends control flow at the indirect call, the member case joins
  1976: `tests/basic_c_noreturn_type.c` under the same `-S` assertion the driver test
  1977: already runs (`must_not_be_reached` must appear nowhere in the assembly;
  1978: registered near `src/buster/tests/compiler/driver/driver_test.c:5350`), and
  1979: `test_all` is green.
  1980: 
  1981: Oracle: `build/Release/ide cc -S -target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu x.c -o x.s`
  1982: and grep for the callee that must not be reached; `clang -c -Wreturn-type` on
  1983: the non-void spelling is the semantic oracle.
  1984: 
  1985: Watch the cost: the note sites run per declarator, and PR 672 measured its
  1986: three at +2 321 528 instructions (+0,0225%) on a fixed `ide.c` compile. A
  1987: member site that scans tokens before proving a function type was derived would
  1988: cost more than that on its own.
  1989: 
  1990: ---
  1991: 
  1992: ## forgejo#678 — c: an attribute list on a member declarator drops the whole aggregate body
  1993: 
  1994: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/678
  1995: 
  1996: A member declarator cannot carry an attribute list of its own. Two shapes are
  1997: rejected, and the whole aggregate body is dropped rather than the attribute
  1998: being ignored: the struct ends up with zero members, so the first error a user
  1999: sees blames an unrelated member access.
  2000: 
  2001: Found 2026-08-29 while fixing #673, which needed only the shared-specifier
  2002: spelling and so did not depend on either of these. `noreturn` is not involved
  2003: — any attribute reproduces both.
  2004: 
  2005: ## The two shapes
  2006: 
  2007: A trailing attribute list on a **parenthesized** member declarator:
  2008: 
  2009: ```c
  2010: struct s { void (*f)(int) __attribute__((aligned(8))); };
  2011: int g(struct s* o) { o->f(1); return 1; }
  2012: // buster: type 's' has no member named 'f' (0 fields available)
  2013: // clang:  accepted
  2014: ```
  2015: 
  2016: A leading attribute list on a member declarator that is not the first of its
  2017: list:
  2018: 
  2019: ```c
  2020: struct s { int a, __attribute__((aligned(8))) b; };
  2021: int g(struct s* o) { return o->b; }
  2022: // buster: type 's' has no member named 'b' (0 fields available)
  2023: // clang:  accepted
  2024: ```
  2025: 
  2026: What already works, and bounds the gap: a trailing attribute on a plain,
  2027: pointer, or array member declarator (`int x __attribute__((aligned(8)));`,
  2028: `int *x ...`, `int x[2] ...`), and a leading attribute at the head of the
  2029: segment, which is the shared-specifier position (`__attribute__((packed)) int
  2030: x;`).
  2031: 
  2032: ## Where it is
  2033: 
  2034: Both live in `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step` in
  2035: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c`, in the declarator loop that
  2036: runs after `C_TYPE_PARSE_STAGE_FALLBACK`.
  2037: 
  2038: - The loop opens with `declarator = frame->declarator_start;` followed by
  2039:   `c_parse_pointer_chain`, with no `c_parse_skip_attributes` first. The
  2040:   segment head skips the leading attributes of the whole segment once, before
  2041:   the base type is parsed, so only the first declarator of the list is covered.
  2042: - The parenthesized path pushes a `C_TYPE_PARSE_FRAME_PARENTHESIZED` child
  2043:   with `end = frame->declarator_end`, which still spans the trailing attribute
  2044:   tokens, and the child requires the declarator to end exactly at `end`. The
  2045:   non-parenthesized path does not hit this because it calls
  2046:   `c_parse_skip_attributes` around its array suffixes.
  2047: 
  2048: Neither is a token-scan cost: an attribute list at either position is a
  2049: `c_parse_skip_attributes` call on a range the loop already walks.
  2050: 
  2051: ## Constraint
  2052: 
  2053: Whatever range the parenthesized child is given must not swallow the trailing
  2054: attributes of a *sibling*: `frame->declarator_end` is already the top-level
  2055: comma boundary, so trimming the trailing attribute list off the end before the
  2056: push keeps it inside this declarator.
  2057: 
  2058: ## Once it parses
  2059: 
  2060: `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step` already scans
  2061: `[frame->declarator_start, frame->declarator_end)` for the `noreturn` marker
  2062: alongside the shared specifiers (added by #673). That half of the scan finds
  2063: nothing today precisely because neither shape above parses; the moment they do,
  2064: `struct ops { void (*fail)(int) __attribute__((noreturn)), (*ok)(int); };`
  2065: should mark `fail` and leave `ok` alone. Adding that pair to
  2066: `tests/basic_c_noreturn_type.c` — the marked one calling `must_not_be_reached`,
  2067: the plain one falling through to a return the runtime half observes — is the
  2068: cheapest way to prove the sibling boundary holds.
  2069: 
  2070: ## Done when
  2071: 
  2072: Both shapes above compile and the attribute takes effect (an `aligned` member
  2073: moves the layout, which `sizeof`/`offsetof` observes), the member-list sibling
  2074: pair in `tests/basic_c_noreturn_type.c` marks only its own declarator, and
  2075: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` is green.
  2076: 
  2077: Oracles: `clang -fsyntax-only` for acceptance, and a `sizeof`/`offsetof` probe
  2078: compared against clang for the layout half.
  2079: 
  2080: ---
  2081: 
  2082: ## forgejo#679 — c: a [static N] array parameter makes the function's definition a LOCAL symbol
  2083: 
  2084: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/679
  2085: 
  2086: ## What is wrong
  2087: 
  2088: A parameter declared with C99's `static` array bound makes the enclosing
  2089: function's **definition** come out as a `LOCAL` ELF symbol instead of `GLOBAL`.
  2090: `ide cc -c` exits 0 and prints nothing, so the gap is completely silent, and
  2091: when nothing in the same translation unit calls the function the now-internal
  2092: definition is dropped: the object comes out with no symbol and no `.text` at
  2093: all.
  2094: 
  2095: Verified on main `0dfd901d`, Release `ide`, x86_64-linux, 2026-08-29.
  2096: 
  2097: ```c
  2098: // r1.c -- LOCAL in buster, GLOBAL in clang
  2099: void f(char b[static 8], unsigned n);
  2100: void f(char *b, unsigned n) { b[0] = (char)n; }
  2101: ```
  2102: 
  2103: ```c
  2104: // r2.c -- absent from the object entirely
  2105: void g(char b[static 8], unsigned n) { g[0] = (char)n; }
  2106: ```
  2107: 
  2108: ```
  2109: $ ide cc -c -o r1.o r1.c && readelf -sW r1.o | grep -w f
  2110:      1: 0000000000000000    54 FUNC    LOCAL  DEFAULT    1 f
  2111: $ clang -c -o r1c.o r1.c && readelf -sW r1c.o | grep -w f
  2112:      3: 0000000000000000    24 FUNC    GLOBAL DEFAULT    2 f
  2113: 
  2114: $ ide cc -c -o r2.o r2.c && readelf -sW r2.o
  2115: Symbol table '.symtab' contains 1 entry:
  2116:    Num:    Value          Size Type    Bind   Vis      Ndx Name
  2117:      0: 0000000000000000     0 NOTYPE  LOCAL  DEFAULT  UND
  2118: ```
  2119: 
  2120: Plain `char b[8]` (no `static`) is fine and comes out `GLOBAL`. The `static`
--- lines 2166-2528 ---
  2166: hidden void __procfdname(char __buf[static 15+3*sizeof(int)], unsigned);
  2167: ```
  2168: 
  2169: The unit compiles, so the `test_musl` compile inventory never sees a problem,
  2170: but the symbol is `LOCAL` in `libc-buster.a` where Clang has it
  2171: `GLOBAL HIDDEN`. It is the rank-2 `LIBCTEST_BLOCKER`, wanted by 15 libc-test
  2172: units. This is the second time a linkability gap has been invisible from the
  2173: compile side; the first was the weak-alias work (PR 642).
  2174: 
  2175: ## How to validate a fix
  2176: 
  2177: ```sh
  2178: ./build.sh build --config Release -t ide
  2179: ./build/build test_musl --config Release ~/dev/musl-v1.2.6 ~/dev/libc-test
  2180: ```
  2181: 
  2182: `LIBCTEST_EXPECTED_PASSING` should move up from 79 and the rank-2 blocker
  2183: should disappear; rebaseline `LIBC_TEST_EXPECTED_PASSING` and
  2184: `LIBC_TEST_EXPECTED_STATE_HASH` in `build.c` deliberately -- the harness
  2185: prints the new values. `MUSL_EXPECTED_COMPILED_UNITS` must **not** move: this
  2186: is a link-side gap, not a compile-side one, and a moving compile count would
  2187: mean the change did something else as well.
  2188: 
  2189: A census against a harness run directory (`build/musl-v1.2.6-<pid>/`) catches
  2190: any siblings:
  2191: 
  2192: ```sh
  2193: readelf -sW libc-clang.a  | awk '$5=="GLOBAL" && $6=="HIDDEN" && $7!="UND" {print $8}' | sort -u > ch.txt
  2194: readelf -sW libc-buster.a | awk '($5=="GLOBAL"||$5=="WEAK") && $7!="UND" {print $8}' | sort -u > bg.txt
  2195: comm -23 ch.txt bg.txt
  2196: ```
  2197: 
  2198: The `$7!="UND"` filter matters on both sides: counting undefined references as
  2199: definitions hides the bug.
  2200: 
  2201: ## Definition of done
  2202: 
  2203: - A `[static N]` parameter no longer changes the linkage of the function that
  2204:   declares it, in any of the four spellings above.
  2205: - A focused fixture under `tests/` pins that such a function is callable from
  2206:   another translation unit -- a single-TU fixture cannot see this, since the
  2207:   call inside the unit is exactly what keeps the internal definition alive.
  2208:   `ide test` never names `tests/basic_c_*` fixtures directly, so the wiring
  2209:   into `driver_test.c` has to be proved by deliberately breaking the assertion
  2210:   and confirming it fails.
  2211: - `test_all` and `test_musl` pass; the musl baselines are rebaselined in the
  2212:   same change, with the compile count unmoved.
  2213: 
  2214: ---
  2215: 
  2216: ## forgejo#680 — c: an `aligned` attribute on one member declarator aligns the whole segment
  2217: 
  2218: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/680
  2219: 
  2220: An `aligned` attribute written on one member declarator raises the alignment of
  2221: every member the segment declares, not just the declarator that carries it.
  2222: Found 2026-08-29 while fixing #678, which made two more member-declarator
  2223: attribute positions parse and so made the divergence reachable from three
  2224: spellings instead of one.
  2225: 
  2226: ```c
  2227: struct t1 { char c; int a, b __attribute__((aligned(32))); };
  2228: struct t2 { char c; int a __attribute__((aligned(32))), b; };
  2229: struct t3 { char c; __attribute__((aligned(32))) int a, b; };
  2230: // clang:  t1 size 64, a at 4,  b at 32
  2231: //         t2 size 64, a at 32, b at 36
  2232: //         t3 size 96, a at 32, b at 64
  2233: // buster: all three size 96, a at 32, b at 64
  2234: ```
  2235: 
  2236: `t3` is the shared-specifier spelling and is right: an attribute before the
  2237: declarators belongs to all of them. `t1` and `t2` are wrong -- buster reads a
  2238: declarator's own list as if it had been written in the shared position.
  2239: 
  2240: This is an ABI divergence, not a missed optimization: `sizeof` and the offset
  2241: of every following member move.
  2242: 
  2243: ## Where it is
  2244: 
  2245: `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step` in
  2246: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` pushes one
  2247: `C_TYPE_PARSE_FRAME_ALIGNMENT` child over the whole segment
  2248: `[frame->start, frame->end)`. That frame appends one `CAlignmentSpecifier` per
  2249: `_Alignas`/`aligned` word it finds anywhere in the range and hands back a
  2250: single `(alignment_start, alignment_count)` run, which every member row of the
  2251: segment then copies verbatim. The frame's scan uses `c_parse_alignment_word`,
  2252: which matches `aligned`/`__aligned__` inside a GNU attribute list as well as
  2253: `_Alignas`, so a declarator-position `aligned` lands in the shared run.
  2254: 
  2255: The records already carry `token_start`, so the segment step has what it needs
  2256: to partition the run: a record before `frame->shared_specifier_end` is shared,
  2257: one inside `[declarator_start, declarator_end)` belongs to that declarator
  2258: alone. The obstacle is that a member row names a *contiguous* run, and
  2259: "the shared ones plus this declarator's own" is not contiguous once a second
  2260: declarator carries a list. Re-appending a filtered run per member is the
  2261: obvious shape; it has to stay inside `alignment_capacity` and inside what
  2262: `c_type_parse_rollback` restores.
  2263: 
  2264: `packed` is deliberately segment-wide and must stay that way -- the comment
  2265: above the `c_parse_layout_attributes` call in the same function says so.
  2266: 
  2267: ## Done when
  2268: 
  2269: `t1` and `t2` above compute clang's numbers, `t3` is unchanged,
  2270: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains all three, and
  2271: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` is green.
  2272: 
  2273: Oracle: `sizeof`/`offsetof` compared against clang.
  2274: 
  2275: Note that `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` today asserts two shapes from #678
  2276: whose attributed declarator sits where the two readings happen to agree
  2277: (`struct list_declarator_aligned`, whose first member is at offset zero).
  2278: Those assertions stay correct under the fix; they are just not the ones that
  2279: would have caught this.
  2280: 
  2281: ---
  2282: 
  2283: ## forgejo#681 — c: an attribute list on a declarator is refused outside an aggregate body
  2284: 
  2285: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/681
  2286: 
  2287: #678 fixed two attribute-list positions for *member* declarators. The same two
  2288: shapes are still refused outside an aggregate body, at file scope and at block
  2289: scope, by different code. Found 2026-08-29 while fixing #678, which did not
  2290: depend on either.
  2291: 
  2292: ```c
  2293: // 1. trailing list on a parenthesized declarator -- file scope
  2294: void (*fp)(int) __attribute__((aligned(64)));
  2295: int g(void) { fp(1); return 1; }
  2296: // buster: use of undeclared identifier 'fp'
  2297: // clang:  accepted
  2298: 
  2299: // 2. the same at block scope
  2300: int g(void) { void (*fp)(int) __attribute__((aligned(64))) = 0; (void)fp; return 1; }
  2301: // buster: use of undeclared identifier 'fp'
  2302: // clang:  accepted
  2303: 
  2304: // 3. leading list on a declarator that is not the first of its list -- block scope
  2305: int g(void) { int a = 1, __attribute__((aligned(8))) b = 2; return a + b; }
  2306: // buster: use of undeclared identifier 'aligned'
  2307: // clang:  accepted
  2308: ```
  2309: 
  2310: The same leading-list spelling at file scope (`int a, __attribute__((aligned(64))) b;`)
  2311: already works, which bounds shape 3 to the block-scope declarator loop.
  2312: 
  2313: Impact is a refused translation unit, not a wrong answer.
  2314: 
  2315: ## Where it is
  2316: 
  2317: Shapes 1 and 2 are the file-scope and block-scope halves of what #678 fixed
  2318: inside `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step`: a
  2319: `C_TYPE_PARSE_FRAME_PARENTHESIZED` child is handed a range that still spans the
  2320: trailing attribute tokens, and the child requires the declarator to end exactly
  2321: at the range it is given. Both sites call
  2322: `c_parse_parenthesized_declaration_type` in
  2323: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` -- around line 8777 for file
  2324: scope, bounded by `c_parse_declarator_segment_end`, and around line 10994 for
  2325: block scope, bounded by its own `suffix_end`. #678 added
  2326: `c_parse_trailing_attribute_start`, which is exactly the trim these two need
  2327: before the call; the member site is the worked example.
  2328: 
  2329: Shape 3 is the block-scope declarator loop failing to skip a leading attribute
  2330: list on a declarator after a comma, the same omission #678 fixed in the
  2331: aggregate segment loop.
  2332: 
  2333: ## Constraint
  2334: 
  2335: The same one #678 records: whatever range is trimmed must not swallow a
  2336: *sibling* declarator's trailing list. Both call sites already bound the range
  2337: at the top-level comma, so trimming inside that bound keeps the list with the
  2338: declarator that wrote it.
  2339: 
  2340: ## Done when
  2341: 
  2342: All three shapes above compile and the attribute takes effect,
  2343: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains them beside the member shapes #678 put
  2344: there, and `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` is green.
  2345: 
  2346: Oracles: `clang -fsyntax-only` for acceptance, `sizeof`/`_Alignof` and the
  2347: object's address modulo its alignment compared against clang for the effect.

  2350: 
  2351: ## forgejo#688 — c: a packed attribute on one member declarator packs the whole segment
  2352: 
  2353: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/688
  2354: 
  2355: A `packed` attribute written on one member declarator packs every member the
  2356: segment declares, not just the declarator that carries it. Found 2026-08-29
  2357: while fixing #680 (PR 687), which fixed the same divergence for `aligned` and
  2358: deliberately left this one alone -- the comment above the
  2359: `c_parse_layout_attributes` call says `packed` is segment-wide on purpose, and
  2360: that is what needs revisiting rather than a bug hiding behind it.
  2361: 
  2362: ```c
  2363: struct u6 { char c; int a __attribute__((packed)), b; };
  2364: struct u9 { char c; int a, b __attribute__((packed)); };
  2365: // clang and gcc:  u6 size 12, a at 1, b at 8
  2366: //                 u9 size 12, a at 4, b at 8
  2367: // buster:         u6 size  9, a at 1, b at 5
  2368: //                 u9 size  9, a at 1, b at 5
  2369: ```
  2370: 
  2371: Both reference compilers agree, so this is an ABI divergence rather than a
  2372: dialect question: `sizeof` and the offset of every following member move. Note
  2373: `u9`, where buster packs `a` because a *later* declarator asked -- the attribute
  2374: reaches backwards.
  2375: 
  2376: ## Where it is
  2377: 
  2378: `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step` in
  2379: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` calls `c_parse_layout_attributes`
  2380: once over `[frame->start, frame->end)` at `C_TYPE_PARSE_STAGE_BEGIN` and stores
  2381: the answer in `frame->is_packed`, which every member row of the segment copies
  2382: into `CMember.is_packed`.
  2383: 
  2384: PR 687 solved the identical partition for the alignment run and left the shape
  2385: to copy: the segment frame knows `frame->shared_specifier_end` and each
  2386: declarator's `[declarator_start, declarator_end)`, so `packed` is this member's
  2387: when the attribute sits before the shared end or inside this declarator's own
  2388: range. `packed` is a single bool rather than a run, so it needs none of the
  2389: re-appending `c_parse_member_alignment_run` does -- two scans, one over the
  2390: shared range and one over the declarator, OR'd together, is the whole change,
  2391: and it is the same two-range split `c_ir_declaration_is_noreturn` and the
  2392: `noreturn` member scan already use. Watch the ordering the existing comment
  2393: protects: the `packed` scan runs before the alignment child frame appends so
  2394: that the alignment run stays contiguous, and per-declarator scans must not
  2395: break that.
  2396: 
  2397: Note that the aggregate-wide spellings -- `struct __attribute__((packed)) P`
  2398: and `struct P { ... } __attribute__((packed))` -- are a different path
  2399: (`c_parse_aggregate_attributes`) and stay as they are.
  2400: 
  2401: ## Done when
  2402: 
  2403: Both shapes above compute clang's numbers, the aggregate-wide and
  2404: `#pragma pack` shapes in `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` are unchanged, that
  2405: fixture gains both, and `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  2406: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green.
  2407: 
  2408: Oracle: `sizeof`/`offsetof` compared against clang.

  2411: 
  2412: ## forgejo#689 — c: an aligned(N) below the natural alignment is rejected instead of ignored
  2413: 
  2414: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/689
  2415: 
  2416: A GNU `aligned(N)` whose N is below the natural alignment of what it is written
  2417: on is rejected rather than ignored. GCC's `aligned` only ever *raises*
  2418: alignment -- lowering it needs `packed` as well -- so a request the type already
  2419: satisfies is a no-op for both reference compilers. Buster treats it as a hard
  2420: failure, and the failure is silent where it matters most. Found 2026-08-29 while
  2421: fixing #680 (PR 687), by an oracle probe that used `aligned(2)` on an `int` as a
  2422: harmless shared record; measured on `main` at 5e04db07 and unchanged by that PR.
  2423: 
  2424: ```c
  2425: struct s1 { char c; __attribute__((aligned(2))) int a; };
  2426: struct s2 { char c; int a __attribute__((aligned(2))); };
  2427: int g __attribute__((aligned(2)));
  2428: ```
  2429: 
  2430: - `sizeof(struct s1)` and `sizeof(struct s2)` fold to **4**. clang and gcc say
  2431:   8, with `a` at offset 4. No diagnostic is issued; the wrong number is simply
  2432:   handed to the program.
  2433: - `_Alignof(struct s1)` fails to lower:
  2434:   `in function 'main': could not lower logical expression core`.
  2435: - Defining an object of the type fails with an internal message:
  2436:   `C IR lowering cannot resolve definition 'g1' with C type 577 (kind 28) and IR
  2437:   type 32`.
  2438: - The object declarator `int g __attribute__((aligned(2)));` is rejected with
  2439:   `invalid object alignment`. clang and gcc accept it.
  2440: 
  2441: The silent `sizeof` is the serious one: a header that writes `aligned(2)` on
  2442: something already 4- or 8-aligned -- which is ordinary defensive style -- gets a
  2443: wrong layout with no warning.
  2444: 
  2445: ## Where it is
  2446: 
  2447: Two engines evaluate the same records and are documented as having to agree:
  2448: 
  2449: - `c_ir_alignment_evaluate` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c`
  2450:   answers false when `requested < natural_alignment`, alongside the genuine
  2451:   rejections (not a power of two, wider than `UINT32_MAX`).
  2452: - `c_parse_layout_alignment_specifiers` in
  2453:   `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` does the same for the `sizeof`
  2454:   folding, and its header comment states the rule it implements.
  2455: 
  2456: Both already compute `BUSTER_MAX(alignment, requested)`, so ignoring a small
  2457: request is what the max does on its own once the rejection is dropped -- the
  2458: work is deciding *which* spelling may be ignored, not the arithmetic.
  2459: 
  2460: `_Alignas` is not the same question and must not be folded into the same
  2461: answer. C requires the alignment of a declaration to be at least the natural
  2462: one, and clang rejects `_Alignas(2) int` with *requested alignment is less than
  2463: minimum alignment of 4 for type 'int'*. So the record needs to carry which
  2464: spelling produced it -- `CAlignmentSpecifier` has no such bit today, and
  2465: `c_parse_alignment_word` matches `_Alignas`, `aligned`, `__aligned` and
  2466: `__aligned__` through one predicate -- and a below-natural `_Alignas` should
  2467: become a diagnostic (`C_DIAGNOSTIC_INVALID_ALIGNMENT`) rather than the
  2468: layout-resolution failure it is now. Note that the aggregate-attribute path
  2469: (`c_parse_aggregate_attributes`) and the object-declarator path reach the same
  2470: two evaluators, so all four spellings above are one fix.
  2471: 
  2472: Whatever the resolution, the failure mode has to change: a rejected specifier
  2473: currently makes a layout unresolvable, and every symptom above is a different
  2474: component's way of reporting that it never got a layout. None of them names the
  2475: attribute.
  2476: 
  2477: ## Done when
  2478: 
  2479: The four shapes above compute clang's numbers (8, 8, offset 4, and an accepted
  2480: object), `_Alignas(2) int` is diagnosed by name rather than failing to lower,
  2481: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains the member and object shapes,
  2482: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  2483: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green.
  2484: 
  2485: Oracle: `sizeof`/`offsetof` compared against clang, plus clang's own diagnostic
  2486: for the `_Alignas` half.
  2487: 
  2488: ---
  2489: 
  2490: ## forgejo#691 — driver: -D NAME= defines NAME as 1 rather than as empty
  2491: 
  2492: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/691
  2493: 
  2494: `ide cc -D NAME=` -- a `-D` whose value is empty -- defines `NAME` as `1` instead of
  2495: as nothing.  Clang and GCC both define it as an empty replacement list; only a `-D`
  2496: with no `=` at all means `1`.
  2497: 
  2498: ## Repro
  2499: 
  2500: ```c
  2501: // dtest.c
  2502: int probe = 0 EMPTY;
  2503: ```
  2504: 
  2505: ```
  2506: $ ide cc -E -DEMPTY= dtest.c
  2507: int probe = 0 1 ;
  2508: 
  2509: $ clang -E -DEMPTY= dtest.c
  2510: int probe = 0 ;
  2511: 
  2512: $ gcc -E -DEMPTY= dtest.c
  2513: int probe = 0 ;
  2514: ```
  2515: 
  2516: The no-`=` form agrees with the other two (`-DEMPTY` gives `1` everywhere), and a
  2517: non-empty value is passed through correctly (`-DEMPTY=7` gives `7`), so the fault
  2518: is specifically the empty right-hand side falling back to the no-value default.
  2519: 
  2520: ## Impact
  2521: 
  2522: `-DNAME=` is the idiomatic way to compile a source twice with a decoration switched
  2523: off -- `-DATTR='__attribute__((aligned(64)))'` versus `-DATTR=` -- and every such
  2524: build fails with a syntax error at the expansion site rather than compiling the
  2525: plain form.  A configure-style probe that spells `-DHAVE_X=` also silently becomes
  2526: `-DHAVE_X=1`, which is a wrong answer rather than a refusal.
  2527: 
  2528: Found 2026-08-29 while building a negative control for #681, which did not depend
--- lines 2543-2917 ---
  2543: 
  2544: ```c
  2545: #include <stdio.h>
  2546: struct s { char c; int b : 5 __attribute__((packed)); char t; };
  2547: int main(void) { printf("%zu\n", _Alignof(struct s)); return 0; }
  2548: ```
  2549: 
  2550: ```text
  2551: cc: error: n.c:3:18: in function 'main': could not lower logical expression core
  2552: ```
  2553: 
  2554: `offsetof(struct s, t)` on the same declaration reports
  2555: `invalid __builtin_offsetof type or member designator`, while
  2556: `sizeof(struct s)` folds and is correct. clang and gcc both accept the
  2557: declaration -- clang gives size 4, alignment 4, `t` at 2 -- and clang requires
  2558: this spelling: the attribute has to follow the width, `int b
  2559: __attribute__((packed)) : 5` is a syntax error there.
  2560: 
  2561: ## Where it is
  2562: 
  2563: `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step` in
  2564: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c`. When it sees the `:` it takes
  2565: everything to `frame->declarator_end` as the width:
  2566: 
  2567: ```c
  2568: bit_width_token_start = declarator;
  2569: bit_width_token_count = frame->declarator_end - declarator;
  2570: ```
  2571: 
  2572: so the attribute's tokens are part of the width expression. The
  2573: `bit_width_token_count == 1 && ... C_TOKEN_PREPROCESSING_NUMBER` fast path
  2574: that folds a plain literal therefore does not fire, `bit_width` stays 0, and
  2575: the token-range evaluation that runs later fails on the attribute tokens. The
  2576: fix is presumably to trim the trailing attribute list off the width range the
  2577: way the parenthesized declarator already trims one with
  2578: `c_parse_trailing_attribute_start`, and to let the trimmed tokens reach the
  2579: member's `packed`/`aligned` scans -- `packed` on a bit-field is meaningful and
  2580: already has an implementation, and `aligned` on one is already diagnosed.
  2581: 
  2582: ## Done when
  2583: 
  2584: The declaration above computes clang's size, alignment and offset, a `packed`
  2585: written there packs the field, an `aligned` written there is diagnosed the way
  2586: one on a plain bit-field declarator already is, and
  2587: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains the shape. `./build.sh build --config
  2588: Release -t test_all` and `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` green.
  2589: 
  2590: Oracle: `sizeof`/`_Alignof`/`offsetof` compared against clang.
  2591:

  2593: 
  2594: ## forgejo#696 — c: an aligned attribute on a typedef is dropped
  2595: 
  2596: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/696
  2597: 
  2598: An `aligned(N)` attribute written on a typedef is parsed and dropped: the
  2599: name it declares keeps the alignment of the type it aliases, in both
  2600: directions, with no diagnostic. GCC and Clang both give the alias the
  2601: requested alignment, and for a typedef they honour it *below* the natural one
  2602: as well -- which is the one place `aligned` lowers without `packed`, because
  2603: it is setting the alignment of a type rather than raising a declaration's.
  2604: Found 2026-08-29 while fixing #689 (PR 695); measured on `main` at `c5c4ccf6`
  2605: and unchanged by that PR.
  2606: 
  2607: ```c
  2608: typedef int raised __attribute__((aligned(16)));
  2609: typedef int lowered __attribute__((aligned(2)));
  2610: struct r { char c; raised a; };
  2611: struct l { char c; lowered a; };
  2612: char probe_size_r[sizeof(struct r)];
  2613: char probe_align_r[_Alignof(struct r)];
  2614: char probe_size_l[sizeof(struct l)];
  2615: char probe_align_raised[_Alignof(raised)];
  2616: ```
  2617: 
  2618: | probe | clang | gcc | buster |
  2619: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  2620: | `sizeof(struct r)` | 32 | 32 | 8 |
  2621: | `_Alignof(struct r)` | 16 | 16 | 4 |
  2622: | `sizeof(struct l)` | 6 | 6 | 8 |
  2623: | `_Alignof(raised)` | 16 | 16 | 4 |
  2624: 
  2625: Silent in every row, which is the same failure mode #689 had before the fix:
  2626: a header that hands out an aligned scalar type through a typedef -- the
  2627: ordinary spelling for a SIMD-aligned or cache-line-aligned scalar -- gets a
  2628: smaller alignment than it asked for, and an object of that type is
  2629: underaligned rather than diagnosed.
  2630: 
  2631: ## Where it is
  2632: 
  2633: The specifier-position spelling is rejected by name already:
  2634: `c_parse_declaration_type_derive` (and `c_parse_local_declarations` for a
  2635: block-scope one) reports *alignment specifier cannot be applied to a typedef*
  2636: for `_Alignas(16) typedef int T;`, which is the C rule -- `_Alignas` may not
  2637: appear in a typedef declaration. The GNU attribute after the declarator is
  2638: the different question, and it reaches `c_parse_layout_attributes`, which
  2639: appends the record to the *declaration*; `declaration->alignment_count` is
  2640: then cleared for a `C_DECLARATION_TYPEDEF` beside that same diagnostic, so
  2641: nothing carries the request to the type the typedef names, and neither layout engine ever sees it: `CType` has no
  2642: alignment of its own, and both `c_ir_alignment_evaluate` and
  2643: `c_parse_layout_alignment_specifiers` read alignment runs off members,
  2644: declarations and aggregate attributes only.
  2645: 
  2646: So the fix is not in the evaluators -- they already compute
  2647: `BUSTER_MAX(alignment, requested)` over whatever run they are handed, and
  2648: after #689 they agree on which requests may be ignored. What is missing is a
  2649: place for a *type* to carry a requested alignment, and the rule that this one
  2650: replaces the natural alignment rather than raising it. The `noreturn` side
  2651: table added in #672 and the packed/aligned side table in #674 are the shape
  2652: this would follow: the population is a handful of typedefs per translation
  2653: unit against a type table of tens of thousands of entries.
  2654: 
  2655: Worth checking in the same change: `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` on a struct
  2656: tag used as a type name, and whether an object declared with the aligned
  2657: typedef gets the alignment as well as the aggregates that embed it.
  2658: 
  2659: ## Done when
  2660: 
  2661: The four probes above compute clang's numbers, an object declared with an
  2662: aligned typedef is placed at the typedef's alignment,
  2663: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains the typedef shape in both directions,
  2664: and `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  2665: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green. Oracle:
  2666: `sizeof`/`offsetof`/`_Alignof` against clang, which gcc agrees with on every
  2667: row above.
  2668:

  2670: 
  2671: ## forgejo#697 — c: a packed bit-field narrower than its declared type is refused instead of read through a narrower unit
  2672: 
  2673: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/697
  2674: 
  2675: A packed bit-field is always read through a whole storage unit of its declared
  2676: type. When the aggregate is smaller than that type the unit hangs off the end
  2677: of the object, there is nowhere to slide it to, and the declaration is refused
  2678: rather than laid out. clang and gcc read the field through a narrower unit and
  2679: lay the object out fine, so this is a refusal on a declaration both reference
  2680: compilers accept.
  2681: 
  2682: ```c
  2683: struct s { char c; int b : 5 __attribute__((packed)); char t; };
  2684: int main(void) { return (int)sizeof(struct s); }
  2685: ```
  2686: 
  2687: ```text
  2688: cc: error: n.c:1:24: packed bit-field 'b' straddles every storage unit of its declared type
  2689: ```
  2690: 
  2691: clang and gcc both give size 3, alignment 1, `t` at offset 2. All three
  2692: spellings of the same layout reproduce it identically -- the attribute after
  2693: the width, the shared-specifier `__attribute__((packed)) int b : 5`, and
  2694: `struct __attribute__((packed))` on the aggregate -- so it is a lowering gap
  2695: rather than a parsing one, and it is pre-existing: it reproduces on a compiler
  2696: built before the change that closed #693, which is what turned the first spelling
  2697: from a parse failure into this one.
  2698: 
  2699: ## Where it is
  2700: 
  2701: The slide loop at the end of the aggregate case of `c_ir_lower`, in
  2702: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c` (search for the diagnostic's
  2703: text). Every packed bit-field whose unit does not already lie inside the
  2704: aggregate is slid back until it does, and the loop reports when it cannot:
  2705: 
  2706: ```c
  2707: if (size < unit || lowest > highest)
  2708: ```
  2709: 
  2710: For the declaration above the aggregate is three bytes and the declared type is
  2711: four, so no position for a four-byte unit exists and the whole definition is
  2712: refused. PR 674 introduced the slide deliberately -- a read-modify-write
  2713: through a unit that reaches past the object clobbers whatever follows it -- and
  2714: left this case diagnosed rather than silently wrong.
  2715: 
  2716: ## What it would take
  2717: 
  2718: The access unit is the declared type's size everywhere, because a bit-field
  2719: member access emits a load and a store through the member's declared IR type at
  2720: `field->offset`; `IrField` carries no separate access width. clang picks the
  2721: narrowest unit that covers the field's bits and fits inside the object. Adding
  2722: that means an access-size field on `IrField` chosen by the same loop, plus the
  2723: five places that read a bit-field through its declared type:
  2724: 
  2725: - the runtime extraction in `c_ir_emit_load_place` (the shift/mask pair already
  2726:   promotes to 32 bits, so it only needs the raw load narrowed),
  2727: - the read-modify-write in `c_ir_emit_store_place`,
  2728: - the two constant-storage folds that OR a value in at `task.bit_offset`,
  2729: - the two designator initializer folds, which also bound `bit_offset` by
  2730:   `child->layout.size * 8`.
  2731: 
  2732: A narrower unit does not remove the refusal entirely -- a field spanning three
  2733: bytes at the very end of a three-byte object still has no power-of-two unit --
  2734: so the diagnostic and its test stay, over a shape that genuinely has none.
  2735: 
  2736: ## Done when
  2737: 
  2738: The declaration above computes clang's size, alignment and offset, its fields
  2739: round-trip values, the shared-specifier and aggregate-level spellings of the
  2740: same layout do too, and the `straddling` case in `c_test_packed_and_aligned_layout`
  2741: still reports for a shape with no unit at all.
  2742: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` and
  2743: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` green.
  2744: 
  2745: Oracle: `sizeof`/`_Alignof`/`offsetof` and value round-trips compared against
  2746: clang, which `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` already compiles cleanly under.
  2747: 
  2748: ---
  2749: 
  2750: ## forgejo#701 — c: an aligned attribute on one object declarator raises the whole list
  2751: 
  2752: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/701
  2753: 
  2754: An `aligned(N)` written on one declarator of an object declarator list is read
  2755: as the whole declaration's: every name in the list gets the alignment, not just
  2756: the one that carries the attribute. GCC and Clang both give it to that
  2757: declarator alone. Found 2026-08-29 while fixing #696 (PR pending); measured on
  2758: `main` at `6996a76b`.
  2759: 
  2760: ```c
  2761: int c __attribute__((aligned(64))), d;
  2762: int main(void) { return (unsigned long)&d % 64 == 0; }
  2763: ```
  2764: 
  2765: | probe | clang | gcc | buster |
  2766: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  2767: | `&c % 64` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  2768: | `&d % 64` | non-zero | non-zero | 0 |
  2769: 
  2770: The typedef spelling of the same list is worse than silent -- it drops the
  2771: whole declaration:
  2772: 
  2773: ```c
  2774: typedef int a16 __attribute__((aligned(16))), plain_after;
  2775: ```
  2776: 
  2777: > error: alignment specifier cannot be applied to a typedef
  2778: 
  2779: Both halves have one cause. `c_parse_declaration_type_derive` scans
  2780: `[declaration->token_start, name_index)` for the declaration's alignment
  2781: specifiers, and for a declarator that is not the first of its list that range
  2782: covers the *previous* declarators, their own attribute lists included. So the
  2783: second declarator inherits the first one's `aligned`, and in the typedef case
  2784: it inherits it into the specifier-position run that
  2785: `alignment specifier cannot be applied to a typedef` rejects by name -- the
  2786: diagnostic is right about the run it is handed and wrong about where the
  2787: attribute was written.
  2788: 
  2789: ## Where it is
  2790: 
  2791: This is the object-declarator sibling of #680, which fixed exactly this for a
  2792: struct member: `c_type_parse_aggregate_segment_step` pushes one alignment frame
  2793: over a whole segment, and `c_parse_member_alignment_run` partitions the run by
  2794: `CAlignmentSpecifier.token_start` against the frame's `shared_specifier_end`
  2795: and each `[declarator_start, declarator_end)`. The shape to copy is that
  2796: partition; what is missing at file scope is the equivalent of
  2797: `shared_specifier_end`, which the derivation already knows -- the first
  2798: declarator's start -- but does not use to bound the specifier scan.
  2799: 
  2800: The block-scope path in `c_parse_local_declarations` bounds its specifier scan
  2801: at `declarator_start` already and scans each segment separately, so only the
  2802: file-scope path is wrong; a fix should keep them agreeing.
  2803: 
  2804: Worth checking in the same change: whether the *shared*-specifier spelling
  2805: (`__attribute__((aligned(64))) int c, d;`) still reaches every declarator after
  2806: the partition, which is the one case where it must, and whether the same
  2807: range is what `packed` and `noreturn` read at file scope.
  2808: 
  2809: ## Done when
  2810: 
  2811: `&d` is not 64-byte aligned while `&c` is, the typedef list above compiles and
  2812: gives `a16` alone the alignment, `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains both
  2813: shapes, and `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  2814: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green. Oracle: object
  2815: addresses and `_Alignof` against clang, which gcc agrees with.
  2816:

  2818: 
  2819: ## forgejo#703 — c: an array of an over-aligned element type is accepted instead of diagnosed
  2820: 
  2821: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/703
  2822: 
  2823: An array whose element alignment exceeds its element size is accepted and laid
  2824: out; GCC and Clang both refuse it. The shape became reachable with #696, which
  2825: gave a typedef an alignment of its own: before it, no scalar type in the
  2826: frontend could be aligned above its own size.
  2827: 
  2828: ```c
  2829: typedef int cache_line __attribute__((aligned(64)));
  2830: typedef cache_line cache_array[2];
  2831: ```
  2832: 
  2833: | compiler | answer |
  2834: | --- | --- |
  2835: | clang | error: size of array element of type 'cache_line' (aka 'int') (4 bytes) isn't a multiple of its alignment (64 bytes) |
  2836: | gcc | error: alignment of array elements is greater than element size |
  2837: | buster | accepted; `sizeof` 8, `_Alignof` 64 |
  2838: 
  2839: Eight bytes is the honest product of the element size and the count, and it is
  2840: also why the shape has to be refused rather than laid out: the second element
  2841: starts four bytes in, at an address the element type says it may not occupy, so
  2842: every access through `a[1]` is misaligned for the type that reaches it. The
  2843: same declaration through an object declarator (`cache_line a[2];`) and through
  2844: a struct member has the same problem.
  2845: 
  2846: ## Where it is
  2847: 
  2848: The array type is built by `c_parse_array_suffixes`, which knows nothing about
  2849: layouts, so the check belongs to whoever does: `c_parse_type_layout` in
  2850: `c_parse.c` folds the size and `c_lower_to_ir` in `c_gen.c` builds the
  2851: `IrType`. `c_parse_type_layout` is the awkward one -- it is a query, it runs
  2852: inside speculative parses that get rolled back, and a diagnostic raised there
  2853: would be reported for a declarator the parse later abandons. The IR mapping
  2854: runs once over a settled type table and already has the element layout in hand
  2855: (the `C_TYPE_ARRAY` branch of the mapping pass), which makes it the cheaper
  2856: place to be right, at the cost of diagnosing a type only when something is
  2857: lowered through it.
  2858: 
  2859: Note that only a *lowered or raised scalar* can trip this: an aggregate padded
  2860: by `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` on its tag has its size rounded up to the
  2861: alignment, so `struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) s { char c; } a[2];` is
  2862: well-formed and thirty-two bytes. `CParseResult.type_alignments` names exactly
  2863: the types that can, which bounds the check.
  2864: 
  2865: ## Done when
  2866: 
  2867: Both spellings above are diagnosed by name -- naming the attribute, the element
  2868: size and the alignment, the way both reference compilers do -- the object and
  2869: member spellings are diagnosed too, aggregates whose size is rounded up by
  2870: their own alignment keep compiling, `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` (or a
  2871: diagnostic fixture) gains the shape, and `./build.sh build --config Release
  2872: -t test_all` plus `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green.
  2873: Oracle: clang's and gcc's own diagnostics.
  2874: 
  2875: ---
  2876: 
  2877: ## forgejo#705 — c: an aggregate initializer zeroes a member sharing a bit-field's storage unit
  2878: 
  2879: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/705
  2880: 
  2881: A brace initializer for a local aggregate writes each bit-field's storage unit
  2882: whole, so a plain member that shares that unit is overwritten with zero. It
  2883: only happens where a bit-field's unit reaches a non-bit-field member, which
  2884: packing is what makes possible.
  2885: 
  2886: ```c
  2887: struct __attribute__((packed)) s { char c; int a : 5; int b : 7; char t; };
  2888: int main(void) { struct s v = { 16, -10, 63, 17 }; return v.c; }
  2889: ```
  2890: 
  2891: clang and gcc both return 16; `ide cc` returns 0. `a` and `b` read back
  2892: correctly, and so does `t`; only `c` is lost.
  2893: 
  2894: The same declaration is right through every other path -- member assignments
  2895: (`v.c = 16; v.a = -10; ...`) and a static object with the same initializer both
  2896: give 16 -- so it is the local aggregate value, not the layout. It is
  2897: pre-existing: it reproduces identically on a compiler built before PR 704.
  2898: 
  2899: ## Where it is
  2900: 
  2901: `machine_x64_select_bit_field_unit` in
  2902: `src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/machine_x86_64.c`, and the identical
  2903: `machine_a64_select_bit_field_unit` in `machine_aarch64.c`. Lowering an
  2904: `IR_OPCODE_AGGREGATE` into the value's stack slot, they accumulate every
  2905: bit-field sharing a unit in a zeroed register and then **store the whole
  2906: unit**:
  2907: 
  2908: ```c
  2909: u32 unit_register = machine_x64_synthesize_register(selector);
  2910: ...
  2911: *zero_row = 0;
  2912: ```
  2913: 
  2914: `a` and `b` here take the four-byte unit at offset zero -- three bytes hold no
  2915: `int` anywhere, so the unit slides back over `c`, which is exactly what the
  2916: slide loop is for -- and the unit store then wipes the byte `c` was written
  2917: into. The comment above the function states the assumption that no longer
--- lines 3039-3129 ---
  3039: A struct reaches the same widths with a leading member -- `struct
  3040: __attribute__((packed)) { char c; int b : 20; }` is four bytes with `b` at
  3041: bit 8, which no `int` unit covers either.
  3042: 
  3043: ## Where it is
  3044: 
  3045: `c_lower_to_ir` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c`, the slide
  3046: loop that runs after the aggregate's size is known (search for `packed
  3047: bit-field '{S8}' straddles`). It tries the declared type's unit first and then
  3048: the ascending power-of-two candidates, and reports when none of them both
  3049: covers the field and fits inside the object. `IrField.access_size` carries the
  3050: narrowed width, zero meaning the declared type's size, and
  3051: `ir_field_access_size` is what its readers ask.
  3052: 
  3053: ## What it would take
  3054: 
  3055: A field with no single unit needs more than one access: clang emits an `i40`
  3056: load, which LLVM lowers to a four-byte plus a one-byte access. That is a new
  3057: shape for every reader of `ir_field_access_size` -- the load and the
  3058: read-modify-write in `c_gen.c`, the four constant-initializer folds there, the
  3059: `IR_OPCODE_AGGREGATE` selectors in `machine_x86_64.c` and
  3060: `machine_aarch64.c`, and the two canonical emitters in `codegen.c` -- and for
  3061: `ir_place_narrow_bit_field_access`, which is the validation exception that
  3062: admits a `LOAD`/`STORE` disagreeing with its place's type. Refusing was
  3063: deliberate while the single-unit model was the whole model (AGENTS.md says
  3064: so); this issue is the other half of it.
  3065: 
  3066: ## Done when
  3067: 
  3068: `sizeof` and a value round-trip of the two declarations above match clang for
  3069: every width in the table, including a neighbouring member that a wide store
  3070: must not clobber, under every allocator through `driver_test.c`. The refusal
  3071: and its test in `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` go away with it.
  3072: 
  3073: Oracle: `sizeof`/`_Alignof` and value round-trips against clang, plus the
  3074: cross-linked pair in `tests/basic_c_packed_layout_caller.c` /
  3075: `_callee.c`, which pins the layout to the platform's rather than to Buster's.
  3076:

  3079: ## forgejo#710 — c: a named bit-field of zero width is accepted
  3080: 
  3081: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/710
  3082: 
  3083: A bit-field with a name and a zero width is accepted. C requires the width of
  3084: a named bit-field to be greater than zero (C23 6.7.3.2p4), and both reference
  3085: compilers refuse it:
  3086: 
  3087: ```c
  3088: struct s { char c; int b : 0; };
  3089: ```
  3090: 
  3091: ```
  3092: error: named bit-field 'b' has zero width          (clang 22)
  3093: error: zero width for bit-field 'b'                (gcc)
  3094: ```
  3095: 
  3096: `ide cc` compiles it, laying `b` out as the zero-width member it is not
  3097: allowed to be: the struct measures 4/4, and `v.b = 0;` followed by a read of
  3098: `v.b` compiles and answers zero. The union spelling
  3099: `union __attribute__((packed)) { char c; int b : 0; }` is accepted the same
  3100: way and measures one byte.
  3101: 
  3102: Measured 2026-08-29 on the tree at PR 708. It is not specific to packing or to
  3103: unions -- the plain struct above is enough -- and it predates that PR: the
  3104: width is read the same way by both layout engines and neither asks whether the
  3105: member has a name.
  3106: 
  3107: ## Where it is
  3108: 
  3109: The two arms that already distinguish a named zero-width bit-field for
  3110: alignment purposes are the places that know both facts at once:
  3111: `c_parse_type_layout` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` and
  3112: the aggregate case of `c_lower_to_ir` in `c_gen.c` both guard the alignment
  3113: they take from a bit-field with `if (member.name.length)`, immediately above
  3114: the zero-width arm. The diagnostic belongs where the width is evaluated, so
  3115: the declaration fails rather than being laid out; `C_DIAGNOSTIC_INVALID_*` is
  3116: the kind, and the member's own location is what names it.
  3117: 
  3118: ## Done when
  3119: 
  3120: The declaration above produces a structured C diagnostic and a failed driver
  3121: result, an unnamed `int : 0;` still lays out as it does today (it is what
  3122: `struct __attribute__((packed)) zero_width_bits` in
  3123: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` covers), and a module test in `c_test.c`
  3124: pins both. A negative fixture belongs with the other rejected-declaration
  3125: cases rather than in `basic_c_packed_layout.c`, which has to keep compiling
  3126: under clang.
  3127: 
  3128: ---
  3129: 
--- lines 3158-3458 ---
  3158: 
  3159: The check added by #712 is a scan at the end of the type-mapping rounds in
  3160: `c_lower_to_ir` (`c_gen.c`), over every `C_TYPE_ARRAY` in `parse.types`. It
  3161: reads the *element's* mapping rather than the array's, which is why an array
  3162: whose own bound never resolved -- `extern cache_line inc[]`, a flexible array
  3163: member, a VLA -- is diagnosed anyway.
  3164: 
  3165: Instrumenting that scan to print every array type it visits shows **no array
  3166: type at all** for either spelling above, while the ordinary `cache_line
  3167: obj[2]` prints one. So this is not a gap in the scan's condition; the array
  3168: type is never added to the settled table:
  3169: 
  3170: - the parenthesized declarator `cache_line (*p)[2]` is modelled without a
  3171:   `C_TYPE_ARRAY` for the pointee. `sizeof(*p)` does not fold either -- it
  3172:   reports `static assertion expression is not an integer constant expression`
  3173:   -- which is a second, pre-existing symptom of the same thing.
  3174: - an array type name in an expression is resolved at lowering time by
  3175:   `c_ir_sizeof_operand_type_attempt` in `c_gen.c`, which builds `IrType`s
  3176:   directly and never goes through `c_parse_array_suffixes`. Note that path
  3177:   runs inside attempts that get rolled back, so a diagnostic raised there
  3178:   would need the same care `c_parse_type_layout` would have.
  3179: 
  3180: ## Severity
  3181: 
  3182: Neither spelling allocates an object through the form that escapes: the
  3183: pointer declaration places no array, and the type name only sizes one. The
  3184: misalignment #703 is about needs an array to exist, and every spelling that
  3185: makes one is now refused. So this is a missing diagnostic rather than wrong
  3186: code, which is why #712 filed it instead of folding it in.
  3187: 
  3188: ## Where to start
  3189: 
  3190: `c_gen.c`, the scan whose comment begins "An array element has to be
  3191: addressable at its own alignment in every slot" -- the condition to reuse is
  3192: `element->layout.size % element->layout.alignment != 0`, and
  3193: `CParseResult.type_alignments` being empty is what makes the whole question
  3194: skippable. The first question to answer is the parse-side one: whether
  3195: `cache_line (*p)[2]` should build a `C_TYPE_ARRAY` for its pointee at all,
  3196: since `sizeof(*p)` wants one too and that is the larger of the two defects.
  3197: 
  3198: ## Done when
  3199: 
  3200: Both spellings are diagnosed with the message #712 introduced, at Clang's
  3201: columns; `sizeof(*p)` folds for a pointer to a well-formed array; the
  3202: well-formed neighbours in `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` still compile and
  3203: run; and `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  3204: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green. Oracle: clang's and
  3205: gcc's own diagnostics.

  3209: ## forgejo#714 — c: a qualified aligned typedef loses its alignment
  3210: 
  3211: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/714
  3212: 
  3213: Qualifying an aligned typedef drops the alignment the typedef asked for. The
  3214: alias is `_Alignof` 64, and `const` of it is `_Alignof` 4. Measured against
  3215: Clang 22 and GCC on 2026-08-29, on `claude/issue-696-pr-c79e3a` at `5afb094e`
  3216: (the branch of #707).
  3217: 
  3218: ```c
  3219: typedef int cache_line __attribute__((aligned(64)));
  3220: struct s { char c; const cache_line f; };
  3221: _Static_assert(_Alignof(cache_line) == 64, "alias");        // passes
  3222: _Static_assert(_Alignof(struct s) == 64, "const member");   // fails on buster
  3223: _Static_assert(sizeof(struct s) == 128, "const member");    // fails on buster
  3224: ```
  3225: 
  3226: | probe | clang | gcc | buster |
  3227: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  3228: | `_Alignof(cache_line)` | 64 | 64 | 64 |
  3229: | `_Alignof(const cache_line)` | 64 | 64 | 4 |
  3230: | `_Alignof(volatile cache_line)` | 64 | 64 | 4 |
  3231: | `_Alignof(struct { char c; const cache_line f; })` | 64 | 64 | 4 |
  3232: 
  3233: This is the defect #696 was filed about, reached through a qualifier: a header
  3234: handing out a cache-line-aligned scalar produces an underaligned object the
  3235: moment a program writes `const` in front of it, with no diagnostic. Both layout
  3236: engines agree on the wrong answer, so `sizeof` folds to it as well.
  3237: 
  3238: ## Where it is
  3239: 
  3240: `#707` records the request in `CParseResult.type_alignments`, keyed on a *copy*
  3241: of the type the typedef declarator arrived at, and the mapping pass in
  3242: `c_gen.c` turns that copy into an `c_ir_add_aligned_type` result. Instrumenting
  3243: the settled type table for `const cache_line q[2] = {1, 2};` prints four types:
  3244: the builtin `int`, the aligned alias copy, a second copy for the qualified
  3245: form, and the array. The IR mapping of that third type has size 4 and
  3246: **alignment 4** -- so the qualified copy is built from something that is not
  3247: the alias, or is built before the alias is remapped and never revisited.
  3248: 
  3249: `c_parse_type_layout` in `c_parse.c` answers the same way, which is why the
  3250: `_Static_assert` above folds rather than diagnosing.
  3251: 
  3252: ## Why it is filed here rather than in #712
  3253: 
  3254: #712 refuses an array whose element size is not a multiple of its element
  3255: alignment. `const cache_line a[2]` is one such array in Clang and GCC, and
  3256: #712's scan does not report it -- correctly, on the numbers it is given: the
  3257: element it reads is alignment 4, so nothing is over-aligned. The shape starts
  3258: reporting on its own once this is fixed, with no change to #712.
  3259: 
  3260: ## Done when
  3261: 
  3262: `_Alignof` and `sizeof` agree with Clang and GCC for `const` and `volatile` of
  3263: an aligned typedef, in a declaration, as a struct or union member and as an
  3264: array element, in both the raising and the lowering direction, in both layout
  3265: engines; `const cache_line a[2]` is then refused by the check #712 added, at
  3266: Clang's column; `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains the qualified shapes; and
  3267: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  3268: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green. Oracle: clang's and
  3269: gcc's `_Alignof`, `sizeof` and `__builtin_offsetof`.

  3273: ## forgejo#715 — c: an aligned attribute among a typedef's specifiers is rejected
  3274: 
  3275: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/715
  3276: 
  3277: A GNU `aligned` attribute written among a typedef's declaration specifiers is
  3278: rejected by name, and the whole declaration is dropped:
  3279: 
  3280: ```c
  3281: typedef int __attribute__((aligned(16))) t5, t6;
  3282: ```
  3283: 
  3284: > error: alignment specifier cannot be applied to a typedef
  3285: 
  3286: Clang 22 and GCC both accept it and give *every* name of the list the
  3287: alignment, which is what a specifier-position attribute means. Measured
  3288: 2026-08-29 against `main` at `ba43b46a`, plus the branch of #701.
  3289: 
  3290: | probe | clang | gcc | buster |
  3291: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  3292: | `_Alignof(t5)` | 16 | 16 | (declaration refused) |
  3293: | `_Alignof(t6)` | 16 | 16 | (declaration refused) |
  3294: 
  3295: The declarator-position spelling of the same request works:
  3296: `typedef int t __attribute__((aligned(16)));` is honoured (#696, PR 707), and
  3297: a declarator list of them is partitioned correctly (#701).
  3298: 
  3299: ## Where it is
  3300: 
  3301: `c_parse_declaration_type_derive` in
  3302: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c` collects the declaration's
  3303: specifier-position alignment run and then rejects it by *position* alone:
  3304: 
  3305: ```c
  3306: if (declaration->alignment_count && (declaration->kind == C_DECLARATION_FUNCTION || declaration->kind == C_DECLARATION_TYPEDEF))
  3307: ```
  3308: 
  3309: The diagnostic is right about `_Alignas` -- it may not appear in a typedef
  3310: declaration at all, and Clang and GCC both refuse `typedef _Alignas(16) int t;`
  3311: -- and wrong about a GNU `aligned` attribute, which is an ordinary type
  3312: attribute in that position. The run does not carry its spelling, but it does
  3313: not have to: `c_alignment_specifier_is_standard` (same file) reads it back
  3314: from the token stream, and is already how #689's `_Alignas`-below-natural rule
  3315: tells the two apart.
  3316: 
  3317: The fix is to reject only the standard-spelled records and hand the rest to
  3318: the type, the way the declarator-position run is handed over in
  3319: `c_parse_declaration_type` -- and the reason those two ends are separate today
  3320: is that the specifier run is collected before the declarator's type is known,
  3321: so the move has to happen at the same place the declarator-position one does.
  3322: Note the shared run reaches *every* declarator of the list, which the
  3323: declarator-position one deliberately does not (#701), so
  3324: `c_parse_add_type_alignment` has to be called for each of them rather than
  3325: once.
  3326: 
  3327: The same question for a **function** is separate and buster is right: neither
  3328: reference compiler lets `aligned` change a function's alignment through this
  3329: spelling (they have `__attribute__((aligned))` on the function declarator for
  3330: that), so only the typedef arm of the condition is in question here.
  3331: 
  3332: ## Done when
  3333: 
  3334: `typedef int __attribute__((aligned(16))) t5, t6;` compiles and gives both
  3335: names `_Alignof` 16; `typedef _Alignas(16) int t;` is still diagnosed by name;
  3336: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains the shape beside the
  3337: `typedef_list_raised` group that #701 added; `./build.sh build --config
  3338: Release -t test_all` and `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are
  3339: green. Oracle: `_Alignof` against clang, which gcc agrees with.

  3343: ## forgejo#719 — c: a store through a dereferenced pointer to an array is dropped
  3344: 
  3345: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/719
  3346: 
  3347: A store whose target is reached by dereferencing a pointer to an array is
  3348: accepted, compiles, and does nothing. Reads through the same expression are
  3349: correct, and the equivalent subscript spelling stores correctly. Measured
  3350: against Clang 22 on 2026-08-29.
  3351: 
  3352: ```c
  3353: static int rows[2][3];
  3354: 
  3355: void store(void)
  3356: {
  3357:     int (*p)[3] = &rows[1];
  3358:     (*p)[1] = 7;        // dropped
  3359:     p[0][1] = 7;        // stores
  3360: }
  3361: ```
  3362: 
  3363: | spelling | clang | buster |
  3364: | --- | --- | --- |
  3365: | `(*p)[i] = v` | stores | **dropped** |
  3366: | `*(*p + i) = v` | stores | **dropped** |
  3367: | `(*(p + 0))[i] = v` | stores | **dropped** |
  3368: | `p[0][i] = v` | stores | stores |
  3369: | `(*p)[i]` read | correct | correct |
  3370: | `*q = v` for `int *q` | stores | stores |
  3371: | `(*r).a = v` for `struct s *r` | stores | stores |
  3372: 
  3373: It is a silent wrong-code bug: no diagnostic, and the program keeps running
  3374: with the old value.
  3375: 
  3376: ## Where it goes wrong
  3377: 
  3378: `void f(int (*p)[3], int v) { (*p)[1] = v; }` compiles to a copy of the whole
  3379: array into a stack temporary, and stores into the copy:
  3380: 
  3381: ```text
  3382: mov    (%rcx),%rax           ; load rows[1][0..1]
  3383: mov    %rax,-0x20(%rbp)      ; into a frame temporary
  3384: mov    0x8(%rcx),%eax        ; load rows[1][2]
  3385: mov    %eax,-0x18(%rbp)
  3386: lea    -0x20(%rbp),%rdx      ; index the temporary
  3387: ...
  3388: mov    %edi,(%rax)           ; store lands in the temporary
  3389: ```
  3390: 
  3391: The sibling `p[0][1] = v` indexes `%rdi` itself and stores through it, which is
  3392: what the deref should have produced. So unary `*` on a pointer to an array is
  3393: being lowered as an rvalue load of the array rather than as a place, and the
  3394: subsequent subscript indexes that materialized copy. The array-to-pointer
  3395: decay that follows a correct `*p` never has to load anything.
  3396: 
  3397: ## Severity and reachability
  3398: 
  3399: Pre-existing, and independent of the base type's spelling: it reproduces with
  3400: `int (*p)[3]` at block scope, which has always parsed. #713 makes it easier to
  3401: reach, since `T (*p)[3]` and `struct s (*p)[3]` at file scope only started
  3402: being declarations at all with that fix, but it is not caused by it.
  3403: 
  3404: `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` covers the well-formed pointer-to-array shapes
  3405: through the subscript spelling and reads for exactly this reason; switching
  3406: those lines to `(*p)[i] = v` is the regression test this wants.
  3407: 
  3408: ## Done when
  3409: 
  3410: All three dropped spellings above store, `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` uses
  3411: the deref spelling for its pointer-to-array store, and
  3412: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  3413: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` are green. Oracle: Clang.
  3414:

  3416: 
  3417: ## forgejo#721 — abi: an aggregate holding a bit-field is passed in memory instead of registers
  3418: 
  3419: Closed 2026-08-29. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/721
  3420: 
  3421: An aggregate that fits in two eightbytes and holds a bit-field is passed and
  3422: returned in memory rather than in registers, which is not what Clang and GCC
  3423: do with it. The disagreement is invisible inside one program and becomes a
  3424: wrong answer as soon as one half of a call is built by another compiler.
  3425: 
  3426: ```c
  3427: struct __attribute__((packed)) a2 { char lead; int value : 20; char tail; };
  3428: struct a2 make2(void) { struct a2 r; r.lead = 7; r.value = 0x12345; r.tail = 9; return r; }
  3429: ```
  3430: 
  3431: Five bytes, so System V classifies it INTEGER and returns it in `rax`; `ide cc`
  3432: returns it through a hidden pointer. Linking a Buster caller against a Clang
  3433: callee prints garbage where both halves built by the same compiler print
  3434: `7 12345 9`. Measured 2026-08-29 on `7a97299a` (`c: merge a bit-field's storage
  3435: unit instead of storing it whole`), so it predates the split-access work in
  3436: #709; the shapes that work today are the ones whose members happen to be
  3437: byte-aligned, which is why `basic_c_packed_layout`'s existing by-value records
  3438: pass.
  3439: 
  3440: ## Where it is
  3441: 
  3442: `ir_system_v_abi_classes` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/ir/ir.c` walks the
  3443: aggregate one field at a time and asks each field's *declared* type where it
  3444: sits: it rejects the whole classification when `task.offset % field_alignment`
  3445: or when `task.offset + type->layout.size > 16`. A bit-field's declared type is
  3446: not what it occupies -- `int value : 20` occupies twenty bits at bit eight, not
  3447: four bytes at whatever the unit offset is -- so a bit-field whose storage unit
  3448: packing slid, or whose declared type is wider than the bits it holds, fails a
  3449: test that System V never applies to it. The rule the walk implements is the
  3450: one about *unaligned fields*, and bit-fields are not fields for that purpose:
  3451: the classifier should merge the classes of the eightbytes a bit-field's bits
  3452: fall in and leave its declared type out of it.
  3453: 
  3454: A split bit-field (#709) makes this reachable for every packed record with a
  3455: wide field, which is why `basic_c_packed_layout_caller.c` /
  3456: `_callee.c` pass the split record by address rather than by value.
  3457: 
  3458: ## Done when

  3501: 
  3502: The reference compilers genuinely disagree about the *value*, so the value is a
  3503: second question and the two should be separated:
  3504: 
  3505: - **Clang** treats `_Atomic T` as constructing a type rather than qualifying
  3506:   one: it gets the alignment an atomic of that width gets, and the alias's
  3507:   `aligned` request does not travel into it.
  3508: - **GCC** keeps the request.
  3509: - Both agree that `_Atomic` written on a typedef whose base was *already*

  3511:   is 64 in both, and buster agrees (fixed on #714's branch).

  3513: #714 chose Clang for the paths it touched, because AGENTS.md names Clang the
  3514: oracle where the two disagree, and because it was already the answer this
  3515: frontend gave through a typedef. The inline spelling was left alone as
  3516: out of scope, which is what this issue is for.
  3517: 
  3518: ## Where it is
  3519: 
  3520: `c_parse_add_qualified_type` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_parse.c`

  3522: declines to inherit the alignment record when the step *adds* `_Atomic`

  3524: spelling in a type name answers 64, which is the alias's own number — the
  3525: number you get by never building a copy at all, so the `_Atomic` is most likely
  3526: being skipped before the copy is made rather than being applied and then

  3529: path; start by instrumenting whether a copy is built for
  3530: `_Alignof(_Atomic cache_line)` at all.
  3531: 
  3532: Both layout engines agree on the wrong answer here — `c_parse_type_layout` in
  3533: `c_parse.c` folds the `_Static_assert` and `c_lower_to_ir` in `c_gen.c` folds
  3534: the same expression in a function body — so the fix belongs where the type is
  3535: built, not in either engine.
  3536: 
  3537: ## Done when
  3538: 
  3539: `_Alignof` and `sizeof` give one answer for `_Atomic cache_line` however it is
  3540: spelled — inline in a type name, through a typedef of it, as a struct or union
  3541: member, and as an array element — and that answer is Clang's, matching the
  3542: choice #714 made. `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` gains the `_Atomic` shapes

--- lines 3745-3835 ---
  3745: | `_Alignof(_Atomic t3)` | 4 | 1 | **1** |
  3746: | `sizeof(at3)` | 4 | 3 | **3** |
  3747: | `_Alignof(at3)` | 4 | 1 | **1** |
  3748: 
  3749: Buster agrees with itself in every spelling and agrees with GCC, so this is a
  3750: value question rather than the consistency question #726 was. It is filed
  3751: because AGENTS.md names Clang the oracle where the two references disagree, and
  3752: because the divergence is an ABI one: an `_Atomic struct` passed or laid out
  3753: across an object boundary is three bytes on one side and four on the other.
  3754: 
  3755: ## What is known
  3756: 
  3757: - Clang rounds an atomic aggregate's size up to the next power of two and sets
  3758:   its alignment to that size, which is what makes the object lock-free-eligible
  3759:   for the `__atomic` builtins: a three-byte record has no three-byte atomic
  3760:   instruction, and a four-byte one does. The padding is part of the type, so
  3761:   `sizeof` sees it.
  3762: - GCC does not, and neither does this: `_Atomic T` is a qualified copy of `T`
  3763:   with `T`'s layout, which is what `c_ir_add_qualified_type` in `c_gen.c`
  3764:   builds (`IrType qualified = *base;`) and what the parse-side engine folds.
  3765: - Only sizes that are not already powers of two differ. `_Atomic` of a
  3766:   one-byte struct is 1/1 in all three, which is why `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c`
  3767:   can pin the aggregate member shape it added in #726 against Clang today.
  3768: - The reachable range is small: 3, 5, 6, 7, and 9..15 bytes, then 17..31 and so
  3769:   on. Clang stops promoting above the target's maximum lock-free width and
  3770:   leaves larger aggregates alone, so the rule is not "round every aggregate
  3771:   up"; that ceiling is the part worth measuring before implementing.
  3772: 
  3773: ## Where it is
  3774: 
  3775: `c_ir_add_qualified_type` in `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c` copies
  3776: the operand's layout wholesale, and `c_parse_type_layout` in `c_parse.c` folds
  3777: `sizeof`/`_Alignof` from the same layout. **Both layout engines have to agree**
  3778: or a folded `sizeof` contradicts the object it measures, which is the rule
  3779: AGENTS.md already states for `packed`/`aligned`. The System V classifier reads
  3780: the result as well: a promoted four-byte record is one INTEGER eightbyte where a
  3781: three-byte one already is, so the argument side may not move, but that has to be
  3782: checked rather than assumed.
  3783: 
  3784: ## Done when
  3785: 
  3786: `sizeof` and `_Alignof` of `_Atomic S` match Clang for every aggregate size the
  3787: promotion reaches, in a type name, through a typedef, as a member, and as an
  3788: array element, in both layout engines, and the promotion stops where Clang's
  3789: does rather than growing every aggregate. Gate with `./build.sh build --config
  3790: Release -t test_all` plus `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`; oracle
  3791: against Clang's `_Alignof`, `sizeof` and `__builtin_offsetof`, recording GCC
  3792: beside it as the second opinion. `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` is where the
  3793: `_Atomic` shapes live and where the promoted sizes belong next to the one-byte
  3794: aggregate that already agrees. Worth confirming first that musl, libc-test and
  3795: the compat harnesses have such an aggregate at all — if the population is empty,
  3796: the value of matching Clang here is the ABI statement rather than any program.
