--- lines 4474-4793 ---
  4474: `c_ir_initializer_narrow_compound_literal_value` in
  4475: `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c` drops the `( type-name )` and
  4476: hands the brace body to the folder that was going to run anyway. Once the
  4477: type name is gone the conversion has nowhere to happen, and folding the
  4478: body straight into the destination gives the wrong answer where the
  4479: literal's own type is narrower than the destination: `(unsigned char){300}`
  4480: is 44 in Clang and would be 300, and `(float){0.1}` widened to `double` is
  4481: 0.10000000149011612 and would be 0.1. The predicate is therefore
  4482: deliberately `c_ir_types_compatible`, and an incompatible literal is left
  4483: alone rather than folded wrong. It is also what keeps `(int[]){1, 2}`
  4484: initializing an `int *` -- an array decaying to a pointer, an address
  4485: rather than a value -- reaching `c_ir_static_compound_literal_address`.
  4486: 
  4487: ## Where to start
  4488: 
  4489: The general answer is a compound-literal operand in the constant
  4490: evaluator, which is where `(int){5} + 1` has to be handled anyway and where
  4491: the conversion has a type to happen at.
  4492: 
  4493: - `c_ir_constant_evaluate` -> `c_ir_constant_evaluate_attempt` ->
  4494:   `c_ir_constant_evaluate_impl` in
  4495:   `src/buster/lib/compiler/frontend/c/c_gen.c` is a shunting-yard
  4496:   evaluator over `CIrConstantValue`, driven by the suspendable query
  4497:   machine (`C_IR_QUERY_FRAME_CONSTANT`, dispatched in `c_ir_query_step`).
  4498:   An operand arm that recognizes `( type-name ) { ... }` needs a
  4499:   sub-query for the type name -- `c_ir_compound_literal_type` is already
  4500:   a query frame, `C_IR_QUERY_FRAME_COMPOUND_TYPE` -- and a nested constant
  4501:   evaluation of the brace body, both of which must resume the way the
  4502:   existing sub-queries do rather than recurse.
  4503: - `c_ir_constant_cast` is the conversion, applied once at the literal's
  4504:   type; the destination's own conversion is the one the callers already
  4505:   apply to whatever the evaluator returns.
  4506: - `c_ir_initializer_compound_literal_info` recognizes the shape and strips
  4507:   redundant parentheses; it is what the narrowing uses.
  4508: 
  4509: ## What the narrowing must keep
  4510: 
  4511: Do not delete `c_ir_initializer_narrow_compound_literal_value` when the
  4512: evaluator grows the operand. It covers three shapes the evaluator does not
  4513: reach, because they are not `CIrConstantValue`s:
  4514: 
  4515: - `(const char *){"lit"}`, which folds through
  4516:   `c_ir_global_string_pointer_initializer`.
  4517: - an 80-bit x87 literal, which folds through `c_ir_ext80_global_literal`
  4518:   and carries more significand than the `f64` the evaluator works in.
  4519: - the C23 empty literal `(int){}`, which is a zero initializer rather than
  4520:   an expression.
  4521: 
  4522: An aggregate literal initializing an aggregate object is a fourth: it goes
  4523: through `c_ir_constant_initializer_context_begin`, which does the same
  4524: narrowing for its own reasons.
  4525: 
  4526: ## Validation
  4527: 
  4528: `tests/basic_c_static_compound_literal.c` reads the value form back at run
  4529: time under all four register allocators; the converting rows belong there,
  4530: with the answers Clang produces rather than the ones the literal's body
  4531: spells -- `(unsigned char){300}` reading back as 44 is the row that fails
  4532: if the conversion is skipped rather than applied.
  4533: `c_test_static_compound_literal` in
  4534: `src/buster/tests/compiler/frontend/c/c_test.c` pins the remaining
  4535: refusals by line and column and pins the count of synthesized literal

  4537: path would show up as an extra object.

  4549: ## forgejo#760 — c: __typeof__ of a conditional expression resolves to no type
  4550: 
  4551: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/760
  4552: 
  4553: `__typeof__` over a conditional expression resolves to no type at all, so a
  4554: declaration written on it declares nothing and every later use of the name is
  4555: an undeclared-identifier error. There is no `void` in the shape and no
  4556: diagnostic naming the `__typeof__`:
  4557: 
  4558: ```c
  4559: int main(void)
  4560: {
  4561:     __typeof__(*(0 ? (double *)0 : (char *)0)) a = 1.5;
  4562:     return (int)sizeof(a);
  4563: }
  4564: ```
  4565: 
  4566: ```
  4567: clang   compiles (warns -Wpointer-type-mismatch), sizeof(a) == 8
  4568: gcc     compiles, sizeof(a) == 8
  4569: ide cc  error: use of undeclared identifier 'a'
  4570: ```
  4571: 
  4572: The conditional is the whole trigger — `__typeof__(*(double *)0)` beside it
  4573: resolves fine, and so does `__typeof__` of an ordinary identifier. Measured
  4574: 2026-08-30 against clang 21 and gcc 15 on x86-64 Linux, on `main` at
  4575: `756ee3c2`.
  4576: 
  4577: This is the shape musl's `<tgmath.h>` is written in:
  4578: `__typeof__(*(0 ? (t *)0 : (void *)!(c)))`, where the conditional selects `t *`
  4579: because the other arm is a null pointer constant, and the `*` names the type
  4580: the macro is generic over. It is a plausible first thing to look at for
  4581: `functional/tgmath`, the unit #728 lists first and describes as the likeliest
  4582: pure-codegen defect of its five — this is not codegen at all, and a macro that
  4583: selects no type would explain a wrong overload rather than a wrong narrowing.
  4584: 
  4585: Found while fixing #743 (`sizeof(void)` was 0, so `void *` arithmetic did not
  4586: step); PR #759 fixes that and leaves this untouched, because giving `void` a
  4587: size does not make the conditional resolve — the spelling without any `void` in
  4588: it fails identically.
  4589: 
  4590: ## Where to start
  4591: 
  4592: `c_ir_sizeof_operand_type_attempt` and the `__typeof__` operand walk in
  4593: `c_gen.c` are what resolve a type name in an expression; the conditional's
  4594: result type is `c_parse_conditional_expression_type` in `c_parse.c`, which is
  4595: the engine `c_test_conditional_type_prediction` already covers. The question is
  4596: which of the two gives up: whether the conditional's composite pointer type is
  4597: never computed, or whether it is computed and the `__typeof__` walk cannot take
  4598: a type out of an expression that is not a type name.
  4599: 
  4600: ## Done when
  4601: 
  4602: `__typeof__` over a conditional declares an object of the selected type, in
  4603: both the pointer-mismatch spelling above and the null-pointer-constant spelling
  4604: musl writes, oracled against clang with gcc recorded beside it, with a runtime
  4605: fixture under `tests/` and a frontend module test for the type the walk
  4606: resolves. Re-run `functional/tgmath` afterwards and record whether it moved —
  4607: it may well have a second cause.
  4608: 
  4609: ---
  4610: 
  4611: ## forgejo#761 — c: _Atomic before a struct, union or enum keyword never reaches the type
  4612: 
  4613: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/761
  4614: 
  4615: `_Atomic` written as a qualifier in front of a `struct`, `union` or `enum`
  4616: keyword is dropped: the type the parser builds is the plain aggregate, so the
  4617: object is not atomic, no atomic access is emitted for it, and `sizeof` and
  4618: `_Alignof` answer the aggregate's own numbers. Measured 2026-08-30 on the
  4619: branch of #731 and on `main` at `6dbdab27` alike; it is pre-existing and the
  4620: #731 layout work neither caused it nor changed it.
  4621: 
  4622: ```c
  4623: struct three { char a, b, c; };
  4624: typedef struct { char a, b, c; } three_alias;
  4625: 
  4626: _Static_assert(sizeof(_Atomic struct three) == 4, "clang: 4");    /* fails: 3 */
  4627: _Static_assert(sizeof(_Atomic three_alias) == 4, "clang: 4");     /* passes */
  4628: _Static_assert(sizeof(struct three _Atomic) == 4, "clang: 4");    /* passes */
  4629: _Static_assert(sizeof(_Atomic(struct three)) == 4, "clang: 4");   /* passes */
  4630: ```
  4631: 
  4632: Three of the four spellings build the atomic type; only the leading qualifier
  4633: before a tag keyword does not. It is not a layout question -- the qualifier
  4634: never reaches the type at all, so `_Atomic struct three x; x = y;` compiles
  4635: into an ordinary aggregate copy where the program asked for an atomic store.
  4636: 
  4637: ## Where it is
  4638: 
  4639: `c_parse_scalar_type_core_begin` in `c_parse.c` scans the specifier prefix
  4640: looking for the aggregate keyword:
  4641: 
  4642: ```c
  4643:     u32 aggregate_index = start;
  4644:     while (aggregate_index < end && preprocess.tokens[aggregate_index].kind == C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER)
  4645:     {
  4646:         ...
  4647:         if (c_token_in_well_known_set(..., C_PARSE_AGGREGATE_KEYWORDS)) { break; }
  4648:         if (!c_parse_type_word_for_dialect_token(preprocess, preprocess.tokens[aggregate_index])) { break; }
  4649:         aggregate_index += 1;
  4650:     }
  4651: ```
  4652: 
  4653: The qualifier words it steps over are never collected, and the aggregate
  4654: branch returns the tag's own type. The trailing position is handled by
  4655: `c_parse_apply_trailing_qualifiers` at the two returns of that branch, which is
  4656: the helper the leading run needs as well; the typedef branch beside it
  4657: (`c_parse_qualified_typedef_type`) already collects a leading run the same way.
  4658: 
  4659: ## What has to happen first
  4660: 
  4661: Fixing the parse gap alone turns a currently-compiling construct into a hard
  4662: failure, because an atomic *aggregate* has no code generation:
  4663: `typedef struct { long long a; } eight; typedef _Atomic eight a8; a8 g; g = v;`
  4664: fails today with `C code generation failed with error 2 ... opcode 9`
  4665: (`IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_STORE`) whichever spelling built the type -- see the sibling
  4666: issue for that. The layout is not involved: the shape above is eight bytes
  4667: aligned eight with and without the promotion. So the order is codegen first,
  4668: then this.
  4669: 
  4670: `const struct S` and `volatile struct S` ride the same prefix run. `const` is
  4671: diagnosed today through the declaration rather than the type
  4672: (`const struct three cx; cx.a = 5;` is rejected), so collecting the run must
  4673: be checked against those two as well rather than assumed to be an `_Atomic`
  4674: question.
  4675: 
  4676: ## Done when
  4677: 
  4678: All four spellings above build one type, `sizeof`/`_Alignof` agree across them
  4679: in both layout engines, and an object declared with the leading spelling takes
  4680: atomic accesses. Oracle against Clang, recording GCC beside it. The `_Atomic`
  4681: shapes in `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c` are where the three working
  4682: spellings are already pinned; the leading one is named there as absent for
  4683: this reason. Gate with `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  4684: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`.
  4685: 
  4686: ---
  4687: 
  4688: ## forgejo#762 — c: an atomic aggregate cannot be loaded or stored
  4689: 
  4690: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/762
  4691: 
  4692: Assigning an atomic aggregate -- reading one, or writing one -- fails code
  4693: generation. Measured 2026-08-30 on the branch of #731 and on `main` at
  4694: `6dbdab27` alike; it is pre-existing, and the #731 layout work neither caused
  4695: it nor changed it.
  4696: 
  4697: ```c
  4698: typedef struct { long long a; } eight;
  4699: typedef _Atomic eight a8;
  4700: static a8 g;
  4701: int main(void) { eight v = {5}; g = v; eight r = g; return (int)r.a; }
  4702: ```
  4703: 
  4704: ```
  4705: cc: error: C code generation failed with error 2, function 1 ('main', ...),
  4706:     instruction 7, opcode 9, operation 73, referenced symbol '<none>'
  4707: ```
  4708: 
  4709: Opcode 9 is `IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_STORE`; the read fails the same way through
  4710: `IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_LOAD`. The layout is not involved: the shape above is eight
  4711: bytes aligned eight both before and after #731's promotion, and a three-byte
  4712: record -- which the promotion does move, to four aligned four -- fails
  4713: identically.
  4714: 
  4715: ## What is known
  4716: 
  4717: - The frontend is doing the right thing. `c_ir_emit_load_place_raw` and its
  4718:   store counterpart in `c_gen.c` choose the atomic opcode from the place's
  4719:   `IrType::is_atomic` and give the loaded value the *unqualified* type, which
  4720:   is the same pairing `ir_validate_canonical_module` admits for every atomic
  4721:   opcode. The IR validates; it is the machine layer that has no lowering for
  4722:   an atomic load or store whose type is a struct or union.
  4723: - `IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_READ_MODIFY_WRITE` and `IR_OPCODE_ATOMIC_COMPARE_EXCHANGE`
  4724:   are already restricted to integer, boolean and pointer operands by the
  4725:   validator, so this is only about the plain load and store.
  4726: - Clang lowers a lock-free-sized atomic aggregate as an integer access of the
  4727:   promoted width -- which is exactly what the #731 promotion exists for: a
  4728:   three-byte record is padded to four so that a four-byte access covers it --
  4729:   and calls `libatomic` above the target's maximum lock-free width. There is
  4730:   no `libatomic` here, so the width-covered case is the one to lower and the
  4731:   wider one needs a decision of its own (a diagnostic is a defensible answer).
  4732: - Nothing in the compat corpus reaches this: `_Atomic` appears in QuickJS over
  4733:   integer scalars only, and musl, libc-test, sbase, SQLite, zlib, cJSON and
  4734:   doomgeneric contain no `_Atomic` at all (measured 2026-08-30). buster's own
  4735:   `AtomicU64` is `_Atomic u64`. So this is an ABI/semantics completeness
  4736:   question rather than a program that is failing.
  4737: 
  4738: ## Done when
  4739: 
  4740: An atomic aggregate whose promoted size is at most the target's maximum
  4741: lock-free width (`TargetDataLayout::atomic_max_width`, 128 bits on x86-64 and
  4742: AArch64) loads and stores through an integer access of that width, under all
  4743: four register allocators, and a wider one gets a diagnostic rather than an
  4744: internal code generation failure. Oracle the values against Clang. #761 waits
  4745: on this: `_Atomic` before a tag keyword is dropped today, and making it reach
  4746: the type would turn programs that compile into programs that hit this failure.
  4747: Gate with `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus
  4748: `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`.
  4749:

  4752: ## forgejo#763 — abi: Clang passes a record containing an atomic member in memory, GCC and this do not
  4753: 
  4754: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/763
  4755: 
  4756: Clang classifies **any record that contains an atomic member** as MEMORY for
  4757: the System V argument ABI, and so does it for an atomic record passed by value.
  4758: GCC does not, and neither does this compiler: both pass such a record in
  4759: registers when its size and fields otherwise allow it. Measured 2026-08-30
  4760: against Clang 22.1.8 and GCC 16.2.1 on `main` at `6dbdab27`; it is
  4761: pre-existing, and the #731 layout work neither caused it nor changed it -- the
  4762: promotion changes the record's *size*, which is a separate statement from its
  4763: class.
  4764: 
  4765: ```c
  4766: struct three { char a, b, c; };
  4767: struct outer { char c; _Atomic struct three v; };
  4768: struct atomic_int_member { char c; _Atomic int v; };
  4769: char f(struct outer x)             { return x.c; }
  4770: char h(struct atomic_int_member x) { return x.c; }
  4771: char g(_Atomic struct three x)     { struct three y = x; return y.a; }
  4772: ```
  4773: 
  4774: Clang gives all three `ptr noundef byval(...) align 8` -- the record rides
  4775: memory. GCC passes each in `%edi`. `_Atomic int` alone as a member is enough;
  4776: the size is not the reason.
  4777: 
  4778: The cause on Clang's side is structural rather than deliberate:
  4779: `X86_64ABIInfo::classify` asks `Ty->getAs<RecordType>()`, and an `AtomicType`
  4780: is not sugar over its value type, so the walk falls through to the "everything
  4781: else is Memory" tail. The psABI text has no such rule -- an `_Atomic` object
  4782: has the size and alignment of the type it is built from and no special class --
  4783: so this is the one place where the oracle looks like an accident.
  4784: 
  4785: ## Why it is filed rather than fixed
  4786: 
  4787: AGENTS.md names Clang the oracle where the two references disagree, and the
  4788: divergence is an ABI one: a `struct { char c; _Atomic int v; }` argument sits
  4789: in a register on one side of a translation-unit boundary and in memory on the
  4790: other. But following Clang here means adding a rule to
  4791: `ir_system_v_abi_classify` that the psABI does not state and that GCC does not
  4792: implement, which would make this compiler disagree with GCC where it agrees
  4793: today. That is a decision worth taking deliberately rather than as a side

  5060: ## forgejo#779 — link: Mach-O and UEFI images refuse __attribute__((constructor)) instead of running it
  5061: 
  5062: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/779
  5063: 
  5064: `__attribute__((constructor))` reaches the object file on every target now
  5065: (issue 771), and the ELF and PE writers call the registered functions from the
  5066: entry stub they synthesize. The Mach-O and UEFI writers do not: they refuse
  5067: the link with `LINK_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`, naming the first initializer,
  5068: rather than placing an array nothing would call.
  5069: 
  5070: Measured on `claude/inspiring-hypatia-6f3376`.
  5071: 
  5072: ## Why they refuse rather than run
  5073: 
  5074: Neither writer synthesizes an entry point. A Mach-O executable's `LC_MAIN`
  5075: carries the file offset of `main` and dyld calls it directly; a UEFI
  5076: application's entry is the firmware's call to `UefiMain`. Every other writer
  5077: in `link.c` builds a `_start` of its own -- that stub *is* the startup, which
  5078: is why `link_x86_build_elf_entry_stub` and `link_x86_build_pe_entry_stub`
  5079: exist -- and `link_initializer_plan_build` hands each of them the list of
  5080: functions to call and an object with the two array sections removed.
  5081: 
  5082: `link_initializer_plan_empty` is the refusal, and it is deliberate: a writer
  5083: that places every non-debug section it is given would otherwise write an array
  5084: with no offset of its own over the image header, and dropping the arrays
  5085: without saying so is the state issue 771 found the whole attribute in.
  5086: 
  5087: ```
  5088: $ ide cc -target aarch64-apple-macos ctor.c -o ctor
  5089: cc: error: native C link failed with unsupported feature: first
  5090: ```
  5091: 
  5092: The object itself is correct on both targets. Mach-O carries
  5093: `__DATA,__mod_init_func` and `__mod_term_func` with the
  5094: `S_MOD_INIT_FUNC_POINTERS`/`S_MOD_TERM_FUNC_POINTERS` types, so an object this

  5323: walk and left this spelling untouched.
  5324: 
  5325: ```c
  5326: struct three { char a, b, c; };
  5327: typedef struct { char a, b, c; } three_alias;
  5328: 
  5329: enum { A = sizeof(_Atomic struct three) };   /* 4, fixed by #761 */
  5330: enum { B = sizeof(struct three _Atomic) };   /* 4, fixed by #761 */
  5331: enum { C = sizeof(_Atomic three_alias) };    /* 4, already worked */
  5332: enum { D = sizeof(_Atomic(struct three)) };  /* fails to compile */
  5333: enum { E = sizeof(_Atomic(three_alias)) };   /* fails to compile */
  5334: enum { F = sizeof(_Atomic(int)) };           /* fails to compile */

  5336: 
  5337: It is not a tag question -- `_Atomic(int)` fails identically -- so it is the
  5338: operator spelling itself that the walk has no branch for.
  5339: 
  5340: ## Where it is
  5341: 
  5342: `c_parse_machineless_sizeof_operand_layout` in `c_parse.c` is the operand walk,
  5343: and `c_parse_machineless_base_type` beside it is what resolves the operand's
  5344: base type. The walk exists because the enum-constant evaluator runs *inside* a
  5345: step of the type-parse machine, which is an explicit frame stack with one
  5346: shared result slot and cannot be reentered; the machine-bearing path uses
  5347: `c_parse_scalar_type` and handles the operator spelling in
  5348: `c_type_parse_scalar_step`, which is why `_Static_assert(sizeof(_Atomic(int)))`
  5349: folds and the enum constant beside it does not.

  5352: then a primitive spelling. `_Atomic` followed by `(` matches none of them: the
  5353: typedef walk steps over `_Atomic` as a qualifier and then finds a `(` where a
  5354: name should be, and the tag walk sees `_Atomic` where a keyword should be.
  5355: `c_parse_atomic_type_specifier_at` (added by #761) is the predicate that names
  5356: the shape; the branch it would gate has to resolve the parenthesised operand
  5357: recursively -- base type, pointer chain, array suffixes -- and then qualify the
  5358: result atomic, refusing the array, function and already-qualified operands the
  5359: machine path diagnoses at `C_DIAGNOSTIC_INVALID_ATOMIC_TYPE`.
  5360:

  5373: ## forgejo#786 — c: an atomic aggregate parameter fails code generation in every spelling
  5374: 
  5375: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/786
  5376: 
  5377: An **atomic aggregate passed or received by value** fails code generation in
  5378: every spelling that builds the type, with an internal-sounding message rather
  5379: than a diagnostic:
  5380: 
  5381: ```c
  5382: typedef struct { char a, b, c; } three;
  5383: typedef _Atomic three at3;
  5384: int takes(at3 p) { return p.a; }
  5385: ```

  5387: ```
  5388: cc: error: ...:3:5: in function 'takes': cannot convert IR type 20 (kind 11) to IR type 19 (kind 11)
  5389: ```
  5390: 
  5391: The trailing spelling (`struct three _Atomic p`) and the leading one
  5392: (`_Atomic struct three p`, which #761 made buildable) fail identically, so it is
  5393: the parameter position rather than any one spelling. Clang and GCC both accept
  5394: the declaration; Clang passes the *promoted* four-byte object. Measured
  5395: 2026-08-30 on the branch of #761; pre-existing, and #761 neither caused it nor
  5396: changed it.

  5398: The two types the message names are the atomic type and its operand: the
  5399: promotion (#731) makes `_Atomic three` four bytes where `three` is three, so

  5401: one as convertible to the other.
  5402: 
  5403: ## What is already settled
  5404: 
  5405: - The layout is not in question: `_Atomic three` is four bytes aligned four on
  5406:   every path, pinned in `tests/basic_c_packed_layout.c`.
  5407: - The *access* is settled too (#762): a load or a store of an atomic aggregate
  5408:   is one integer access of the promoted width, refused with a diagnostic naming
  5409:   the width when the target has no lock-free access that wide.
  5410: - AGENTS.md already records the argument-side layout answer: "On the argument
  5411:   side the promotion moves nothing: a promoted four-byte record is one INTEGER
  5412:   eightbyte where the three-byte one already was." That is the classification;
  5413:   what is missing is the lowering that builds the parameter's frame object and
  5414:   the conversion between the value and the object.
  5415: - A **return** of an atomic aggregate should be checked in the same change; it
  5416:   was not measured separately.
  5417: 
  5418: ## Done when
  5419: 
  5420: A function may take and return an atomic aggregate by value in all four
  5421: spellings, the bytes match Clang's (including the padding the promotion added,
  5422: which Clang zeroes), and a width past the target's lock-free ceiling is refused
  5423: with the #762 diagnostic rather than an internal failure.
  5424: `tests/basic_c_atomic_aggregate.c` is the fixture -- it runs under all four
  5425: register allocators and bakes in Clang's bytes -- and the parameter and return
  5426: round trips go there. Gate with
  5427: `./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all` plus

  5432: ## forgejo#789 — link: constructor priority does not order across objects in Buster's own linker
  5433: 
  5434: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/789
  5435: 
  5436: `ld` runs every prioritized constructor before every unprioritized one,
  5437: ascending, across the whole program. PR #788 gave Buster's **objects** that
  5438: shape: `object_write_elf64` splits `OBJECT_SECTION_INIT_ARRAY` into one
  5439: `.init_array.NNNNN` ELF section per priority group, so an external linker
  5440: orders two Buster translation units exactly as it orders Clang's.
  5441: 
  5442: Buster's **own** linker still does not. `link_objects` concatenates each input
  5443: object's whole array in link order, and `link_initializer_plan_build` then reads
  5444: that concatenation off the merged `OBJECT_SECTION_INIT_ARRAY` slot by slot. The
  5445: priority is gone by then: `object_read_elf64` merges every `.init_array*`
  5446: section of an input into the one section of the kind (in `ld`'s order within
  5447: that input, as of #788, but still one section), so nothing downstream can tell
  5448: a `constructor(101)` from an unprioritized one.
  5449: 
  5450: This is **not a regression** and **not producer-specific**. Measured on
  5451: `claude/suspicious-chaplygin-0558e7` (PR #788), 2026-08-30, with
  5452: 
  5453: ```c
  5454: /* a.c */ __attribute__((constructor))      static void a_plain(void) { note("a_plain"); }
  5455:           __attribute__((constructor(120))) static void a_120(void)   { note("a_120"); }
  5456:           int main(void) { return 0; }
  5457: /* b.c */ void note(const char* name) { printf("%s\n", name); }
  5458:           __attribute__((constructor))      static void b_plain(void) { note("b_plain"); }
  5459:           __attribute__((constructor(101))) static void b_101(void)   { note("b_101"); }
  5460:           __attribute__((constructor(150))) static void b_150(void)   { note("b_150"); }
  5461: ```
  5462: 
  5463: | link | order |
  5464: | --- | --- |
  5465: | Clang objects, system `ld` | `b_101 a_120 b_150 a_plain b_plain` |
  5466: | Buster objects, system `ld` (after #788) | `b_101 a_120 b_150 a_plain b_plain` |
  5467: | Buster objects, `ide cc a.o b.o` | `a_120 a_plain b_101 b_150 b_plain` |
  5468: | **Clang** objects, `ide cc a.o b.o` | `a_120 a_plain b_101 b_150 b_plain` |
  5469: 
  5470: The last row is the point: Buster's linker gets Clang's objects wrong in exactly
  5471: the same way, so this is a linker gap rather than anything about how Buster
  5472: writes objects.
  5473:

  5783: and check the rest of the `__LINKEDIT` chain for the same pattern -- export
  5784: info, function starts and the code-signature blob if they grow one later. The

  5801: ## forgejo#806 — x86-64: the exact-form XCHG has no byte variant, so width-1 sequential atomic stores encode-fall-back
  5802: 
  5803: Closed 2026-08-31. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/806
  5804: 
  5805: **Task for an agent.** x86-64 machine encoder vocabulary gap, small and sharply scoped.
  5806: 
  5807: ## What is wrong
  5808: 
  5809: A sequentially consistent atomic store of a **one-byte** value selects on the x86-64 machine path (`MACHINE_X64_ATOMIC_STORE_XCHG`, payload width 1) but fails at the **encode stage** and falls back to the canonical emitter. Measured 2026-08-30 on main + PR 805:
  5810: 
  5811: ```c
  5812: _Atomic char gc; void store_char(char v) { gc = v; }
  5813: ```
  5814: 
  5815: `ide cc -v -c -fregister-allocator=fast` reports `CODEGEN_FALLBACK_STAGES verify=0 placement=0 encode=1`. Widths 2/4/8 encode fine. The same happens for one-byte atomic *aggregates* since PR 805 (its `keep_low_bytes` + XCHG path), and pre-existed on the scalar path — this is not a selection bug.
  5816: 
  5817: ## Where to work
  5818: 
  5819: `src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/machine_x86_64.c`: the exact-form registry entry `[34]` (`MACHINE_X64_XCHG_EXACT_FORM_ID = 9837`) resolves its operand widths from the row payload (`MEMORY_BASE_PAYLOAD_SIZE` / `GPR_PAYLOAD_SIZE`). The metadata form behind id 9837 evidently has no 8-bit variant (`xchg r/m8, r8` is opcode 0x86, a *different form* from 0x87), so the width-8-bit lookup fails and the encoder fails closed ("Migrated DIRECT rows have no handwritten byte fallback"). Follow how CMPXCHG spells its variants for the pattern.
  5820: 
  5821: ## How to validate
  5822: 
  5823: The probe above at every allocator: `CODEGEN_FALLBACK_STAGES` disappears and `fallback_functions=0`. Then `tests/basic_c_atomic_aggregate.c` natively (its one-byte shapes stop encode-falling-back) and `ide test`. Byte XCHG needs a REX prefix for SIL/DIL/SPL/BPL sources — make sure the variant table covers those registers, an allocator is free to pick them.
  5824: 
  5825: ## Definition of done
  5826: 
  5827: - Width-1 ATOMIC_STORE_XCHG encodes on the machine path; no encode-stage fallbacks left in `basic_c_atomic_aggregate.c` / an `_Atomic char` probe.
  5828: - `ide test` and `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` green.
  5829:

  5833:

  5835: 
  5836: **Task for an agent.** x86-64 machine-selector catch-up: the AArch64 selector now carries a larger bare-__int128 body subset than x86-64, and every piece has a direct x86 spelling.
  5837: 
  5838: ## What x86-64 refuses that AArch64 now selects (measured 2026-08-30, FAST)
  5839: 
  5840: Probe (each function alone, `-v -c -fregister-allocator=fast`, count CODEGEN_FALLBACK):
  5841: 
  5842: ```c
  5843: typedef unsigned __int128 U128; typedef __int128 S128;
  5844: U128 add(U128 a, U128 b) { return a + b; }            // refuses (BINARY)
  5845: U128 sub(U128 a, U128 b) { return a - b; }            // refuses
  5846: U128 land(U128 a, U128 b) { return a & b; }           // refuses (and | ^)
  5847: U128 shl64(U128 a) { return a << 64; }                // refuses (left + signed-right shifts; only constant unsigned >> selects)
  5848: S128 ashr65(S128 a) { return a >> 65; }               // refuses
  5849: U128 mul(U128 a, U128 b) { return a * b; }            // refuses (needs MULX/ADC or mul+umulh-equivalent lowering)
  5850: ```
  5851: 
  5852: Also refusing on x86-64: **i128-typed constants** (`(I128Wrapper){0}` in `tests/basic_c_aarch64_i128_abi.c` — `wrapper_after_one` falls back at opcode 14) and the **ordered i128 comparisons** in `check_i128`-shaped code (opcode 31). Equality and integer↔integer casts already select.
  5853: 
  5854: ## Where to work
  5855: 
  5856: `src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/machine_x86_64.c`. The AArch64 versions to mirror (same file layout on the a64 side): `machine_a64_select_constant`'s slot-backed halves branch, `machine_a64_select_i128_shift` (all three directions, constant amounts), `machine_a64_select_i128_binary` (bitwise per half; add/sub with the carry as a SETcc boolean off the low halves — x86 could instead use its native ADC once a flags-pairing row exists, but the boolean spelling needs no new rows; equality; the eight ordered comparisons as strict-high blended with unsigned-low behind high-equality). The x86 slot-classification list already covers CAST/BINARY for INTEGER-128; CONSTANT_INTEGER needs adding there.
  5857: 
  5858: ## How to validate
  5859: 
  5860: The machine-subset section of `tests/basic_c_aarch64_i128.c` (checks 37–60) is target-independent and exercises every listed op at the half boundaries; today the driver tests only run it cross-compiled to aarch64 under qemu, so wire a native x86 lane across the four allocators alongside the fix, and break one expected value once to prove that lane gates. `ide test` + `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`.

  5864: ## forgejo#814 — aarch64: no 16-byte atomic access exists, so _Atomic __int128 fails to compile
  5865: 
  5866: Closed 2026-08-30. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/814
  5867:

  5871: 
  5872: ```
  5873: build/Release/ide cc -c -target aarch64-linux tests/basic_c_int128.c
  5874: cc: error: C code generation failed with error 2, function 'test_atomic_wide' ... opcode 9 ...

  5877: `_Atomic unsigned __int128` (and any 9–16-byte atomic aggregate, e.g. `wide_round_trip`/`takes_nine`/`gives_nine` in `tests/basic_c_atomic_aggregate.c`, which are x86-gated today) has no lowering: the canonical AArch64 atomic load/store blocks in `codegen.c` accept widths 1/2/4/8 and return `CODEGEN_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_INSTRUCTION` at 16. x86-64 has its CMPXCHG16B path; AArch64 needs the LDXP/STXP exclusive-pair loop (baseline; LSE2's aligned LDP/STP single-copy atomicity is a model-gated improvement, not the starting point).

  5882:

  5884: 
  5885: - The fixture compiles and runs under qemu-aarch64 across all four allocators (qemu executes exclusives faithfully).
  5886: - Un-gate the aarch64 side of the 16-byte shapes in `basic_c_atomic_aggregate.c` if they are target-gated, and check the bytes against clang's answers like the rest of that fixture.
  5887: - Cross-check against clang with the freestanding probe recipe; note clang's own seq-cst 16-byte atomics on baseline aarch64 also use CASP/LDXP loops — compare semantics, not bytes.
  5888: - `ide test` + `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`.

  5891: 
  5892: ## forgejo#818 — c: a positional initializer stores into anonymous bit-fields instead of skipping them
  5893: 
  5894: Closed 2026-08-31. Original: https://code.buster14a.com/buster/buster/issues/818
  5895: 
  5896: A positional brace initializer for a struct containing anonymous bit-fields
  5897: assigns initializers *to* the anonymous fields instead of skipping them, so
  5898: every named field at or after the first anonymous one receives the wrong
  5899: value (usually its right-hand neighbour's, the last ones zero). C11 6.7.9p9:
  5900: unnamed members of structure objects do not participate in initialization.
  5901: 
  5902: ```c
  5903: struct S { unsigned a : 3; unsigned : 5; unsigned b : 7; };
  5904: int main(void) { struct S x = { 1, 2 }; return x.a * 10 + x.b; }
  5905: ```
  5906: 
  5907: clang and gcc return 12 (`a`=1, `b`=2); `ide cc` returns 10 (`a`=1, the
  5908: anonymous field swallows the 2, `b`=0). Both register-allocator modes agree
  5909: with each other and disagree with clang. Found on `55dfe872` (2026-08-30).
  5910: 
  5911: Differentiation:
  5912: 
  5913: - member assignment (`x.a = 1; x.b = 2;`) is right,
  5914: - a designated initializer (`{ .b = 2 }`) is right,
  5915: - `= {0}` is indistinguishable (zero lands in the anonymous field),
  5916: - a zero-width separator diverges the same way:
  5917:   `struct { unsigned a : 3; unsigned : 0; unsigned b : 5; } x = { 1, 2 };`
  5918:   reads back `b` as 0.
  5919: 
  5920: Found by `tools/differential_c_harness.py --families bit_field`: of the 143
  5921: divergent units in a 120-seed run, 115 stop diverging when the brace
  5922: initializer is rewritten to `= {0}` and nothing else changes; the remaining
  5923: 28 are the attributed-struct typedef alignment bug, filed separately.
  5924: 
  5925: ---
  5926:

===== docs/gcc13-sanitized-acceptance.md =====
--- lines 1-58 ---
     1: # GCC 13 sanitized runtime acceptance
     2: 
     3: The ordinary desktop combination matrix intentionally keeps its GCC row
     4: compile-only. That row proves compiler portability, but it does not execute the
     5: registered suite or the sanitizer canaries with GCC. The opt-in
     6: `GCC 13 sanitized runtime acceptance` workflow closes that evidence gap without
     7: adding a second GCC matrix to every pull request.
     8: 
     9: The workflow runs on Ubuntu 24.04 with `/usr/bin/gcc-13` selected through
    10: `BUSTER_GCC`. A Clang-built `build.c` driver is the documented hosted bootstrap
    11: exception; GCC 13 remains the configured application compiler. The workflow
    12: uses the repository-owned fatal ASan/UBSan/LSan policy and does not set a
    13: competing workflow-wide sanitizer environment.
    14: 
    15: ## Reproduction
    16: 
    17: With an idle build directory and GCC 13 installed:
    18: 
    19: ```sh
    20: export BUSTER_GCC=/usr/bin/gcc-13
    21: export BUSTER_TEST_JOBS=1
    22: export CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=4
    23: 
    24: clang -Isrc -Wall -Werror -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable \
    25:   -g build.c -o /tmp/buster-build
    26: /tmp/buster-build generate --sanitize --cc gcc --ci --linker DEFAULT -- \
    27:   -DBUSTER_UNITY_BUILD=OFF -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
    28: /tmp/buster-build build --config Debug -t test_all -- -j4
    29: ```
    30: 
    31: A successful run means the complete GCC 13 Debug application builds and links
    32: with warnings as errors, then the full registered suite executes. This includes
    33: the sanitizer module's clean controls, fatal undefined-behavior child and the
    34: supported LeakSanitizer children. A compile-only GCC row or a successful focused
    35: object build is not a substitute.
    36: 
    37: ## ELF data alias control
    38: 
    39: The workflow also retains the failure-first boundary behind #594. Its generated
    40: shared library gives `pair_0` and `data_0` one aliased definition. First, the
    41: old GCC 13 `-fPIE` object plus `-no-pie` link must fail the identity/value
    42: program, demonstrating that the control can still distinguish the two-copy
    43: relocation layout. Then GCC 13 and Clang each compile the reference as
    44: `-fPIC -pie`; both binaries must observe one address and the mutation through
    45: `pair_0` through `data_0` and `read_0()`.
    46: 
    47: This standalone check supplements rather than replaces
    48: `compiler_driver_test_elf_data_scaling`. The registered GCC suite must remain
    49: green with every existing shape, count and Buster-side `reference=0` assertion.
    50: 
    51: ## Workflow boundary
    52: 
    53: The workflow has read-only repository permissions, retains its exact checkout
    54: SHA, compiler versions, complete suite log and alias-control files, and never
    55: cancels an active acceptance attempt. It runs automatically only for the
    56: issue-scoped implementation branch; after integration it is available by
    57: manual dispatch. Ordinary `CI complete`, self-host and review requirements
    58: remain independent merge gates.
===== docs/instruction-selection-benchmark.md =====
--- lines 1-127 ---
     1: # Instruction-selection throughput benchmark
     2: 
     3: `ide bench-select <self-contained-source.c>` measures the production native
     4: x86-64 or AArch64 selector. It does not measure the diagnostic declarative rule
     5: matcher in `machine_select_generated.c`. No timers or counters are added to
     6: ordinary `ide cc` execution, and selection, legalization, feature policy,
     7: placement, and encoding are unchanged.
     8: 
     9: ## Run and reproduce
    10: 
    11: Build through the repository driver with the same configuration for baseline
    12: and candidate. First reproduce `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release`
    13: and the relevant correctness matrix; this benchmark is not a replacement.
    14: 
    15: ```sh
    16: python3 tools/selection_benchmark.py --self-test
    17: python3 tools/selection_benchmark.py --compiler build/Release/ide --samples 8 --allocators none fast mir-stack quality --check --output build/selection-benchmark/smoke.json
    18: python3 tools/selection_benchmark.py --compiler /absolute/base/ide --candidate /absolute/candidate/ide --samples 12 --allocators none fast mir-stack quality --check --cpu 0 --build-description 'Record commit IDs, host compiler/version, complete flags, configuration and host here' --output build/selection-benchmark/ab.json
    19: ```
    20: 
    21: Choose an allowed logical CPU for `--cpu`; it is optional and requires host
    22: support for affinity. Do not run other builds or timing children concurrently.
    23: The runner alternates A/B order. Even sample counts balance which binary runs
    24: first. Pinning one vCPU does not eliminate VM interference, CPU throttling,
    25: frequency changes, or shared-cache effects.
    26: 
    27: With no `--source`, the runner generates three deterministic self-checking C
    28: programs: 256 small functions with arities zero through four; a 512-step
    29: unsigned arithmetic chain; and an ABI/memory corpus covering zero through
    30: 24 parameters, register and stack arguments, a mixed integer/double aggregate
    31: argument and result, signed extension, indexed memory, and loop/branch forms.
    32: Python computes independent integer checksums modulo 2^64. `--check` executes
    33: them under each requested allocator and requires zero exit status and identical
    34: stdout/stderr bytes. It also exercises malformed command lines, empty and
    35: invalid sources, declaration-only input, and the current 25-argument selector
    36: fallback. Update that last fixture deliberately when the supported ABI limit
    37: changes; do not silently stop testing fallback rejection.
    38: 
    39: `--source path.c` is repeatable. Inputs must be self-contained: external
    40: include lookup is disabled. The input arena and macro-expansion budget are
    41: 64 MiB. Use the ordinary compiler driver to measure full include closures or
    42: other target/PIC settings rather than silently altering the workload to make
    43: this microbenchmark accept it. Custom executable workloads must return zero
    44: for success when `--check` is used.
    45: 
    46: ## What is timed
    47: 
    48: The command preprocesses, parses, analyzes, prepares/validates canonical IR
    49: through `ir_prepare_canonical_module`, and freezes target ABI records once.
    50: One untimed selection replay verifies every selected machine function and
    51: warms retained IR/metadata. A Release run then takes 30 samples; Debug takes
    52: five. Each sample prepares fresh module type facts and lazy call plans, selects
    53: all lowered functions with `machine_select_validated_canonical_function`, and
    54: rewinds caller-owned function scratch after every function. Module scratch is
    55: rewound after every module. The target is native and position-independent
    56: selection is disabled.
    57: 
    58: The reported selection interval includes the function walk, small work-count
    59: bookkeeping, selection, lazy call-plan construction, and arena rewind. It
    60: excludes frontend work, canonical preparation/validation, eager ABI-record
    61: preparation, MIR verification, allocation/placement, scheduling, encoding,
    62: object writing, and linking. Therefore it is **warm-IR selector replay**, not
    63: cold whole-compilation latency. In particular, a change to canonical promotion
    64: needs its own timing; do not claim this excludes no compiler work.
    65: 
    66: `BENCH_SELECT version=1` is one whitespace-separated key/value row:
    67: 
    68: | Field | Meaning |
    69: | --- | --- |
    70: | `iterations` | Timed inner samples, excluding warmup/verification |
    71: | `functions`, `fallback_functions` | Lowered functions attempted and unsupported attempts |
    72: | `ir_instructions` | Sum of selector-reported selected typed instruction counts |
    73: | `mir_instructions` | Sum of emitted `MachineInstruction` rows before placement/encoding |
    74: | `min_ns`, `median_ns` | Minimum and upper-middle median selection intervals, nanoseconds |
    75: | `prepare_median_ns` | Median eager module-preparation interval, nanoseconds |
    76: | `total_median_ns` | Median of paired preparation + selection intervals, not sum of medians |
    77: | `arena_bytes` | Sum of caller-owned function arena position deltas for one replay |
    78: | `peak_arena_bytes` | Maximum of those function deltas |
    79: | `module_bytes` | Sum of module arena deltas, including lazy plans |
    80: 
    81: `BENCH_SELECT_TARGET` records architecture, OS, CPU model and target features.
    82: The Python report preserves every inner-summary row, object-compilation wall
    83: time and SHA-256, compiler/source SHA-256, host, affinity, and build description.
    84: It summarizes outer samples using the median of selection medians, divided by
    85: `mir_instructions` to give **nanoseconds per emitted MIR row**. This denominator
    86: is neither encoded ISA instruction count nor host retired instructions; one
    87: MIR row can expand to multiple ISA instructions.
    88: 
    89: Arena deltas are not allocator-call counts, committed pages, total process
    90: allocation, or peak RSS. They exclude retained frontend IR and any allocation
    91: outside the supplied arenas. Use a separate allocator/RSS profile for those
    92: questions; do not label these fields as total compiler memory usage.
    93: 
    94: The runner separately starts a fresh `ide cc -g0 -O2` process for each object
    95: compilation and allocator. Its wall time includes startup, preprocessing,
    96: analysis, canonical preparation, selection or fallback, placement, encoding,
    97: object writing, and shutdown, but not linking. It does not drop the OS page
    98: cache. Run `test_self_host` as well for complete compiler executable generation.
    99: 
   100: ## Correctness and CI guardrails
   101: 
   102: There is no successful timing row for invalid IR, failed MIR verification,
   103: zero functions/instructions, unsupported functions, or unstable replay work.
   104: Declining selection coverage cannot manufacture a lower ns/MIR value. The
   105: runner rejects malformed/version-mismatched reports, duplicate or missing
   106: metrics, changed target/work counts, missing/empty output objects, mutated
   107: inputs/binaries, and changed object bytes. Old output objects are removed
   108: before every invocation. Program output comparison preserves raw bytes and
   109: keeps stdout separate from stderr; replacement UTF-8 decoding is not an oracle.
   110: 
   111: Object identity is intentionally strict for throughput-only transformations.
   112: An intentional change to selected code needs an independently reviewed
   113: semantic/ABI proof and quality comparison, not a disabled hash check disguised
   114: as a throughput win. This benchmark does not exercise placement/encoder
   115: fallback coverage directly; inspect ordinary verbose `CODEGEN_FALLBACK` and
   116: `CODEGEN_FALLBACK_STAGES` reports as well.
   117: 
   118: Archive JSON and fail CI on command/test/coverage failures. Do not fail a shared
   119: runner on a percentage threshold derived from one wall-clock run. Before an
   120: optimization is accepted, reproduce on the intended Zen 5 host with identical
   121: build policy, controlled repeated A/B order, all allocator regressions,
   122: self-hosting, applicable sanitizers, unchanged output/coverage, and both local
   123: selector and end-to-end results. Record cycles, retired instructions,
   124: branches/misses and cache counters separately when PMU access is available.
   125: Keep the NONE allocator as a control: it bypasses machine selection, so a
   126: similar apparent gain there is evidence against attributing the whole change
   127: to this selector experiment.

===== docs/metamorphic-testing.md =====

     1: # Source-equivalence metamorphic tests
     2: 
     3: `ide test` includes a deterministic, bounded native smoke campaign. `ide
     4: metamorphic` exercises a wider target matrix. Both are implemented in C in
     5: `src/buster/tests/compiler/metamorphic/metamorphic_test.c`; there is no script
     6: harness, source-rewriting dependency, or new compiler executable.
     7: 
     8: ## Run
     9: 
    10: Build normally, then run the native smoke tests through the existing test target:
    11: 
    12: ```sh
    13: ./build.sh build --config Release -t test_all
    14: ```
    15: 
    16: Run the wider campaign (four seeds by default):
    17: 
    18: ```sh
    19: build/Release/ide metamorphic
    20: ```
    21: 
    22: A larger deterministic campaign, with a fresh artifact directory:
    23: 
    24: ```sh
    25: BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_SEED=100 BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_CASES=16 BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_OUTPUT=build/metamorphic-seed-100 build/Release/ide metamorphic
    26: ```
    27: 
    28: The default uses direct frontend SSA. Set `BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_FRONTEND_SSA=0`
    29: to exercise the reference frontend explicitly with the same seeds and targets.
    30: Both independent reference and Buster invocations preserve the repository's wrap,
    31: aliasing and unsigned-plain-char options. This grammar itself uses unsigned
    32: arithmetic and does not rely on signed overflow or aliasing exceptions.
    33: 
    34: Require actual execution rather than accept compile-only rows on one native target:
    35: 
    36: ```sh
    37: BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_TARGET=linux-x64 BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_REQUIRE_EXECUTION=1 build/Release/ide metamorphic
    38: ```
    39: 
    40: Drive a second compiler binary with the same generator, oracle and reducer:
    41: 
    42: ```sh
    43: BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_COMPILER=/absolute/path/to/baseline/ide BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_CASES=1 BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_TRANSFORMS=256 BUSTER_METAMORPHIC_OUTPUT=build/metamorphic-baseline build/Release/ide metamorphic
    44: ```
    45: 
    46: The executable needs `BUSTER_INCLUDE_TESTS=1`. Shell environment assignment above
    47: is POSIX syntax; on Windows set the same environment variables before invoking
    48: `build/Release/ide.exe metamorphic`. Run from the repository root. Choose a fresh
    49: output directory: each pair and reducer replay owns a monotonically numbered
    50: `work-N` directory, and an existing campaign folder is not an append-only database.
    51: 
    52: ## Generated programs and semantic preconditions
    53: 
    54: The generator renders a small typed grammar, rather than modifying arbitrary C
    55: with regular expressions. A seed chooses one to three arithmetic terms, one to
    56: three loop iterations, and small constants. Eight fixed input pairs include zero,
    57: equal and unequal inputs, the 32-bit boundary, the 64-bit sign boundary, and
    58: `UINT64_MAX`. Computation uses `unsigned long long` on the supported 64-bit-integer
--- lines 121-211 ---
   121: Foreign native rows still compile and link when execution is unavailable. They
   122: are reported as `unexecuted`; no disassembly check is called a behavior check.
   123: A runner which is found but fails to launch/validate/execute is a failure, not a
   124: skip. Before a Wasm campaign, Node validates a fixed Memory64 module without
   125: extra options. If needed, the harness retries that capability probe with
   126: `--experimental-wasm-memory64` and uses the successful invocation for generated
   127: programs. If both probes fail, campaign setup fails explicitly before source
   128: generation or reduction. This supports both engines where Memory64 is enabled
   129: by default and older engines that require the flag.
   130: 
   131: The eBPF interpreter supports the generated subset and has bounded instruction
   132: execution and checked stack accesses. It does not implement local calls: only
   133: mask 1024 is excluded for that row, with an explicit
   134: `METAMORPHIC_TRANSFORMS_UNAVAILABLE` record. All previously supported relations
   135: and aggregate materialization still run. This is a coverage exclusion, not an
   136: execution pass for the call relation. This change adds multiplication to that
   137: existing interpreter, with separate 32- and 64-bit multiplication cases in its
   138: existing compiler tests. An interpreter refusal is reported as a runner failure,
   139: not incorrectly classified as a successful guest result or a proven compiler bug.
   140: 
   141: The local aggregate-copy relation is lowered by both nonnative backends.
   142: Wasm64 uses private shadow-stack snapshots and bulk memory operations; eBPF
   143: allocates each snapshot within its existing 512-byte frame and copies exact
   144: bytes without over-reading packed objects. Neither representation aliases a
   145: mutable source object. The canonical IR and aggregate function ABI contracts
   146: are unchanged. Aggregate block parameters and bit-field aggregate construction
   147: remain explicit unsupported cases; eBPF snapshot alignment is at most eight
   148: bytes, and oversized frames still fail with a diagnostic.
   149: 
   150: The same five repository-relative C cases cover plain, packed, nested and union
   151: copies plus independent mutations. The ordinary driver suite checks both
   152: frontend forms through Node for Wasm64; the existing codegen test module checks
   153: eBPF output in its bounded VM, including all input pairs at the signed boundary
   154: and wraparound. Negative cases retain eBPF aggregate ABI, alignment and frame
   155: limits. VM execution does not certify kernel verifier/JIT acceptance.
   156: 
   157: Wasm32 is not supported by the current driver. The external SPIR-V, NVPTX,
   158: AMDGCN, Metal and DXIL pipelines accept different source-language/toolchain
   159: contracts and reject native allocator options. They are **not covered** by this
   160: canonical-C harness. Neither are booting UEFI images or mobile/device deployment.
   161: GPU-specific source generation and device execution require separate adapters;
   162: this suite does not claim that coverage.
   163: 
   164: The ordinary test suite runs one seed across all native allocator modes: 48
   165: pairs, 96 compilations/executions, with no optional engine dependency. Desktop CI
   166: gets this smoke coverage from its existing `test_all` jobs. Mobile builds retain
   167: the preprocessing and harness self-tests and explicitly report native execution
   168: as unavailable.
   169: 
   170: ## Failure detection, reduction and artifacts
   171: 
   172: Compiler invocations and native/LLVM/Wasm execution use isolated child processes
   173: with a ten-second deadline. The comparator checks phase, launch status, timeout,
   174: process result, raw platform status, stdout and stderr. Equal crashes, equal
   175: nonzero self-check exits and equal timeouts are failures, never evidence of
   176: equivalence. Failure-class self-tests cover these cases and stream mismatches.
   177: Each pair and reducer replay writes its sources, intermediate artifacts and
   178: executables in a distinct `work-N` directory. The work index is claimed
   179: atomically, so parallel work items within one campaign cannot collide, and a
   180: later Windows compile never overwrites an executable image whose process has
   181: only just exited. Each compilation still clears its expected output paths and
   182: must produce a nonempty new artifact before consumption or execution. A compiler
   183: that exits successfully without writing output cannot reuse a preceding Clang
   184: reference executable or an earlier generated program.
   185: 
   186: For each distinct target/failure signature, up to 16 bundles are retained. The
   187: same signature in another allocator is still counted and reported, but does not
   188: repeat reduction. Each `failure-N` preserves the first observed outcomes and
   189: available source/artifact files under `observed-*` names before attempting a
   190: replay. Replay logs with exact argument vectors, `reproducer.txt`, and a
   191: `minimized` directory are retained separately, so a flaky replay cannot erase
   192: the initial failure evidence.
   193: 
   194: The reducer removes transformation bits, arithmetic terms and loops, simplifies
   195: constants and reduces the input count. It regenerates **both** programs from the
   196: same specification. A candidate is retained only after two replays preserve the
   197: original phase/status/diagnostic signature and kind of output mismatch. Source
   198: paths and locations are removed from compilation-diagnostic comparison so a
   199: smaller source can keep the same diagnostic. At most 64 candidate replays are
   200: allowed; timeout failures are saved without attempting expensive reduction.
   201: This is bounded grammar-aware reduction, not a claim of global minimality for
   202: arbitrary C. `signature_preserved` records the final replay result.
   203: 
   204: A five-minute campaign budget (one minute for ordinary smoke; five minutes when
   205: the compiler itself is sanitized), checked between work
   206: units, turns incomplete campaigns into failures. The current bounded pair or
   207: reduction can finish after that budget; it is not a hard wall-clock supervisor
   208: for the entire process. Pair scratch storage is rewound, while only the capped
   209: set of unique failure signatures remains retained.
   210: 
   211: Reduced cases are artifacts, not automatically accepted compiler fixes. Check

    78: Without `--baseline-ide`, the same compiler supplies its direct `none` reference.

    84: ## Frozen inventory and matrix
    85: 
    86: `git ls-files -z -- tests` supplies the sorted input inventory. Every tracked
    87: `.c` file is a subject except twelve explicitly named diagnostic-rejection
    88: fixtures. Every input's role, byte count and `buster_hash_64` fingerprint
    89: is recorded, including excluded inputs. The decision uses exact paths:
    90: `basic_c_negative_constant_widening.c` remains a positive subject. Dormant `.bbb`
    91: files never become compilation rows. Headers and other support files are copied
    92: with the subjects, preserving their relative paths. Compilation reads these

   111: their diagnostic wording. The literal-register assembly case is an intentional
   112: codegen rejection; it is not a supported native subject. Excluded source bytes
   113: remain in `inputs.tsv` and the snapshot. Counts are discovered afresh; newly
   114: tracked C fixtures are rejected until a reviewed contract update explicitly
   115: classifies and hashes them. Nothing untracked silently enters a run.
   116:

   118:

   120: | --- | --- |
   121: | `tests/basic_c_constexpr.c` | `-std=c23` |
   122: | `tests/basic_c_constexpr_leaf.c` | `-std=c23` |
   123: | `tests/basic_c_nullptr.c` | `-std=c23` |
   124: | `tests/basic_c_typeof.c` | `-std=c23` |
   125: | `tests/basic_c_dialect.c` | `-std=c23 -DEXPECTED_STDC_VERSION=202311L -DEXPECTED_GNU=0` |
   126: | `tests/basic_c_predicate_bank.c` | x86-64 uses `-mcpu=skylake-avx512`; other architectures retain the manifest CPU |
   127: | `tests/basic_c_atomic_aggregate.c` | x86-64 uses `-mcpu=haswell` for the required `cx16`; other architectures retain the manifest CPU |
   128: 
   129: The first three settings match their registered driver tests. The `typeof`
   130: fixture uses `typeof_unqual`, whose C23 keyword gate is covered by the C frontend
   131: tests. The dialect recipe selects the registered strict C23 variant; the driver's
   132: other seven GNU/strict dialect variants remain separate coverage. Other inputs
   133: retain the pinned compiler's dialect default, including similarly named files.
   134: `inputs.tsv` freezes each recipe name and exact added flags; `rows.tsv` repeats
   135: the recipe name, and executed children retain every argument byte in `.argv`.
   136: 
   137: Executed rows require `--resource-include`. The harness refuses symbolic links,
   138: copies that complete tree into `dependencies/resource-include`, records every
   139: file's SHA-256 in `dependencies.tsv`, and hashes the ordered closure. Both
   140: compiler legs then receive `-nostdinc -isystem <frozen-copy>`; the resource path
   141: compiled into either executable and host include search paths are not used.
   142: Object rows intentionally have no host sysroot. Linux GNU rows receive only the
   143: target-matched, authenticated musl include roots from the project snapshot;
   144: Windows, Apple, Android and UEFI rows do not receive those Linux headers.
   145: 
   146: Repo-owned project dependencies use the checked-in
   147: [`native-retirement-dependencies-v1.json`](native-retirement-dependencies-v1.json)
   148: descriptor. Before `evidence-candidate.txt` is created, the workflow runs the
   149: offline external-closure verifier against the exact candidate checkout first.
   150: That verifier proves pristine GitHub worktrees at the seven descriptor pins
   151: (cJSON, DoomGeneric, LZ4, yyjson, stb, zlib and musl), checks each admitted
   152: path as a tracked blob at that revision, and derives only musl's upstream
   153: `alltypes.h`/`syscall.h` outputs for x86-64 and AArch64. It performs no fetch and
   154: does not vendor upstream files into the repository. The materializer then admits
   155: only the listed paths after matching their authenticated byte count and SHA-256,
   156: rejects source symlinks, hard links, descriptor/output-parent symlinks, TOCTOU
   157: changes, and all network provenance (including SCP/SSH spellings), and publishes
   158: the tree atomically at `evidence/dependency-materialized`. Generated metadata
   159: names are reserved. Every destination is exactly its kind's compiler include
   160: root (`dependencies/resource-include` or `dependencies/project-include`) and the
   161: include-relative path is one global namespace: a `same.h` resource and project
   162: record cannot coexist. Normalized duplicate destinations or provenance,
   163: kind/root mismatches, arbitrary destinations, and metadata collisions fail
   164: closed; an exact repeated resource is emitted once in deterministic order. A
   165: full census must provide both the project include and the descriptor/receipt
   166: paths shown above. The C producer replays the materializer's authenticated
   167: project closure and ledger digests and copies the exact descriptor, receipt, and
   168: materializer ledger into evidence; alternate self-consistent dependency trees
   169: are rejected by the independent validator.
   170: 
   171: The materializer also requires a canonical descriptor-relative `source_root`
   172: spelling and rejects control characters in fixture labels before serializing
   173: its ledger. During census startup, each resource/project header copy is read
   174: back and SHA-256 checked before it is admitted to the compiler include closure;
   175: a truncated or otherwise altered snapshot therefore fails the dependency
   176: contract before any object row runs.

     1: `2026-08-09ag` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 5 —
     2: copy coalescing: the largest single quality win of the project.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** Two halves. The encoder skips a full-width
     5:   MOV_RR whose operands landed on the same register (the narrower
     6:   moves are *not* identities — they clear the upper bits, so only the
     7:   64-bit form qualifies). The allocator then makes that case common:
     8:   when a copy's source virtual register has no use after this row —
     9:   non-escaping and its last use is this instruction, already consumed
    10:   by the use pass — the destination binds to the source's register and
    11:   ownership transfers directly, without routing through an eviction
    12:   that would write a dying value back to a slot nobody reads.
    13: - **Why it pays so much here.** The selector mirrors the canonical
    14:   path, which materializes a copy for nearly every value-producing
    15:   construct (casts, unary setup, address staging). Under MIR_STACK
    16:   those copies are load/store pairs; under FRA they were
    17:   register-to-register movs; now most of them are nothing at all.
    18: - **Numbers** (buster-built stage comparison, compiling ide.c under
    19:   NONE): fast-built compiler **47.21G instructions, from 53.28G
    20:   (-11.4% in one step)** — against canonical's 70.05G that is
    21:   **-32.6%**. Text 20,057,883, from 20,787,008 (canonical 25,699,964,
    22:   **-22.0%**).
    23: - **Gates:** test_all green with a new regression guard (the fast
    24:   encoding of the loop corpus function must stay strictly smaller than
    25:   the stack encoding, so a future change cannot silently disable
    26:   coalescing), MIR and FAST soaks byte-identical on fresh references,
    27:   self-host fixed point holds.

     1: `2026-08-09ah` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 5 —
     2: allocator traffic metrics, and two negative results they explain.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** `cc -v` now reports `CODEGEN_ALLOCATOR reloads=
     5:   spills= boundary_spills= copies=` summed over the machine-emitted
     6:   functions, splitting boundary write-backs from eviction pressure
     7:   because the two want different fixes. Also a small correctness
     8:   refinement: once an instruction's uses and defines are placed, a
     9:   value whose last use *is* that instruction has been read for the last
    10:   time, so the call flush and the block write-back drop its store
    11:   instead of keeping the strict "past the last use" test.
    12: - **The measurement that matters.** FAST against MIR_STACK on the same
    13:   compile: reloads **41,253 vs 988,799 (-95.8%)**, spills **90,157 vs
    14:   968,541 (-90.7%)**, plus 58,268 register copies FAST introduces and
    15:   MIR_STACK cannot. Only **2,805 of 90,157 spills (3.1%)** come from
    16:   block boundaries.
    17: - **Negative result 1 — deferring the boundary write-back.** When a
    18:   block's sole successor inherits its register file, the write-back can
    19:   defer down the chain. Implemented, byte-identical, and worthless:
    20:   spills moved 90,154 -> 90,157 and text grew 26KB from shifted
    21:   allocation decisions. The 3.1% boundary share is the reason, and the
    22:   earlier flat result for straight-line inheritance (`2026-08-09w`) has
    23:   the same root: this frontend's block graph has almost no
    24:   single-predecessor/single-successor chains. Reverted. **Do not
    25:   retry any boundary-write-back optimization without first moving that
    26:   3.1%.**
    27: - **Negative result 2 — a loop-reentry floor for escaping values.**
    28:   Escaping values can never be declared dead, which looked like the
    29:   reason spills (90K) run 2.2x reloads (41K). Added a floor — the
    30:   lowest instruction any backward edge can land on — so an escaping
    31:   value whose last use sits below it retires for good. Zero effect
    32:   (90,157 -> 90,161). Reverted. The ratio needed no fix: read-modify-
    33:   write rows re-dirty a value after each reload, so
    34:   `spills ~= reloads + values-ever-spilled` is the expected shape, and
    35:   49K distinct values spilling once each accounts for it exactly.

     1: `2026-08-09ai` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 7
     2: lead — constant rematerialization, taken early because it is local.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** A pre-pass marks every virtual register whose
     5:   entire definition is one constant materialization; a second definition
     6:   of any kind disables the recipe, since which constant is current would
     7:   then depend on the path. Such a value never pays for a store and never
     8:   occupies a frame slot: eviction drops it silently and a later reload
     9:   becomes `MACHINE_EDIT_REMATERIALIZE`, which re-emits the immediate.
    10: - **Two latent bugs fixed on the way.** The slot-needed derivation keyed
    11:   on every edit's `subject`, but a copy edit's subject is a *physical
    12:   register* and a rematerialization's is an *immediate index*. With few
    13:   virtual registers in a function that write ran past the end of the
    14:   array — a live out-of-bounds write introduced with copy edits in
    15:   `2026-08-09v` and never triggered because the arrays were usually long
    16:   enough. The derivation now filters on edit kind. Separately, the first
    17:   draft of the remat table let a constant definition *after* a
    18:   non-constant one enable the recipe; a definition-seen flag fixes it.
    19: - **Numbers** (buster-built stage comparison, compiling ide.c under
    20:   NONE): spills **90,157 -> 77,394 (-14.2%)**, reloads **41,253 ->
    21:   32,693 (-20.7%)**, with 8,570 rematerializations taking their place —
    22:   21,323 memory operations removed for 8,570 immediate loads. Frame
    23:   bytes 3,663,056 -> 3,602,392. Instructions 47.07G (canonical 70.05G,
    24:   **-32.8%**), text 20,038,638.
    25: - **Honest scale note:** the instruction win is small (-0.3%) because a
    26:   rematerialization replaces a reload one-for-one and only the dropped
    27:   *stores* are pure profit. The memory-traffic and frame-size wins are
    28:   the real result, and the out-of-bounds fix is worth the patch on its
    29:   own.

===== docs/performance-audits/2026-08-09al.md =====
--- lines 3-51 ---
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** `machine_quality_placement_build`: a live interval
     5:   and a weight per virtual register, loop extension across every backward
     6:   edge, a max-heap priority walk, and greedy assignment of the
     7:   highest-weight non-overlapping intervals to callee-saved registers for
     8:   the whole function. The local scan then places everything else around
     9:   the pins and never picks, binds, spills, or reloads a pinned value.
    10:   Callee-saved is the class that makes a whole-function binding sound
    11:   without a clobber analysis: calls preserve it and every encoder scratch
    12:   and macro-op sequence in this backend works out of the caller-saved
    13:   half. Functions with a case table opt out, because switch targets live
    14:   outside the block-ref operands the loop extension walks.
    15: - **A pin verifier is part of the mode, not a debug aid.** After
    16:   placement, every operand naming a pinned register must belong to that
    17:   pin's value, and no edit may land on one; a violation falls back to the
    18:   local allocator. It earned itself immediately: copy coalescing steals a
    19:   dying source's register, and when that source was pinned it handed a
    20:   globally-reserved register to an unrelated value. The symptom was
    21:   `lea r15,[rbp-0x310]` / `mov r15,rax` / `mov [r15],r15` — a store
    22:   through a pointer that had just been overwritten by the value being
    23:   stored. Coalescing now refuses pinned registers.
    24: - **The negative result, measured four ways.** Compiling ide.c, FAST is
    25:   **45.16G** instructions. QUALITY: five callee-saved registers ungated
    26:   **49.28G**; gated on crossing a call **45.74G**; also requiring loop
    27:   residency **45.64G**; capped at two registers **45.35G**. Every
    28:   loosening costs more, and the limit of the series is FAST itself.
    29: - **Why.** A pin costs a push and a pop on every entry, and it removes
    30:   the register from the local pool for the whole function — allocator
    31:   traffic confirms the pressure, with spills and copies rising as pin
    32:   count rises. FRA already binds callee-saved registers for call-crossing
    33:   values where it locally pays, so it collects most of the benefit
    34:   without the function-wide reservation. The self-host corpus is not
    35:   register-pressure-bound, which is exactly the corpus the plan's
    36:   stage-7 acceptance criterion ("quality wins over FRA on pressure
    37:   corpus") asks about.
    38: - **Status against the plan.** Stage 7 lands its scaffolding — exact-ish
    39:   intervals, priority queue, hints, budget bound
    40:   (`MACHINE_QUALITY_MAXIMUM_CANDIDATES`), rematerialization (already in
    41:   FAST from `2026-08-09ai`) — but **not** its acceptance criterion.
    42:   QUALITY must stay opt-in and must not become any optimization level's
    43:   default until it wins on a pressure corpus. Eviction cascades, live
    44:   range splitting, and stage 8 recoloring are the remaining levers that
    45:   could change the verdict; splitting is the one that directly attacks
    46:   the cost measured here, since it would let a pin cover only the loop
    47:   that needs it instead of the whole function.
    48: - **Gates:** test_all green (a corpus assertion holds QUALITY's traffic
    49:   at or below the everything-in-slots baseline), all three soaks —
    50:   MIR_STACK, FAST, QUALITY — byte-identical on fresh references,
    51:   self-host fixed point holds.

===== docs/performance-audits/2026-08-09an.md =====

     1: `2026-08-09an` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 7 —
     2: QUALITY stops guessing and starts measuring, and finally wins.)
     3: 
     4: - **What changed.** Every heuristic from `2026-08-09al` is gone —
     5:   crossing a call, loop residency, occurrence weights, the register-file
     6:   cap. QUALITY now runs the local scan once with no pins, counts the
     7:   memory edits each value actually cost, and pins by that measured
     8:   traffic: a value must have cost at least three edits, because the pin
     9:   it earns adds a push and a pop. The priority heap is keyed on real
    10:   traffic instead of a guess.
    11: - **Acceptance on modeled improvement.** The pinned placement is
    12:   compared against the baseline it was derived from and kept only if
    13:   `traffic_after + 2 * newly_reserved_registers < traffic_before`.
    14:   A pin also raises local pressure, which can add traffic elsewhere, and
    15:   this test sees that because it measures the whole placement rather
    16:   than the intended saving. QUALITY therefore cannot be worse than FAST
    17:   by construction, which is what stage 8's "accepted only on modeled
    18:   improvement" rule asks for, applied a stage early.
    19: - **Numbers** (compiling ide.c): QUALITY **45.137G** instructions
    20:   against FAST's **45.169G**, text 19,445,006 against 19,447,822.
    21:   Reloads 30,303 vs 32,205 (-5.9%), spills 76,403 vs 77,012. Pins fall
    22:   from 12,116 under the heuristics to **640** — two orders of magnitude
    23:   more selective, and the first configuration to come out ahead.
    24: - **Honest scale.** The win is 0.07%. The self-host corpus is not
    25:   register-pressure-bound, so there is little for a global allocator to
    26:   recover; the result that matters is that the mechanism is sound,
    27:   self-limiting, and measured rather than assumed. A pressure corpus is
    28:   needed before stage 7's acceptance criterion can be called met in
    29:   spirit as well as in letter.
    30: - **Gates:** test_all green, MIR, FAST and QUALITY soaks all

===== docs/performance-audits/2026-08-09ao.md =====
