     1: `2026-08-09ao` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; the pressure corpus, and the
     2: finding that reframes the rest of the register-allocator plan.)
     3: 
     4: **Read this before starting stage 8, 9, or any further allocator work.**
     5: 
     6: - **What was built.** `tests/basic_c_register_pressure.c`: sixteen values
     7:   live across a loop (more than the allocatable file), eight values live
     8:   across a call in every iteration, and a deep expression tree whose
     9:   intermediates all survive to one combine. It self-checks, so it is an
    10:   execution test under every mode as well as a benchmark. Built because
    11:   `2026-08-09al` and `ak` could not evaluate QUALITY honestly on the
    12:   self-host sources, which keep almost nothing live.
    13: - **Numbers** (200 iterations of the three bodies, executed
    14:   instructions): canonical **395.95M**, MIR_STACK **595.95M**, FAST
    15:   **186.92M (-52.8% against canonical)**, QUALITY **186.92M**, and
    16:   `clang -O2` **95.37M**. So FAST more than halves the canonical
    17:   emitter's work under real pressure — a far larger margin than the
    18:   -35% seen on the self-host sources — and lands within 1.96x of clang.
    19: - **QUALITY is bit-for-bit FAST here, on the corpus written to favour
    20:   it.** Its allocator traffic explains why: over the whole corpus the
    21:   local scan emits **1 reload, 24 spills, 0 pins**. There is nothing to
    22:   allocate globally.
    23: - **Root cause, and it is not in the allocator.** The C frontend keeps
    24:   every local in memory. `a0 += a1 ^ a15` lowers to load, load, compute,
    25:   store, so the only values the allocator ever sees are the temporaries
    26:   between one load and the next store. The generated loop body is a
    27:   procession of `mov -0x10(%rbp),%r8` / `mov %r8,-0x28(%rbp)` pairs.
    28:   Sixteen simultaneously live C variables are, to the allocator, sixteen
    29:   independent two-instruction lifetimes.
    30: - **What this means for the plan.** Stage 8 (recoloring, regional graph
    31:   colouring) and stage 9 (pressure-aware scheduling) both optimize the
    32:   assignment of long-lived values to registers. Neither can pay while
    33:   there are no long-lived values. The missing pass is promotion of
    34:   address-not-taken locals to virtual registers — mem2reg — and it is
    35:   worth more than every remaining allocator stage combined: it is the
    36:   bulk of the 1.96x gap to clang, and it is the precondition that makes
    37:   QRA's machinery meaningful. **Do that first.**
    38: - **Corollary for the wins already banked.** The gains from
    39:   `2026-08-09ag` (copy coalescing) and `ag`/`ah` (folded addressing) were
    40:   large precisely because they attack the short-lifetime, copy-heavy
    41:   shape this lowering produces. That was the right thing to optimize for
    42:   the IR as it stands, and it stays right after promotion lands.
    43: - **Gates:** test_all green, the corpus executes identically under NONE,
    44:   MIR_STACK, FAST and QUALITY.
===== docs/performance-audits/2026-08-09ap.md =====
--- lines 1-39 ---
     1: `2026-08-09ap` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; local promotion built,
     2: measured, and reverted — with the sequencing it proves.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was tried.** The pass `2026-08-09ao` called for: at selection,
     5:   every C local of register width whose address never leaves a load or a
     6:   store becomes a virtual register instead of a frame slot, so loads and
     7:   stores of it become copies. Roughly 90 lines in the selector: a
     8:   two-pass promotability scan (eligible by type, then disqualified by any
     9:   use that is not the place of a same-width scalar load or store), vreg
    10:   creation in classification, copy lowering in the LOAD and STORE cases,
    11:   and a refusal in the address helper so a promoted local can never
    12:   acquire an address behind the analysis's back.
    13: - **It was correct.** test_all green and the FAST soak byte-identical —
    14:   the promoted compiler still reproduces canonical stage-2 bytes exactly.
    15: - **It was slower, on both corpora.** Self-host: **46.72G** instructions
    16:   against 45.17G (+3.4%), text +0.9%. Pressure corpus: FAST **212.3M**
    17:   against 186.9M, QUALITY **205.8M**.
    18: - **Why, in one number.** Boundary spills went from 2,891 to **26,672**,
    19:   a factor of nine; reloads tripled, 32,205 to 95,957. Promotion does
    20:   exactly what it promises — it turns short two-instruction lifetimes
    21:   into long-lived values — and the local scan then writes every one of
    22:   them back at every block boundary, which for a loop body is the store
    23:   and load per iteration that promotion was supposed to remove, plus the
    24:   copies.
    25: - **The sequencing this proves.** On the pressure corpus QUALITY beat
    26:   FAST for the first time with promotion in place (205.8M vs 212.3M):
    27:   the global layer only has something to hold once values are long-lived.
    28:   So the two changes are a pair. Promotion alone is a regression;
    29:   promotion plus cross-block register assignment is the design clang is
    30:   beating us with. **Land them together, or not at all**, and the
    31:   gating measurement is boundary spills, not instruction count.
    32: - **What is needed for the pair.** Full stage-5 edge contracts: agreeing
    33:   a register assignment across each edge and resolving the difference
    34:   with parallel copies, so a promoted local stays in its register through
    35:   a loop instead of round-tripping at every boundary. Stage 8 recoloring
    36:   refines that; it does not substitute for it.
    37: - **State of the tree.** Reverted — the branch keeps the 45.17G / -35.5%
    38:   configuration. The patch is described here in enough detail to rebuild
    39:   in an afternoon, and should be rebuilt only alongside edge contracts.

     1: `2026-08-09s` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 4 —
     2: the FAST local allocator, first allocator to survive the soak.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** `register_allocator_fast.c`: a forward block-local
     5:   scan over the machine IR producing the same placement contract the
     6:   encoder already consumes (per-slot `operand_registers` plus point-sorted
     7:   reload/spill edits), so the encoder is byte-for-byte shared with
     8:   MIR_STACK. Allocatable file {RAX,RCX,RDX,RSI,RDI,R8-R11}, LRU eviction
     9:   by age clock, lazy dirty spills at BEFORE points, constrained opcodes
    10:   keep their canonical scratch layout, calls and terminators flush
    11:   (block-local state; everything caller-saved). Fixed-register hazards
    12:   all bind in place: a MOV_RR use into a fixed physical destination
    13:   stages its source in that register, and a MOV_RR def *from* a fixed
    14:   physical source (entry captures, call results) binds the vreg in the
    15:   source register itself.
    16: - **Four placement/encoder bugs found by the soak, none by unit tests
    17:   at first.** (1) The encoder's edit-merge loops assumed RELOAD@BEFORE /
    18:   SPILL@AFTER and emitted FRA's BEFORE-point spills as loads — both loops
    19:   dispatch on `edit->kind` now. (2) LEA_FRAME/LEA_SYMBOL dropped REX.R,
    20:   so `lea → r10` encoded as `lea → rdx`. (3) An argument-staging reload
    21:   free-picked a register that already held a placed argument
    22:   (os_file_write wrote base64 garbage instead of an ELF). (4) The entry
    23:   argument captures free-picked destinations in enumeration order, so
    24:   capture #2 bound RCX and destroyed incoming argument 4 before its own
    25:   capture read it — os_reserve passed flags=0 to mmap (EBADF) and the
    26:   fast-built compiler died in arena creation. A function needs four or
    27:   more register arguments to expose it; the corpus had `six()` but the
    28:   FAST section never executed it. The FAST differential now runs six()
    29:   (red before the fix: none=654321 fast=650341, exactly d replaced by b).
    30: - **Gates:** machine_tests 20088-suite green including the new capture
    31:   differential; test_all green; fixed point holds; MIR soak and **FAST
    32:   soak both byte-identical** (fast-built compiler reproduces canonical
    33:   stage-2 bytes exactly). Debug bisection knob removed from codegen.c.
    34: - **Stage-4 quality numbers** (buster-built stage comparison — validation
    35:   metrics, not clang-binary perf tracking): compiling ide.c, the
    36:   canonical-built compiler executes 70.05G instructions, the
    37:   mir-stack-built compiler 80.26G (+14.6%), the fast-built compiler
    38:   70.77G (+1.0%) — FRA recovers ~93% of the everything-in-slots penalty
    39:   at 52.9% machine coverage. Text bytes: canonical 25,699,964; mir-stack
    40:   26,602,780 (+3.5%); fast 25,676,908 (marginally below canonical).
    41: - **Method note, paid for twice:** rebuild the byte-identity oracle from
    42:   the current tree immediately before every bisection run. A stale
    43:   reference (or a reference the failing chain never wrote) makes `cmp`
    44:   fail universally and fingers an innocent function; both false leads
    45:   cost real time.

     1: `2026-08-09t` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 5,
     2: first slice — liveness-driven spill kills put FAST ahead of canonical.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** Two linear pre-passes over the machine IR before
     5:   the forward scan: defining block per vreg (defs dominate uses but
     6:   layout order does not prove precedence, hence the separate pass), then
     7:   last textual use and a block-escape flag. A dirty register whose
     8:   non-escaping owner is strictly past its last use drops its spill store,
     9:   and eviction prefers dead owners over LRU (displacing them costs
    10:   nothing). Escaping values always reach their slots, which keeps
    11:   loop-carried values and goto layout-order hazards safe by construction
    12:   — the block-boundary flush contract is unchanged.
    13: - **Numbers** (buster-built stage comparison, compiling ide.c under
    14:   NONE): fast-built compiler 63.76G instructions vs canonical 70.05G —
    15:   **9.0% below the canonical stack emitter**, from +1.0% in
    16:   `2026-08-09s`; the everything-in-slots penalty was +14.6%. Text
    17:   24,958,388 vs canonical 25,699,964 (−2.9%). Block-local expression
    18:   temporaries dominate the vreg population, so killing their dead stores
    19:   converts most of MIR_STACK's store traffic into pure register traffic
    20:   at 52.9% machine coverage.
    21: - **Gates:** test_all green (20088 unit / 30 module), FAST soak
    22:   byte-identical on fresh references, self-host fixed point holds.
    23: - **Left open for the rest of stage 5:** traces and edge location
    24:   contracts (values still reload once per block), per-preg future-active
    25:   buckets, loop-carried retention in registers, and edge parallel-copy
    26:   resolution.

     1: `2026-08-09v` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; register-allocator stage 6 —
     2: callee-saved registers, and register-copy edits instead of memory moves.)
     3: 
     4: - **What was built.** Three coupled pieces. (1) RBX/R14/R15 join the
     5:   allocatable file (R12/R13 wait on their ModRM base quirks): the
     6:   encoder pushes the placement's callee-saved mask after the frame
     7:   pointer in fixed order and restores through `lea rsp,[rbp-8N]` plus
     8:   reversed pops; unwind actions cover each push (X64Register and the
     9:   DWARF CFI map gained R12-R15; the machine-path unwind capacity rose to
    10:   six). Call flushes keep the callee-saved members. (2) A per-block
    11:   next-call pre-pass: only values that stay live past the next call bind
    12:   callee-saved registers — the first, indiscriminate version *lost* 1.8%
    13:   instructions and 38KB of text to push/pop pairs on values that never
    14:   crossed a call. (3) `MACHINE_EDIT_COPY`: when a value must move to a
    15:   fixed register (argument staging, encoder scratches) and already lives
    16:   in a register, the placement emits one register copy carrying its
    17:   dirtiness instead of a park store plus reload through its slot.
    18: - **Numbers** (buster-built stage comparison, compiling ide.c under
    19:   NONE): fast-built compiler 63.58G instructions (canonical 70.05G,
    20:   **-9.2%**; the previous entry stood at 63.62G), text 24,739,532
    21:   (canonical 25,699,964, -3.7%). Callee-saved alone was net negative
    22:   even with the crossing heuristic (63.67G) — the copy edits are what
    23:   turn retention into profit, because a retained value's next use
    24:   usually stages into a fixed argument register.
    25: - **Gates:** test_all green, FAST soak byte-identical on fresh
    26:   references, self-host fixed point holds.

    13: - **What moved.** A stack-passed argument was placed immediately after the one
    14:   before it, so an argument wanting more than eight bytes of alignment landed
    15:   wherever the pushes left it. `codegen_canonical_x64_call_layout` now records
    16:   each stack argument at an offset rounded up to its own alignment and the
    17:   area's own alignment alongside it; the `IR_OPCODE_ARGUMENT` prologue walks
    18:   the incoming area by the same rule, and the `va_arg` overflow cursor rounds
    19:   before reading. A call whose area wants more than sixteen bytes cannot be
    20:   built by pushing at all — it saves the stack pointer to a frame slot, lowers
    21:   and rounds it down, fills the area with `mov`, and restores from the slot.
    22: - **What it cost and why it was paid anyway.** The gate moves for three
    23:   additions, all of them per value or per argument rather than per
    24:   instruction: the frame loop's flag for the save slot, the code-buffer
    25:   reserve for an area filled an eightbyte at a time, and the rounding in the
    26:   layout and prologue walks. **Two shapes were measured.** Computing the prior
    27:   parameter's alignment once at the top of the prologue's walk instead of
    28:   inside the branches that place a stack argument is *not* where the cost is:
    29:   making it lazy measured `5.2078 G` against `5.2073 G`, inside the `54 K`
    30:   spread two runs of identical code show. Reading the flag and the reserve off
    31:   the `slot_alignment` the two value loops already compute, instead of loading
    32:   `layout.alignment` again, is worth `2.3 M` and is what is in the tree; it
    33:   over-approximates — an over-aligned local that is never an argument also
    34:   reserves the eight bytes — which costs a frame slot and no work.
    35: - **The reserve is the part to revisit.** `aligned_argument_capacity` pays
    36:   `15` bytes per eightbyte plus `32` for every value wider than sixteen bytes,
    37:   because the flat 48-bytes-per-instruction module reserve does not carry a
    38:   call that copies a 64-byte argument in eightbytes. It is charged per value
    39:   and not per call that actually passes one, since finding those needs the
    40:   call-layout pre-pass only Windows runs today. **If this is wanted back**, the
    41:   shape is a flag on `CodegenBuffer` set only where `codegen_emit_u8` refuses a
    42:   byte and surfaced on the result, so a short estimate becomes a retry with
    43:   more room rather than a `CODEGEN_ERROR_CAPACITY` that cannot be told apart
    44:   from the ones a bigger buffer will never fix — an out-of-range frame
    45:   displacement, a frame past `UINT32_MAX`. The flat per-instruction reserve is
    46:   short for the same reason anywhere an instruction moves an aggregate, so
    47:   that flag would pay for more than this entry.

     9: - **What moved.** The module code buffer was reserved at a flat 48 bytes per
    10:   IR instruction on x86-64 (128 on aarch64), but an instruction that moves an
    11:   aggregate encodes a load and a store per eightbyte, so its size grows with
    12:   the type and not with the instruction count. Two 64-byte vectors by value
    13:   was already more code than a whole small module was given, and the buffer
    14:   ran out. `codegen_generate_canonical_module` now adds a reserve for the
    15:   values wider than an eightbyte that each instruction can move — its own and
    16:   every operand it reads — which costs one walk of the instruction and operand
    17:   arrays per function that holds such a value.
    18: - **What it cost and why it was paid anyway.** The walk is the whole `+0.78%`:
    19:   a `perf` line profile of one stage-1 compile splits it about evenly between
    20:   filling the per-value reserve alongside the frame-slot loop that already
    21:   reads every value's type, and the instruction and operand walk itself. Two
    22:   cheaper shapes were measured and rejected — recomputing each operand's type
    23:   in the walk instead of tabling it per value is worse, and splitting the table
    24:   fill into a second value pass taken only by functions that hold a wide value
    25:   is also worse, because most C functions hold one. Those two were measured
    26:   before this work was rebased, against the pre-`2026-08-09h` main, where the
    27:   shipped shape cost `+0.96%` (`5.1329 G` to `5.1822 G`) against the other
    28:   two's `+1.59%` and `+1.27%`; the ordering is what the numbers are for, not
    29:   the absolute values. The alternative that costs nothing in the
    30:   common case is to keep the cheap estimate and generate the module again with
    31:   more room when it runs out; it was left untaken because
    32:   `CODEGEN_ERROR_CAPACITY` is also raised for reasons a bigger buffer cannot
    33:   fix (an out-of-range frame displacement, a frame past `UINT32_MAX`), so a
    34:   retry needs a signal that the code buffer specifically overflowed, and there
    35:   is no return path in that function that carries one today. **If this
    36:   percent is wanted back, that is the shape to build**: one flag on

     9: - **What moved.** x86-64 SystemV and Darwin can now pass and return a vector
    10:   wider than any register the target owns. `ir_classify_abi_value` classifies
    11:   a vector by the psABI rule alone — a 512-bit vector is one
    12:   `IR_ABI_CLASS_VECTOR` part whatever the machine — so the canonical backend
    13:   is where the target gets a say. Two helpers say it once:
    14:   `codegen_canonical_x64_vector_part_registers` reports how many consecutive
    15:   registers a part occupies and how much each carries, and
    16:   `codegen_canonical_x64_abi_value_in_registers` answers whether the value
    17:   fits the registers its classification named. A return and a call result
    18:   split across as many registers as it takes — `xmm0`–`xmm3` for a 64-byte
    19:   vector without AVX, `ymm0`/`ymm1` with it; an argument that does not fit one
    20:   register is passed in memory, because it competes for a shared pool a return
    21:   does not. Both are what clang emits for the same declaration, verified by
    22:   linking the two compilers' halves of one program at all three widths, both
    23:   directions, at 32 stack offsets each and under `gdb`.
    24: - **What it cost.** Three predicate calls per argument — the call layout, the
    25:   callee's own argument, and each argument before it in the callee's
    26:   register-accounting walk, which was already quadratic in the parameter
    27:   count. The cost is the calls, not their work: making the answer for a
    28:   scalar part a single `size > 16` compare instead of a CPU-feature-set walk
    29:   moved nothing measurable, and the figure only came down (`-1.8 M`, measured
    30:   before this was rebased) when the two 48- and 56-byte structs stopped being
    31:   passed by value. That is the floor for this shape. **If this tenth of a
    32:   percent is wanted back**, the shape is to fold the predicate into the
    33:   classification the backend already reads, so the answer is computed once per
    34:   type per convention where `IrTypeAbi` caches it rather than once per
    35:   argument occurrence — which needs that cache keyed by target and not only by
    36:   convention.
    37: - **What this depended on.** The stack-passed half of it only works because
    38:   `2026-08-10a` aligned the System V outgoing argument area first. This work
    39:   found that gap and left it — a stack-passed 512-bit vector read back with
    40:   `vmovaps zmm` agreed or faulted by where the stack happened to be — and
    41:   `2026-08-10a` took it, which is why `vector_ninth`'s spilled ninth argument
    42:   is deterministic here and was a lottery when it was written. The two land
    43:   in either order; only together do they make the fixture's nine-vector shape

    66: - **Two latent holes closed on the way.** The loop extension ran once in
    67:   block order, so overlapping goto loops could leave an interval

    77:   opt-in). And the span-aware pin verifier now also rejects a copy

    47: - **Flag safety is by construction, verified against every edit form.**
    48:   The fused compare is the row immediately before the terminator, so

    50:   FLAGS_USE (the machine.c attributes already stated the contract;
    51:   nothing consumed them). Every edit form is a flag-preserving move on
    52:   both targets: frame load/store movs, register-copy movs, and movabs
    53:   rematerialization on x86-64; ldr/str, orr copies, and movz/movk
    54:   rematerialization on AArch64. The disassembly shows the shape
    55:   working: a spill mov sits between `cmp` and `jb` in the fused
    56:   wide_live_loop head, exactly the allowed intruder.
    57: - **Sinking the reads is the one soundness obligation.** The fused
    58:   compare reads its operands at the branch row instead of the
    59:   member's, and on x86-64 promoted locals are the one source of
    60:   multi-definition vregs: a store between the compare and the branch
    61:   would redefine what the sunk read sees. The marking walk stamps
    62:   every promoted local's latest store ordinal and the commit rejects
    63:   any fusion whose read (through the load-alias root) was re-stored
    64:   past the deepest absorbed member. Cross-block stores need no check
    65:   for the same reason load aliasing is sound — a jump re-enters at a
    66:   block head, above the compare, never between it and the branch. The
    67:   AArch64 selector has no promotion, so every vreg is
    68:   single-definition and sinking is unconditionally safe.

    70:   The corpus is arithmetic-dense, so fusion trims only its loop heads

    73:   locals alike, since the C frontend stamps every local with its type's
    74:   layout alignment — canonical allocates `size + alignment - 1` raw
    75:   bytes and emits lea/add/and at the LOCAL instruction, storing a
    76:   runtime-aligned pointer through which every access then indirects
    77:   (`codegen.c`'s `aligned_local_offsets` and the `alignment > 16`

    80:   record stands corrected here. The machine path now mirrors the
    81:   indirect shape for over-aligned non-vector locals: classification
    82:   gives them a padded slot deliberately kept out of `value_stack_slots`
    83:   plus a GENERAL vreg holding the aligned pointer, the LOCAL row emits
    84:   LEA_FRAME(+alignment-1) / MOV_RI(-alignment) / AND64, and every
    85:   consumer dispatches down the same pointer paths a GLOBAL's address
    86:   already takes — so a missed consumer can only fall back, never read
    87:   the padded slot as data. Promotion now runs before the alignment
    88:   check: a promotable over-aligned local promotes, its alignment
    89:   unobservable without an address.

    91:   Stage 10's sixteen-byte clamp for `IR_TYPE_VECTOR` locals is kept: all
    92:   machine vector accesses are unaligned forms, the kernels' vector locals
    93:   promote anyway, and re-routing them through the indirect shape would
    94:   tax exactly the slots stage 10 measured. The honest cost is that a

    97:   program inspecting the address. The new `vunion` differential returns

    92:   per-block contracts over a ≤16-entry register file and the quality

    97:   branching), the prepass is 2.9% of linear decode, and the one loop
    98:   that ever matched the stage-12 shape — the fourteen-lane prefix sum —
    99:   is exactly what trim 3 removed rather than vectorized. A 512-bit
   100:   kernel has nothing to run on; the acceptance bar (whole-allocator Zen
   101:   5 win, Zen 4 break-even, bit-identical output) is unreachable when no
   102:   candidate loop is dense, so the stage closes as understood-and-
   103:   recorded rather than built. The nearest miss is recorded for

   105:   resident value against the 14-entry contract row (~0.5% of quality
   106:   mode, one `vpcmpeqd` in shape) — too small to clear the

   108: - **What stays, understood.** The dual scan per quality function is the
   109:   candidate-selection design (`2026-08-09ai`: measured traffic beats
   110:   every guessing heuristic) — the prepass halves its overhead without
   111:   touching the decision. The kept schedules' second placements are the
   112:   stage-7 acceptance currency. The main scan's remaining cost is the
   113:   allocation itself; its loops are the register file's width and carry
   114:   per-iteration side effects, so neither wider hardware nor a kernel

    43:   vector arguments stay canonical (their AL protocol counts vector
    44:   registers; the subset keeps the zero-vector convention), as does any call
    45:   whose stack vector argument would open an alignment gap the push machinery
    46:   cannot produce.
    47: - **vzeroupper became row-conditional, not unconditional.** The encoder used
    48:   to emit vzeroupper before every CALL and RET in a vector-touching function
    49:   — sound while every vector value was dead at those points, and exactly
    50:   wrong for a value *staged* there: vzeroupper zeroes bits 128+ of ZMM0-15,
    51:   so a staged argument or a live ZMM0 return would arrive truncated. A new
    52:   per-row flag (`MACHINE_X64_INSTRUCTION_FLAG_VECTOR_LIVE`, set by the
    53:   selector on calls with register vector arguments and on vector-returning
    54:   RETs) suppresses that row's vzeroupper. This is the same answer the
    55:   canonical path reaches by ordering — its lazy vzeroupper fires before the
    56:   call's staging code — and the same one clang implements as
    57:   no-vzeroupper-when-ZMM-live. A vector *returning* call keeps its
    58:   vzeroupper: it fires before the call, and ZMM0 arrives after.
    59: - **Found en route: INDEX on a 512-bit rvalue mis-selected as a pointer
    60:   copy.** `machine_x64_select_place_address_offset` treats any vreg-held
    61:   base as an address to copy — meaningless for a vector-class register, and
    62:   unreachable until vector-ABI functions selected, whereupon
    63:   `basic_c_wide_vector_argument`'s `main` (an `identity[lane]` read on a
    64:   call result the frontend loads whole) selected its way into a wild load
    65:   and SIGSEGVed under every machine mode. The base now snapshots into a
    66:   dedicated 64-byte slot and hands out that slot's address — sound because
    67:   the SSA value is immutable — which is also what lets `vector_mixed`'s
    68:   lane reads select. Array-typed rvalue INDEX keeps its reject.

    54: - **The frequency-weighted fold.** `11f` prices every spill/reload edit
    55:   by `4^depth` of the block it executes in (capped), both for candidacy
    56:   and for the whole-placement acceptance test. Since a split's boundary
    57:   rows sit outside the region by construction, they land at a strictly
    58:   lower enclosing depth than the traffic the split removes — so bucketing
    59:   a candidate's baseline edits into per-region weighted sums (reusing the
    60:   exact `instruction_weights` array `11f` already built) and comparing
    61:   that against the boundary rows' own weighted cost is a strictly more
    62:   principled gate than this entry's original ad hoc iteration-credit
    63:   constant, and needed no floor: `best_traffic <= entry_weight +
    64:   exit_weight + prologue_cost` rejects, matching the whole-placement
    65:   acceptance's own units exactly. A marginal candidate (admitted on
    66:   frequency alone, raw edit count under three) keeps its caller-saved-only
    67:   restriction through the split probe for the same reason `11f` imposed
    68:   it on whole placement: a static loop is not evidence the loop runs.
    69: - **Measured, frozen `a838308` ide.c as the workload (min of 3, same
    70:   session, both sides).** QUALITY stage `40.903G` to `40.881G`
    71:   (**`-22M`**, pins 10,415 to 10,642, **244 splits** firing), static
    72:   traffic essentially flat (reloads 55,847 to 55,790, spills 84,089 to
    73:   84,148, the difference absorbed by the boundary rows: boundary_spills
    74:   14,623 to 14,759). Quality-mode compile cost `9.1898G` to `9.3882G`
    75:   (**`+2.2%`**, the region metadata, the per-candidate region-traffic
    76:   matrix, and the split probing on top of `11f`'s own frequency-weighted
    77:   economics; quality stays opt-in). Canonical compile cost flat
    78:   (`5.87000G` to `5.87001G`), fast-mode flat (`7.3598G` to `7.3933G`,

    83:   (`91.08M`/`84.44M`) both repeat to the instruction with zero splits —
    84:   single-region bodies whose whole file is already contended over that
    85:   one region, so there is nothing to split into. Every paired execution

    88:   landing.** A two-phase body — values defined before a call-free hot

    53: pattern-aware value and only then reads the effective source, and an exact

     1: `2026-08-15d` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; a second, value-keyed byte-template
     2: table, based on `ec884958`). Stage 1 `30,171,862,831` -> `26,751,605,860`
     3: instructions (**-11.3%**) and stage 2 `429,417,305,821` -> `389,039,815,381`.
     4: A single-lane stage-1 compile measured 3,255 ms -> 2,721 ms of task-clock
     5: (-16.4%). Cumulative across the four 2026-08-15 audits: stage 1
     6: `63,683,992,612` -> `26,751,605,860`, **-58.0%**, and `test_self_host` stage-1
     7: wall 2.679 s -> 1.858 s, **-30.6%**.
     8: 
     9: **This replaces the one-patch-slot design `2026-08-15b` proposed; do not build
    10: that.** A hit census settled it. Over 4,864,621 canonical emissions in one
    11: stage-1 self-compile, the existing value-free key hits `4,838,212` times
    12: (**99.46%**) but only 16.5% of emissions are value-free and therefore
    13: templatable under `2026-08-15c`. Hashing the same key *plus* the operand values
    14: matches **60.9%**. So rather than teaching a patch slot to re-derive the
    15: computed displacement inside the byte-authority module, the values simply go in
    16: a key — and then the byte string is fully determined and a hit has nothing to
    17: patch at all.
    18: 
    19: The two tables answer different questions and are sized for it. The existing
    20: one answers *which form is this*, which operand values do not change, so it
    21: stays value-free and keeps its 99.46% hit rate feeding
    22: `buster_x86_metadata_emit_form_selected`. The new one answers *what are the
    23: bytes*, which values do change; it is keyed by shape plus every operand payload
    24: that can reach the bytes without changing the shape (signed and unsigned
    25: immediates, the memory displacement, and both addends). One key build serves
    26: both. A template miss falls through to the form table, so this cannot make
    27: emission worse than not having it. Capacity is 4096 entries of 32 bytes per
    28: lane; the fragment-arena reservation already scales with
    29: `sizeof(CodegenX64MetadataCache)` and needed no change.
    30: 
    31: Value-free rows keep their template on the form entry rather than moving to the
    32: value table, because the shape alone pins them and nothing there can evict
    33: them.
    34: 
    35: One correctness gap is closed explicitly rather than by inference. A **symbol**
    36: is the one operand payload the key cannot carry: two different symbol names
    37: give the same shape and the same values. Such a row also needs a relocation and
    38: this path offers no relocation capacity, so it fails before reaching the
    39: capture — but the guard now sits next to the key instead of resting on that,
    40: at a measured cost of 0.13%. The same reasoning that pins the bytes in
    41: `2026-08-15c` otherwise carries over unchanged.
    42: 
    43: The value hashes then stopped walking the key words a second time. The shape
    44: hashes already summarize every word, so folding the operand values into those
    45: gives the same separation for half the work: `26,495,655,699` ->
    46: `25,935,567,890` instructions, a further **-2.1%**, for the stage-1 total
    47: above.
    48: 
    49: **A local `test_all_combinations_ci` is not sufficient for a change that alters
    50: a shared structure's size, and this audit is the proof.** The matrix is
    51: Linux-only; aarch64 and Windows exist only in remote CI. The value-keyed table
    52: took `CodegenX64MetadataCache` past 64 KiB, and the macOS self-host then failed
    53: to compile `codegen_canonical_parallel_lane` for aarch64 with *"C code
    54: generation failed with error 4 ... opcode 22, operation 73"* — buster could no
    55: longer compile itself. Reduced to a fixture, **the AArch64 backend cannot lower
    56: a variable index into an array whose element stride reaches 2^16**: 65,520
    57: bytes compiles, 65,536 fails. That is a pre-existing backend gap that any array
    58: of >=64 KiB structs indexed by a variable will hit, recorded here because this
    59: is where it surfaced; it is not fixed by this audit. The cache array became one
    60: pointer per lane, each cache its own allocation, so the indexed stride is 8
    61: bytes whatever the cache grows to. That costs nothing measurable
    62: (`25,935,803,166` against `25,935,567,890`).
    63: 
    64: Validation: byte-identical stage-1/stage-2 fixed point, 302,625 Release
    65: assertions across 38 modules, and a full local `test_all_combinations_ci` —
    66: with the caveat above that the aarch64 and Windows verdicts come only from
    67: remote CI, and must be waited for.

     1: `2026-08-15h` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; the byte-template table is probed as
     2: a cache instead of a dictionary, based on `37d59296`). Stage 1
     3: `18,150,530,759` -> `15,900,336,190` instructions (**-12.4%**) measured

     5: 2026-08-15 audits: stage 1 `63,683,992,612` -> `15,900,336,190`, **-75.0%**.
     6: 
     7: The dominant find was the probe loop, not the hash and not the transform.
     8: `codegen_canonical_x64_template_entry` walked up to **64** slots and inserted
     9: only into an empty one. Both halves of that are wrong once the table fills,
    10: and it filled: instrumented on one stage-1 self-compile at the then-current
    11: 65536 ceiling, the table reached **100% occupancy** (65,536 of 65,536), took
    12: its last insertion at that point and never took another, **32.8%** of
    13: 4,920,459 lookups walked all 64 slots to return nothing, and the average
    14: lookup cost **22.15 probe steps** for 109,010,573 steps in total. A third of
    15: the lookups were futile by construction and the table had frozen on whatever
    16: the module emitted first.
    17: 
    18: It is now a bounded window with replacement: probe two slots from home, and
    19: when both belong to other keys, claim one of them. A key therefore always
    20: lives within `home .. home + 1`, which is the invariant the lookup relies on
    21: and the insertion maintains. The same instrumentation after: **1.34** steps
    22: per lookup (6,193,886 for 4,614,842 lookups, a **17.6x** reduction) and the
    23: hit rate up from 64.6% to **75.5%**, with 322,049 evictions showing the table
    24: now tracks the working set.
    25: 
    26: The victim is picked from the guard rather than fixed at the home slot, so
    27: eviction spreads across the window instead of one slot absorbing every
    28: conflict. It stays a pure function of the key, which matters: cache contents
    29: now depend on how work is split across lanes, so the emitted bytes must not.
    30: Verified directly — the same unit compiled at 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 16 lanes
    31: produces six byte-identical executables.
    32: 
    33: **The window is narrow, and that is measured, not assumed.** Probe steps are
    34: paid on every emission while associativity only buys hits. Swept at the 65536
    35: ceiling: 17.86 G instructions at a window of 1, **17.73 G at 2**, 17.74 G at
    36: 4, 17.83 G at 8, 18.07 G at 16. One slot loses too many hits; past two the
    37: walk costs more than it wins.
    38: 
    39: **Bounding the probe also overturns `2026-08-15e`'s capacity ceiling, which
    40: should now be read as a consequence of the old probe.** That entry chose 65536
    41: because a larger table cost memory "for no measured wall improvement" — but
    42: under a 64-slot never-replacing probe, a larger table helped mainly by staying
    43: unsaturated. With the window bounded, only the slots a key actually lands on
    44: are ever touched, so capacity costs address space rather than pages until it
    45: outgrows the codegen arena's own high-water mark. Re-swept with peak RSS taken
    46: from `VmHWM`:

    52:  524288     16 MiB       15,568,244,627     1,393,996 kB
    53: ```
    54: 
    55: 262144 is the largest capacity that is **free** in resident memory, and the
    56: ceiling moved there; `2026-08-15e` had rejected it at an assumed 128 MiB cost.
    57: 524288 buys a further 2.1% for 55 MB and was not taken. The instrument is

     1: `2026-08-15i` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; the form-selection candidate loop
     2: stops re-deriving loop-invariant work, based on `91eba52e`). Stage 1
     3: `15,991,731,490` -> `15,600,981,922` instructions (**-2.4%**) measured

     6: 
     7: All three finds are in `buster_x86_metadata_select_form`'s per-candidate loop,
     8: which runs on the ~24.5% of emissions the byte table misses. Nothing in the
     9: loop's *result* changed — see the verification below.
    10: 
    11: **`emit_parse_pattern` was already cached, so its cost was the copy.** It
    12: returns `BusterX86MetadataPatternSemantics` **by value**, and that record is
    13: 176 bytes; the cache hit is a 176-byte copy out of a table the caller could
    14: read in place. `buster_x86_metadata_pattern_semantics_borrow` already existed
    15: for exactly this and was already used by `emit_bind_form` and
    16: `emit_form_to_scratch` — the candidate loop was simply never converted. It
    17: called `emit_parse_pattern` **three times per candidate** (the filter pattern,
    18: the implicit-one test, and the FMA4 tie-break) and read four fields, one
    19: field, and two fields from the three copies. This is precisely the leftover
    20: `2026-08-15g` pointed at when it said to check whether any other consumer
    21: still derives the per-form facts the long way.
    22: 
    23: **A 2,304-byte dead zero-initializer.** `candidate_operands[16] = {0}` zeroed
    24: sixteen 144-byte operands per candidate, and both writers `memcpy` the query's
    25: whole operand prefix before touching it. The array is now uninitialized; the
    26: one later read is guarded by `inferred_memory_width`, which is set only on
    27: those memcpy paths, so no uninitialized byte is ever read. Note that the
    28: matrix's sanitizers are ASan+UBSan, neither of which detects an uninitialized
    29: read, so this was established by reading every use rather than by a run.
    30: 
    31: **Three loop-invariant probes.** `aggregate_memory_source_topology_internal`,
    32: `block_memory_source_topology_internal` and `prepare_typed_memory_query` each
    33: begin by rejecting on conditions that depend only on the query, and the query
    34: does not change across candidates — so each candidate paid a call and an
    35: 80-byte query copy to re-derive one constant answer. The query-side tests are
    36: now hoisted out of the loop. They are used as a **necessary** condition, so
    37: the guard can only skip a call that would have returned false; exhaustiveness
    38: was not required and was not claimed. The two families are mutually exclusive
    39: by construction, the topology pair requiring no decorator at all and the typed
    40: probe requiring the broadcast decorator.
    41: 
    42: **Verification that selection did not move.** The byte-identity gates here are
    43: stronger than a test count, because this loop chooses instruction encodings.
    44: The pre-change and post-change compilers, given identical input, produce
    45: identical output: 46 of 46 `tests/basic_c_*.c` fixtures compile to
    46: byte-identical objects with matching exit status, and the complete self-host
    47: unit compiles to a byte-identical **45,626,304**-byte executable. A change
    48: that altered form selection anywhere in that 27 MB of code could not produce
    49: that result.
    50: 
    51: Validation: byte-identical stage-1/stage-2 fixed point, byte-identical output
    52: at 1, 4 and 16 lanes, 305,278 Release assertions across 39 modules, the
    53: cross-compiler byte comparison above, and a full local
    54: `test_all_combinations_ci`. That matrix is Linux-only, so the aarch64 and
    55: Windows verdicts come from remote CI.
    56: 
    57: The remaining profile is flat: after this, no single symbol outside
    58: `codegen_canonical_x64_metadata_emit_attributes` exceeds 8% of retired
    59: instructions. That function is now the standing lever and is **not** a
    60: cache-miss problem any more — it is the ~430 instructions per emission spent
    61: building the key (packing up to 80 words, two hash chains over them, then a
    62: ten-multiply value fold per operand) before either table is touched. Shortening
    63: the value fold's dependent chain by mixing the five per-operand values with one
    64: linear combination was considered and **not** taken: it would collapse a
    65: nonlinear compression into a linear form whose collisions are constructible,
    66: and a collision here is a silent miscompile, not a slow path.

     1: `2026-08-16b` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; **compiler throughput** — the
     2: shared selection prepass stops rescanning the function per promotable local,
     3: based on `ac583f40`). Stage 1 `18,717,675,527` -> `16,289,240,873`
     4: (**-13.0%**), stage 2 `131,730,693,610` -> `119,829,765,574` (**-9.0%**),
     5: `test_self_host` stage-1 wall 1.87 s -> 1.78 s.
     6: 
     7: **A quadratic in the shared prepass, and it was the top symbol.**
     8: `machine_selection_prepass_build` was **10.8%** of a stage-1 compile, more
     9: than twice the next symbol, and ~85% of its samples sat on the two compares
    10: at the top of one loop. That loop asked, for every local it had just marked
    11: promotable, whether every use of that local is a legal load/store place — by
    12: walking the whole function's instruction and operand lists once per
    13: candidate.
    14: 
    15: The early exit makes the cost shape counterintuitive: the scan stops at the
    16: first disqualifying use, so the locals that cost the most are exactly the
    17: ones that *survive* to be promoted. A function with N surviving candidates
    18: and M operands paid N*M.
    19: 
    20: The question is per (use, local), not per local. One pass over every operand
    21: now answers it for all candidates at once — look the operand's value up, skip
    22: it unless it is still a live candidate, clear the flag when its place is
    23: illegal — and a function with no promotable local skips the pass outright.
    24: Clearing is monotone and the per-use verdict does not depend on the order
    25: uses are visited, so the final flags are identical.
    26: 
    27: **The x86 selector already had the linear form.** `machine_x86_64.c` derives
    28: its own target-refined promotion set and disqualifies inside the operand walk
    29: (around line 3806), which is why only the shared pass was quadratic. Worth
    30: knowing before assuming the two are the same code twice.
    31: 
    32: **A leftover 264-byte copy per emission.**
    33: `buster_x86_metadata_emit_machine_fast` took its `BusterX86MetadataForm` by
    34: value while the caller held `record->form`, a pointer into the same immutable
    35: generated table; it read about two dozen scalar fields out of the copy. This
    36: is exactly the leftover `2026-08-15i` named when it converted the candidate
    37: loop to the borrow accessors — the fast emitter was simply never converted.
    38: Small: `-31.6 M` (-0.19%). The remaining copies on this path are the 120-byte
    39: `BusterX86MetadataEmitQuery` built at `x86_64_metadata.c:8512` and passed by
    40: value at `:8539`, which is the single hottest instruction in
    41: `buster_x86_metadata_emit_exact_machine`; it was left untaken because
    42: `emit_form_with_form` has four call sites and the measured return on the
    43: larger 264-byte copy was already only 0.19%.
    44: 
    45: **Method note — do not A/B the self-host output against itself.** The
    46: self-host executable *is* the compiler's own source, so a change to any
    47: compiler file legitimately changes those bytes: comparing a pre-change and
    48: post-change self-host output measures the source edit, not codegen, and the
    49: first reading here was a false alarm (a 64-byte size delta that was entirely
    50: the added code). The valid comparison runs **both compiler binaries over the
    51: same source tree**. Beware two more confounders met on the way: the output
    52: path is embedded, so both sides must write to the same path, and 9 of the 55
    53: `tests/basic_c_*.c` fixtures are negative tests that produce no object, so a
    54: fixture sweep must gate on exit status or it will report nine phantom
    55: differences.
    56: 
    57: **Verified equivalent rather than argued.** The rewrite looked obviously
    58: equivalent and the first byte comparison appeared to contradict that, so the
    59: flags were compared directly: a probe build ran both the old and the new
    60: derivation over every function of the self-host unit and reported zero
    61: divergences in flags or widths. Both changes then passed byte-identity —
    62: identical input, pre- and post-change compilers, byte-identical self-host
    63: executable and byte-identical objects for all 46 compiling fixtures with
    64: matching exit status on the 9 negative ones. Stage-1/stage-2 fixed point
    65: holds (`bytes=35869408`, both stages converging on 2.948.479 tokens), full
    66: Release `test_all` green: 308,714 assertions across 39 modules.
    67: 
    68: `ide bench` is unchanged and is expected to be: both finds are in codegen and
    69: x86 metadata, and the benchmark measures the C frontend path only. Its
    70: run-to-run median spread on this host was 1.05-1.23 ms, wider than any effect
    71: these changes could have there.
    72: 
    73: **What the profile looks like now.** Flat, and more so than before: the top
    74: symbol is `buster_x86_metadata_emit_exact_machine` at 6.1% self, and nothing
    75: else exceeds 4.3%. By phase, codegen is 47%, `c_lower_to_ir` 24.7%,
    76: `c_analyze_semantics` 9.9%, `c_preprocess` 8.2%. Checked and found *not*
    77: worth taking: the FAST allocator's placement loops are bounded by operand
    78: count, not function size; `c_ir_constant_initializer_bytes_legacy` is a real
    79: fallback for non-brace initializers rather than a duplicate of the new path;
    80: and arena allocations are explicitly dirty (`arena.c` reuse contract), so the
    81: selectors' per-function zero-init loops are required, not redundant. One
    82: latent non-performance bug was noted in passing: `register_allocator_fast.c`
    83: compares a `u8` slot against `UINT32_MAX` (~line 1692), a guard that can
    84: never fire and is harmless today only because the following loop's own filter

    33: (1 GB reserved, pages commit on touch), whose tail is the stream.  Nothing
    34: else allocates from it, so successive reservations are contiguous and the
    35: base is the finished `result.tokens` the moment the last line lands.  There
    36: is no reordering to defeat: both output paths only ever append.  The stronger
    37: form recorded in the survey — the *lexer* writing the final array — stays
    38: impossible for a real reason worth recording: the lexed stream still carries
    39: the newlines, directive lines, and inactive-conditional regions the
    40: preprocessor consumes, and expansion rewrites what remains, so finality
    41: simply does not exist at lex time.  The preprocessor's line loop is the first
    42: point that knows which tokens survive, and that is where the write now
    43: happens.
    44: 
    45: **The shape.**  `CTokenStream` replaces `CPreprocessTokenRange`: a line
    46: reserves its upper bound at the arena tail (its lexed token count, or the
    47: expansion's node count), writes the tokens that survive the newline or
    48: pragma strip, and hands the surplus slots back
    49: (`arena_set_position`, the `c_space_shrink` idiom).  A no-expansion line —
    50: the 64% — now streams straight from the lexed array; its staging copy is
    51: gone, and the macro scan and the expansion wrap read `lex.tokens` directly.
    52: An expanded line materializes its node list into the stream tail instead of
    53: a scratch array.  The range list, its append/coalesce helper, and the final
    54: 269 K-piece copy are deleted outright.  The arena rides in
    55: `CSourceMapRecovery` beside the spelling arena with the same lifetime
    56: contract; the bench loop destroys both.

     1: `2026-08-22T120959Z` (Linux x86_64, Zen 4 7940HS; **attribute the include
     2: amplification per header, then drop guard-shaped re-includes unread**).
     3: The SOURCE table has always carried the include amplification as a ratio —
     4: this tree opened at 295 unique files / 27,23 MB against 448 lexed / 29,39 MB,
     5: 2,16 MB re-read across 153 re-inclusions — without saying which headers the
     6: re-read bytes belong to. This audit adds the attribution to the compiler,
     7: uses it, and closes what it names. Baseline reproduced first:
     8: `test_self_host` at the byte-identical fixed point, stage 1 at
     9: 10.172.846.827 instructions.
    10: 
    11: **The attribution lives in the tree, not in a script.** The metrics file set
    12: that already decides unique-vs-lexed (`c_source_metrics_file_row` in
    13: `c_source.c`) now keeps one row per distinct path — lex count and one lex's
    14: scanned bytes — and `-v` prints every file lexed more than once with the
    15: bytes its re-reads added, largest first, plus a total that equals the two
    16: aggregates' scanned-byte difference exactly. It is deliberately not the
    17: token-carrying file table beside `map_entry`: that one is populated lazily so
    18: token-free headers never enter the program's source map across hosts, while
    19: attribution needs precisely the files that contribute nothing twice.
    20: 
    21: **What it said.** One in-tree file owned 47,9% of the re-read bytes: the
    22: 1.034.723-byte `aarch64-canonical-decoder.generated.h`, included by both
    23: `aarch64_encoding.c` and `aarch64_semantic_vm.c`, lexed twice. Nearly all
    24: the rest was glibc — `features.h` 31 lexes / 593.580 bytes, `bits/types.h`
    25: 35 / 299.404, `string.h`, `unistd.h`, thirty smaller `bits/*` files. And
    26: every one of these, the generated header included, already carries a classic
    27: whole-file `#ifndef` guard; the preprocessor just only recognized
    28: `#pragma once`, so the guard kept the tokens out while the bytes were
    29: re-read, re-translated, re-lexed and re-interned at every inclusion. That
    30: settled the close: guarding in-tree headers with `#pragma once` would have
    31: covered 48% and left glibc untouched, so the fix is the multiple-include
    32: optimization, which covers both from one mechanism.
    33: 
    34: **The estimate, before the measurement.** Re-read material: 2.160.707
    35: scanned bytes, 511.240 tokens (16,1% of all lexed tokens), 65.824 lines. At
    36: the SIMD lexer's few instructions per byte plus per-token interning and the
    37: inactive-line walk, the guess was 25–40 M instructions, ~0,3% of stage 1.
    38: 
    39: **The mechanism.** While walking an include frame the preprocessor proves
    40: the guard shape: SEARCHING until the file's first top-level directive, which
    41: must be `#ifndef NAME`; GUARDED inside that conditional; CLOSED when its
    42: `#endif` returns to the frame's base; DISQUALIFIED by any token or directive
    43: at the frame's top level outside it, an `#elif`/`#else` arm on it, or end of
    44: file inside it. A CLOSED frame records path → interned guard symbol
    45: (`CIncludeGuardTable`), and a later `#include` of a recorded path is dropped
    46: unread while the symbol is a defined macro — one macro-table lookup, the
    47: same suppression `#pragma once` takes, testable at every inclusion so an
    48: `#undef` of the guard re-arms the header. Deliberately multi-section files —
    49: the builtin `stddef.h`, glibc's `bits/wordsize.h`,
    50: `bits/libc-header-start.h` — disqualify themselves by construction and keep
    51: their re-reads, now 28.182 bytes in total where 2.160.707 stood. New
    52: fixtures cover suppression, `#undef` re-arming, and a token after the
    53: guard's `#endif`.
    54:

    63: **The selector's dispatch is adjudicated against, with numbers.**  Census:
    64: 1.068.727 switch dispatches (plus 157.878 `fused_dead` rows that bypass

    66: `CAST` 6,9%; marginal entropy 3,663 bits, `H(next|prev)` 2,359,
    67: `P(next==prev)` 13,4% — run-grouping is dead, and a perfect first-order
    68: predictor would reach only 40,5%.  Sorting or partitioning by class is not
    69: available at all: every handler appends machine rows in program order
    70: through shared selector state, so the emission order is the algorithm.  The
    71: one classification the structure offers is positional — a lowered block's
    72: last row is its terminator, and `BRANCH`/`BRANCH_IF`/`RETURN` cover 99,69%
    73: of 113.978 block ends, leaving a 954.749-row body population at 3,382 bits
    74: and a terminator population at 1,429.  Both spellings of that split were
    75: built and measured against the merged tree, five alternated pairs each.
    76: Splitting the loop with the ladder's default calling the full selector
    77: outlines `machine_x64_select_instruction` (two call sites) and costs
    78: **+32,1 M instructions (+0,32%), 0/5**, misses +136 K (2/5, noise).
    79: Forcing it back inline (`BUSTER_INLINE`) duplicates the selector complex
    80: and still costs **+21,5 M instructions (+0,22%), 0/5**, misses +217 K
    81: (1/5).  The reason the miss column never moves is worth recording: the row
    82: loop's exit branch retires immediately before every terminator dispatch, so
    83: the indirect predictor's global history already carries exactly the signal
    84: the split encodes — the entropy is in the opcode sequence itself, and at
    85: 13 cycles a miss the whole 429 K site is a ~5,6 M-cycle ceiling that
    86: cannot pay for tens of millions of restructuring instructions.  Do not
    87: retry this split, and treat opcode-peeling variants (`if (opcode ==
    88: CONSTANT_INTEGER)` ahead of the switch) as the same trade: they add the
    89: compare per row without adding information the predictor lacks.

    38:   1).** One AArch64 story: a sixteen-byte vector rides a whole V
    39:   register at the ABI edges while the value stays slot-backed
    40:   (VLOAD_FRAME/VSTORE_FRAME, fixed-V payload rows on the scheduler's
    41:   float-state chain), and everything past sixteen bytes — aggregate or
    42:   vector — travels as a pointer in the integer file, overflowing to a
    43:   scalar stack part like any integer. The machine caller points that
    44:   pointer at a **defensive copy**: AAPCS64 licenses the callee to
    45:   scribble on the pointed-at memory, which the canonical caller's
    46:   pass-the-value-slot shortcut does not survive. The callee copies in
    47:   through the pointer at entry and the parameter is an ordinary
    48:   slot-backed aggregate from there.

   180: 
   181: ## The differential gate, and the compiler bug it found
   182: 
   183: The gate is `#if !BUSTER_OPTIMIZE` inside `c_parse_token_census`: unoptimized
   184: builds recompute the census the reference way and require all nine counters to
   185: agree. That puts the check on **every translation unit the suite compiles**
   186: rather than on a hand-written list of token streams, and -- because the
   187: self-hosted stages are built without `-DBUSTER_OPTIMIZE` -- it also runs
   188: inside the stage-1 and stage-2 compilers over the whole unity unit. It was
   189: proved load-bearing by perturbing the kernel to miscount a single token in one
   190: window, which failed the suite.
   191: 
   192: It immediately earned its keep. With the gate in, `test_self_host` failed
   193: while `ide test` and an eleven-pair byte-identical A/B both passed: the
   194: clang-built compiler computed the census correctly and the **buster-built**
   195: one did not. Splitting the check per counter named
   196: `declarator_list_comma_count`, the only one using `mask64_prefix` with a
   197: runtime count, and the fault reduces to five lines with no SIMD in them:
   198: 
   199: ```c
   200: u32 lane = 32;                 /* opaque */
   201: u64 value = lane >= 64 ? ~(u64)0 : (((u64)1 << lane) - 1);
   202: /* clang: 0x00000000ffffffff.  ide cc: 0xffffffffffffffff. */
   203: ```
   204: 
   205: That is `mask64_prefix` from `<buster/lib/simd.h>` expanded. `-emit-llvm` on
   206: the same function shows the cause: the conditional's result slot is allocated
   207: **i32**, both arms are computed correctly in 64 bits, then `trunc`ed into it
   208: and `sext`ed back on the reload, so every count in [32, 64) returns `~0`. The
   209: predicted type, not the resolved one, sizes the slot -- and the misprediction
   210: needs both arms to be what they are: `cond ? ~(u64)0 : x` and
   211: `cond ? y : ((u64)1 << lane) - 1` are each fine, and only the pair fails. All
   212: four allocator modes fail identically, so it is upstream of code generation.
   213: 
   214: The bug is **pre-existing**: the binary built from the parent commit
   215: miscompiles the same five lines. The only other runtime-count user in the tree
   216: is `ir_source_search_vector` (`ir.c:92-93`), where `mask64_prefix(lanes * 4)`
   217: covers [32, 64) for 8 to 15 lanes; there the wrong mask over-reads the loaded
   218: vector and the extra lanes are masked out of `covered` immediately after, so
   219: it is latent rather than visible -- but it is a real over-read in the
   220: self-hosted stages. The existing coverage misses it because
   221: `simd_test.c` and `tests/basic_c_simd.c` only ever ask for
   222: `mask64_prefix(0)`, `(1)` and `(64)`, all compile-time constants.
   223: 
   224: This audit does not fix it: the fault is in the C frontend's expression-type
   225: prediction, a separate subsystem from anything the census touches, and a
   226: speculative change there risks the fixed point. The census avoids it instead
   227: by spelling the mask `c_parse_census_lanes_below(lane)`, a bare
   228: `((Mask64)1 << lane) - 1` -- `lane` always comes from `mask64_first_set` of a
   229: non-zero mask, so `mask64_prefix`'s `count >= 64` arm was dead weight here
   230: anyway. **The next task on this thread is the prediction bug itself**, with
   231: the five-line case above as its fixture and `ir.c:92` as its second caller.
   232:

===== docs/performance-audits/2026-08-24T131821Z.md =====
--- lines 1-75 ---
     1: #545 — skip the fresh template-cache memset with an arena dirty watermark
     2: 
     3: ## Change
     4: 
     5: The canonical x86 template cache can reserve 262,144 entries (32 bytes each,
     6: 8 MiB). `Arena.dirty_position` now retains the high-water mark across logical
     7: rewinds, while `arena_dirty_position` takes the maximum of that saved mark and
     8: the live cursor. Allocations therefore add no watermark store to the arena's
     9: hot path. Fresh mappings start at `arena_minimum_position`; logical and
    10: temporal rewinds save the cursor, and pooled reuse carries the mark through the
    11: header rewrite. Parking an arena accounts for the pool link written into the
    12: first payload bytes. A successful decommit clamps the mark to its decommit
    13: boundary, since recommitted pages are fresh again.
    14: 
    15: Codegen snapshots the mark immediately before allocating the metadata header,
    16: then allocates the template array as before.  It clears only
    17: `[template_start, min(dirty_position, template_end))`; the suffix above the
    18: watermark is zero from a fresh mapping or a successful decommit.  A watermark
    19: that lands inside an entry is intentionally cleared bytewise through the
    20: boundary.  The lookup probe window, insertion, replacement, and eviction
    21: choice are unchanged.
    22: 
    23: The invariant is therefore: every byte below
    24: `max(dirty_position, position)` may contain contents from an earlier arena
    25: generation, while every byte at or above it in a newly committed suffix has
    26: not yet been handed out by this generation. The mark is conservative
    27: (alignment padding and pool metadata may extend it), so a false positive costs
    28: a smaller memset but can never expose stale cache fields.
    29:

    33: - `arena_tests`: **39/39** assertions passed, including fresh allocation,
    34:   rewind, pooled reuse, pool-link accounting, and decommit/recommit watermark
    35:   checks.
    36: - `codegen_tests`: **333/333** assertions passed, including byte-identical
    37:   canonical output across two lifetimes of a pooled arena.
    38: - `git diff --check` and Clang syntax checks for `arena.c` and `codegen.c` are
    39:   clean.

   425:   instructions:u one, and it is recorded, not taken.

   427: **The five patterns behind almost every number above**, as the ranking pass
   428: put them, because they are what the next audit should look for first:
   429: (1) spelling ladders where the token already carries an interned symbol id,
   430: in the parser, the preprocessor, the lowering and the driver's keyword hash;
   431: (2) facts re-derived per query instead of recorded by the pass that already
   432: held them — specifier sets, group facts, line marks, encode capacity,
   433: `has_vector`, definition points, decoded literals; (3) by-value copies of
   434: wide records that no `memcpy` census can see because arena struct stores
   435: never reach libc (`CPpToken` 36 bytes copied 8-10 times, `CIrQueryFrame`
   436: 140, `MachineX64CallPlan` 1,4 KB); (4) per-value and per-token side arrays
   437: allocated separately and filled by scalar loops, where one block with a
   438: 0xff region and a 0x00 region and two memsets does the same work, with the
   439: rare populations gated by an existing summary; (5) generic containers on hot
   440: paths — the chunked builder stream, the linked block-parameter and macro
   441: chains, the statement tree — against typed cursors and index-linked arrays,
   442: since the fixed point needs the same order, not the same container. One-byte
   443: projections (token shape and class, row opcode, type class, place kind) are
   444: the enabling layout for all of it, and an emitter's cost has to be repaid by
   445: at least two consumers landing with it.
   446:

   346: ## What this round learned about measuring, which cost it real time
   347: 
   348: 1. **`/tmp` here is a 16 GB RAM-backed tmpfs with a shared per-uid quota, and
   349:    exhausting it does not produce an error you would notice.** It presents as
   350:    a dead shell (commands "produce no output", redirections create empty
   351:    files), as `os_file_write_partially` assertions inside `test_self_host`, as
   352:    spawned test binaries failing with "Exec format error" (730 phantom driver
   353:    failures in one run), as clang's "IO failure on output stream: Disk quota
   354:    exceeded", and as a `cmp: DIFFER` on an innocent patch. Worst, **it silently
   355:    inflates `instructions:u`**, because the compiler's output-write path
   356:    retries: an unmodified baseline binary measured 8.946 M and 9.406 M instead
   357:    of 8.739 M. Two branches lost an A/B to it and one lost a session. **Canary
   358:    the unmodified `ide.before` against the frozen tree before reporting any
   359:    delta**, and `rm -rf build/self-host` after every self-host run.
   360: 2. **`cycles:u` is not a usable currency on this host under load**: ±45%
   361:    run-to-run for the *same* binary, against `instructions:u` at 0,002%. Every
   362:    latency and mispredict claim in this audit is therefore stated as a
   363:    structural claim from miss counts, never as a cycles number — including the
   364:    ones where the branch-miss survey made the case for the work.
   365: 3. **A fixed-period `instructions:u` sample profile can alias with a hot
   366:    loop.** `c_lex_dispatch` reads **3,68% at period 20.000 and under 2,1% at
   367:    period 200.003** on the same binary and the same workload. Cross-check any
   368:    single symbol's share at two periods before pricing work on it; this one
   369:    sent a branch off with a target 1,8x too large.
   370: 4. **Line attribution inside a hot function overstates by roughly 2x from
   371:    skid.** Two lexer items priced at ~11 M from the line profile delivered
   372:    6,1 M; everything priced analytically from a census afterwards held.
   373: 5. **Idempotent doubling prices a pass the profile misreads**: run the pass
   374:    twice and take the delta, the downstream state being identical. `perf
   375:    annotate` put the selector's flat LOCAL scan at ~21 M; doubling says
   376:    **12,8 M**. Probes worth keeping as constants of this compiler: a bare
   377:    linked walk of the 1.401.051 IR rows is **10,8 M (7,7 instructions a row)**;
   378:    a bare flat walk of the 1.710.401 machine rows is **4,4 M (2,6 a row)**; the
   379:    opcode-to-exact lookup plus three field reads is **25,7 M (15 a row)**; one
   380:    selector candidate pass is **8,3 M (19 instructions a visit)**.
   381: 6. **Symbol-level shares are not comparable across builds.** In a unity build
   382:    the inlining decisions move code between symbols, so a symbol that grew its
   383:    share after a change that provably removed instructions from it has usually
   384:    absorbed a callee. Only whole-program `instructions:u` compares.
   385:

    40: 
    41: ## Controlled scope-allocation A/B
    42: 
    43: The checked-in regression builds 256 and 1,024 functions, each with a root,
    44: child and grandchild. Scope ids are grouped by depth, so descendants are not
    45: adjacent to their parents. The measured arena delta begins after allocating
    46: the input model and includes output buffers, relocations, types and scratch.
    47: The A/B restores only the original scope walker/allocation from `main` in
    48: otherwise identical patched code; it does not conflate the type-stream fix
    49: with traversal cost. Clang 17 Debug, non-unity, same process environment:
    50: 
    51: | Functions / scopes | Original walker | Indexed reusable walker |
    52: | --- | ---: | ---: |
    53: | 256 / 768 | 1,707,296 bytes | 144,672 bytes |
    54: | 1,024 / 3,072 | 25,701,152 bytes | 576,288 bytes |
    55: 
    56: Four times the input takes about 15.05 times the allocation with the old
    57: walker versus 3.98 times with the new one. At 1,024 functions this removes
    58: 25,124,864 allocated bytes, including the unchanged output allocation in
    59: both totals. Restoring the old walker fails exactly the three allocation
    60: bound/scaling assertions; the other 395,026 assertions still pass. No timing
    61: or retired-instruction speedup is claimed from this experiment.
    62: 
    63: ## Correctness and local gates
    64: 
    65: - Pristine `main`: 323,786/323,786 assertions, 39/39 modules, Clang 17 Debug.
    66: - Patched non-unity Debug: 395,029/395,029 assertions, 39/39 modules.
    67: - New structural tests decode 4,096-member structures and enums through at
    68:   least two continuation links, verify every member's order/value/type and
    69:   padding, exercise the exact single-member boundary and its overflow, and
    70:   merge two large PDB modules whose identical local indices name different
    71:   builtins. Final MSF module-stream tests check two procedures, four nested
    72:   blocks and two inline scopes, with interleaved C13 line subsections.
    73: - DWARF tests apply actual address relocations at two distinct nonzero module
    74:   bases, then interpret CU-relative function/scope/location ranges.
    75: - A 65,300-byte C member identifier is legal to the frontend but too large
    76:   for a CodeView record. `-g` now returns `OBJECT_ERROR_DEBUG_INFO` and a clear
    77:   diagnostic; the same source succeeds with `-g0`.
    78: - Real compiler probes produce single-/two-TU Linux executables, a Windows
    79:   executable/PDB and a 4,096-field COFF object. The pristine compiler silently
    80:   emits zero-sized `.debug$S` and `.debug$T` for the large aggregate; the fix
    81:   retains both. Extracted `.text` is byte-identical before/after for all four
    82:   probes (197, 197, 272 and 51 bytes respectively). Whole debug artifacts are

    20: 
    21: `machine_fast_owner_match_mask(owner, active, value)` now accepts the active
    22: mask directly. A sixteen-owner tile uses `simd512_load` and
    23: `simd512_equal_word` only if every lane of that tile is active. Other active
    24: lanes use the existing set-bit walk. This preserves sparse uninitialized
    25: rows, partial target files, and bounded loads without adding a sentinel fill
    26: or padded owner storage. The population test and dense-tile classification
    27: are additional overhead that still needs pricing on the target workload.
    28: 
    29: Membership, pending-blocker, dirty-owner, and split-span duplicate-removal
    30: queries use the helper. Owner-location search order is unchanged, including
    31: the last-match behavior of the fallback source search. The snapshot-based
    32: `machine_fast_conform_edge_parameters` is unchanged: PR #212 replaces that
    33: algorithm to repair parallel edge-copy semantics, and this patch does not
    34: compete with that correctness change.
    35: 
    36: Clang's Release `machine_fast_conform_edge` contains inlined queries: dense
    37: tiles emit `vpbroadcastd`, a memory-operand `vpcmpeqd`, and `kmovw`. There is
    38: no helper call or vector spill in those query loops. Inlining does not remove
    39: the sparse-path classification and result-mask costs.

    42: ## Scope lookup change and correctness
    43: 
    44: `c_parse_index_scope_children` retains the existing CSR arrays and order.
    45: During its existing fill pass it certifies that every child interval is
    46: well formed and that each sibling run is ordered and disjoint:
    47: `previous.token_end <= current.token_start`. It publishes one Boolean with
    48: that index. No extra index array, process-global cache or per-query
    49: allocation is added. The production builder runs once scopes are final,
    50: in `c_lower_to_ir`; its lifetime remains that of the existing temporary
    51: scope index. Rebuilding the index also recomputes the certificate.
    52: 
    53: A certified query finds the upper bound of the token among child starts.
    54: Only its predecessor can contain the token, and a separate end comparison
    55: preserves half-open ranges. It then descends iteratively. Equal-range
    56: parent/child pairs still resolve to the deepest child. Empty ranges,
    57: exclusive ends, gaps and tokens outside the supplied root keep their old
    58: answers. Scope IDs, entity IDs and diagnostic ordering do not change.
    59: 
    60: Certification is deliberately conservative. An out-of-order or overlapping
    61: hand-built model retains the original indexed scan, including its
    62: last-containing-sibling behavior. A manually built index whose new Boolean
    63: is zero also retains that path. A model with no CSR keeps the old full
    64: scan/ancestry fallback. Binary searching an assumed ordering would have
    65: silently changed those cases; early exit alone would still be quadratic.
    66: 
    67: For S scopes, depth D and B_i children at each visited level:
    68: 
    69: | Operation | Before | After |
    70: | --- | --- | --- |
    71: | Build child index | O(S) time and storage | O(S) time and storage; certification in existing pass |
    72: | Certified query | O(D + sum B_i) | O(D + sum log(B_i + 1)) |
    73: | Q queries across N siblings | Theta(Q*N); Theta(N squared) when Q is proportional to N | O(Q log N) |
    74: | Query scratch | O(1), no allocation | O(1), no allocation |
    75: | Unary nesting | O(D) per query | O(D) per query |
    76: | Uncertified/no-index models | Original scan costs | Unchanged fallback costs |
    77: 
    78: This does **not** make arbitrary semantic analysis linear. Repeated queries
    79: along a deep unary chain can still accumulate quadratic work, and #241 is
    80: an independent, worse asymptotic problem.
    81: 
    82: ## Stress benchmark
    83: 
    84: `tools/semantic_stress.py` generates sibling loops, deep/shadowing scopes,
    85: many common-prefix symbols, C23 constants, `_Generic`, rejected out-of-scope
    86: references and shared function-type DAGs. Generated programs are compiled,
    87: never executed. Depths for the DAG are separate from symbol/scope counts so
    88: requesting 32,768 symbols cannot accidentally request a depth-32,768 DAG.
    89: 
    90: The tool excludes one warmup, alternates compiler order, saves every wall/
    91: child-CPU/per-child-RSS sample, hashes source/compiler bytes, and compares
    92: exit status, stdout, stderr and optional object bytes across compilers and
    93: repetitions. A mismatch is a failure. Timeouts terminate the whole child
    94: process group on POSIX. No noisy wall-clock threshold is installed as a CI
    95: gate. GNU time provides per-child RSS; a cumulative `RUSAGE_CHILDREN`
    96: high-water mark is not treated as an independent sample.
    97:

   157: typedef int (*T0)(int);
   158: typedef T0 (*T1)(T0,T0);
   159: typedef T1 (*T2)(T1,T1);

   166: has 34 semantic types / 31 parameters. Syntax-only baseline medians at

   169: parse/semantics and 0.4 ms to lowering at depth 14.
   170: 
   171: Each function pair schedules its return and both parameter pairs, all
   172: sharing the preceding type. The traversal obeys
   173: `W(k) = 3*W(k-1) + O(1)` even though source and type-graph size are linear.
   174: A correct fix needs query-local dependency/pair accounting, late-mismatch
   175: tests and careful array-bound/mutation/qualifier handling. This PR does not
   176: install a speculative cross-query compatibility cache to make that test
   177: appear fast.

   165: FAST's timing improvement must not be credited to this queue change; binary
   166: layout and this VM's execution variability are possible confounders. The
   167: patch is justified by removal of demonstrably repeated work and dead
   168: representation surface, not a claim of an end-to-end compiler speedup.
   169: 
   170: All measured full-compilation outputs are byte-identical before/after.
   171: The 256-function pressure corpus schedules and keeps all 256 functions;
   172: real `machine.c` schedules and keeps 43 of 446. Both have zero backend
   173: fallbacks. Checksums, sizes, CPU time, individual timings and commands are
   174: in the raw JSON/log evidence.
   175: 
   176: GNU time measurements in the CPU-2 series avoid the inherited Python-fork
   177: RSS floor present in the initial wait4-only pilot. Median peak RSS is
   178: 230,978 versus 231,072 KiB for 2,048 pressure functions, 106,616 versus
   179: 106,612 KiB for machine.c, and 894,938 versus 895,040 KiB for frozen unity.
   180: There is no meaningful RSS improvement. No dynamic allocation-count change
   181: was measured or claimed. `perf_event_open` for hardware cycles returns
   182: ENOENT in this VM, so cycles, retired instructions and cache/branch events
   183: are unavailable, not zero.

    39: ## What actually selects instructions
    40: 
    41: `machine_select_generated.c` contains ten named declarative rules, but the
    42: call-site search for `machine_selection_rule_select` finds only the definition,
    43: declaration, and tests. Production native selectors do not dispatch through
    44: that matcher. Packing those rows or indexing them by opcode would optimize a
    45: diagnostic/test path, not current compiler throughput.
    46: 
    47: The diagnostic matcher has meaningful behavior that should not be casually
    48: changed: FAST picks the first eligible rule in table order; QUALITY continues
    49: the ordered scan and retains at most four additional alternatives. Candidate
    50: cost is static rank plus a side-effect flag, not a measured target cost model.
    51: The fallback row is QUALITY-legal but not FAST-legal; the no-match result has
    52: `UINT16_MAX` estimated cost and sets the legacy-fallback flag. An attractive
    53: microbenchmark must not erase these distinctions or masquerade as production
    54: selection timing.
    55: 
    56: Production entry points are `machine_select_validated_canonical_function`,
    57: `machine_select_canonical_function_x86_64`, and the AArch64 selector. The native
    58: selectors directly dispatch canonical opcodes and selected operand forms.
    59: There is no general production DAG-covering search to accelerate by indexing
    60: this diagnostic rule table. Existing direct selection is the baseline, not a
    61: proposed new abstraction layer.
