    53: CPUs, 4 GiB memory. Clang 17.0.0, GNU binutils 2.44, split Release build,
    54: `-O2 -DNDEBUG`, frame pointers enabled, debug information disabled. Both
    55: compilers use the same feature target, source path and output path convention.
    56: Native AVX-512 execution works on this host; no APX execution is assumed.
    57: 
    58: The three assembly inputs contain 24,000 instructions each. The scalar cycle
    59: is `movq %rax,%r8`; `addq $7,%rax`; `leaq 24(%rbx,%rcx,4),%rdi`;
    60: `xorq %r9,%r10`. The vector cycle is
    61: `vaddps 64(%rax),%zmm1,%zmm0{%k1}`;
    62: `vaddpd -128(%rbp),%ymm1,%ymm0{%k1}`;
    63: `vpaddd 32(%rax,%rcx,4),%xmm1,%xmm0{%k1}`. The broadcast cycle is
    64: `vaddps 64(%rax){1to16},%zmm1,%zmm0{%k1}`;
    65: `vaddpd -1024(%rbp){1to4},%ymm1,%ymm0{%k1}`;
    66: `vpaddd 508(%rax,%rcx,4){1to4},%xmm1,%xmm0{%k1}`.
    67: Each source starts with `.text`, repeats its cycle to 24,000 instructions,
    68: and ends with a newline. Compile with `ide cc -c -march=native input.s -o out.o`.
    69: 
    70: Each compiler is pinned to logical CPU 4. Two warm-up pairs precede nine
    71: measured pairs, alternating which compiler runs first. Measurements use
    72: monotonic wall time and child `wait4` CPU time/peak RSS. Every repeated output
    73: hash is checked for determinism. These are process-level compile measurements,
    74: not a counter-based encoder-only microbenchmark.
    75: 
    76: | Input | Baseline wall median | Fixed wall median | Baseline CPU median | Fixed CPU median | Peak RSS median, both | Object bytes before -> after |
    77: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    78: | Scalar | 1.380619 s | 1.387028 s | 1.376861 s | 1.383705 s | 93,352 KiB | 90,448 -> 90,448 |
    79: | Vector | 0.567687 s | 0.578178 s | 0.567452 s | 0.577976 s | 94,376 KiB | 176,448 -> 176,448 |
    80: | Broadcast | 0.585680 s | 0.596564 s | 0.585484 s | 0.596352 s | 94,760 KiB | 200,448 -> 176,448 |
    81: 
    82: Medians of the nine paired fixed/baseline wall ratios are 1.0058, 1.0323,
    83: and 1.0021 respectively. Their 95% bootstrap intervals, resampling pairs
    84: 10,000 times, are [0.9336,1.0434], [0.9720,1.0599], and [0.9505,1.0663].
    85: These intervals all include no change. This noisy run cannot resolve a
    86: small regression or establish a speedup. Part of the experiment overlapped
    87: compilation on other affinity CPUs; the shared CPU quota is another reason
    88: not to overinterpret the estimates. The broadcast size reduction follows
    89: correct scalar disp8 compression, not equivalent behavior from baseline's
    90: incorrect encodings. No allocation-count or hardware-counter claim is made:
    91: `perf` is absent, and allocation counting was not instrumented.

   177: from pathlib import Path
   178: out = Path('build/ssa-corpus')
   179: out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
   180: (out / 'functions.c').write_text(''.join(
   181:     f'int f{i}(int x) {{ int value=x+{i}; for(int j=0;j<5;j++) '
   182:     '{ if(value&1) value+=j+3; else value^=j+7; } return value; }\n'
   183:     for i in range(1280)))
   184: (out / 'diamonds.c').write_text('int diamonds(int x) { int result=x;\n' +
   185:     ''.join(f'if ((x >> {i % 16}) & 1) result += {i % 29 + 1}; '
   186:             f'else result ^= {i+1};\n' for i in range(700)) +
   187:     'return result; }\n')
   188: ```

   195: ```

   201: ```

   205: invocation. Independently time a direct child process with a monotonic clock and
   206: collect its CPU time/RSS with `wait4`; process startup, object writing and linking

    26: ## Lifetime and capacity contract
    27: 
    28: Previously every nonempty function body reserved `body_token_count + 1`
    29: 12-byte `CParserBlockFrame` records in the translation-unit arena. The frame
    30: array is private scratch for statement splitting; no published declaration,
    31: assertion or diagnostic stores a frame pointer.
    32: 
    33: The syntax pass now owns one vector that starts at 16 frames, doubles when
    34: its live prefix fills, and is reused for later bodies. Reallocation copies
    35: only live frames, and the body walker refreshes its pointer before the next
    36: access. Old chunks remain arena-owned until the translation unit ends, so
    37: cumulative frame storage is less than twice the largest allocated capacity;
    38: it scales with maximum simultaneous body depth, not cumulative body tokens.
    39: The syntax pass's existing token-count limit bounds the last possible capacity
    40: doubling at 2^30 to 2^31. Declaration records, static-assertion ranges and the
    41: token-indexed diagnostic/delimiter arrays retain their existing lifetimes.
    42: 
    43: ## Same-input storage evidence
    44: 
    45: The test-only `BUSTER_PARSER_FRAME_CENSUS=1` switch prints the arena-position
    46: delta around `c_parse_ast`, after preprocessing has finished. Its
    47: `published_bytes` accounting subtotal combines the unchanged diagnostic and
    48: delimiter arrays with the published declaration and assertion sizes. Alignment
    49: remains in the measured total.
    50: There is no production allocation observer and no timed gate.
    51: 
    52: The same regression source and census code were run with the old and new
    53: body walker. Each shallow function has one assertion, ordinary statements

    15: 
    16: `ir_system_v_abi_classes` previously reserved
    17: `max(program->types.count * 16, 16)` tasks for every small aggregate query.
    18: It now starts with 32 local tasks and grows scratch geometrically only when
    19: the pending frontier requires it. Growth copies the live prefix. The old
    20: type-count-derived acceptance limit remains; array counts are checked before
    21: addition, including an impossible count that could wrap a widened sum. Only
    22: classification values escape, through the existing caller-owned ABI context.
    23: 
    24: The regression uses over 1,000 unrelated types and a fresh thread context:
    25: the two-field FLOAT/INTEGER query leaves every scratch position and dirty
    26: watermark unchanged. Nested forty-way unions force two growth steps while a
    27: pending floating field survives both copies. Growth and invalid-type failure
    28: rewind scratch. Poisoning it afterward does not change the cached result, and
    29: the context's classification counter proves that the repeated query reuses its
    30: cache. A malformed maximum-count array with a pending sibling is rejected
    31: before frontier arithmetic can wrap. Existing ABI oracle coverage is retained.
    32:

    34: It does not establish a compiler speedup or a reduction in peak process memory.

    26: ## Change and correctness boundary
    27: 
    28: Keep 32 rows of each search array in fixed local storage. When the initialized
    29: prefix fills the current capacity, grow all arrays geometrically together,
    30: copy that prefix, and preserve the index-valued parent chain. Keep the type
    31: count as the original validity/cycle bound. The reversed field path uses
    32: `found_depth + 1` entries, with the same 32-entry local allowance.
    33: 
    34: Breadth-first order, the nearest-depth rule, same-depth ambiguity, qualified
    35: places, invalid-type handling and the existing error-unwind paths are
    36: unchanged. Emitted values, instructions, operands, immediates and allocated
    37: diagnostics remain in the persistent builder arena. Search arrays and a deep
    38: path belong only to the temporal arena. The fixed local arrays total 640
    39: bytes of element storage. Growth retains earlier allocations until rewind,
    40: so an unusually large reachable graph can request more than one full grown
    41: array set; this is not a universal reduction in every graph's peak scratch.
    42: 
    43: The direct regression builds a real 4,096-type table. A small lookup must
    44: leave the temporary arena's dirty high-water mark unchanged, whereas the
    45: previous four array requests alone required 65,552 bytes at that table size.
    46: Wide and deep searches must restore the position and stay below 4 KiB of
    47: requested scratch in the tested shapes. This high-water mark measures the
    48: allocated byte range retained across rewind; it does not measure physical
    49: pages dirtied, cumulative bytes across a full compile, or peak RSS.
    50: 
    51: The regression also covers 80 anonymous siblings (two growth boundaries),
    52: a 41-field path crossing structs and unions, direct members before and after
    53: anonymous siblings, equal-depth ambiguity, missing members, a cyclic/invalid
    54: anonymous edge, invalid root types, and inherited/field volatility and
    55: read-only places. It overwrites the entire released scratch prefix before
    56: checking the emitted field chain or missing-member diagnostic.
    57: 
    58: The recovered runtime fixture runs all four allocators with both frontend
    59: SSA settings. It combines wide/deep member paths, const volatile reads and
    60: aggregate calls whose results are consumed after later function lowering.
    61: Independent Clang/GCC callers and callees use the same fixture in both link
    62: directions.

    51: 
    52: For a leaf root, the production validator now uses one local `CTypeId` entry.
    53: Only array/struct/union roots acquire the existing private graph scratch.
    54: Both storage choices feed the same checks in the same order: atomic,
    55: volatile/restrict, complete-object kind, then array bounds or aggregate
    56: members. Pointees are not subobjects. Invalid declaration/storage/type
    57: preconditions retain their diagnostic precedence and source locations.
    58: Touched control flow has one final return and remains nonrecursive.

    61: `(T + M + 1) * sizeof(CTypeId) + (T + 1) * sizeof(bool)` scratch bytes and
    62: explicitly clears `T + 1` visited bytes. The candidate requests no scratch for
    63: that leaf. These are source-derived work counts, not observed timings or RSS.
    64: Composite queries still have the old universe-sized storage and explicit
    65: visited walk; #259 is **not closed** by this slice. No persistent cache, wider

    12: ## Objective and boundary
    13: 
    14: The configured host compiler now controls the mixed-object fixture command
    15: family, including its wrapper argument. The ELF linker ignores an unused
    16: undefined `_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_` marker emitted by GCC on x86-64 Linux while
    17: preserving ordinary undefined-symbol failures and referenced marker handling.
    18: Both PIC and non-PIC assertions remain active.
    19: 
    20: Clang 18 and GCC 13 disagree on the SysV register class of a record containing
    21: a float and a nonzero unnamed integer bitfield. The explicit driver option
    22: `-fsysv-unnamed-bitfields=integer|padding` selects that narrow boundary;
    23: `padding` remains the default. The policy belongs to an `IrAbiContext`, is set
    24: before ABI queries, and does not mutate canonical record layout or shared
    25: types. Other native calling conventions and non-native/LLVM output reject an
    26: explicit setting. Zero-width unnamed fields remain padding in both modes.
    27: 
    28: The configured host probe observes XMM0 with a mandatory later float argument
    29: and identifies the actual host convention without guessing a version cutoff.
    30: Mixed fixtures cover arguments, later scalar arguments, results, nested shapes,
    31: both link directions, all four allocators, and both frontend forms. A separate
    32: assembly return control clears the unused return register so a wrong policy
    33: cannot pass merely because a previous instruction left the expected value.
    34: 
    35: Primary upstream evidence: LLVM [#216777](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/216777)
    36: changed this classification; [#220788](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/220788)
    37: gates that behavior above Clang ABI compatibility version 23. This does not
    38: establish which released compiler includes those changes. Buster's option is
    39: not a general Clang ABI-version emulation switch.

     7: Verified missing MIR coverage, not a measured performance optimization.
     8: The frozen integration base is `e2395299585de664602dd081f220d25d524760d6`
     9: (tree `ef406394f4f1e463f74b33f0f8eb0a55c2b13d0a`), after #397, #366 and
    10: #407. The local tracked-source archive was checked against its Git tree;
    11: the separate round-2 audit on main is preserved. Issues #36 and #69 remain
    12: open: this implements zero counts only, not native backend retirement.
    13: 
    14: On the unchanged `tests/basic_c_aarch64_i128.c`, FAST/AArch64 Linux initially
    15: reports 38 functions and 12 fallbacks: nine CAST, one UNARY, two BINARY.
    16: After this change it reports 11: nine CAST and two BINARY. The new focused
    17: fixture initially refuses strict compilation with five fallback functions,
    18: first `leading32`; it then selects all seven functions under every MIR mode.
    19: Neither fixture was reduced to manufacture zero fallback.
    20: 
    21: ## Implementation
    22: 
    23: Append four opcodes, preserving previous replay opcode numbers. Consume
    24: CLZWr/CLZXr/RBITWr/RBITXr from the existing normalized assembly metadata via
    25: the importer; no handwritten production instruction words. Scalar trailing
    26: counts are RBIT followed by CLZ. The i128 path loads both limbs, counts each,
    27: and selects the primary count or 64 plus the secondary count with ordinary
    28: MIR comparison/mask/arithmetic rows before allocation. The high result limb
    29: is explicitly zeroed; the existing direct AArch64 zero-pair result of 128
    30: is preserved. No new graph, allocation callback or encoder macro-operation.
    31: 
    32: The registered regression adds 24 object-compilation legs: three AArch64
    33: desktop targets, four allocators including NONE, both frontend forms. MIR
    34: legs require zero fallback and codegen verification. Native AArch64 desktop
    35: hosts additionally execute the fixture in eight mode/frontend combinations.
    36: Foreign object compilation is not recorded as target execution.
    37: 
    38: The fixture checks every 32/64/128-bit one-bit position, low/high and mixed
    39: limbs, all-ones and all-zero pairs, and prefilled result storage. Its wide
    40: builtin spelling is an existing Buster AArch64 extension; the Clang/GCC
    41: control uses guarded 64-bit limb calls rather than truncating the operand or
    42: calling a standard zero-input builtin. This AArch64-specific fixture is not
    43: a new claim of x86 i128 builtin support. Eight independently assembled words
    44: cover each width and zero-register operands. Production-plan tests retain
    45: complete membership, invalid-field and packed-decoder-independence checks.
    46:

   125: ## Limits and disposition
   126: 
   127: The flag is not applied. It is a hidden LLVM option without a stability
   128: guarantee, Apple Clang's copy was not exercised, and it changes generated code
   129: for every function over the threshold — at this revision the module driver and
   130: the three test functions above. Adopting it would need a Clang-only
   131: configuration, matched builds on the CI runner, `test_all`, the self-host fixed
   132: point and the throughput guard on the resulting compiler, for a gain of about 2%
   133: of object-compile instructions.
   134: 
   135: Moving the direct emitter into a coarse helper was not attempted: the helper
   136: would inherit its roughly 4,700 blocks and the same transform chains, #36
   137: restricts that backend to correctness fixes until retirement, and #90 asks for
   138: splits at documented semantic boundaries rather than moves. Deleting the direct
   139: emitter under #36 is the change that would remove most of this function's cost,
   140: and it remains gated by #36's coverage, differential and budget criteria. At
   141: recording time GitHub showed #36 closed: the closing phrase "close #36" in
   142: `bc69d279`'s message ("This does not retire the direct backend or close #36")
   143: closed it on merge, while its latest comment says it stays open.
   144: 
   145: After this function, no single function exceeds 3.3% of the traced compile, and
   146: the optimizer is 43% to 54% of it. #413's remaining cost is a long tail, not a
   147: second outlier. This is documentation only: compiler tests and the self-host
   148: fixed point were not run because no compiler input changed.

    33: reverse-lookup sequence performs 2N²+N old comparisons (2,098,176 at N=1024).
    34: The registered production probe records 4,087 map reads at N=1024, within its
    35: 4N bound. This is deterministic work evidence, not a timing threshold.
    36: The counter exists only when both INCLUDE_TESTS and BENCH_ALLOCATIONS are ON;
    37: ordinary compilers have neither counter storage nor increments.

     1: `2026-09-12T152116Z` (Linux x86-64 shared KVM guest, Intel Xeon Platinum
     2: 8573C, Clang 18.1.3; **Stable linear source-map finalization**).
     3: 
     4: ## Scope and ordering contract
     5: 
     6: [GitHub #104](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/issues/104) requires source-map
     7: finalization whose cost does not depend on region displacement. Baseline:
     8: `fd0ba8ff8175952d12bbdb367adef13effcc4865`.
     9: 
    10: `c_source_map_sort` first scans adjacent unsigned 32-bit `start` keys. An
    11: already ordered or empty map allocates nothing and changes no rows. Otherwise,
    12: four stable least-significant-byte radix passes alternate the existing region
    13: array with one temporary array. Forward scatter preserves append order for
    14: ties. All fields move together, and the fourth pass finishes in the original
    15: array before its arena checkpoint is rewound. Origin recovery, publication,
    16: binary-search keys, pages and C23 respelling retain their existing order.
    17: 
    18: The initial scan performs at most N-1 comparisons. Each of four passes performs
    19: N histogram visits, 256 prefix entries and N row scatters. Thus finalization is
    20: O(N), independently of inversion count, with no recursion or new dependency.
    21: This bounds this finalizer, not every preprocessing operation.
    22: 
    23: The private test seam calls that production helper. Registered tests cover
    24: empty/singleton maps, ordered/equal/reverse/permuted keys, all four byte
    25: boundaries through UINT32_MAX, stable ties, permutation uniqueness, every
    26: semantic payload field, surrounding canaries, scratch poisoning and repeated
    27: finalization. Small source fixtures check exact line, column, logical file and
    28: token spelling across `#line`, macro arguments, stringification, pasting and
    29: builtins. The benchmark separates record-level ordering from whole-process
    30: preprocessing of ordinary checked-in source; it does not establish end-to-end
    31: worst-case source scaling.
    32: 
    33: ## Finalization time and storage
    34: 
    35: The trusted Clang Release binary ran the registered opt-in benchmark, one
    36: warmup and seven samples for each size/order. Construction, checks and poisoning
    37: are outside the timer; histogram/scatter, arena allocation and rewind are
    38: inside. These runs were serial with this task's builds and other measurements,
    39: but the shared host was not exclusive or physically qualified as Zen 5.
    40: 
    41: | Regions | Ordered median, us | Reverse median, us | Permuted median, us | Temporary arena bytes, unordered |
    42: |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    43: | 1,024 | 0.845 | 41.505 | 40.248 | 81,920 |
    44: | 4,096 | 2.246 | 160.467 | 159.772 | 327,680 |
    45: | 16,384 | 19.595 | 970.170 | 1,166.554 | 1,310,720 |
    46: | 65,536 | 171.565 | 4,136.038 | 4,341.846 | 5,242,880 |
    47: 
    48: All five orderings and all 140 raw samples are in
    49: [sort-bench.log](evidence/2026-09-12T152116Z/sort-bench.log). Cache effects and
    50: scheduling noise make wall time nonuniform per row; the bounded traversal above
    51: establishes complexity. No timing threshold is added to tests.
    52: 
    53: The old finalizer used no temporary arena buffer. The replacement uses exactly
    54: `N * sizeof(IrSourceRegion)` bytes plus possible alignment for unordered maps:
    55: 80N bytes on this host, measured with fresh arenas so old pool high-water marks
    56: cannot contaminate the result. All ordered/equal cases measured zero. The
    57: temporary allocation is logically rewound on every sorting call, and the
    58: histogram occupies another 1,024 bytes on the stack. Logical rewind does not
    59: decommit physical pages. Published row sizes/counts and retained storage are
    60: unchanged; peak resident memory must be assessed separately.

   160: instruction and costs only bandwidth, so a counter-based audit would see this
   161: change as a small regression and be wrong about it. Which of the two numbers
   162: matters is a property of the machine, not of the diff, and this host cannot
   163: settle it: 69,6 MB is a few milliseconds of one DDR5 channel at its peak
   164: against a compile that takes about 1,7 s of user time here, but a store that
   165: never leaves the write-combining path costs less than that and a cold one
   166: costs more, and the 5,58 M added instructions are predicted, dependency-free
   167: and spread over 3,36 M tokens. What the change does establish is that the
   168: compile writes 20,6% less memory for the same bytes out.
   169: 
   170: **Peak resident memory falls with the fill, and repeats.** A fill is not only
   171: bandwidth: a page that is written is a page that must be resident, and these
   172: arrays were being touched end to end for a sentinel the reader could infer.
   173: Three runs of each native compiler, peak RSS and page faults from the child's
   174: own `rusage`:
   175: 
   176: | native stage-1 | pristine | this head |
   177: |---|---:|---:|
   178: | peak RSS | 1.029.800 / 1.029.968 / 1.030.024 KB | 1.011.184 / 1.011.260 / 1.011.176 KB |
   179: | minor faults | 255.740 / 255.896 / 255.889 | 254.046 / 254.052 / 254.050 |
   180: 
   181: That is **-18.784 KB of peak RSS (-1,82%)** and **-1.839 minor faults
   182: (-0,72%)** on medians, and both series repeat to within 200 KB and 6 faults —
   183: a spread two orders of magnitude below the delta, which is what makes this the
   184: one end-to-end result this host can actually support. It is smaller than the
   185: 69,6 MB of fill removed, and it should be: some of those bytes were being
   186: written over pages the compile then uses anyway, and only the pages nothing
   187: ever touches leave the resident set.
   188: 
   189: The tiny compile (`ide cc -c` of `int main(void){return 0;}`) is
   190: 118.337.339 -> 118.337.377 Ir, which is the expected shape: the arrays are
   191: sized by token count and a four-token unit has nothing to fill either way.
   192: 
   193: Wall time on this host does not support a claim and none is made. Min-of-four
   194: user time on the native stage-1 compile is 1,641 s pristine against 1,680 s
   195: here, medians 1,936 s against 1,772 s — the two orderings disagree, which is
   196: what a shared 4-vCPU guest looks like. `ide bench` is 1.618.246 ns min /
   197: 1.691.373 ns median pristine against 1.653.755 / 1.707.248 here, on a 21.042-byte

   221: and one architecture, so the Debug/sanitizer matrix, the mode matrix and every
   222: non-x86-64 lane belong to CI on the submitted head and are not claimed.
   223: 
   224: ## Left standing, ranked
   225: 
   226: Shares are against 13.685,20 M, where 1% = 136,9 M. Fill figures are bytes
   227: written a compile, which this instrument reports directly.
   228: 
   229: - **`c_ir_ssa_grow_slots` writes 70,8 MB a compile, the largest single item
   230:   left**, and it is not a sentinel problem: the direct-SSA slot table doubles
   231:   from 64 entries and is cleared whole at every doubling, so 8.172 grows for
   232:   4.755 functions pay for the same table several times over. It is a
   233:   per-function scratch arena, so the zeroed path cannot help; what would is a
   234:   first capacity taken from the body's local count, which the builder already
   235:   knows before the first insert.
   236: - **The selector's per-value block is 51,5 MB** (33,9 zero + 17,6 "none"), the
   237:   item `2026-09-07T013544Z` ranked second and which has grown with the tree. The
   238:   "none" half is five or six `u32` arrays set to `UINT32_MAX`; the bias that
   239:   landed here does not apply, because the block is a per-function scratch arena
   240:   that is dirty by construction — a one-byte present bitmap beside them would,
   241:   at the cost of a load and a test on each read.
   242: - **`CIrExt80Big shifted = {0}` is 8,65 MB over 2.101 calls** (`c_gen.c:8634`),
   243:   which is a 4 KB `u32 limbs[1024]` zeroed on the stack for a shift that then
   244:   writes `value->count + limb_shift` of them. Clearing to the used length is a
   245:   two-line change; it is left here only because it is not a fill of the class
   246:   this audit was working.
   247: - **`ir_validate_canonical_module` is 1.181 M Ir, 8,6% of the compile.** The
   248:   validation is required before backend consumption and is not a candidate for
   249:   removal, but nothing has ever measured what inside it costs, and 8,6% is
   250:   larger than the whole of `machine_encode_x86_64`.
   251: - **`ir.c:4404`'s instruction-owner map, 9,9 MB over 14.265 calls.** It looks
   252:   like the same `0xff` shape as the four arrays above and is not: the buffer
   253:   is one scratch array sized to the largest function and reused for every
   254:   function in the module, so the fill is already only
   255:   `function->instruction_count` entries (692 bytes a call) and it is *load
   256:   bearing* — without it the previous function's owners would read as this
   257:   one's. Biasing the sentinel would not remove a byte. The only form that
   258:   would is a generation stamp compared on each read, which trades 9,9 MB of
   259:   fill for a compare in the ownership walk and has to be measured rather than
   260:   assumed.

   140:

   142: `5dab18af0208cfa7fa65673b6884d5c253fda85b`, not this report's main SHA. Its
   143: Clang 18.1.3 compiler ran under Valgrind 3.22 in a four-vCPU KVM guest with
   144: `-march=x86-64-v3`. AVX-512 was disabled in that measured binary. Its
   145: 13,749,246,043 Callgrind `Ir` total and inclusive `c_preprocess` contribution
   146: of approximately 1,409 million / 10.2% are **neither retired hardware
   147: instructions nor current-main wall time nor a native Zen 5 profile**.
   148: 
   149: That workload reported 30,729,994 lexed source bytes, 3,021,627 lexed tokens,
   150: 3,364,471 preprocessed tokens and 124,859 macro expansions. Applying the
   151: current 12-byte row size to those historical token counts gives 36,259,524
   152: and 40,373,652 payload bytes respectively, plus their one-byte sidecars. This
   153: is illustrative arithmetic, not a measured allocation total, simultaneous peak
   154: RSS or a candidate saving. Do not infer `N` or `F` from expansion count.
   155: 
   156: The [August 22 census][a22] found 283,569 windows advancing 13,963,372 bytes,
   157: about 49.2 useful bytes per 64-byte window, and approximately half of all
   158: lexed bytes passing through the then-scalar escape. The host long-item scans
   159: were subsequently improved there, with a reported 37,030,960-instruction
   160: stage-1 reduction (0.3700%); noisy cycles were not a wall-time win. The same
   161: audit rejected adding cross-chunk escape parity to the long-item search.
   162: These are historical observations explaining candidate selection, not fresh
   163: headroom on the current compact path.
   164: 
   165: For any *measured* phase fraction `f` and isolated phase speedup `s`, an
   166: otherwise unchanged whole workload has the model
   167: `S = 1 / ((1 - f) + f / s)`. A Callgrind fraction cannot be substituted for a
   168: wall-time fraction. A high byte-throughput number for a stop scanner also
   169: cannot be substituted for `s` of all preprocessing.

    53: ## 3. Evidence ledger: observations versus hypotheses
    54: 
    55: ### Historical measurements, not rerun
    56: 
    57: The [newest audit][latest-audit] used frozen compiler/workload source `5dab18af0208cfa7fa65673b6884d5c253fda85b`, Clang 18.1.3, a virtualized x86 host and an x86-64-v3 Callgrind producer. It reports approximately **1,000 million Callgrind Ir / 7.3%** in `machine_select_canonical_function_x86_64`, and approximately **2,874 million Ir / 20.9%** in `codegen_generate_canonical_module_with_trace`. These inclusive figures overlap; do not add them. Callgrind Ir is not hardware retired instructions, current-main wall time or an AVX-512 measurement.
    58: 
    59: That audit reports selector initialization traffic of **33,949,578 zero-fill bytes** and **17,551,853 sentinel-fill bytes**, each over 4,755 calls, plus **15,921,423 address-cache fill bytes** over 3,871 calls. The numbers motivate charging startup, clearing and temporary storage. They do not prove a present bottleneck or justify an extra full-function projection pass.
    60: 
    61: A separate [historical #131 comment][131-profile] reports a native Ryzen 7 9700X Superluminal capture at `44a90fcbff44988624878aff9db3346a8bc6550b`: selection **71.727 ms inclusive / 37.867 ms exclusive**, FAST prepass **21.481 ms inclusive**, and a **708.685 ms compiler-lane** denominator. It was one 8 kHz sampling capture, not controlled A/B evidence. The [later correction][131-correction] retracts unsupported locality/bottleneck/whole-compiler-ceiling inferences. This report does not repeat them.
    62: 
    63: ### Evidence missing for a production decision
    64: 
    65: The inspected evidence does **not** provide a current-pin joint distribution of `(opcode, suboperation, type, target features, selected family)`, homogeneous run lengths, address-cache query transcripts, eligible tile occupancy, scheduling-unit occurrence counts, ready-event lengths, score recomputation multiplicity or duplicate-touch refresh frequency. Aggregate canonical/MIR counts are not these distributions.
    66: 
    67: Consequently, the following are hypotheses: that signature batching pays for packing; that masked evaluation beats predictable scalar dispatch; that a gathered table load is faster than scalar loads; that an occurrence cache is worthwhile; and that AVX-512 beats AVX2 or scalar bitsets. No fabricated timings, occupancy percentages, thresholds or speedup estimates are supplied.
    68: 
    69: The requested five-way comparison is a specified experiment below, not a completed measurement. Source-level invariants and arithmetic cost models are the new evidence in this report.
    70: 
    71: ## 4. Selection design: bounded pure-decision tiles, ordered publication
    72: 
    73: ### 4.1 Separate six kinds of work
    74: 
    75: **Fact discovery:** reuse validated canonical rows, `MachineTypeClass`, existing value facts, immutable target configuration and completed target-owned fusion/promotion facts. Do not add a second ownership/use scan. Rows not covered by existing compact facts take the original scalar path.
    76: 
    77: **Legality:** preserve exact type width, signedness, ABI, target-feature and operand-shape checks. A fast signature is not proof that an operation is legal. Invalid input follows the existing validated/unvalidated entry contract; do not remove canonical validation or duplicate it for every tile.
    78: 
    79: **Classification:** assign a bounded family only after its pure prerequisites are known: ordinary scalar integer arithmetic/bit operations; scalar constants and width conversions; already-discovered address/immediate predicates. Calls, assembly, atomics, volatile memory, dynamic stack, wide ABI transport, complex vectors, predicate residency and fusion-dependent cases initially remain scalar.
    80: 
    81: **Decision:** compute only the choices currently made by the target helper. No new instruction form, folding opportunity, reassociation, instruction ordering or cost heuristic is selected. A legal ISA immediate form which current lowering does not choose is not authorization to start choosing it.
    82: 
    83: **Operand construction:** resolving/materializing operand registers, assigning new vregs, defining values, assigning frame slots, recording relocations, expanding CFG blocks and appending immediates are ordered effects. `machine_x64_operand_register`, `machine_a64_operand_register`, the target row appenders and all ABI helpers remain in this phase.
    84: 
    85: **Publication:** consume decisions in the exact original target walk order. Preserve zero-row lowered instructions, source marks, definition points, CFG/edge copies and first-refusal diagnostics. A tile stores temporary choices, not a second machine IR.
    86: 
    87: ### 4.2 Proposed private layout
    88: 
    89: The following is a research layout, not an existing public type or a requested permanent schema:
    90: 
    91: ```c
    92: // One worker-owned tile; explicitly align its allocation to 64 bytes.
    93: // Arrays have capacity 16; only [0, count) may be read.
    94: typedef struct SelectionDecisionTile SelectionDecisionTile;
    95: struct SelectionDecisionTile
    96: {
    97:     u64 signature[16];
    98:     u32 canonical_row[16];
    99:     u16 plan[16];
   100:     u8 original_lane[16];
   101:     u8 status[16];
   102:     u32 count;
   103:     u16 active_mask;
   104:     u16 decision_mask;
   105: };
   106: ```
   107: 
   108: The arrays total 256 bytes; the final fields add 8, so the ordinary 8-byte-aligned layout is 264 bytes and a 64-byte-rounded allocation is **320 bytes**. An optional 16-element `u64` immediate stream costs another **128 bytes**. Address projection storage is separate and only allocated for an admitted address family; copying sixteen complete existing address facts would cost **896 bytes**, before alignment. This cost is not hidden in the core tile. Never allocate a full-function decision array by default.
   109: 
   110: A lossless signature for the admitted subset can encode 16-bit opcode, 16-bit suboperation, and the four existing 8-bit `MachineTypeClass` fields. Add compile-time bounds checks and an explicit scalar escape for any enum/domain that does not fit. Do not silently truncate, hash without equality checking, discard vector lane shape or infer unresolved layout. Wide/aggregate/vector cases needing facts beyond this signature are not admitted by the initial subset.
   111: 
   112: Target architecture, OS/ABI, PIC policy, predicate-residency policy and the complete effective feature configuration belong to the immutable tile context, not a lossy feature hash in each row. An optional compact feature-policy index must identify that exact context, with its lifetime and equality guaranteed. Host SIMD availability and features of the generated-code target are independent.
   113: 
   114: `plan` is a small selector-private choice already understood by the owning target helper, not a global matcher ID. Make the helper's existing decision the single authority: extract/reuse the decision expression and feed it to that same producer. Do not retain a second scalar decision tree beside a table that can drift.
   115: 
   116: ### 4.3 Pseudocode and order proof
   117: 
   118: ```text
   119: complete the existing target prepasses and their mutation
   120: for each block in the existing target order:
   121:     preserve block-entry and ABI emission
   122:     while source rows remain and selection remains supported:
   123:         identify a bounded prefix with immutable decision inputs
   124:         stop at every cold/state-dependent boundary
--- lines 287-379 ---
   287: 
   288: T_cached  = same_unchanged_terms + cache_build(E)
   289:           + cached_score_reads(R) + event_stage(P) + reductions(P)
   290:           + scratch_cost + any cache-pressure cost
   291: ```
   292: 
   293: A cache breaks even only when saved repeated decode/read cost exceeds construction, extra demand representation, memory and replay costs. For a one-use unit the cache may be strictly extra work. `P`, `R/E`, event-size distributions, tail occupancy and the fraction rejected by pressure gates are necessary denominators. A role-lane microkernel speedup alone cannot establish a backend gain.
   294: 
   295: Measure complete backend including selection, legalization/refusal, placement, scheduling and any second placement, encoding, relocation handling and final publication. Measure fresh-process whole compilation including source metrics, canonical preparation/validation, startup, tables, object writing/shutdown, plus executable-generation/self-host completeness separately. Do not add nested inclusive profiler costs or sums of medians. Report cold process versus warm retained-IR selector replay separately. Neither includes a claim of cold OS page-cache behavior unless explicitly tested.
   296: 
   297: ## 7. Metadata startup, ownership and footprint
   298: 
   299: Compare these alternatives without silently retaining all of them:
   300: 
   301: **Existing serial prewarm:** retain `machine_opcode_rows_prewarm` and its single authority. The smallest candidate reuses it, so there is no new table to initialize. Hoist a table pointer, not repeated once-guards into an operand loop.
   302: 
   303: **Checked-in/generated constants:** possible only if generated by the existing metadata authority and verified byte-for-byte against runtime projection. Count read-only binary bytes, relocations, loader/page-fault effects, self-host build cost and tiny-compile startup. No handwritten duplicate table or metadata importer is proposed here.
   304: 
   305: **Cached operation facts:** module type facts are already amortized. Add only facts actually consumed by an admitted kernel. Per-function scratch is not assumed zero; historical fill traffic is a warning against a universal cache. Arena rewind/lifetimes and cache invalidation after canonical mutation must remain explicit.
   306: 
   307: Shared global tables are initialized serially under `BUSTER_CHECK_SERIAL_INITIALIZATION()` and publish readiness last. No new atomics, locks, per-row memory fences, non-temporal stores or worker-side lazy global writes are necessary. Per-lane scratch is private; existing lane barriers and deterministic work-indexed publication provide ownership transfer. A module's lazy signature plans must not become shared across concurrent function selectors without a separate ownership proof.

   226: Buster on an authorized runner before selecting vector thresholds.
   227: 
   228: ## Common dependency and readiness contract
   229: 
   230: A descriptor is ready only when its exact facts are available through the
   231: existing authoritative path. Source-text proximity does not establish readiness.
   232: A batch key includes its caller/phase, target/dialect, original request order and
   233: semantic snapshot or bounded lifetime. A generation is a design requirement,
   234: not a claim that current source already exposes a universal mutation counter.
   235: Where it does not, end the batch at the existing helper boundary.
   236: 
   237: | C concern | Independent work | Dependency-bearing work and required barrier |
   238: |---|---|---|
   239: | Typedef names | Punctuation class, fixed keyword class, identifier symbol already present | Whether `T` is a typedef in this scope and declaration prefix; cast/declaration disambiguation stays with lookup/type parsing. Never set a global typedef bit from spelling. |
   240: | Scope and declaration order | Already-bound entity IDs and immutable source offsets | `typedef int T; { int T; ... }`, redeclarations, tags and declarations that affect later declarators require source-order publication. Finish before crossing a binding mutation. |
   241: | Incomplete types | Kind/qualifier observations in a stable snapshot | Completion, inferred array bounds, alignment and enum underlying types can change later answers. No cross-epoch compatibility or layout cache. |
   242: | Constant expressions | Classify an already-typed operator or test already-computed integer flags | Evaluate with existing target arithmetic, short-circuit, overflow and diagnostic rules. Do not execute both branches, invent a host-width evaluator, or fold identifiers before binding. |
   243: | Initializers | Pure predicates on the already-established destination type | Designators, brace elision, member order, inferred bounds, compound literals and initializer evaluation remain authoritative scalar work. Do not build a second initializer image. |
   244: | Unevaluated operands | Type-only constraints that remain required, such as named-call arity | Unevaluated does not mean unchecked. VLA `sizeof`, `_Generic`, `typeof` and diagnostics cannot be handled by blanket skipping or eager evaluation. |
   245: | Target-dependent rules | Predicates within one frozen target/dialect group | Pointer and integer widths, plain-char policy, atomic layout, vector widths, ABI and C17/C23 prototype rules must not leak across groups. |
   246: | Malformed source | Bounds-safe lexical facts about present tokens | Existing recovery, mismatched delimiters, failure precedence, diagnostic suppression and no-artifact policy remain unchanged. Scalar fallback is not permission to silently accept. |
   247: 
   248: Across declarations, stop before publishing anything that can change the next
   249: request's binding or type facts. Across functions, only immutable lexical
   250: summaries are ready merely because body boundaries are known; shared semantic
   251: queries need the #531 readiness contract. Across expressions inside an existing
   252: query, children become ready according to existing continuation frames. Across
   253: independent type queries, batch only when the caller already owns a set of
   254: requests with identical frozen context; manufacturing that set by reparsing or
   255: rebinding is duplicated work.
   256: 
   257: ### Diagnostics and bounded scratch
   258: 
   259: Use the **existing semantic traversal/phase order**, not a global sort by source
   260: location. Macro expansion and include provenance do not sort like filenames;
   261: LIFO type checks do not necessarily visit members in textual order. In a caller
   262: whose current diagnostics are source ordered, preserve its preprocessed-token
   263: ordinal and intra-token diagnostic order. A result key is conceptually
   264: `(phase, original_request_ordinal, original_local_check_ordinal)`.
   265: 
   266: Workers or vector lanes return facts/error codes, never formatted diagnostics,
   267: new entities or published types. The scalar coordinator commits only the next
   268: original request. A later lane's failure cannot overtake an earlier unresolved
   269: one. Keep current first-error and warning policies; format the selected failure
   270: with the existing formatter and original provenance. Cancel/discard the suffix
   271: at an error or mutation barrier. Charge any work already performed on it.
   272: 
   273: Scratch is reclaimed at the existing query mark; capacities use checked integer
   274: arithmetic. A bounded queue, for example 256 descriptors, is a research parameter
   275: rather than a chosen production default. Queue saturation or allocation refusal
   276: must take the ordinary scalar path without changing errors. No whole-TU sidecar
   277: is justified merely because it is easy to allocate.
   278: 
   279: ## A1: indexed operator summaries for the existing expression-type machine
   280:

   282: 
   283: In `c_type_parse_sizeof_step`, the scan for `best_operator` is repeated for
   284: subranges as tasks split. The implementation already handles unary prefixes
   285: without restarting a known-empty operator search and skips complete indexed
   286: nested groups. The remaining hypothesis is that some long, flat binary ranges
   287: still accumulate enough repeated visits to justify a reusable operator index.
   288: That is a source-derived possibility, not a measured current hotspot.
   289: 
   290: First retain a no-allocation scalar threshold. The strongest scalar alternative

   409: ## A2: ordered batches of bound-call predicates
   410: 
   411: ### Existing semantic seam and readiness
   412: 
   413: `c_semantic_check_named_call_arities` already scans a caller-provided range in
   414: token order. It recognizes an identifier followed by `(`, first uses the bound
   415: identifier-use record, and otherwise uses the existing innermost-scope lookup.
   416: It excludes declaration name tokens, resolves a function or named function
   417: pointer, skips indexed nested groups when counting arguments, and retains the
   418: first diagnostic. Its outer scan still visits calls inside those groups.
   419: 
   420: The predicate is already cheap:
   421: 
   422: ```text
   423: accept = (variadic OR effective_unprototyped)
   424:          ? argument_count >= parameter_count
   425:          : argument_count == parameter_count
   426: ```
   427: 
   428: `effective_unprototyped` includes the existing C23 dialect gate. This checker
   429: covers named callees only, not arbitrary computed/member/builtin-only callees,
   430: argument conversions or all language constraints. Its existence does not
   431: certify semantic-only compilation.
   432: 
   433: A ready descriptor contains already-resolved `entity_id`, effective signature
   434: counts/flags, call-token index, complete argument count, original ordinal and
   435: caller context. Sourcepoint visibility must be the current resolver's answer,
   436: not a late lookup in a final symbol table. Symbol interning, scoped lookup,
   437: type completion, argument-boundary discovery and errors are coordinator work.
   438: Prepare them once through existing helpers; do not rebind the expression in a
   439: vector prepass.
   440: 
   441: ### Representation and algorithm
   442: 
   443: Use query-local SoA columns for `argument_count`, `parameter_count`, normalized
   444: flags and original ordinal; keep token/entity IDs in cold side columns. Six
   445: 32-bit columns would be 24 bytes per descriptor, or 6 KiB at a hypothetical
   446: capacity of 256. Charge those stores and subsequent reads. Persist neither the
   447: queue nor duplicate signatures after the existing checking range completes.
   448: 
   449: The guaranteed-independent kernel begins **after** these facts are ready and
   450: frozen. A transparent interposer on today's sequential producer cannot always
   451: fill it: after preparing a call whose predicate has not yet been evaluated,
   452: preparing later calls is speculation unless those preparations are proven
   453: nonmutating, nondiagnostic and independent of the earlier result. Default to
   454: flushing before such a helper. Do not hide that limitation by assuming a
   455: semantic-only work queue that current source does not have.
   456: 
   457: ```text
   458: coordinator visits named-call candidates in the original order:
   459:     perform existing binding/type/count preparation exactly once
   460:     if preparation needs a mutation/error-capable boundary:
   461:         commit pending prefix first, or stay scalar
   462:     if descriptor is ready in this stable context:
   463:         append to bounded queue
   464:     else:
   465:         use original scalar check
   466:     flush at capacity, query end, dependency barrier, or required result
   467: 
   468: pure_kernel(queue):
   469:     floor = variadic | effective_unprototyped
   470:     bad = (argument_count < parameter_count)
   471:           | ((~floor) & (argument_count != parameter_count))
   472:     return bad mask, never diagnostics or new types
   473: 
   474: commit(queue, bad):
   475:     choose earliest bad original ordinal, not completion/lane order
   476:     call c_semantic_call_arity_message for that item only
   477:     preserve original token/provenance and stop policy
   478:     discard suffix; release scratch at caller's original boundary
   479: ```
   480: 
   481: Bitwise notation above operates on normalized predicate masks, not arbitrary
   482: integer flag complements. A real implementation must preserve valid-lane masks
   483: and the original unsigned count domain. Out-of-range IDs are rejected or handled
   484: before gathers; there are no masked invalid-pointer reads on scalar fallbacks.
   485: 
   486: Argument-count discovery may consume existing comma/open-group masks, but it
   487: must retain nested-group ownership. A ternary middle operand containing a comma
   488: is a particularly important differential case; no fresh correctness reproduction
   489: was run here. Initially keep conditional/malformed argument structure on the
   490: original path rather than certifying a new counter from a lexical comma count.
   491: Likewise, computed or member callees remain explicitly unsupported by this
   492: narrow batching seam, not silently blessed.
   493: 
   494: ### Beyond arity, without duplicate semantics
   495: 
   496: The same ready queue concept can group already-produced call-constraint facts
   497: such as prototype flags or prepared scalar category predicates, **only when the
   498: existing authoritative checker already computes those facts**. Pointer conversion,
   499: null-pointer-constant recognition, lvalue requirements, qualifier stripping and
   500: ABI layout are not reduced to arity; they need their own readiness proof and
   501: shared predicate authority. This report does not add a second checker for them.
   502: 
   503: Cross-expression batching is possible inside an already-established immutable
   504: checking range. Cross-declaration/function batching is conditional on the caller
   505: having bound entities and sourcepoint-correct signatures without intervening
   506: publication. C17 `f()` versus C23 `f()`, shadowing and later redeclarations make a
   507: single translation-unit-wide signature table unsound for this purpose.
   508: 
   509: ### Break-even and disposition
   510: 
   511: Let B ready predicates be produced in one stable interval, w be 8 or 16 u32
   512: lanes, P the per-item incremental projection cost, Vw the vector kernel cost,
   513: C the scalar predicate cost, F setup cost and D deferred/error/flush overhead.
   514: Preparation common to both alternatives cancels only when it really is identical:
   515: 
   516: ```text
   517: Tscalar_predicates = B*C
   518: Tbatch = F + B*P + ceil(B/w)*Vw + D
   519: necessary large-batch condition: C > P + Vw/w
   520: finite threshold: B > (F + D)/(C - P - Vw/w), with tail terms restored
   521: ```
   522: 
   523: When that denominator is nonpositive, no queue length rescues this kernel.
   524: Measure the fused scalar resolver/count/check path as well, because a separate
   525: queue can prevent early exit and keep more state live. The best scalar control
   526: may remove a redundant scan or fold the predicate into descriptor production.
   527: That is preferable to a slower SIMD implementation.
   528: 
   529: | Alternative | What it tests |
   530: |---|---|
   531: | Improved scalar | Inline the existing comparison after count discovery; no allocation, no deferred first error. Primary baseline. |
   532: | Bit-parallel | Pack scalar predicate outcomes into an ordered failure mask; useful mainly for shared publication, not count arithmetic. |
   533: | Scalar-batched | Same SoA queue with a scalar loop; exposes locality gains and measures queue overhead independently of SIMD. |
   534: | AVX2 | Eight unsigned count comparisons per group; normalize floor/equality masks and mask tails. |
   535: | AVX-512 | Sixteen count lanes and compact failure masks; wider only helps when a genuine ready population exists. |
   536: 
   537: The static parameter distribution supplies small-signature controls but not B.
   538: The default harness's 512 ordinary calls do not supply B either. Record eligible
   539: named calls **per actual checker invocation**, stable-interval occupancy, nesting,
   540: lookups, fallback reasons and the work discarded after the first failure. A2 is
   541: currently a **measurement-gated, likely packing-sensitive hypothesis**, not the
   542: first production SIMD patch.

   177: Two operands can resolve to the same value, and many lanes can target one counter. **Vector gather/add/scatter is not a valid count increment or decrement implementation** in the presence of repeated destinations. A conflict-detect/aggregate method must preserve multiplicity and zero-transition enqueue order, and must count grouping/sorting/conflict overhead. It is not required for the proposed seed kernel and is not a new primitive/dependency request.
   178: 
   179: Compare these forms:
   180: 
   181: | Form | Mechanism | Main losing region |
   182: |---|---|---|
   183: | Existing scalar | Read canonical rows; seed FIFO directly | Extra row footprint when many rows and counts are already hot |
   184: | Improved scalar | Same algorithm, no resident projection | Limited upside if counters/root walks dominate |
   185: | Scalar-batched | Small candidate/count tiles and stable scalar selection | Packing and extra stores exceed saved row traffic |
   186: | Bitset | Zero-result/eligible masks with ascending bit extraction | Mask construction/maintenance dominates; sparse irregular IDs |
   187: | AVX2 | 8-lane u32 zero comparisons, scalar loads or guarded gathers, ordered mask extraction | Gather latency, mostly full/empty masks, small K |
   188: | AVX-512 | 16-lane u32 zero comparisons and masks using existing SIMD vocabulary | Packing/gather cost, memory bound, unsupported interface/features |
   189: 
   190: The boolean seed predicate is suitable for a mask; the exact occurrence counts are not reducible to one bit. Do not substitute a boolean 'used' flag for reference counts. A dense-zero bitset is built only after all counts, and deletion-time updates are charged if it is reused. Different functions may batch independently only through the existing lane infrastructure with work-indexed output; this research adds no concurrency.
   191: 
   192: ### Cost model and work elimination
   193: 
   194: Let N be instructions, V values, E surviving operand occurrences, J incoming occurrences, R deleted rows, E_D their operands, K seed candidates and C root-helper work. Baseline includes `zero(4V) + row_scan(N) + count(E+J) + seed_scan(N) + queue(R+E_D) + C`, plus common preparation/compaction/publication. Existing visit counters omit terms as described above.
   195: 
   196: Projection cost adds at least 8K bytes written and 8K bytes read, capacity/zeroing effects, packing counts, mask extraction and fallback dispatch. Benefit is fewer canonical-row/metadata loads during seed scanning, not fewer use increments. Compare `T_pack + T_tile + T_selected_purity` against the original complete seed scan. Cold pages, TLB misses and write-allocate traffic can make 8K payload much more expensive than its nominal bytes. Peak scratch and arena capacity must be measured, not inferred from payload alone.
   197: 
   198: For graph diameter/chain length L, the FIFO drain remains proportional to removed occurrences rather than L full scans. Dense repeated zero-use sweeps would cost up to `L*(N+E)` and are a rejected default. SIMD across a tiny frontier does not justify that algorithmic regression.
   199: 
   200: Fusion with the admission scan is not equivalent: fold/address replacements and removals happen afterward, so those early counts would require repair or another scan. Fusion into the final selected rewriting pass is only a gated experiment after proving all relevant roots/removals are final, including forward references, incoming uses and disabled-pass combinations. A speculative early seed queue is forbidden. Eliminating optional setup for disabled/no-work populations is more valuable than maintaining a permanent use table across passes.

Ligra's published default threshold is not a Buster threshold. Its duplicate-update requirements reinforce the need for explicit notification/counter-conflict handling. No Ligra dependency, callback framework, GPU offload or shared-state atomic algorithm is introduced.

   225: 
   226: Vary one dimension at a time, then selected interacting corners; do not run an unbounded Cartesian product.
   227: 
   228: - N and B: empty, tiny (1-32), then logarithmic sizes through 2^16, plus the actual work/scratch boundary. V, P and J vary independently where well-formed IR permits.
   229: - Active fraction: 0, one candidate, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5 and 1. Report degree-weighted activity and absolute population, not fraction alone.
   230: - Incoming/use fan-out and fan-in: 0, 1, 2, 4, 16 and 64; duplicate references, self references, early versus late conflicts, hub roots and a heavy-tailed mixture.
   231: - Iteration/dependency depth: 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 16 and 64. Parameter output must still match exactly after four allowed sweeps; depth five is a critical boundary case, not permission for a fifth sweep. DCE chains test queue depth without introducing repeated sweeps.
   232: - CFG shapes: straight lines, diamonds, nested loops, switches, irreducible/multiple-entry components and unreachable SCCs; both storage orders. Preserve current validation contracts when generating fixtures.
   233: - Locality: contiguous versus scattered incoming nodes, shared operand slices, compact and sparse result IDs, alias-chain lengths, repeated preparations and provenance/budget skips.
   234: 
   235: For every applicable distribution compare current scalar, better scalar, scalar-batched, u64 bitset, AVX2 and AVX-512 forms with complete setup/maintenance/teardown. Unsupported ISA/interface forms remain explicitly unrun; adding compiler intrinsics is not part of this research. Use existing `<buster/lib/simd.h>` operations and compiler/feature guards. MSVC, AArch64 and self-host fallbacks are mandatory correctness paths. Inspect emitted host instructions on the authorized machine for loads, shuffles, useful lanes, spills and frequency effects; width is not a performance result.
   236: 
   237: ### Required recorded fields
   238: 
   239: Record per function `N,V,B,P,J,E,K`, selected/pass-skip bits, frontend/mode, actual parameter sweeps, block/parameter/incoming visits, removals, early-conflict positions, root traversal steps, alias notifications including stale/duplicate entries, dirty-frontier sizes, queue lengths, seed-scan rows, setup/zeroing bytes, allocated capacity, conversion counts and peak live scratch. Keep statistics in existing diagnostic infrastructure, with no hot-row growth. Aggregate distributions/quantiles and weighted time contributions rather than averages that hide tiny functions.
   240: 
   241: ## 6. Equivalence and adoption gates
   242: 
   243: **G0 — relevance:** obtain current native per-pass cost including uncounted seed/block/setup work. Reject a target whose real cost cannot repay setup. Historical shared-promotion zero populations are a warning, not a reason to disable a different pass.
   244: 
   245: **G1 — exact scalar oracle:** on identical pre-pass IR, compare replacements, live parameter lists/order/counts, instruction deletion set and ordered queue trace where applicable. Include alias chains, all-self/empty parameters, cycles without zero-use DCE seeds, duplicate operands, forward references and cap boundaries. Preserve existing `parameter_budget_hits`, changes and skip meaning; work-count differences should reflect the new actual work and must not be disguised as identical counters.
   246: 
   247: **G2 — canonical and diagnostic equivalence:** run existing structural tests, canonical ownership/semantic verification before and after transformations at their required boundaries, repeated-preparation checks and shared-slice/source/extra metadata remapping checks. Preserve accepted legacy shapes and diagnostics/refusal on unsupported pure-looking operations. Baseline and candidate outputs must be byte-identical for the same configuration; runtime agreement alone is insufficient for this implementation-only task.
   248: 
   249: **G3 — coverage:** all 16 canonical pass subsets x NONE/MIR_STACK/FAST/QUALITY; frontend SSA on/off; promotion controls; Debug/Release, unity/non-unity, sanitizer, explicit transform checking, one-lane and supported parallel settings. Exercise desktop native execution, supported mobile object/lifecycle coverage and Wasm64/eBPF/LLVM-bitcode consumers. Existing runtime or external-compiler oracles must be used where available; otherwise record the missing engine gate.
   250: 
   251: **G4 — self-host:** trusted Clang-built compiler performance measured separately; byte-identical self-built stage fixed point and required token/byte metrics checked through the repository's existing self-host workflow. Preserve compiler support for the SIMD fallback implementation itself.
   252: 
   253: **G5 — total-cost acceptance:** existing frozen corpus, all supported modes, all-enabled and leave-one-pass-out, A/A noise control and paired total latency/RSS evidence on qualified hardware. Require the existing no-confirmed-regression policy. Kernel wins with setup losses, extra parameter iterations, excess scratch or whole-compile regressions do not qualify. Generated program runtime/code quality is reported separately and is not credited as faster compilation.
   254: 
   255: **G6 — selection:** current scalar remains the initial default. A calibrated policy must include source size, candidate/degree-weighted activity, expected remaining sweeps, full projection cost, memory cap and CPU feature support. Prefer a small deterministic policy with measured safety margin and hysteresis, not a learned runtime optimizer or expensive sampling pass. Fall back before allocating/projection when prediction is uncertain. No numerical crossover has been measured here.
   256:

    17: ### An explicit meaning of “fastest correct C compiler”
    18: 
    19: A useful first championship contract is deliberately narrower than “all C on every machine”:
    20: 
    21: | Dimension | Proposed comparison contract |
    22: |---|---|
    23: | Language | GNU C11 mode, with an immutable eligibility manifest covering the C features/extensions actually admitted at this source pin. Include preprocessing, type/constraint checking, ABI behavior, and required diagnostics. Unsupported cases stay visible in a separate coverage ledger; they are not silently discarded after timing. This does not claim complete GNU C or ISO conformance. |
    24: | Primary output | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, fixed x86-64-v3 output feature contract and fixed ABI, relocatable ELF and hosted executable as separate rows. Host AVX2/AVX-512 selection must not change the generated target feature set. |
    25: | Primary policy | Buster FAST, debug information off/on as separate rows. NONE, MIR_STACK, and QUALITY are independent policy rows, not interchangeable performance numbers. Preserve all supported targets and modes through regression gates even when the initial competition is narrower. |
    26: | Inputs | Frozen source plus include closure, generated configuration headers, argument vector, environment-dependent include resolution, libraries, and output location policy. Include tiny files, medium libraries, macro-heavy and aggregate-heavy inputs, large CFGs, and the frozen self-host unity input. |
    27: | Internal correctness | For the three representation/query changes proposed here, exact diagnostics and accepted/rejected results, canonical identities/order, selected machine rows and side tables, and final artifact bytes under unchanged policy. Preserve the existing self-host executable and preprocessed-stream fixed points. |
    28: | Cross-compiler correctness | Independent execution/ABI/diagnostic oracles; different compilers need not emit identical bytes. Defined-behavior tests must agree. An internal verifier is necessary but is not an independent runtime oracle. |
    29: | Output quality | Internal candidates must preserve bytes, so generated-code quality is unchanged. For a cross-compiler speed claim, predeclare a quality-qualified row: every runtime workload within 5% of the pinned Buster FAST reference, with text size no larger than that reference, after accounting for measurement uncertainty. These are proposed comparison limits, not an existing repository policy. Also publish the full compile-time/runtime/size Pareto frontier rather than hiding nonqualifying compilers. |
    30: | Completion | Measure process start through successful artifact write/close, including preprocessing, metadata and linking where requested. State whether durable storage synchronization is included; do not call a merely written artifact crash-durable. Report failed inputs separately rather than crediting early failure as throughput. |
    31: | Latency versus capacity | Single-file process latency, warm persistent-process latency, and saturated multi-input artifacts/second are three different experiments. State cache state, job/lane counts, memory limits, and startup/prewarm treatment. |
    32: 
    33: A “fastest” claim requires this contract, immutable comparator versions/configurations, reproducible raw samples, uncertainty, and no failing correctness gate. This report establishes neither a current record nor a numerical forecast. A compiler that omits semantics, lowers output quality, times only an internal phase, or excludes linking has not won the same contest.

    35: ## 2. What is already implemented, and what the historical profile means
    36: 
    37: The [September 12 audit][HA] measured a frozen `5dab18af0208cfa7fa65673b6884d5c253fda85b` workload with Clang 18.1.3, glibc 2.39, and Valgrind 3.22.0 in a shared four-vCPU Emerald Rapids KVM guest without PMU access. The measured compiler used `-march=x86-64-v3` because that Valgrind could not decode the EVEX path. Its input had 30,729,994 translated bytes and 3,364,471 preprocessed tokens. Its total was 13,749,246,043 Callgrind Ir.
    38: 
    39: These are **historical counting-instrument results**, not current-main wall-time fractions, hardware retired instructions, or Zen 5 kernel timings:
    40: 
    41: | Historical region | Inclusive share | Accounting constraint |
    42: |---|---:|---|
    43: | `c_lower_to_ir_with_options` | 38.0% | Contains body lowering and global initialization; do not add its children again. |
    44: | `codegen_generate_canonical_module_with_trace` | 20.9% | Contains selection, placement, and encoding. |
    45: | `ir_prepare_canonical_module` | 14.4% | Contains validation, not an additional budget beside it. |
    46: | `c_analyze_semantics` | 11.6% | Separate top-level region in that report. |
    47: | `c_preprocess` | 10.2% | Includes its source/lexical work; a lexer percentage cannot be added independently. |
    48: | Unlisted remainder | Approximately 4.9% | Arithmetic remainder of rounded shares, not a newly measured phase. |
    49: 
    50: Within those parents, validation was 8.6% of total Ir, x86 selection 7.3%, `machine_predicate_placement_build` 6.9%, and x86 encoding 4.1%. **The predicate-placement number must not be interpreted as predicate-only work.** The current [implementation][RP] calls `machine_fast_placement_build_core`, `machine_quality_placement_build_core`, or `machine_stack_placement_build_core` inside that wrapper. It also already respects `predicate_absence_certified`. Optimizing a seven-register predicate choice cannot claim the wrapper's inclusive budget.
    51: 
    52: The same audit removed 69,627,498 bytes of fill per compile, chiefly by plus-one sentinel encodings in four per-token arrays and zeroed-arena allocation of constant-initializer images. Its total Ir fell 0.466%, while instructions outside the libc fill accounting increased. Native peak RSS improved in the recorded experiment, but noisy wall-time orderings disagreed. That is a useful warning: neither “fewer instructions” nor “fewer bytes” alone decides elapsed time. These landed changes are the baseline, not new recommendations.
    53: 
    54: Other already-existing infrastructure materially changes the research:
    55: 
    56: * [`c_lex_compact`, `CPpClassMasks`, and token shape sidecars][CS] already classify/compact byte or token populations. The lexer has an independent scalar differential path and item-aligned windows. Do not propose initial SIMD lexing or initial preprocessor class masks as missing work.
    57: * [`c_parse_token_census`, predefined-symbol word bits, matching-delimiter/position indices][CP] already avoid repeated spellings or wide token-row walks. [`ir_source_search_vector` and the dual source-map cursor][IR] already use short-span masked comparisons and locality-aware lookup.
    58: * [Direct SSA][FG] already has sparse `(block, owner)` state, single-entry-definition forwarding, whole-owner memory restoration, and stable retirement of empty parameter-bearing blocks. [PR #497][P497] is not a new candidate. Its integration/performance acceptance must not be replaced with another implementation of the same list.
    59: * [PR #375][P375] is merged. Its AArch64 direct-call facts are accumulated in an existing operand walk, without a replacement stream. A future #132 experiment must beat this fused scalar baseline, not its removed prewalk.
    60: * [`MachineInstruction` is a 24-byte row; `MachineOpcodeInfo` remains 96 bytes; the simple `MachineOpcodeRow` projection is 16 bytes][MG]. Type-class projections, compact opcode facts, immutable recipes, module call plans, and a bounded demand-only address cache already exist. Do not resurrect the unused matcher removed under #42/#269 or split the canonical row merely to claim SoA.
    61: 
    62: Current coordination: [#128][I128] is the throughput architecture umbrella; [#447][I447] owns direct-SSA throughput; [#132][I132] owns residual selector prewalk/query work; [#564][I564] is **attribution only**. Its current draft [PR #576][P576], read at head `46f96daf2725f9dccc06c16b2d3c60e484d045a4`, owns diagnostic-only validation census work. This report does not claim that work, change validation semantics, or authorize an optimization under #564. Focused searches and these discussions establish relevant overlap, not an atomic ownership lock on all future changes.

    64: ## 3. Algorithm coverage matrix
    65: 
    66: Notation: **W** = SIMD within one item; **A** = SIMD across independent items/queries/functions; **B** = bit-parallel formulation. **S** = semantic ordering, **G** = algorithmic dependency, **R** = representation-induced serialization, **I** = API-imposed serialization. A scalar implementation is not evidence that all four forms of serialization are inherent.
    67: 
    68: Evidence labels: **body** means an inspected implementation region; **map** means an inspected source orientation/header or current guide; **historical** means the cited old profile. Every proposed formulation below is unmeasured here. Source links identify exact files and searchable symbols, rather than stale historical line numbers.
