A: independent demanded queries. B: fact-valid and candidate masks. Scalar: fused reads and existing bounded memoization. | G: address chains; S: exact subobject/symbol identity and memory opacity. Whole-function eager address projection can add work the current cache deliberately avoids. |
   112: | **Residual operand prewalks** — [`machine_select_canonical_function_x86_64`, `machine_select_canonical_function_aarch64`][MX] | Map/discussion: #375 fused one AArch64 walk; #132 remains broader work. | W: long call/operand slices. A: many operand queries in a tile. B: role masks and monotone per-value reductions. Scalar: fuse all eligible consumers into the existing walk first. | R/I: repeated row/operand decoding, if any remains after fusion. **Candidate C** below; no assumed residual population or new permanent stream. |
   113: | Authoritative instruction selection — [`machine_a64_select_instruction`, `machine_x64_select_call`, `machine_x64_select_row`][MX] | Body/map: actual target switches own emitted MIR; complex ABI paths exist. | W: local bit packing/shape checks. A: independent functions or pure selection queries. B: opcode-class candidates. Scalar: compact tables, direct switch and special cases. | S/G: result IDs, synthesized rows, call staging and mutable state. Parallel count/emit would need an identical recipe/ID proof and is outside Candidate C. Do not install another matcher that reports rules without emitting rows. |
   114: | Machine verification/dominance — [`machine_verify_function`][MG] | Contract: storage first; operand roles/classes; unreachable source SCCs and mutable-register exceptions. | W: operand kind/bounds tests. A: verified independent functions/rows after safe preflight. B: sparse/dense use, def, reachability or dominance sets. Scalar: iterative graph algorithms with compact adjacency. | G: graph fixed points; S: dominance cannot follow storage order. Bitsets are representation choices, not permission to ignore disconnected components or edge-copy uses. |
   115: | Scheduling dependencies/memory — [`machine_schedule_frame_access`, `machine_schedule_memory_access`][SC] | Body/map: frame-range proof, conservative memory chains and barrier rules. | W: interval overlap checks and class masks. A: independent blocks or ready-candidate scoring. B: use/def/ready sets, sparse word blocks. Scalar: current certified range chains and early no-pressure gate. | S: calls, atomics, fences, physical staging, FLAGS pairs and volatile state. A stateful schedule can still have batchable scoring; retain deterministic tie rules. Whole dense dependency matrices add quadratic space. |
   116: | Pressure-aware schedule choice — [`MachineOpcodeRow.schedule_flags`, `machine_schedule_remap_line_marks`][SC] | Body/contract: deterministic greedy policy and stable line-mark remap. | W: pressure-delta vectors across classes/candidates. A: score ready units against one frozen live set, choose one winner. B: ready masks and popcount intersections. Scalar: sparse ready list and the same tie order. | G: winner updates the next state. SIMD scores do not allow simultaneous conflicting winners. Extra score arrays and reductions must beat a short scalar ready set. |
   117: | General allocation/placement — [`machine_fast_placement_build_core`, `machine_quality_placement_build_core`, `machine_stack_placement_build_core`][RP] | Body call sites/contract: independent allocator policies under predicate wrapper. | W: compare candidate registers/interval endpoints. A: independent intervals' immutable scores or separate functions. B: physical-register masks, live/use sets, spill eligibility. Scalar: bounded masks, touched lists, sparse liveness and current exact traffic ordering. | G/S: assignments, evictions, parallel copies and weighted tie policy. Do not vectorize a dependency chain by speculatively committing several register choices. Preserve QUALITY's exact u64 costs. |
   118: | Predicate allocation — [`machine_predicate_pick`, `machine_predicate_placement_build`][RP] | Body: seven allocatable k registers, absence certificate, conditional projection. | W: compare small age set only if measured useful. A: separate functions. B: held/dirty/reserved masks already fit a byte. Scalar: bit selection and seven-element search. | G: eviction state. Width alone offers little population; projection copying is a separate cost. Do not spend SIMD setup to optimize a tiny set or credit ordinary allocation to this kernel. |
   119: | Edge-copy lowering — [`MachineFunction` edge/parameter contract, `machine_predicate_placement_build`][RP] | Body/contract: positional incoming sources and separate predicate copies. | W: classify copies. A: independent edges with private scratch. B: pending-source/destination sets. Scalar: exact parallel-copy cycle resolver. | S: parallel assignment semantics and cycles. Sequentializing a cycle changes values. Stable compaction must use the same keep decisions for destination parameters and incoming sources. |
   120: | x86 encoding — [`machine_encode_x86_64`][HA] and immutable recipe contract [MG] | Historical/contract: exact recipes already exist; no run census here. | W: pack one instruction's fields. A: homogeneous independent recipe rows, then prefix-sum byte lengths. B: optional prefix/REX/SIB/displacement masks. Scalar: exact template lookup and contiguous stores. | G: relaxation/layout; S: relocations and final row order. Variable-length scatter/store overlap, packing and restoration can dominate; #59's homogeneous-run census remains prerequisite, not a speedup claim. |
   121: | Fixed-width/direct backends — [`codegen_generate_canonical_module_with_trace`, alternate emissions in `compiler_driver_execute_c_single`][DR] | Map/contract: native and direct non-native routes retained. | W: field insertion into fixed-width words. A: independent rows/functions after layout. B: fixup-kind masks. Scalar: direct checked word stores; Wasm variable-length integer encoding handled separately. | S: target ABI, endianness, feature refusal, stack model and relocation bounds. AArch64 fixed instruction width does not make literal pools/veneers or Wasm layout independent. |
   122: | Source/debug metadata — [`ir_source_region_position`, `machine_schedule_remap_line_marks`, `link_pe_resolved_codeview`][IR] | Body/map: indexed source recovery; stable bounded-run merge sort exists for reordered marks. | W: short source-position spans/varint pieces. A: independent functions' metadata streams and relocations. B: change/line-state masks and prefix lengths. Scalar: existing cursor/index, omit unchanged records, stable merge. | S: source order, equal-row marks, debug IDs and section offsets. Do not retry the historically negative cursor stepping experiment as a new idea. Metadata can dominate after code generation improves. |
   123: | Archive extraction and symbol resolution — [`compiler_driver_execute_invocation`, archive worklist ownership][DR]; [`link_objects`][LK] | Map: serial archive selection boundary; weak-symbol resolution and relocation rebasing. | W: symbol-name/fingerprint comparisons. A: independent index construction/queries against frozen tables. B: unresolved/selected membership. Scalar: indexed pass-ordered extraction, avoid rescanning all members. | S: archive order, weak/strong definitions and duplicate diagnostics. A global simultaneous fixed point must reproduce the original extraction policy, not just find some set of definitions. |
   124: | Final layout, relocations, imports, output — [`link_native_executable`, `link_elf_index_initialize`, `link_objects`][LK] | Map: format-specific writers; import aliases and weak-symbol rules already shared. | W: relocation field arithmetic and range checks. A: independent patches into disjoint validated ranges. B: relocation/section class masks; prefix-sum sizes/alignments where composable. Scalar: exact counts, sparse indices and contiguous writes. | G: layout/relaxation; S: symbol binding, aliases, constructors, startup and stable section order. Concurrent overlapping patches are not safe. OS write/close and optional durability are outside SIMD compute and must remain in end-to-end time. |
   125: 
   126: This map deliberately distinguishes an opportunity to process pure facts in parallel from permission to change a phase's semantics. For example, greedy scheduling is not globally parallel under an identical decision policy, but scoring its ready population is; macro execution is ordered, but copying/classifying an already-expanded immutable run is not inherently serial.
   127: 
   128: ## 4. CPU-resident execution model and cost vocabulary
   129: 
   130: Keep canonical IR and existing machine rows as the authoritative representations. A transient projection has one named producer, named consumers, a lifetime bounded by a function/query epoch, and an explicit invalidation event. It must not become a third graph IR, a shared mutable cache with implicit epochs, or a new general execution framework.
   131: 
   132: Use the existing persistent gang: SPMD across lanes, SIMD inside each lane, private function/TU scratch, stable work-indexed result slots, serial deterministic publication. Prewarm shared immutable tables before `lane_run`, publish readiness last, and use the same path at one lane and in single-threaded builds. Independent function tasks should normally expose more parallelism with less divergence than packing unrelated parser states into a vector. Do not nest unbounded per-function gangs beneath per-TU gangs; total runnable work and scratch memory need one owner.
   133: 
   134: A candidate tile size of 256 rows is an experimental starting point, not a hardware constant. Test 32/64/128/256/512 and include tiny populations that bypass tiling. A 16-byte logical SoA record at 256 rows occupies 4 KiB before other live arrays. AoSoA is useful when scalar consumers need several fields of the same item and vector consumers need one field across a small tile; a whole-program SoA conversion is not implied.
   135: 
   136: For a region with N useful items, use:
   137: 
--- lines 345-491 ---
   345:         Masks masks = classify_consumed_roles(batch);
   346:         // Read-only queries use already-validated IDs and immutable type facts.
   347:         BatchResult facts = evaluate_requested_facts(state, batch, masks);
   348:         // First experiment serializes updates that can name the same value.
   349:         for (u32 lane = 0; lane < lanes; lane += 1)
   350:         {
   351:             reduce_one_original_ordered_fact(state, batch, facts, lane);
   352:         }
   353:     }
   354: }
   355: ```
   356: 
   357: Again these are conceptual helpers, not a new dispatch framework. Real code uses direct functions and the existing `simd.h` vocabulary. Width selection is outside the inner loop in an implementation; the notation compares scalar, eight-dword and sixteen-dword forms.
   358: 
   359: One concrete reduction shape is direct-call use classification: each occurrence contributes “matching direct callee” and/or “other use” after the existing definition/call symbol-identity check. Two Boolean summary bits form an associative OR reduction; convert that summary back to the existing scalar state representation. “Other” remains absorbing. Preserve the actual incoming-edge policy. This example explains what can be batched, **not a proposal to recreate #375's removed scan**.
   360: 
   361: ### Conflicts and order
   362: 
   363: Different lanes frequently reference the same value. A gather/update/scatter sequence loses updates even when every address is valid. The initial variant keeps per-value updates scalar in original occurrence order. A later stable grouping can reduce duplicate value IDs, but must pay classification, grouping, scratch and output restoration. AVX-512 conflict detection identifies conflicts; it does not make the reduction atomic or decide the required winner.
   364: 
   365: Only proven commutative reductions may ignore occurrence order. First-use/last-use identity, diagnostics, synthesis of IDs, calls and target selection retain original ordinals. Partitioning by opcode or role does not authorize reordering the emitted program. Per-function scratch is private; no locks or global atomics are necessary for independent functions.
   366: 
   367: Address/provenance facts retain exact canonical identity and existing cache invalidation. Do not infer alias freedom from equal roots or offsets. If a consumer needs a fact produced by another consumer in the same traversal, either fuse that dependency inside the tile in the same order or keep the consumer scalar; a shared array is not proof of independence.
   368: 
   369: ### Break-even and experiments
   370: 
   371: Let k be the number of genuinely remaining consumers, I canonical rows visited, E operand occurrences, `B_walk` the measured effective bytes/cycles of a row/operand traversal, and `B_fact` the compact bytes each consumer needs. A rough traffic comparison is:
   372: 
   373: `removed repeated traversal traffic - projection writes - projected reads - extra gathers - grouping/restoration traffic`.
   374: 
   375: Do not replace it with `(k - 1) * sizeof(IrInstruction) * E`: rows and operands have different populations, cache hits matter, and some consumers are sparse. With a full 16-byte record, projection alone can write 16E and subsequent complete consumers read up to 16kE. A fused scalar traversal with zero projection can easily win. Cache-resident tiling reduces retention and often traffic, but does not erase packing instructions.
   376: 
   377: Time breaks even only if the removed traversals plus vector work savings exceed setup, plane packing, per-value updates and cleanup. At k=1, demand a demonstrated kernel gain large enough to repay packing; do not claim amortization across nonexistent consumers. If scattered value maps miss cache, SIMD arithmetic width may be irrelevant.
   378: 
   379: Compare current source, fully fused scalar, scalar tiled with only consumed planes, AVX2, and AVX-512. Measure per-consumer visits, short/long operand distributions, value-ID duplicate rate, gather locality, unsupported shapes, scratch high-water and exact selected rows. Include no-call functions, many arguments beyond 255, repeated callees, escaping/indirect uses in both orders, linked order different from dense storage, vectors, block parameters and both native targets. Byte-compare machine rows and every consumed side table; preserve checked/prevalidated entry agreement and fallback reason counts.
   380: 
   381: Review boundaries: C1 is a consumer census and another no-allocation fusion only if a real remaining traversal exists; C2 is one private tile shared by named read-only consumers; C3 adds the simplest profitable vector classifier. A whole-function stream, persistent selector IR, new matcher, new allocator policy, or address-analysis rewrite is outside this candidate.
   382: 
   383: ## 8. Cross-cutting scalar, bitset, AVX2, and AVX-512 comparison
   384: 
   385: | Form | Where it can win | Costs that must be included | Rejection condition |
   386: |---|---|---|---|
   387: | Current implementation | Tiny inputs, predictable scalar state, existing mature mask kernels | Existing repeated visits and allocations are measured, not assumed | It remains the default unless a candidate improves the full contract. |
   388: | Improved scalar/bitset | Eliminating queries, sparse queues, 64-way membership, stable rank, direct table lookup | Bitset clearing, index construction, population density, mutation invalidation | A dense bitmap or full scan costs more than touched IDs or a short list. |
   389: | Scalar-batched | Exposes independent loads, shares classification, amortizes setup and improves locality without ISA requirements | Tile stores/loads, extra loop nesting, order restoration, working-set growth | One fused scalar walk is cheaper, or tiles introduce latency without reuse. |
   390: | AVX2 | Eight u32 lanes, common compares/arithmetic, interleaved probes and dense remaps | Tail handling, movemask conversion, compaction permutation/control costs, gather misses | Packing and low occupancy consume all arithmetic savings. |
   391: | AVX-512 | Sixteen u32 lanes, mask-valued predicates, masked tails, dword compression and Boolean fusion | Exact feature subset, gathers, compress form, register pressure, stores and whole-kernel frequency/throughput | Wider code is slower on a required host, spills, or only improves a microbenchmark. |
   392: 
   393: [The Intel Intrinsics Guide][R4] distinguishes AVX-512F, BW, CD, VBMI2 and other subsets; “AVX-512” is not a sufficient feature guard. Dword compression and byte/word compression have different feature requirements. AVX2 has no direct equivalent of AVX-512 mask compression; compare scalar filling and permutation-based packing rather than silently assuming a native compress instruction. A masked instruction's semantics do not legalize unrelated earlier C accesses. Inspect actual generated code and the exact instruction forms selected.
   394: 
   395: [AMD's Zen 5 optimization-guide entry][R5] was consulted as the vendor documentation starting point. No instruction throughput table was extracted from it here, and no blanket “every 512-bit kernel is twice as fast” claim follows. Price the complete kernel on physical Zen 5 and check Zen 4 separately. In particular, gather locality, store throughput, dependency chains and pressure can defeat width gains. The repository's SIMD interface remains the implementation boundary; any genuinely missing primitive requires the existing builtin/IR-shape/validation/lowering/fallback/test chain, not direct vendor intrinsics scattered through compiler code.
   396: 
   397: Small cache-resident columnar batches are also a useful architectural analogy to [MonetDB/X100][R3]: avoid both per-tuple interpretation and uncontrolled whole-column materialization. The transferable idea is bounded batching. Database execution results are not evidence of a compiler speedup, and no database framework or dependency is proposed.
   398: 
   399: ## 9. Combined end-to-end model and bottleneck migration
   400: 
   401: Choose **disjoint** measured regions: A is the selected post-SSA tail, B the selected validation families after retained prerequisites, C the remaining selector-query work. Never use all lowering for A, all preparation for B, or the predicate-placement wrapper for C.
   402: 
   403: Let `f_A`, `f_B`, `f_C` be their fractions of one frozen baseline's elapsed time, `s_A`, `s_B`, `s_C` their local speedups, and h additional costs not already included in those local measurements. Then:
   404: 
   405: `T_new / T_old = 1 - f_A*(1 - 1/s_A) - f_B*(1 - 1/s_B) - f_C*(1 - 1/s_C) + h`.
   406: 
   407: Do not multiply three standalone whole-compiler speedups, and do not add h twice when per-region timings already include packing. Re-measure the combined build: shared cache capacity, scratch lifetime and instruction-cache interactions can make even disjoint algorithms interact.
   408: 
   409: For sensitivity only, **not a forecast**, suppose the eligible disjoint regions are 4%, 6%, and 5%, local speedups are 2, 1.5, and 1.5, and new global overhead is 0.5% of the original compile. The ratio is approximately 0.9483, or about 1.0545 times throughput at fixed work: roughly 5.45%, not 2 x 1.5 x 1.5 = 4.5 times. At infinite local speed and zero new cost those assumed regions cap the improvement at `1/0.85`, about 1.1765. All assumed shares and speedups in this paragraph require measurement.
   410: 
   411: The historical phase shares identify likely migration, not a current budget: after SSA/query/check improvements, preprocessing, semantic layout/typing, global initializer work, encoding, metadata, linking, startup or page faults can become dominant. Within A, root traversal can give way to pool writes; within B, regular comparisons to ownership or call/provenance checks; within C, classification to random value-table access or serial MIR publication. The next change should follow that new profile, not repeat the old ranking.
   412: 
   413: Single-file latency additionally contains the critical path through ordered preprocessing, shared declaration publication and the largest function. Bulk throughput instead approaches the minimum of useful compute capacity, memory bandwidth and output capacity, subject to lane imbalance and barriers. Summing function times is not a parallel elapsed-time model; use the slowest lane's assigned work plus shared phases and merges. Increasing lanes can increase total RSS enough to lose cache locality or induce paging. Pin one benchmark job per reserved host region; do not oversubscribe a dedicated performance run with other agents.
   414: 
   415: ## 10. Experiment and acceptance plan
   416: 
   417: Use the existing native `bench_throughput` harness and its current documented invocation; do not add a replacement benchmark framework or a transport workflow in this documentation PR. Commands must be checked against the submitted build driver before execution. Freeze the compiler source, trusted producer/toolchain, build flags, input tree, generated headers, output target/features, libraries and argument vector independently. Source added by a candidate must not silently enlarge its own self-compile workload.
   418: 
   419: Run each candidate independently before the combined configuration. The comparison ladder is current -> improved scalar/bitset -> scalar-batched -> AVX2 -> AVX-512, with algorithm and ISA ablations separately identifiable. Pin actual host identity, core/SMT/affinity, frequency policy, RAM, OS and compiler hashes. Use paired/interleaved runs, warmups, raw samples and confidence intervals supported by the native harness. Keep wall-time binaries free of diagnostic counters; run work/PMU/allocation probes separately and verify their output hashes against the ordinary binary.
   420: 
   421: | Required experiment/gate | Purpose | Status for this report |
   422: |---|---|---|
   423: | Current frozen exclusive phase/profile and work populations | Establish f values and whether there is meaningful removable work | Unrun; old Callgrind evidence only |
   424: | #564/#576 per-check attribution and independently countable census agreement | Select B's family without weakening validation | Owned elsewhere; not claimed complete here |
   425: | Exact intermediate snapshots and scalar/vector differential fixtures | Detect wrong IDs, aliases, error order, tails and conflicts | Proposed; unrun |
   426: | Release `test_all`, sanitized Debug, four-mode matrix, supported platforms/configurations | Preserve semantics and portability | Unrun; not needed merely to publish this docs-only change |
   427: | Ordinary self-host and byte-identical fixed point/preprocessed streams | Preserve whole-pipeline behavior | Unrun for candidates |
   428: | Frozen full-source and preprocessed-input controls | Separate ingestion/PP from later-stage gains without substituting the control for artifact latency | Unrun |
   429: | Physical Zen 5 paired artifact timing/PMU, plus Zen 4 nonregression | Determine actual width/setup/cache tradeoffs | No runner reservation or result established |
   430: | Small, medium, macro/aggregate, huge CFG and frozen self-host inputs | Detect shape-specific wins/regressions and bottleneck migration | Unrun |
   431: | One lane versus bounded multi-lane capacity, jobs-by-lanes cross product | Separate latency, throughput, oversubscription and memory growth | Unrun |
   432: | Negative-input precedence/safety/complexity tests | Protect the cold path and avoid an attractive valid-input-only result | Unrun |
   433: | Final combined A+B+C profile and cross-compiler quality-qualified comparison | Establish end-to-end benefit and any fastest-compiler claim | Unrun; no such claim made |
   434: 
   435: Accept only a positive, reproducible end-to-end result under the declared policy, with unchanged output/correctness, bounded scratch, and required-host nonregression. Publish small-input losses and uncertainty. A hardware retired-instruction reduction without elapsed-time improvement is evidence about work, not acceptance by itself. A correctness-only CI runner is not a substitute for an exclusively reserved performance host.
   436: 
   437: For each candidate, preserve a durable evidence bundle: baseline/candidate and producer hashes, frozen workload/include manifest, exact commands, host/affinity/ISA data, raw samples, counter availability and enabled/running ratios where relevant, output hashes, test outcomes, and a disposition. Negative results should be recorded rather than turned into a permanent “SIMD-ready” regression.
   438: 
   439: ## 11. Publication and disposition
   440: 
   441: **Disposition: publish the architecture and three gated experiments; do not implement or promise an optimization in this research session.** A is the strongest direct regular-population candidate from inspected code. B has a potentially substantial historical parent but must wait for its independently owned attribution. C is a residual-query hypothesis whose first and strongest competitor is already-landed scalar fusion. This is a conditional structural ranking, not a measured ranking of current-main opportunity.
   442: 
   443: Keep this audit as the single canonical detailed report. Cross-link substantive summaries into #128, #447, #132 and #564/#576 rather than create duplicate speculative issues. No new production owner, competing branch, code change, CI change, merge, issue closure or force-push is requested. A future implementation session must re-read current main and those discussions before selecting a slice.

An encoded branch-path fetch was rejected by the connector URL validator; the supported Git-ref read succeeded. This was a read-route limitation, not a write-permission failure. No credentials were requested, disclosed or searched outside configured authorization.

   479: Primary research/instruction documentation consulted; these support algorithmic mechanisms, not Buster speedup claims:
   480: 
   481: * **R1 — Guy E. Blelloch, _Prefix Sums and Their Applications_ (1990), CMU-CS-90-190.** Associative prefix operations provide stable offsets/ranks and expose parallel work in apparently serial accumulation. [Primary institutional record][R1].
   482: * **R2 — Siddhartha Chatterjee, Guy E. Blelloch, Marco Zagha, _Scan Primitives for Vector Computers_ (1990).** Segmentation allows independent runs to share vector execution without carrying state across segment boundaries. [Primary author/institutional page][R2].
   483: * **R3 — Peter Boncz, Marcin Zukowski, Niels Nes, _MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution_ (CIDR 2005).** Bounded vectorized batches are an architectural comparison, not a replacement framework. The conference paper and relevant page images were consulted. [Conference paper][R3].

   150: wall-clock probes say the fill side of the trade is worth nothing to begin
   151: with. No version of this trade pays.
   152: 
   153: ## Why the capacity hypothesis for the zero half is false here
   154: 
   155: The zero half rests on "the block is sized by `function->value_count`, the whole
   156: value id space, and the selector visits the values a function actually defines".
   157: On this workload those are the same set. `value_def_blocks` is present for
   158: **1.007.264 of 1.007.264 entries** — every value id in `[0, value_count)` is
   159: defined, as a block parameter or an instruction result — and the per-function
   160: high-water mark of touched ids sums to exactly `value_capacity`. There is no
   161: capacity to reclaim without changing what the IR hands the selector, which is
   162: outside this issue and belongs to #52.
   163: 
   164: Sparse id spaces do exist: `tests/basic_c_atomic_pair_contention.c` selects 49
   165: value ids of which 24 are defined. They are not what the unity self-compile
   166: looks like, and they occur in small functions where the absolute bytes are
   167: trivial.
   168: 
   169: ## Small inputs
   170: 
   171: Three, screened the same way. `functions_with_atomic` exercises the conditional
   172: map the unity workload never allocates.
   173: 
   174: | input | functions | value ids | `indirect` sentinel | `def_blocks` sentinel | atomic fns |
   175: |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
   176: | `basic_c_register_pressure.c` | 5 | 287 | — (0 reads) | 0 of 19 | 0 |
   177: | `basic_c_atomic.c` | 5 | 358 | 37 of 37 (100%) | 0 of 95 | 2 |
   178: | `basic_c_atomic_pair_contention.c` | 3 | 49 | 3 of 3 (100%) | 0 of 0 | 1 |
   179: 
   180: The two invariants that matter hold on every input measured:
   181: `value_indirect_slots` never holds a value, and `value_def_blocks` never
   182: returns its sentinel to a reader.
   183: 
   184: ## Measurements not available
   185: 
   186: - **No PMU.** `perf` is absent and the guest exposes no counters, so cycles,
   187:   cache misses and stalls are unmeasured. Ir and wall clock are the whole
   188:   currency here, as in the filing.
   189: - **No per-array read populations for the seven zero-region arrays.** They were
   190:   not instrumented individually. The zero half was screened on its stated
   191:   premise, capacity, which `value_def_blocks`' 100% density refutes directly,
   192:   and on the fill-cost probes, which cover both regions together.
   193: - **Ir on `-march=x86-64-v3`; timings on both `v3` and `native`.**
   194:   Architecture-neutral byte counts transfer, Ir totals do not.
   195: - **No self-host, `test_all`, `test_mode_matrix` or sanitized run.** This audit
   196:   changes no code, and the documentation row of the validation table in
   197:   `AGENTS.md` does not require them. The tree was rebuilt clean afterwards and
   198:   reproduces the frozen object above.
   199: - **Uninstrumented paired measurements exist only for the probes**, not for a
   200:   candidate implementation, because none was written. That is the finding.
   201: 
   202: ## One defect noticed while screening, not fixed here
   203: 
   204: [`machine_x86_64.c`](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/c96696e41329ca3b62b06e9b2d441d8ddf30ca49/src/buster/lib/compiler/codegen/machine_x86_64.c#L6703-L6704)
   205: stores `atomic_success_registers[instruction->result.value] = success_register`
   206: twice in a row, identically, on the `CMPXCHG16` path. The second store is dead.
   207: It is harmless and unrelated to this screen's subject, so it is left to a
   208: focused change rather than folded into an audit.
   209: 
   210: ## If this is revisited
   211: 
   212: Do not re-screen the fill. The result to overturn is not the byte count, which
   213: is confirmed, but the 0,069% and the invisible 8× probe. A revisit needs a host
   214: where the fill is not L1/L2-resident — a far larger `value_count` per function,
   215: or a PMU showing the fill's stores actually stalling — and it must price the
   216: read side, because that is where the proposed fix spends. On this tree and this
   217: workload the per-value block's initialization is not a throughput problem.

    74: ## Seed storage
    75: 
    76: Seed arrays now grow with what recording emits instead of reserving
    77: `debug values x (rows + 1)`. On this workload that bound reserved 357M seeds
    78: (20 GB) to emit 167k. The regression fixture records a function whose bound
    79: would be 41.7 GiB — past the 32 GiB translation-unit reservation that used to
    80: abort the compile — and it now completes inside a normal arena.
    81: 
    82: ## Change-point dedupe
    83: 
    84: The timelines were not as sparse as the design intends. A row's own sample
    85: supersedes the steady state the previous row published for that same row, and
    86: the push compared the incoming selection against the entry it was about to
    87: overwrite instead of the one that would end up preceding it. A row whose
    88: sample differs from its own steady state therefore kept an entry, and a
    89: function of such rows kept one per row, all carrying the same location. Every
    90: value naming that register then walked all of them: the whole-function replay
    91: again, once per value.
    92: 
    93: Measured on a function of 40,000 rows and 20,000 values naming one register
    94: (`codegen_test_machine_debug_seed_sizing`), replay iterations were
    95: 800,020,000 -- exactly `values x (rows + 1)` -- across a timeline of 40,000
    96: entries that describe one location. With the comparison made against the
    97: surviving neighbour the timeline is 1 entry and the emitted seeds are
    98: unchanged.
    99: 
   100: | Build | `codegen_tests` | whole Debug suite |
   101: |---|---|---|
   102: | before this change | 33.258 s | 2 m 27.5 s |
   103: | after | 0.282 s | 1 m 51.6 s |
   104: 
   105: The Debug (`BUSTER_OPTIMIZE=0`, non-unity) suite is what the mobile lanes run
   106: under a per-payload deadline, so this was a CI-visible regression, not only a
   107: pathological-shape one. On the stage-1 workload above the same fix is worth
   108: about 1.5% (2.981 s -> 2.936 s user CPU, best of three): real functions rarely
   109: name one register from many values across many rows.
   110: 
   111: `codegen_test_machine_debug_widest_timeline` reports the widest timeline a
   112: recording builds, so the fixture asserts the sparsity structurally rather than
   113: by wall clock. Reverting the dedupe fails that assertion.

    30: ## The problem, with the population it affects
    31: 
    32: `ir_prepare_canonical_module` (`src/buster/lib/compiler/ir/ir_fast.c`)
    33: validates at up to four boundaries: uncertified input, promotion output, FAST
    34: input, and FAST output. For a producer-certified module in a build with
    35: `BUSTER_IR_TRANSFORM_CHECKS` on, local promotion's mutation triggered a
    36: promotion-output scan, and then the FAST input guard -- `if (input_certified)`
    37: -- scanned the same, unmutated rows again before any transform ran. FAST's
    38: output scan followed. Three scans per module; the middle one asked exactly the
    39: predicate the first had just answered.
    40: 
    41: `BUSTER_IR_TRANSFORM_CHECKS` is `!BUSTER_OPTIMIZE || BUSTER_INCLUDE_TESTS ||
    42: BUSTER_SANITIZE || BUSTER_VERIFY_IR_TRANSFORMS`. The CMake default builds
    43: `ide` with `-DBUSTER_INCLUDE_TESTS=1`, so the affected population is the
    44: trusted Clang-built Release `ide` that `test_self_host`, `bench_throughput`
    45: and every local benchmark run, plus Debug, sanitizer and explicit
    46: verification builds. Self-hosted stages are built `-DBUSTER_INCLUDE_TESTS=0`
    47: and already ran one scan (the guard) after promotion; they are unchanged, as
    48: is every uncertified-caller path, where the guard never ran.
    49: 
    50: A `gdb` breakpoint census on the baseline `-g0` compile of the unity unit
    51: counted exactly three `ir_validate_canonical_module` calls, all from
    52: `ir_prepare_canonical_module`. The baseline `perf record` profile attributed
    53: 10.2 % of self samples to the validator, the largest single symbol at `-g0`.
    54: 
    55: ## The change
    56: 
    57: One local `bool validated` in `ir_prepare_canonical_module`: true while the
    58: strict validator has passed over the module in exactly its current state. A
    59: successful input or promotion-output scan sets it; promotion's mutation clears
    60: it; the FAST input guard is now `if (!validated)`. Nothing else moves: the
    61: uncertified input scan, the promotion-output scan under transform checks, the
    62: FAST output scan, `-fverify-codegen`, and CFG publication keep their trust
    63: preconditions. The guard still scans a certified module promotion left
    64: untouched (nothing has proven those rows) and in optimized non-test builds
    65: (no promotion-output scan ran). Producer certificates remain input
    66: certificates only.
    67: 
    68: Regressions (`ir_fast_test.c`, `ir_promotion_test.c`): a certified module
    69: promotion changes and a certified module promotion leaves alone are prepared
    70: with `IR_FAST_ALL`; under `BUSTER_BENCH_ALLOCATIONS` the boundary counters
    71: must read promotion-output `1`/FAST-input `0` versus `0`/`1`, with FAST-output
    72: `1` and a passing independent revalidation in both; the corrupted-module
    73: skip case must still spend exactly one FAST-input scan; and a failed
    74: promotion-output scan must leave `fast.functions == 0` and `!fast_complete`.

   135: ## Ranked leads
   136: 
   137: Ranked by the cycles they can return per line of change, with the evidence
   138: each rests on. None is taken here; each is a byte-identical rewrite of work,
   139: not of output, and each states its validation. Every lead is filed as an
   140: issue (the number in its heading), so the next session can pick it up cold;
   141: lead 4 joins the existing #447.
   142: 
   143: ### 1. The FAST stack-slot liveness fixed point: 4,8% of all cycles in twelve lines (#789)
   144: 
   145: `machine_fast_close_live_ranges` (`register_allocator_fast.c:1662`) widens
   146: slot ranges with a dense-bitset backward dataflow: `live_in = reads | (live_out
   147: & ~writes)` per block, then a merge into every predecessor's `live_out`, swept
   148: over *all* blocks in reverse index order until a whole sweep changes nothing.
   149: Lines 1682–1694 and the range materialization at 1709–1723 are 4,8% of the
   150: compile's cycles (1,24% + 1,11% + 0,76% + 0,47% + 0,35% + 0,35% + 0,24% +
   151: 0,15% + 0,11% by leaf IP); the enclosing
   152: `machine_fast_placement_build_prepassed` is 8,9% of L1d misses and 5,9% of
   153: branch misses, most of both on these lines. The
   154: plane is `block_count × ceil(stack_slot_count / 64)` words and every sweep
   155: touches all of it; the unity unit's largest frames (`max_stack_frame_bytes`
   156: 660.648, 4,85 MB of frames over 4.929 functions) are the functions where both
   157: factors are in the thousands, and a sweep count of loop depth plus two
   158: multiplies it. The fixed point is unique, so the result — and every byte after
   159: it — is independent of the iteration order.
   160: 
   161: Two changes keep the result and cut the work: (a) a worklist of blocks whose
   162: `live_out` changed, seeded with every block once, so a converged region is
   163: never re-swept; (b) computing `live_in` only for the blocks pulled from the
   164: worklist and merging only into the predecessors whose word actually changed
   165: (the compare at 1694 already exists; today its result only sets a global
   166: flag). Validation: `test_self_host` fixed point, `test_mode_matrix` for the
   167: allocator legs, and the allocator's own regressions; the slot ranges handed to
   168: `machine_fast_color_slots` must be identical, which the fixed point guarantees.
   169: Expected return: most of the 4,8%; the survey's `x cycles` of 1,0 says this
   170: loop is compute, not memory, so the saving is the iterations themselves.
   171: 
   172: ### 2. `debug_variable_add_location` rescans a function's seeds once per variable: 4,4% (#790)
   173: 
   174: `debug.c:295`. The seed index groups `DebugLocationSeed`s by *function
   175: symbol*; each variable then walks its function's whole bucket twice (count,
   176: then copy) testing `seed->local == local` at `debug.c:312`/`328`. With L named
   177: locals and S location seeds in one function that is 2·L·S seed reads, and the
   178: unity unit's large functions carry both in the hundreds to thousands
   179: (`2026-09-15T152933Z` measured 167 K seeds emitted over this workload). It is
   180: 4,1% of cycles plus 0,6% in `debug_symbol_equal`, which Clang left out of
   181: line, 4,2% of L1d misses, and it holds the fifth and sixth lines of the flat
   182: profile by IP (`debug.c:328` 1,10%, `debug.c:312` 0,90%).
   183: 
   184: The lead is a second `order` array keyed on `(function_symbol, local)` —
   185: same bucket construction as `debug_location_index_build`, hash mixed over both
   186: words — used for the exact queries `debug_add_canonical_locals` issues, while
   187: the existing symbol-keyed index keeps serving the `IR_LOCAL_ID_INVALID`
   188: wildcard that `debug_add_canonical_globals` issues. A stable counting sort
   189: keeps the within-key seed order that the emitted ranges depend on, so the
   190: DWARF is byte-identical. Validation: `-g -c` objects of the unity unit before
   191: and after (`cmp`), `test_self_host`, the debug and DWARF regressions. Expected
   192: return: nearly all of the 4,4%, since a variable's own seeds are a few rows.
   193: 
   194: ### 3. The pipeline is module-wide between lowering and selection, and pays for it in DRAM (#791, #792)
   195: 
   196: `ir_prepare_canonical_module` validates every function, then promotes every
   197: function, then runs FAST over every function, then publishes every function's
   198: CFG; only then does codegen loop over functions. The average function is 274
   199: rows of 64 bytes — 17,5 KB, an L2 working set — but every one of those passes
   200: streams the whole module's 86 MB of rows from DRAM because the previous pass
   201: evicted it. The survey's ranking by DRAM fills is that pipeline read
   202: backwards:
   203: 
   204: | pass | share of DRAM fills | share of cycles | x cycles |
   205: |---|---:|---:|---:|
   206: | `ir_validate_canonical_module` | 15,9% | 5,7% | 2,8 |
   207: | `ir_fast_function` | 10,9% | 2,3% | 4,8 |
   208: | `machine_select_canonical_function_x86_64` | 9,9% | 2,8% | 3,5 |
   209: | `ir_cfg_publish_instruction_rows` | 6,3% | 2,1% | 3,1 |
   210: | `ir_promote_function` | 4,5% | 1,3% | 3,5 |
   211: | `ir_function_publish_cfg` | 4,2% | 1,1% | 4,0 |
   212: 
   213: Together 52% of the compile's 13 M DRAM fills, against an `x cycles` of 1,0
   214: for the per-function FAST allocator that runs on rows the selector just
   215: wrote. Within those passes, four scans exist only to compute a fact the
   216: producer already knows, and are the cheapest part of this lead to take:
   217: 
   218: - `ir_fast_function` (`ir_fast.c:408–413`) reads every row of the function to
   219:   sum `operand_count` and to look for `LABEL_ADDRESS`/`INDIRECT_BRANCH` before
   220:   deciding whether the function fits the FAST budgets. That scan alone is
   221:   6,1% of DRAM fills (lines 411–412). `IrFunction` already carries
   222:   `opcode_summary` for exactly this question, and `ir_function_add_instruction`
   223:   already holds `instruction.operand_count` at append time (the diagnostic
   224:   census counts it as `OPERAND_SLOTS_APPENDED`): adding the two opcodes to
   225:   `IR_OPCODE_SUMMARY_TRACKED` and an exact `operand_total` counter (decremented
   226:   by the single retraction at `c_gen.c:28667`, rebuilt by `ir_rewrite_compact`,
   227:   unknown for hand-built functions, which keep the scan) removes the pass
   228:   without changing a budget decision.
   229: - `machine_select_canonical_function_x86_64` (`machine_x86_64.c:7346`) scans
   230:   every row for `IR_OPCODE_LOCAL` definitions to size the target-local
   231:   promotion; 5,9% of DRAM fills (lines 7352–7353). The 2026-08-22 survey moved
   232:   it from a per-value form to this row form because the per-value fetch was
   233:   random; the per-*local* form is neither: `IR_LOCAL_PROMOTION candidates=27775`
   234:   says the unit has 27,8 K candidate locals against 1,35 M rows, and
   235:   `function->local_places` indexes them.
   236: - `ir_promote_function` (`ir_promote.c:711`) scans every row for `LOCAL` and
   237:   barrier opcodes whenever the summary admits a LOCAL row, which under direct
   238:   frontend SSA is most functions (5,6 LOCAL rows per function on average); the
   239:   same per-local form applies to the count, and the barrier opcodes are
   240:   candidates for the summary.
   241: - `ir_validate_canonical_module` proves instruction ownership by walking each
   242:   block's `next` chain (`ir_function_instruction_owners`, `ir.c:4416`, 3,7% of
   243:   DRAM fills and 2,6% of branch misses on its own), and
   244:   `ir_cfg_publish_instruction_rows` (`ir_cfg.c:259`, 1,8%) walks the same
   245:   chains to permute the rows into block order. Between the two walks FAST
   246:   rewrites the function, so they are not the same state and `2026-09-13T130555Z`
   247:   was right not to fuse them; but a function that FAST left unchanged (`changes
   248:   == 0`) is the same state, and whether the validator's walk can leave the
   249:   publication its ownership result for such a function is the least certain
   250:   item in this list.
   251: 
   252: The larger form of the lead — running validate, promote, FAST, publish, select,
   253: allocate and encode function by function so each function's rows stay in L2
   254: across all of them — is the structural answer, and it points the same way as
   255: the independent function tasks of the `2026-09-13T132324Z` architecture note.
   256: It is not priced here beyond the fills table: the module-level steps in
   257: between (`ir_prepare_program_abi`, the promotion statistics, the f80 cache)
   258: would need per-function forms, and the deterministic-merge rules of
   259: `parallelism.md` apply. The four scans above are the part that can land alone.
   260: 
   261: ### 4. Direct-SSA slot table growth: 4,4% of branch misses and a memset per doubling (#447)
   262: 
   263: `c_ir_ssa_grow_slots` (`c_gen.c:4972`) doubles the per-function open-addressing
   264: table from 64 entries, zeroing the new table and re-probing every old entry.
   265: The `if (entry.block_plus_one)` at 4985 over a half-full table is the single
   266: most mispredicted line of the compile (2,31 M of 52 M misses, 4,4%); together
   267: with the probe loops at 5012–5013 (2,1%) and the finish-time slot lookups the
   268: table is 7,7% of all branch misses; `c_ir_ssa_grow_slots` as a function is
   269: 4,9% of the LBR mispredictions (2,9% under the `branch-misses:u`
   270: cross-check) and 0,95% of cycles, and its `memset` at 4978 is 1,6% of the
   271: DRAM-fill samples. At finish time the builder knows
   272: `local_count`, the block count and `event_count`, and the key population is
   273: bounded by the events: sizing the table once from that bound removes every
   274: rehash; keeping the high-water table across functions in the scratch arena
   275: and clearing only its used prefix removes the memsets. Output does not depend
   276: on table capacity. Validation: `test_self_host`, the direct-SSA regressions.
   277: 
   278: ### 5. The debug-location recorder residue: about 6% (#793)
   279: 
   280: `codegen_machine_debug_index_scan` 2,0%, `codegen_machine_debug_timeline_for`
   281: 1,4%, `machine_debug_values_build` 1,2% (and 5,3% of L1d misses through
   282: `machine_debug_block_value`), `codegen_machine_debug_index_build` 1,0%,
   283: `codegen_record_machine_locations` 0,3%. This is what `2026-09-15T152933Z`
   284: left after taking the recorder from 9,7 s to 3,1 s on a container and named as
   285: the per-function index (paid once per function whatever the value count) and
   286: the replays. Zen 5 confirms the split. The index scan and the timelines are
   287: instruction-bound (`x cycles` 0,4 on L1d misses) and run on the machine rows
   288: the allocator just wrote; `machine_debug_values_build` is the exception, at
   289: 4,3 L1d-miss shares per cycle share through `machine_debug_block_value`
   290: (`machine.c:2933–2939`), which is the one line of this group worth a data
   291: layout look before an algorithmic one.
   292: 
   293: ### 6. The section bytes are copied four times: 2 M DRAM fills, about 1% (#794)
   294: 
   295: The DWARF-unwound survey names the `memcpy` call sites exactly:
   296: `object.c:10111` copies `module->code` into the object's text section,
   297: `driver.c:4430` copies every section of the unit's object into the invocation
   298: arena, `link.c:1590` copies every input section into the merged object, and
   299: `link.c:4544` copies every merged section into the ELF image. Each moves the
   300: ~40 MB of output; the four together are 8,5% of the survey's DRAM-fill
   301: samples (2,60% + 2,44% + 2,26% + 1,17%) and most of libc's 2,4% of cycles.
   302: `2026-08-22T091548Z` took the linker's image copy once already; the driver
   303: copy is the odd one — for a single input it duplicates an object the unit
   304: arena still holds — and merging a single object into the link costs a full
   305: copy of it for nothing. The target is the `-g -c` object and the executable,
   306: both byte-identical.
   307: 
   308: ### 7. What is not a lead
   309: 
   310: - **Preprocessing and lexing.** 1,84 G instructions, 0,136 s, IPC 3,4;
   311:   `c_lex_dispatch` 1,3%, `c_preprocess` 1,4%, `c_symbol_intern` 1,0%. The
   312:   kernels of `2026-08-22T140940Z` and `2026-08-22T203845Z` hold on Zen 5.
   313: - **Canonical validation as such.** `2026-09-13T130555Z` measured 2,9% of Ir
   314:   and found the checks proportionate; this audit finds 5,7% of *cycles*
   315:   because the walk runs on cold rows, which is lead 3's mechanism and not a
   316:   reason to check less.
   317: - **The linker's own work**, under 0,5% of instructions.
   318: - **Register pressure and generated code quality.** Out of scope by
   319:   `AGENTS.md`; stage 2's 107,7 G instructions are the price of an
   320:   unoptimizing self-compile and are recorded as a reference, not a target.
   321: 
   322: ## The TCC bootstrap was broken
   323: 
   324: The first workflow run failed in `./build.sh generate`: TCC 0.9.28rc reports
   325: `tools/native_retirement_census.c:1672: error: assignment of read-only
   326: location` for `settings.rows = nrc_open(...)`, and `-Werror` makes the driver
   327: unbuildable. Bisected by inserting `settings.rows = 0;` probes: the variable
   328: becomes read-only in TCC's view after the `string_format(...)` call that
   329: passes the three `String8 const` archive hashes (`nrc_archived_input_sha256`
   330: and siblings, `native_retirement_census.c:42–44`) by value through `...`;
   331: copying them into non-const locals first compiles cleanly, and Clang 22 is
   332: unaffected either way. That call arrived with `e099c9e2` on 2026-09-12. No CI
   333: lane caught it because the GitHub-hosted workflows build the driver with
   334: Clang under the documented bootstrap exception; the canonical path is only
   335: exercised by a developer machine with TCC on `PATH` — this Arch build of TCC
   336: reproduces it locally too. The fix is this branch's second commit (the first
   337: adds the workflow), and the second run of the workflow bootstrapped with TCC
   338: (`tcc version 0.9.28rc 2026-01-17`). #795 asks for a lane that guards the
   339: bootstrap; #786 records the unrelated native-retirement closure failure that
   340: every pull request showed at the time (the closure pinned the pre-#774
   341: `ir.h`).
   342: 
   343: ## Limits
   344: 
   345: - Sampling density: `perf record` at 4.999 Hz over a 1,15 s run is 5,9 K
   346:   samples, so a 1% share is 59 samples; where a number is quoted to a tenth
   347:   it comes from the survey's 59,7 K period-sampled cycles or from `perf stat`.
   348: - No A/B: nothing here compares two compilers. The reference numbers are one
   349:   compiler on one host, repeated five (timing) or three (counters) times with
   350:   spreads of 0,4% on wall and 0,00% on instructions.
   351: - The 9700X's own noise floor for paired A/B is still owned by #426; the runs
   352:   here were serialized by the runner rather than admitted through the
   353:   dedicated-host lease of `tools/throughput/DEDICATED.md`.
   354: - `test_all` was not run on the runner; the branch's only source change is to
   355:   the build driver and the GitHub matrix builds that driver with Clang.

    17: `cfd7d02d53f8975749c1a4da41eb6b8f75473501` matched the local Release binary.
    18: The capture reported 123 calls to `c_parse_generic_constant_tokens`, 3100.821 ms
    19: inclusive, with 98.643% of its source time on the full-token-stream `memcpy`.
    20: The largest unresolved leaf, `libc.so.6+0x1B0883`, was one instruction in
    21: `__memcpy_evex_unaligned_erms`; missing libc debug information split adjacent
    22: instructions into separate `Unknown` functions.
    23: 
    24: The same-revision source metrics reported 3,465,808 preprocessed tokens. At 12
    25: bytes per `CToken`, each ordinary enumerator copied 41,589,696 bytes. The 123
    26: calls therefore copied 5,115,532,608 bytes (4.76 GiB) before evaluating their
    27: small expression ranges.
    28: 
    29: The implementation now scans only the requested range for a syntactic
    30: `_Generic`. A range without one returns the original token pointer and count;
    31: the existing materialization and explicit range-stack path remains responsible
    32: for selected and nested generic associations. The private regression observes
    33: pointer identity directly, so the performance contract is not a wall-time
    34: assertion or a production counter.
    35: 
    36: ## Trusted self-host A/B
    37: 
    38: Both runs used `./build.sh test_self_host --config Release` on the same machine
    39: and existing Release build directory. The baseline ran before the compiler
    40: edit; the candidate ran after `test_all` rebuilt the Clang Release producer.
    41: `STEP_INSTRUCTIONS` is the primary comparison. The candidate source is slightly
    42: larger (3,466,025 versus 3,465,808 preprocessed tokens), so the removed work is
    43: not explained by a smaller workload.

    48: | stage 1 wall time | 4.856623 s | 2.069305 s | -2.787318 s (-57.39%) |
    49: | stage 1 instructions/token | 5,811.743 | 4,727.979 | -18.65% |

    53: The near-identical absolute instruction reduction in the trusted-host and
    54: self-built-host compiles is consistent with deleting the same 4.76 GiB copy

    56: wall-time gate is inferred from one pair.

===== docs/self-host-audit.md =====
--- lines 1-59 ---
     1: # Self-host fixed-point audit
     2: 
     3: The native build driver owns this gate. On a configured Linux x86-64 tree:
     4: 
     5: ```sh
     6: ./build.sh self_host_audit_self_test
     7: ./build.sh test_self_host_audit --config Release
     8: ```
     9: 
    10: Run `./build.sh generate` once before the second command on a fresh checkout.
    11: Do not regenerate the tree or change compiler sources while an audit is running.
    12: The `.github/workflows/self-host-audit.yml` job uses the documented hosted
    13: Clang bootstrap exception. The existing multi-platform/configuration matrix and
    14: ordinary `test_self_host` gate remain in place.
    15: 
    16: ## What a pass means
    17: 
    18: Let C0 be the host-built compiler. Independently execute C0 twice to produce
    19: C1a/C1b; C1a twice to produce C2a/C2b; and C2a twice to produce C3a/C3b.
    20: Every child must compile successfully, produce complete evidence and pass its
    21: behavioral probes before it can be used as a producer. Compare both repeats in
    22: each generation, then C1a/C2a and C2a/C3a. This checks repeatability separately
    23: from a three-generation fixed point; equality of only C1/C2 does not establish
    24: repeat-run determinism.
    25: 
    26: Compare the following in pipeline order, stopping at the first mismatch:
    27: 
    28: 1. Actual preprocessed token kinds and spellings, not just token counts.
    29: 2. Semantic canonical IR records and selected MIR records; selected MIR also
    30:    runs the general verifier, including for selector-certified functions. A
    31:    rejected function is never sent to allocation or dereferenced for tracing.
    32: 3. Compile stdout, stderr and exit status, then the complete generated binary.
    33: 4. Source metrics within every repeated generation and across C2/C3.
    34: 
    35: Physical lexing metrics are retained and validated for every compile, but are
    36: not required to be equal between C1 and C2: C0 reads host resource headers,
    37: whereas C1 reads Buster's built-in resources. Token evidence must nevertheless
    38: match byte for byte across that boundary. The old comparator's token/byte
    39: counts are now explicitly counts, never proof of identical input. Missing,
    40: truncated, malformed, duplicate or unsupported-version required metrics fail
    41: both the ordinary comparator and this audit.
    42: 
    43: C0 and every generated compiler also compile and execute the same behavioral
    44: fixture in `none`, `mir-stack`, `fast` and `quality` modes. It covers pointer
    45: joins, integer width/sign handling, floating/integer aggregate arguments and
    46: returns, and register/stack argument boundaries. Variadic checks include named
    47: integer/floating parameters, default integer/float promotions, ordered integer
    48: and floating arguments exhausting both register files, and independent
    49: `va_copy` cursors created before consumption and at an integer-register
    50: boundary. Each copy remains usable after the original list is consumed and
    51: ended. The fixture uses variadic builtins directly: it does not introduce host
    52: resource headers into the exact per-probe token and source-metric comparisons.
    53: Compare those mode-specific phase traces, binaries, outputs and statuses
    54: against C0. An invalid-source fixture must be rejected without crashing,
    55: timing out or producing an executable, with identical diagnostics and status
    56: across generations. Captured sanitizer findings are failures even when the
    57: child exits zero.
    58: 
    59: This is a finite, same-host, same-source, same-configuration empirical invariant,

    84: ## Consumer trace and regression ownership
    85: 
    86: `target_parse_triple` preserves the UEFI OS discriminator. `target_data_layout`
    87: and the `target_uses_llp64_data_model`, `target_uses_16_bit_wchar`,
    88: `target_uses_unsigned_wchar` policies provide the frontend's C layouts and
    89: predefines. No layout policy or shared `target.c` row changes in this repair.
    90: The existing target-parser tests include both UEFI architectures; the new
    91: registered boundary test also checks parsed architecture/OS and LLP64/unwind
    92: policy alongside ordinary compiled-C results.
    93: 
    94: The canonical IR ABI selection in `compiler/ir/ir.c` keeps AAPCS64 distinct from
    95: Darwin and Windows AArch64 for parameter/result classification. Frontend
    96: variadic operations retain builtin-list identity and lower through VA_START,
    97: VA_ARG, VA_COPY and VA_END rather than treating the type as a pointer macro.
    98: The native consumers continue to use the existing 32-byte AAPCS list; no
    99: 32-to-8-byte storage change or backend-dispatch change is made. The compiled
   100: and runtime regressions below exercise the actual producer/consumer boundary.
   101: 
   102: `compiler_driver_llvm_target_triple`, `compiler_driver_llvm_data_layout` and
   103: `compiler_driver_execute_invocation` own the repaired export boundary. COFF/PE
   104: writing and `target_uses_pe_unwind` remain separate format policies. LLVM's
   105: other deliberate unsupported-IR diagnostics are unchanged.
   106: 
   107: `llvm_bitcode_test_uefi_boundary` is registered in the existing bitcode test
   108: module, which is already included in `test_all`. It checks Linux, Android,
   109: macOS, iOS, Windows and UEFI AArch64, plus x86-64 UEFI. Ordinary C controls keep
   110: the LP64/LLP64, binary128/binary64, short-wchar and pointer/record-list distinctions.
   111: Both UEFI architectures compile under NONE, MIR_STACK, FAST and QUALITY with
   112: both frontend SSA settings. Negative bitcode tests require no artifact, no new
   113: output, exact diagnostics and preservation of an existing output sentinel for
   114: parsed, direct-API and multiple-input invocations.
   115: 
   116: `tests/uefi_abi_contract.h` is shared by the existing structural C fixture and
   117: `tests/uefi_boot.c`. It checks size, alignment and record offsets, consumes all
   118: integer argument registers and five stack arguments, copies a partially
   119: consumed list, advances both cursors independently, and checks volatile guards
   120: immediately before and after each public list object. The runtime also checks
   121: unsigned short `wchar_t` behavior.
   122: 
   123: The AArch64 runtime oracle is not just a Buster-to-Buster call. A hand-written
   124: AAPCS64 leaf producer writes x0-x7 and the five reserved outgoing stack slots,
   125: then tail-calls the C variadic consumer. A separate leaf receiver inspects the
   126: register/stack interface produced by C, with a deliberately incorrect last
   127: argument as a negative control. Both leaves preserve SP/LR and all callee-saved
   128: registers, so neither adds a frame requiring its own unwind description.
   129: These are integer ABI checks, not a floating-point firmware service test.

===== docs/uefi-target.md =====
--- lines 35-125 ---
    35: The target selects the required calling convention automatically. A different symbol can be selected with `-e`, `--entry`, or `--entry=<symbol>`:
    36: 
    37: ```sh
    38: build/Debug/ide cc --target=x86_64-unknown-uefi --entry=FirmwareEntry -g0 firmware.c -o BOOTX64.EFI
    39: ```
    40: 
    41: ## Building images
    42: 
    43: ```sh
    44: build/Debug/ide cc --target=x86_64-unknown-uefi -g0 firmware.c -o BOOTX64.EFI
    45: ```
    46: 
    47: ```sh
    48: build/Debug/ide cc --target=aarch64-unknown-uefi -g0 firmware.c -o BOOTAA64.EFI
    49: ```
    50: 
    51: Without `-o`, the executable name is `a.efi`. Debug information is enabled by default; `-g` writes CodeView information into the image and a sibling PDB, while `-g0` omits source-debug data. Firmware unwind metadata is emitted independently of `-g`.
    52: 
    53: For removable media, place the resulting executable at the architecture-specific path shown above on the EFI System Partition. The compiler emits an EFI application image (`Subsystem = 10`), not a boot-service driver or runtime driver.
    54: 
    55: ## Headers and libraries
    56: 
    57: UEFI compilation is deliberately freestanding. The driver does not inject host C system-header paths, because host libc headers describe the wrong runtime and ABI. Supply firmware headers explicitly with `-I` or `-isystem`, for example an EDK II include tree.
    58: 
    59: Multiple C translation units and static archives are supported. `-l` must resolve to a static archive for a UEFI target. Dynamic libraries, import tables, host frameworks, raw `-Wl,` options, thread-local storage, and DWARF unwind sections are rejected rather than silently producing an invalid firmware image.
    60: 
    61: ## Image contract
    62: 
    63: The native linker writes a PE32+ image with:
    64: 
    65: - x86-64 (`0x8664`) or AArch64 (`0xaa64`) machine type;
    66: - EFI application subsystem;
    67: - no import directory or CRT startup stub;
    68: - `UefiMain` or the requested entry symbol as `AddressOfEntryPoint`;
    69: - `.reloc` blocks with `IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64` entries for absolute addresses;
    70: - `.pdata` and `.xdata` exception/unwind information;
    71: - deterministic section layout and optional CodeView/PDB debug data.
    72: 
    73: Current deliberate exclusions are UEFI drivers with subsystem 11 or 12, TLS, dynamic imports, and arbitrary external-linker flag passthrough.
    74: 
    75: ## Reference firmware execution gate
    76: 
    77: `test_uefi` in the native build driver compiles and boots this repository's
    78: `tests/uefi_boot.c` with both targets and all four allocators (`none`,
    79: `mir-stack`, `fast`, `quality`). The existing structural tests remain in
    80: `test_all`; a structural pass does not certify firmware execution.
    81: 
    82: From the repository root, after building `ide`:
    83: 
    84: ```sh
    85: ./build.sh build --config Release -t ide
    86: ./build.sh test_uefi --self-test build/uefi-self-test
    87: ./build.sh test_uefi build/Release/ide build/uefi
    88: ```
    89: 
    90: Both output directories must be new. The harness refuses existing output,
    91: including partial runs, so stale markers and images cannot pass a later run.
    92: The firmware root defaults to `/usr/share`; set `BUSTER_UEFI_FIRMWARE_ROOT`
    93: when packages have been extracted elsewhere. QEMU and `sha256sum` must be on
    94: `PATH`. Missing prerequisites report `status=unavailable runtime_validated=0`
    95: and fail the command. A version/hash mismatch also fails before booting;
    96: there is no structural-only success or optional skip for this gate.
    97: 
    98: The reference lane uses Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 packages from the immutable
    99: [2026-08-28 Ubuntu snapshot](https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/20260828T000000Z/):
   100: 
   101: | Input | Pin |
   102: | --- | --- |
   103: | `qemu-system-x86`, `qemu-system-arm`, `qemu-system-common`, `qemu-system-data` | `1:8.2.2+ds-0ubuntu1.18` |
   104: | `ovmf`, `qemu-efi-aarch64` | `2024.02-2ubuntu0.9` (EDK2 2024.02) |
   105: | x86-64 machine / CPU | `pc-q35-8.2` / `qemu64` |
   106: | AArch64 machine / CPU | `virt-8.2` / `cortex-a57` |
   107: | Both machines | TCG, one emulation thread, one CPU, 512 MiB RAM, no network, no display, serial log, no reboot; normal QEMU timers and fixed RTC (`2024-02-01T00:00:00`, VM clock) |
   108: 
   109: `tools/uefi_boot.c` verifies the exact QEMU version line and SHA-256 of each
   110: firmware code image and pristine variable template. The GitHub `UEFI firmware
   111: boot` job installs those exact packages from the snapshot and is required by
   112: `CI complete`. It uses the ordinary PR merge checkout, main/tag pushes,
   113: merge groups and manual dispatches, under the existing `GH_ACTIONS_CI_ENABLED`
   114: switch. Update the snapshot, package versions, firmware hashes and machine
   115: configuration together when intentionally refreshing the reference lane.
   116: 
   117: Each boot gets a deterministic raw disk with a 16 MiB FAT16 EFI System
   118: Partition (MBR type `0xef`, starting at LBA 2048), containing `EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI` or
   119: `EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI` and a private copy of the pristine variable store. The C harness writes the
   120: fixed filesystem layout, dates and volume ID directly; it uses no formatter,
   121: mount, or QEMU virtual-FAT backend.
   122: The fixture checks the image handle and system table signature, firmware
   123: service calls, ten-argument direct and indirect calls (including stack

===== docs/windows-matrix-benchmark.md =====
--- lines 1-50 ---
     1: # Paired Windows matrix benchmark
     2: 
     3: The `Windows paired matrix benchmark` workflow compares two immutable repository
     4: commits using the ordinary complete Windows x86-64
     5: `build/build.exe test_all_combinations_ci --verbose=1` target. Dispatch it with
     6: full lowercase `baseline` and `candidate` commit SHAs. The repository variable
     7: `GH_ACTIONS_CI_ENABLED` must be enabled, as for ordinary CI.
     8: 
     9: Three hosted `windows-2025` jobs each run both arms sequentially on the same VM,
    10: in separate clean checkouts and build directories. Trials 1 and 3 run baseline
    11: first; trial 2 runs candidate first. The existing native driver's four-thread
    12: admission policy and complete configuration matrix remain responsible for work
    13: inside each arm. There is no fixture or child-process timing instrumentation.
    14: The branch-only pull-request trigger validates this workflow's initial #708
    15: comparison; ordinary pull requests do not run benchmark jobs.
    16: 
    17: Each arm retains its actual checkout SHA, wall-clock start and finish, monotonic
    18: elapsed matrix time, exit status, raw logs, and independently validated coverage
    19: manifest. Coverage identity uses that arm's source SHA; `workflow_sha` records
    20: the triggering workflow revision separately. CPU description, runner image,
    21: Clang version, order, and trial number accompany the pair. The coverage report
    22: also records the detected compiler identities and the six required rows.
    23: 
    24: A failed arm still leaves evidence and allows the other arm to run; any matrix
    25: or coverage failure fails the pair. A successful pair additionally requires
    26: three matching driver-module assertion inventories. This catches differences
    27: in native execution coverage that can otherwise follow hosted CPU features.
    28: All attempts, including failures and cancellations, belong in the final audit.
    29: The two source trees must preserve the same semantic workload; equal assertion
    30: counts alone do not establish that contract.
    31: 
    32: Passing this workflow means the two arms completed with matching driver
    33: assertion counts. It is not a speedup verdict. Analyze paired full-matrix and
    34: module durations, runner-job durations and queue delay separately; inspect
    35: actual source changes and native classifications before accepting a result.
    36: CPU consumption and peak simultaneous process-tree RSS are explicitly
    37: unavailable in the uninstrumented result. Normal platform, sanitizer, mode,
    38: throughput, and self-host checks remain separate requirements for a code PR.
    39: 
    40: ## Why the original #708 samples are insufficient
    41: 
    42: [Run 35368006821](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/35368006821)
    43: used separate hosted VMs for baseline `f7c4e868` and candidate `72dca950`.
    44: All six matrices and coverage summaries passed, but their driver assertion
    45: inventories differed. Two baseline trials recorded 34,187 / 32,360 / 32,360
    46: assertions; baseline trial 2 and all candidate trials recorded
    47: 34,091 / 32,264 / 32,264. The candidate reported 192 executions, 44 links and
    48: 148 cache hits per invocation. The old coverage identity also used the
    49: workflow merge SHA, so source identity must instead be recovered from the
    50: checkout output and `source-sha.txt` for those historical artifacts.

  8822: // Converts an i128 pair in a frame slot to an AArch64 scalar FP value. The
  8823: // halves are converted as an unsigned magnitude, with an integer sticky-bit
  8824: // combine before the final double conversion. Converting the halves
  8825: // independently and adding them can double-round a halfway value (the low
  8826: // half's sticky bit would have been lost by ucvtf), so the common path first
  8827: // rounds a target-precision significand (53 bits for binary64, 24 for binary32)
  8828: // and scales it by the discarded-bit count.
  8829: // Signed inputs are made positive first and negated in FP after the magnitude
  8830: // has been formed. The final narrowing is done only once when the requested
  8831: // destination is float.
  8832: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool codegen_canonical_a64_i128_to_float(CodegenBuffer* buffer, u32 source_offset, u32 result_offset, u32 target_width,
  8833:                                                             bool signed_value)

  8837:         codegen_canonical_a64_frame_memory_operation(buffer, 9, source_offset, 8, false, false) &&
  8838:         codegen_canonical_a64_frame_memory_operation(buffer, 10, source_offset + 8, 8, false, false))
  8839:     {

  8841:         {

  8843:             codegen_emit_u32(buffer, 0xca0f012d); // eor x13, x9, x15
  8844:             codegen_emit_u32(buffer, 0xca0f014e); // eor x14, x10, x15
  8845:             codegen_emit_u32(buffer, 0xeb0f01ad); // subs x13, x13, x15
  8846:             codegen_emit_u32(buffer, 0xda0f01ce); // sbc x14, x14, x15

  9007: // Converts a scalar float/double in a frame slot to an i128 pair. Values are
  9008: // split at 2^64 so each FCVTZU consumes a representable unsigned 64-bit
  9009: // range; signed inputs use the absolute magnitude and restore the sign in the
  9010: // integer pair. Float inputs are widened to double before the split.

  2105: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool machine_builder_canonical_pair_parameter(MachineFunctionBuilder* builder, IrFunction* function,
  2106:                                                                  IrCfgBlock const* block, u32 parameter_index, MachineCanonicalPair** pairs)
  2107: {
  2108:     if (!*pairs)
  2109:     {
  2110:         *pairs = arena_allocate(builder->arena, MachineCanonicalPair, function->value_count);
  2111:         memset(*pairs, 0xff, sizeof(**pairs) * function->value_count);
  2112:     }
  2113:     bool valid = true;
  2114:     IrPublishedCfg const* cfg = function->published_cfg;
  2115:     IrCfgParameter const* parameter = cfg->parameters + block->parameter_offset + parameter_index;
  2116:     u32 value = parameter->value.value;
  2117:     for (u32 index = 0; index <= block->predecessor_count && valid; index += 1)
  2118:     {
  2119:         if (index)
  2120:         {
  2121:             IrCfgEdge const* edge = cfg->edges + cfg->predecessors[block->predecessor_offset + index - 1];
  2122:             value = cfg->arguments[edge->argument_offset + parameter_index].value;
  2123:         }
  2124:         if (value >= function->value_count)
  2125:         {
  2126:             valid = false;
  2127:         }
  2128:         else if ((*pairs)[value].registers[0] == UINT32_MAX)
  2129:         {
  2130:             for (u32 part = 0; part < 2; part += 1)
  2131:             {
  2132:                 (*pairs)[value].registers[part] = machine_builder_virtual_register(builder, (MachineVirtualRegister){
  2133:                     .definition_point = MACHINE_POINT_INVALID, .register_class = MACHINE_REGISTER_CLASS_GENERAL,
  2134:                     .typed_origin = value});
  2135:             }
  2136:         }
  2137:     }
  2138:     return valid;
  2139: }

  2141: // Canonical publication owns terminator topology and edge-argument lookup.
  2142: // Selection translates each already ordered argument once; i128 values expand
  2143: // to their two register limbs without changing the canonical CFG.

  2145:                                                         MachineCanonicalPair const* pairs)
  2146: {

  2157:             u32 incoming = cfg->arguments[edge->argument_offset + parameter_index].value;

  2159:             u32 count = wide ? 2u : 1u;

  2161:             for (u32 part = 0; valid && part < count; part += 1)
  2162:             {
  2163:                 valid = registers[part] != UINT32_MAX;
  2164:                 if (valid)
  2165:                 {
  2166:                     IR_CONSTRUCTION_RECORD(CFG_COPY_SOURCES, 1);
  2167:                     machine_builder_edge_copy_source(builder, machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_VIRTUAL_REGISTER, registers[part]));
  2168:                 }
  2169:             }
  2170:         }
  2171:         u32 copy_count = builder->edge_copy_sources.total_count - copy_offset;
  2172:         valid = valid && copy_count <= UINT16_MAX;
  2173:         if (valid)
  2174:         {
  2175:             machine_builder_edge(builder, (MachineEdge){.source_block = edge->source.value, .destination_block = edge->destination.value,
  2176:                                                        .copy_offset = copy_offset, .copy_count = (u16)copy_count});
  2177:         }
  2178:     }
  2179:     return valid;
  2180: }
  2181: 
  2182: MachineFunction machine_function_builder_finish(Arena* arena, MachineFunctionBuilder* builder)
  2183: {
  2184:     BUSTER_CHECK(!builder->block_is_open);
  2185:     BUSTER_CHECK(builder->edges.total_count == 0 || builder->edges.total_count <= MACHINE_REF_PAYLOAD_LIMIT);
  2186:     BUSTER_CHECK(builder->block_parameters.total_count == 0 || builder->block_parameters.total_count <= MACHINE_REF_PAYLOAD_LIMIT);
  2187:     BUSTER_CHECK(builder->edge_copy_sources.total_count == 0 || builder->edge_copy_sources.total_count <= MACHINE_REF_PAYLOAD_LIMIT);

     1: // AArch64 machine selection and encoding. Included by machine.c in the
     2: // backend-implementation-file pattern; not a standalone translation unit.
     3: // The subset covers scalar integer functions — arguments, constants,
     4: // casts, unary and binary arithmetic including divides and shifts,
     5: // comparisons, direct locals and pointer dereference, member addresses,
     6: // branches, and scalar returns — plus the AAPCS64 signature shapes, calls,
     7: // symbol addresses, aggregate/array literal construction into frame slots,
     8: // scalar float bodies (arithmetic, comparison, negation, and conversions
     9: // over the bit-image model, riding V0/V1 internally), scalar stack
    10: // arguments through a fixed outgoing area at the frame bottom, ELF
    11: // variadic definitions using the public ELF AAPCS64 va_list and platform
    12: // pointer lists on Darwin and Windows,
    13: // sixteen-byte short-vector arguments and results as slot-backed values
    14: // touching the V file only at the ABI edges, indirect arguments — any
    15: // aggregate or vector past sixteen bytes — behind a caller-side defensive
    16: // copy, over-aligned locals as runtime-aligned pointers into padded raw
    17: // slots, and rvalue array/vector INDEX bases through their storage
    18: // snapshot. Wide division expands into scalar MIR blocks before placement.
    19: // Sixteen-byte atomics use constrained pair rows, including readback on a
    20: // failed compare-exchange so the returned old image is single-copy atomic.
    21: // Everything else is an explicit unsupported result, never a
    22: // silent misselection.
    23: // machine_a64_select_inline_hint selects the fixed NOP/YIELD literal rows.
    24: //
    25: // Register conventions: values live zero-extended in X registers exactly
    26: // like the x86-64 register model. X28 is the frame base (the canonical
    27: // AArch64 path's convention), X29/X30 the frame-pointer pair, X16/X17 the
    28: // encoder's address scratches (and the linker's veneer registers), X18 the
    29: // platform register — none are allocatable. Frame slots sit at positive
    30: // X28-relative offsets; a placement offset o addresses X28 + frame_size - o,
    31: // which keeps the shared placement's grows-down offset convention intact.
    32: 
    33: #include <buster/lib/compiler/codegen/machine.h>
    34: // For codegen_canonical_integer_aggregate_parts: the canonical emitter's
    35: // named-parameter walk is the variadic model's defining simulation, and
    36: // VA_START must run the exact same one.
