   281: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool machine_a64_value_shape(IrProgram* program, IrTypeId type_id, Target target, IrAbiUse use, MachineA64ValueShape* shape)
   282: {
   283:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&program->types, type_id);
   284:     if (machine_a64_type_is_scalar_register(type))
   285:     {
   286:         *shape = (MachineA64ValueShape){
   287:             .part_sizes = {8},
   288:             .part_count = 1,
   289:             .byte_size = 8,
   290:             .exact_byte_size = (u32)type->layout.size,
   291:         };
   292:         return true;
   293:     }
   294:     if (machine_a64_type_is_float_scalar(type))
   295:     {
   296:         *shape = (MachineA64ValueShape){
   297:             .part_is_float = {(u8)!(target.os == OPERATING_SYSTEM_WINDOWS && use == IR_ABI_USE_VARIADIC_ARGUMENT)},
   298:             .part_sizes = {(u8)(type->bit_width / 8)},
   299:             .part_count = 1,
   300:             .byte_size = 8,
   301:             .exact_byte_size = (u32)type->layout.size,
   302:         };
   303:         return true;
   304:     }
   305:     // A bare 128-bit integer is the AAPCS64 even-aligned X pair — the same
   306:     // two INTEGER parts a sixteen-byte wrapped pair builds — carried by the
   307:     // aggregate machinery over the value's 16-byte slot, exactly like the
   308:     // x86-64 selector's RAX:RDX shape. The pair bit comes from the shared
   309:     // ABI helper so argument and result uses keep the canonical answer.
   310:     if (type && type->layout.resolved && type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER && type->bit_width == 128)
   311:     {
   312:         *shape = (MachineA64ValueShape){
   313:             .part_offsets = {0, 8},
   314:             .part_sizes = {8, 8},
   315:             .part_count = 2,
   316:             .byte_size = 16,
   317:             .aggregate = true,
   318:             .even_integer_pair = ir_abi_value_is_aarch64_even_integer_pair(program, type_id, ir_abi_convention_for_target(target), use),
   319:         };
   320:         return true;
   321:     }
   322:     if (!type || !type->layout.resolved ||
   323:         (type->kind != IR_TYPE_STRUCT && type->kind != IR_TYPE_UNION && type->kind != IR_TYPE_SLICE && type->kind != IR_TYPE_VECTOR &&
   324:          !(type->kind == IR_TYPE_VA_LIST && (type->layout.size == 8 ||
   325:            (type->layout.size == 32 && ir_abi_convention_for_target(target) == IR_ABI_CONVENTION_AAPCS64)))))
   326:     {
   327:         return false;
   328:     }
   329:     if (type->layout.size > UINT32_MAX - 7)
   330:     {
   331:         return false;
   332:     }
   333:     IrAbiValue abi = ir_type_abi_value(program, type_id, ir_abi_convention_for_target(target), use);
   334:     if (type->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR && !abi.indirect && !abi.memory && abi.part_count == 1 && abi.parts[0].abi_class == IR_ABI_CLASS_VECTOR)
   335:     {
   336:         // A short vector rides one V register — the whole register for
   337:         // the sixteen-byte form, the low bytes for anything smaller — and
   338:         // the value itself is slot-backed with only the ABI edges
   339:         // touching the vector file. Sizes without a sized FP transfer
   340:         // encoding (the non-power-of-two lane counts) stay canonical.
   341:         if (abi.parts[0].size != 1 && abi.parts[0].size != 2 && abi.parts[0].size != 4 && abi.parts[0].size != 8 && abi.parts[0].size != 16)
   342:         {
   343:             return false;
   344:         }
   345:         IrType* vector_element = ir_type_from_id(&program->types, type->element_type);
   346:         bool widened_result = use == IR_ABI_USE_RESULT && abi.parts[0].size < 8 && vector_element && vector_element->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER &&
   347:                               (type->element_count == 2 || type->element_count == 4) &&
   348:                               (vector_element->bit_width == 8 || vector_element->bit_width == 16) &&
   349:                               type->layout.size == type->element_count * (vector_element->bit_width / 8);
   350:         *shape = (MachineA64ValueShape){
   351:             .part_is_float = {1},
   352:             .part_sizes = {(u8)abi.parts[0].size},
   353:             .part_count = 1,
   354:             .byte_size = (abi.parts[0].size + 7u) & ~7u,
   355:             .exact_byte_size = (u32)type->layout.size,

   940: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool machine_a64_select_argument(MachineA64Selector* selector, IrInstruction* instruction, u32 result_register)
   941: {
   942:     // The typed ARGUMENT can appear anywhere the frontend first used
   943:     // the parameter; the value itself was captured by the entry rows
   944:     // before any scratch register could clobber the incoming fixed
   945:     // registers.
   946:     bool selected = false;
   947:     if (instruction->immediate_count && instruction->immediates)
   948:     {
   949:         u32 argument_index = (u32)instruction->immediates[0];
   950:         selected = argument_index < selector->parameter_count &&
   951:                    (result_register != UINT32_MAX || selector->value_stack_slots[instruction->result.value] != UINT32_MAX) &&
   952:                    selector->argument_values[argument_index] == instruction->result.value;
   953:     }
   954:     return selected;
   955: }

   957: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool machine_a64_select_constant(MachineA64Selector* selector, IrInstruction* instruction, u32 result_register)
   958: {
   959:     IrProgram* program = selector->program;
   960:     IrFunction* function = selector->function;
   961: 
   962:     bool selected = false;
   963:     if (result_register != UINT32_MAX)
   964:     {
   965:         // Float constants carry their IEEE bit pattern in the immediate,
   966:         // exactly like the canonical shared constant path.
   967:         u64 immediate = instruction->immediates[0];
   968:         if (instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_CONSTANT_INTEGER && instruction->immediate_is_negative)
   969:         {
   970:             immediate = 0 - immediate;
   971:         }
   972:         u32 immediate_index = machine_a64_append_immediate(selector, immediate);
   973:         u32 row = machine_a64_select_row(selector, (MachineInstruction){
   974:                                                        .operands = {machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_VIRTUAL_REGISTER, result_register),
   975:                                                                     machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_IMMEDIATE, immediate_index)},
   976:                                                        .opcode = MACHINE_A64_MOV_RI,
   977:                                                    });
   978:         machine_a64_define(selector, result_register, row);
   979:         selected = true;
   980:     }
   981:     else if (instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_CONSTANT_INTEGER && instruction->result.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
   982:              instruction->result.value < function->value_count && selector->value_stack_slots[instruction->result.value] != UINT32_MAX)
   983:     {
   984:         // A 128-bit integer constant is slot-backed like every i128 value.
   985:         // The second eightbyte is the canonical emitters' selection: an
   986:         // explicit second immediate when the frontend recorded one,
   987:         // otherwise the negated low half's sign fill.
   988:         IrType* constant_type = ir_type_from_id(&program->types, instruction->canonical_type);
   989:         if (constant_type && constant_type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER && constant_type->bit_width == 128)
   990:         {
   991:             u32 result_slot = selector->value_stack_slots[instruction->result.value];
   992:             u64 low = instruction->immediate_is_negative ? 0 - instruction->immediates[0] : instruction->immediates[0];
   993:             u64 high = instruction->immediate_count > 1 ? instruction->immediates[1] : instruction->immediate_is_negative ? UINT64_MAX : 0;
   994:             u64 halves[2] = {low, high};
   995:             for (u32 half_index = 0; half_index < 2; half_index += 1)
   996:             {
   997:                 u32 half_register = machine_a64_synthesize_register(selector);
   998:                 machine_a64_select_row(selector, (MachineInstruction){
   999:                                                      .operands = {machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_VIRTUAL_REGISTER, half_register),
  1000:                                                                   machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_IMMEDIATE,
  1001:                                                                                    machine_a64_append_immediate(selector, halves[half_index]))},
  1002:                                                      .opcode = MACHINE_A64_MOV_RI,
  1003:                                                  });
  1004:                 machine_a64_select_row(selector, (MachineInstruction){
  1005:                                                      .operands = {machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_STACK_SLOT, result_slot),
  1006:                                                                   machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_VIRTUAL_REGISTER, half_register)},
  1007:                                                      .payload = half_index * 8,
  1008:                                                      .opcode = MACHINE_A64_STORE_FRAME64,
  1009:                                                  });
  1010:             }
  1011:             selected = true;
  1012:         }
  1013:     }
  1014:     return selected;
  1015: }

  1021:                                                                   u32 source_bits, u32 source_register, u32 result_register)
  1022: {

  1037:                                                  .opcode = extend_opcode,

  1045:                                                        .opcode = convert_opcode,
  1046:                                                    });

  1048:         selected = true;
  1049:     }

  1835: // Binary32/64 widen exactly into a binary128 frame image. Normalize the

  1916: // Match the direct oracle's 2^64 magnitude split using ordinary scalar MIR.
  1917: // Widen f32 exactly before splitting. For representable finite inputs the high

  1919: // limb; FCVTZU supplies truncation toward zero. Restore signed values with an

  1921: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool machine_a64_select_float_to_i128(MachineA64Selector* selector, IrInstruction* instruction,
  1922:                                                           IrType* source_type, IrType* target_type)

  1927:     u32 source = UINT32_MAX;

  1930:                     (signed_value || instruction->conversion_operation == IR_CONVERSION_FLOAT_TO_UNSIGNED_INTEGER) &&
  1931:                     machine_a64_operand_register(selector, instruction->operands[0], &source);

  1933:     {

  1948:         u32 scaled = machine_a64_select_float_to_pair_step(selector, MACHINE_A64_FARITH, source, inverse_limb_scale, 0x102);
  1949:         u32 high = machine_a64_select_float_to_pair_step(selector, MACHINE_A64_CVT_F64_TO_U64, scaled, UINT32_MAX, 0);

  1953:         u32 residual = machine_a64_select_float_to_pair_step(selector, MACHINE_A64_FARITH, source, high_contribution, 0x101);
  1954:         u32 low = machine_a64_select_float_to_pair_step(selector, MACHINE_A64_CVT_F64_TO_U64, residual, UINT32_MAX, 0);

  1963:         }

  2087: // Normalize the unsigned magnitude as a pair, then round its top 24/53 bits
  2088: // once using round/sticky/parity. Converting limbs independently would lose
  2089: // the low limb's sticky bit and double-round halfway inputs. A zero high limb

  2188: // add/subtract per half (the carry and borrow are CSET booleans off the

  2790: {

  2817:     // read below safe; nothing here may be hoisted above them.

  2823:                                                     left_register, right_register, result_register);

    29: // The register shape of one argument or result under the subset: scalar
    30: // values occupy one integer register; small integer-class aggregates occupy
    31: // one or two, with the part offsets taken from the IR-owned System V
    32: // classification. Anything else (floats, memory or indirect classes) is

    35: struct MachineX64ValueShape

    43:     bool force_stack;
    44:     // Indirect result: returned through a hidden pointer in RDI.
    45:     bool indirect;

    47:     // part in the floating register sequence. Win64 arguments carry this
    48:     // value through an indirect pointer part; results use ZMM0 directly.
    49:     bool vector;
    50:     u8 f80_result;
    51:     // The System V argument-area alignment of the value's stack home in
    52:     // bytes when it exceeds the eightbyte floor: 16 for the __int128 pair
    53:     // and sixteen-aligned memory-class aggregates, 64 for a whole ZMM
    54:     // vector, zero for the plain eightbyte floor. The placement rounds the
    55:     // stack cursor up to it — the same padding eightbytes the canonical
    56:     // layout counts on both sides of a call. Win64 indirect arguments reuse
    57:     // this field for their private copy's alignment, with a sixteen-byte floor.
    58:     u32 stack_alignment;
    59:     // For a sub-32-bit scalar integer argument, the MOVSX/MOVZX opcode that
    60:     // widens it into its argument register: the de-facto System V contract
    61:     // clang's callers implement extends such arguments to 32 bits, and
    62:     // callees exist that read the widened register directly. Zero when a
    63:     // plain move suffices.
    64:     u16 scalar_extend_opcode;
    65:     // A frame-backed sixteen-byte value occupies one whole XMM ABI register.
    66:     bool xmm128;
    67:     // Frame-backed vectors split into consecutive XMM/YMM/ZMM ABI parts.
    68:     // The regular scalar/aggregate part arrays remain two entries: vector
    69:     // offsets are part_index * vector_part_bytes and need no extra storage.

  2264: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool machine_x64_select_constant(MachineX64Selector* selector, IrInstruction* instruction, u32 result_register)
  2265: {
  2266:     IrProgram* program = selector->program;
  2267:     IrFunction* function = selector->function;
  2268: 
  2269:     bool selected = false;
  2270:     if (result_register != UINT32_MAX)
  2271:     {

  2273:         // exactly like the canonical shared constant path.
  2274:         u64 immediate = instruction->immediates[0];

  2276:         {
  2277:             immediate = 0 - immediate;

  2282:                                                                     machine_ref_make(MACHINE_REF_IMMEDIATE, immediate_index)},
  2283:                                                        .opcode = MACHINE_X64_MOV_RI,
  2284:                                                    });
  2285:         machine_x64_define(selector, result_register, row);
  2286:         selected = true;
  2287:     }
  2288:     else if (machine_x64_type_is_f80(selector, instruction->canonical_type) && instruction->immediate_count == 2 &&

  2290:     {
  2291:         u32 slot = selector->value_stack_slots[instruction->result.value];
  2292:         selected = slot != UINT32_MAX;
  2293:         if (selected)
  2294:         {
  2295:             machine_x64_select_frame_store64(selector, slot, 0, machine_x64_select_immediate_register(selector, instruction->immediates[0]));
  2296:             machine_x64_select_frame_store64(selector, slot, 8, machine_x64_select_immediate_register(selector, instruction->immediates[1]));
  2297:         }
  2298:     }
  2299:     else if (instruction->opcode == IR_OPCODE_CONSTANT_INTEGER && instruction->result.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
  2300:              instruction->result.value < function->value_count && selector->value_stack_slots[instruction->result.value] != UINT32_MAX)
  2301:     {
  2302:         // A 128-bit integer constant is slot-backed like every i128 value, so
  2303:         // it has no result register and is written half by half. The second
  2304:         // eightbyte is the canonical emitters' selection: an explicit second
  2305:         // immediate when the frontend recorded one, otherwise the negated low
  2306:         // half's sign fill. This mirrors machine_a64_select_constant.

  2308:         if (constant_type && constant_type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER && constant_type->bit_width == 128 && instruction->immediate_count &&

  2310:         {
  2311:             u32 result_slot = selector->value_stack_slots[instruction->result.value];
  2312:             u64 low = instruction->immediate_is_negative ? 0 - instruction->immediates[0] : instruction->immediates[0];
  2313:             u64 high = instruction->immediate_count > 1 ? instruction->immediates[1] : instruction->immediate_is_negative ? UINT64_MAX : 0;
  2314:             u64 halves[2] = {low, high};

  2316:             {

  2318:                                                  machine_x64_select_immediate_register(selector, halves[half_index]));
  2319:             }
  2320:             selected = true;
  2321:         }
  2322:     }
  2323:     return selected;
  2324: }

 14278: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL void machine_x64_emit_f80_padding(MachineX64Encoder* encoder, s32 displacement)
 14279: {
 14280:     (void)machine_x64_emit_metadata_memory_immediate(encoder, S8("MOV"), MACHINE_X64_RBP, displacement + 10, 0, 16, 16, 0);

 14284: // Every arithmetic/conversion sequence balances its own x87 stack and keeps
 14285: // the caller's precision/rounding control. C integer casts temporarily select
 14286: // truncation using baseline FISTP; SSE3 FISTTP is not assumed available.
 14287: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL void machine_x64_emit_f80(MachineX64Encoder* encoder, MachineInstruction* instruction, MachineStackPlacement* placement)
 14288: {
 14289:     s32 offsets[3] = {0};
 14290:     bool compare = instruction->opcode == MACHINE_X64_F80_COMPARE;
 14291:     u32 count = instruction->opcode == MACHINE_X64_F80_BINARY || compare || instruction->opcode == MACHINE_X64_F80_CONVERT ? 3u :
 14292:                 instruction->opcode == MACHINE_X64_F80_NEGATE ? 2u : 1u;
 14293:     for (u32 operand = compare ? 1u : 0u; operand < count; operand += 1)
 14294:     {
 14295:         offsets[operand] = -(s32)placement->stack_slot_offsets[machine_ref_payload(instruction->operands[operand])];
 14296:     }
 14297:     if (instruction->opcode == MACHINE_X64_F80_BINARY)
 14298:     {
 14299:         String8 names[] = {S8("FADDP"), S8("FSUBP"), S8("FMULP"), S8("FDIVP")};
 14300:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FLD"), offsets[1], 80);
 14301:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FLD"), offsets[2], 80);
 14302:         BusterX86MetadataPhysicalOperand operands[] = {machine_x64_x87_operand(1), machine_x64_x87_operand(0)};
 14303:         (void)machine_x64_emit_x87(encoder, names[instruction->payload], operands, 1);
 14304:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FSTP"), offsets[0], 80);
 14305:         machine_x64_emit_f80_padding(encoder, offsets[0]);
 14306:     }
 14307:     else if (instruction->opcode == MACHINE_X64_F80_NEGATE)
 14308:     {
 14309:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FLD"), offsets[1], 80);
 14310:         (void)machine_x64_emit_x87(encoder, S8("FCHS"), 0, 0);
 14311:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FSTP"), offsets[0], 80);
 14312:         machine_x64_emit_f80_padding(encoder, offsets[0]);
 14313:     }
 14314:     else if (compare)
 14315:     {
 14316:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FLD"), offsets[2], 80);
 14317:         machine_x64_emit_x87_memory(encoder, S8("FLD"), offsets[1], 80);
 14318:         BusterX86MetadataPhysicalOperand operands[] = {machine_x64_x87_operand(0), machine_x64_x87_operand(1)};
 14319:         (void)machine_x64_emit_x87(encoder, S8("FUCOMIP"), operands + 1, 1);
 14320:         (void)machine_x64_emit_x87(encoder, S8("FSTP"), operands, 1);
 14321:         String8 names[] = {S8("SETZ"), S8("SETNZ"), S8("SETB"), S8("SETBE"), S8("SETNBE"), S8("SETNB")};
 14322:         (void)machine_x64_emit_metadata_register(encoder, names[instruction->payload], MACHINE_X64_RAX, 8, 0);
 14323:         if (instruction->payload < 4)
 14324:         {
 14325:             bool unequal = instruction->payload == 1;
 14326:             (void)machine_x64_emit_metadata_register(encoder, unequal ? S8("SETP") : S8("SETNP"), MACHINE_X64_RCX, 8, 0);
 14327:             (void)machine_x64_emit_metadata_registers(encoder, unequal ? S8("OR") : S8("AND"), MACHINE_X64_RAX, MACHINE_X64_RCX, 8, 0);
 14328:         }
 14329:         BusterX86MetadataPhysicalOperand extend[] = {machine_x64_exact_gpr_operand(MACHINE_X64_RAX, 64), machine_x64_exact_gpr_operand(MACHINE_X64_RAX, 8)};

   830: // The GNU attributes a struct or union definition carries on the definition
   831: // itself, either before the tag (`struct __attribute__((packed)) P { ... }`)
   832: // or after the closing brace (`struct P { ... } __attribute__((packed));`).
   833: // They live in a side table rather than in CType because the population is a
   834: // handful of aggregates in a translation unit while the type table is tens of
   835: // thousands of entries: a flag word per type would grow every one of them.
   836: // Both layout engines -- the sizeof folding in c_parse.c and the IR layout in
   837: // c_gen.c -- read this table, and they must agree or a folded sizeof
   838: // contradicts the object it sizes.
   839: typedef struct CAggregateAttributes CAggregateAttributes;
   840: struct CAggregateAttributes
   841: {
   842:     u32 type_index;

   844:     u32 alignment_start;
   845:     u32 alignment_count;
   846:     bool is_packed;
   847:     u8 reserved[3];

   850: // The alignment a declarator wrote on the *type* it declares rather than on an
   851: // object it declares: `typedef int cache_line __attribute__((aligned(64)))`.
   852: // GNU `aligned` there sets the alignment of the type, so unlike every other
   853: // alignment record in this file it *replaces* the natural alignment instead of
   854: // raising it, and it is the one place the attribute lowers one without
   855: // `packed` -- `typedef int pair __attribute__((aligned(2)))` is two-byte
   856: // aligned in both GCC and Clang. The record keys on the alias copy the
   857: // declarator made, never on the type it aliases, so `int` keeps its own
   858: // alignment -- and on every qualified copy of that alias, because a qualifier
   859: // cannot take an alignment away and the qualified copy points past the alias
   860: // at the type it strips to (#714). It lives in a side table for the reason
   861: // CParseResult.noreturn_function_types does: the population is a handful of
   862: // typedefs per translation unit against a type table of tens of thousands of
   863: // entries, so a field on CType would cost every one of them.

   409:         return S8("int");
   410:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT:
   411:         return S8("unsigned int");
   412:     case C_TYPE_LONG:
   413:         return S8("long");
   414:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG:
   415:         return S8("unsigned long");
   416:     case C_TYPE_LONG_LONG:
   417:         return S8("long long");
   418:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG:
   419:         return S8("unsigned long long");
   420:     case C_TYPE_INT128:
   421:         return S8("__int128");

   423:         return S8("unsigned __int128");

  4607: // May the parenthesized group opening at `open` spell a type name?  False
  4608: // only when the token after the `(` proves it cannot, without entering the
  4609: // query machine.  c_ir_type_name_prefix accepts a type name that begins with
  4610: // a type, qualifier, tag, typeof or _Atomic keyword, a decoration
  4611: // c_ir_primitive_type_kind steps over (an attribute, an asm label, a `[[`
  4612: // attribute) or an identifier naming a typedef, and nothing else, so:
  4613: // - a number, a string, a character and every punctuator but `[` is refused
  4614: //   outright;
  4615: // - an identifier the parser bound to a local, object, parameter,
  4616: //   enumerator or function is refused too: the prefix reads that binding
  4617: //   before any scope lookup, and none of them is a typedef.  Its spelling
  4618: //   must not be one of the keywords above, which
  4619: //   c_parse_type_name_start_word_token answers from the word bits (an
  4620: //   interned spelling outside the predefined range is no keyword; symbol 0
  4621: //   is unclassified and stays a candidate).

  4623: // and a typedef is the candidate the probe exists for.

  4633:         }

  4641:                          kind != C_ENTITY_FUNCTION;

  4643:         }
  4644:     }
  4645:     return result;
  4646: }

  6734: // The address of the bytes a bit-field occupies, as `unsigned char*`.
  6735: // `c_ir_emit_address_of_place` refuses a bit-field place because C does --
  6736: // `&s.b` is not an expression -- but a field with no single storage unit is
  6737: // read and written one piece at a time, and the pieces past the first are
  6738: // bytes the member place cannot name. The place still starts at
  6739: // `field->offset`, which is the first byte of the span.
  6740: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_bit_field_storage_address(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrSourceRange source)
  6741: {
  6742:     IrTypeId place_type = builder->function->values[place.value].canonical_type;
  6743:     IrTypeId pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, place_type);
  6744:     IrTypeId byte_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR));
  6745:     if (pointer_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || byte_pointer_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6746:     {
  6747:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6748:     }
  6749:     IrValueId address = c_ir_add_result(builder, pointer_type);
  6750:     if (address.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6751:     {
  6752:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6753:     }
  6754:     builder->function->values[address.value].points_to_read_only = builder->function->values[place.value].is_read_only;
  6755:     IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_ADDRESS_OF, pointer_type);
  6756:     instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
  6757:     instruction.operands[0] = place;
  6758:     instruction.operand_count = 1;
  6759:     instruction.result = address;
  6760:     IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
  6761:     builder->function->values[address.value].definition = id;
  6762:     return c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, byte_pointer_type, source);
  6763: }

  6784: // The bits of `field` that lie in one piece of its span, as the half-open
  6785: // range [`low`, `high`) of span bit positions. Empty when the piece holds none
  6786: // of them, which no piece of a span that is exactly the field's bytes does,
  6787: // but a caller that walks pieces should not have to know that.
  6788: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL void c_ir_bit_field_piece_bits(IrField const* field, IrFieldAccessPiece piece, u32* low, u32* high)
  6789: {
  6790:     u32 piece_low = (u32)piece.offset * 8;
  6791:     u32 piece_high = piece_low + (u32)piece.size * 8;
  6792:     u32 field_high = field->bit_offset + field->bit_width;
  6793:     *low = BUSTER_MAX(piece_low, field->bit_offset);
  6794:     *high = BUSTER_MIN(piece_high, field_high);
  6795: }
  6796: 
  6797: // A packed bit-field the aggregate left no single storage unit for is read one
  6798: // piece at a time and reassembled: each piece contributes the bits of its own
  6799: // byte range that belong to the field, shifted down to the field's low bit.
  6800: // The assembly runs at sixty-four bits, which covers every bit-field there is,
  6801: // and the result narrows to the declared type on the way out -- the same shape
  6802: // the single-unit extraction has, with the load replaced by a sum of loads.
  6803: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_split_bit_field_load(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrField* field, IrTypeId type, u64 access_size,
  6804:                                                            IrSourceRange source)
  6805: {
  6806:     IrFieldAccessPiece pieces[IR_FIELD_ACCESS_PIECE_CAPACITY];
  6807:     u32 piece_count = ir_field_access_pieces(access_size, pieces);
  6808:     IrType* value_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
  6809:     IrTypeId wide_type = c_ir_unsigned_type_of_size(builder, 8);
  6810:     IrValueId address = piece_count && value_type && wide_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
  6811:                             ? c_ir_emit_bit_field_storage_address(builder, place, source)
  6812:                             : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6813:     if (address.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6814:     {
  6815:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6816:     }
  6817:     CToken token = {0};
  6818:     IrValueId assembled = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6819:     for (u32 index = 0; index < piece_count; index += 1)
  6820:     {
  6821:         u32 low = 0;
  6822:         u32 high = 0;
  6823:         c_ir_bit_field_piece_bits(field, pieces[index], &low, &high);
  6824:         if (low >= high)
  6825:         {
  6826:             continue;
  6827:         }
  6828:         IrTypeId piece_type = c_ir_unsigned_type_of_size(builder, pieces[index].size);
  6829:         IrValueId piece_place =
  6830:             piece_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_bit_field_piece_place(builder, address, pieces[index].offset, piece_type, source)
  6831:                                                          : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6832:         IrValueId loaded = piece_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, piece_place, piece_type, source)
  6833:                                                                         : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6834:         IrValueId part = loaded.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, loaded, wide_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6835:         if (part.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6836:         {
  6837:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6838:         }
  6839:         if (low > (u32)pieces[index].offset * 8)
  6840:         {
  6841:             IrValueId shift = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, low - (u32)pieces[index].offset * 8, false, token, wide_type);
  6842:             part = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, part, shift, wide_type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
  6843:         }
  6844:         u64 mask = high - low == 64 ? UINT64_MAX : ((u64)1 << (high - low)) - 1;
  6845:         IrValueId mask_value = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, mask, false, token, wide_type);
  6846:         part = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, part, mask_value, wide_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
  6847:         if (low > field->bit_offset)
  6848:         {
  6849:             IrValueId shift = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, low - field->bit_offset, false, token, wide_type);
  6850:             part = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, part, shift, wide_type, IR_BINARY_SHIFT_LEFT, source);
  6851:         }
  6852:         assembled = assembled.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
  6853:                         ? part
  6854:                         : c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, assembled, part, wide_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_OR, source);
  6855:         if (assembled.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6856:         {
  6857:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6858:         }
  6859:     }
  6860:     if (assembled.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6861:     {
  6862:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6863:     }
  6864:     // The sign lives at the field's own top bit, so it is stretched from
  6865:     // there rather than from the assembly width; an unsigned field already
  6866:     // has zeroes above it from the masks.
  6867:     if (value_type->is_signed && field->bit_width < 64)
  6868:     {
  6869:         IrTypeId signed_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, C_TYPE_LONG_LONG);
  6870:         IrType* signed_value_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, signed_type);
  6871:         if (!signed_value_type || signed_value_type->bit_width != 64)
  6872:         {
  6873:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6874:         }

  6876:         assembled = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, assembled, signed_type, source);
  6877:         assembled = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, assembled, shift, signed_type, IR_BINARY_SHIFT_LEFT, source);
  6878:         assembled = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, assembled, shift, signed_type, IR_BINARY_SIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
  6879:     }
  6880:     IrValueId result = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, assembled, type, source);
  6881:     c_ir_mark_unsigned_bit_field_value(builder, result, field);
  6882:     return result;
  6883: }

  6961: 
  6962: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_load_place(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId type, IrSourceRange source)
  6963: {
  6964:     // C 6.3.2.1p4: a function designator is converted to a pointer to the
  6965:     // function; there is nothing to load out of one. The place reaches here
  6966:     // when the name resolves to an entity rather than to a call — a
  6967:     // block-scope `extern void sighandler(int);` declares such a name, and
  6968:     // sbase's make then stores it in a `struct sigaction`.
  6969:     IrType* designated_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
  6970:     if (designated_type && designated_type->kind == IR_TYPE_FUNCTION)
  6971:     {
  6972:         return c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, place, type, source);
  6973:     }
  6974:     IrField* field = c_ir_bit_field_from_place(builder, place);
  6975:     IrType* value_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
  6976:     // A `_Bool` bit-field's bits are extracted like any other's. Its declared
  6977:     // type is not an integer, so the extraction used to be skipped and the
  6978:     // whole `_Bool` unit came back -- every neighbouring field's bits with it,
  6979:     // normalized to one, which is why a `_Bool` that happened to be the only
  6980:     // set bit still read correctly. The unit it is read through has to be an
  6981:     // integer of the same width for the shift to see the raw byte.
  6982:     bool boolean = value_type && value_type->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN;
  6983:     bool extract =
  6984:         field && value_type && (value_type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER || boolean) && field->bit_width && field->bit_width <= value_type->bit_width;
  6985:     // A packed bit-field the aggregate left no room for a declared-type unit
  6986:     // of is read through the narrower one its layout recorded; every other
  6987:     // field reads its own type. A span that is no integer's width -- five
  6988:     // bytes for `long long b : 40` -- has no such unit and takes several
  6989:     // accesses instead.
  6990:     IrTypeId access_type = type;
  6991:     if (extract && (field->access_size || boolean))
  6992:     {
  6993:         access_type = c_ir_unsigned_type_of_size(builder, ir_field_access_size(&builder->program->types, field));
  6994:         if (access_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  6995:         {
  6996:             return c_ir_emit_split_bit_field_load(builder, place, field, type, field->access_size, source);
  6997:         }
  6998:     }
  6999:     IrValueId value = c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, place, access_type, source);
  7000:     if (extract)
  7001:     {
  7002:         CToken token = {0};
  7003:         // The extraction runs in the promoted type, never in a narrower one:
  7004:         // the machine backends model shifts at 32 and 64 bits only, so a
  7005:         // 16-bit `shl`/`sar` pair executes at 32 bits and the sign bit of a
  7006:         // `short a : 9` never reaches the top. Promoting here is also what C
  7007:         // does with the value, and the result narrows back on the way out.
  7008:         // The memory load removes object qualifiers. Extraction and its
  7009:         // constants must use that same value type, including volatile fields.
  7010:         IrTypeId result_type = value_type->is_atomic || value_type->is_volatile ? value_type->unqualified_type : type;
  7011:         IrTypeId extract_type = result_type;
  7012:         IrType* extract_type_value = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, extract_type);
  7013:         if (value_type->bit_width < 32)
  7014:         {
  7015:             extract_type = value_type->is_signed ? builder->s32_type : builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT];
  7016:             extract_type_value = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, extract_type);
  7017:         }
  7018:         if (extract_type_value && extract_type.value != access_type.value)
  7019:         {

  7765: // Do two types agree closely enough that a function prototype built from them
  7766: // is the same prototype? Identical ids always do. Beyond that only the coarse
  7767: // shape is compared -- the kind, and for the scalar kinds the width and
  7768: // signedness -- because two spellings of one aggregate can reach here as two
  7769: // ids and refusing them would reject valid code. This is the deliberate
  7770: // conservatism c_ir_function_prototypes_compatible documents.
  7771: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_scalar_shapes_agree(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId left, IrTypeId right)
  7772: {
  7773:     IrType* left_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, left);
  7774:     IrType* right_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, right);
  7775:     bool result = left.value == right.value;
  7776:     if (!result && left_type && right_type && left_type->kind == right_type->kind)
  7777:     {
  7778:         result = left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER && left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT && left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN;
  7779:         result = result || (left_type->bit_width == right_type->bit_width && left_type->is_signed == right_type->is_signed &&
  7780:                             (left_type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT || left_type->float_format == right_type->float_format));
  7781:     }
  7782: 
  7783:     return result;
  7784: }

  8739: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_integer_literal_fits(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CTypeKind kind, u64 value)
  8740: {
  8741:     u64 limit = builder->literal_limits[kind];
  8742:     if (limit)
  8743:     {
  8744:         return value <= limit;
  8745:     }
  8746:     IrTypeId type = builder->scalar_types[kind];
  8747:     IrType* integer = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
  8748:     bool result;
  8749:     if (!integer || integer->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
  8750:     {
  8751:         result = false;
  8752:     }
  8753:     else if (integer->bit_width >= 64)
  8754:     {
  8755:         result = !integer->is_signed || value <= INT64_MAX;
  8756:     }
  8757:     else if (!integer->is_signed)
  8758:     {
  8759:         result = value <= (((u64)1 << integer->bit_width) - 1);
  8760:     }
  8761:     else
  8762:     {
  8763:         result = value <= (((u64)1 << (integer->bit_width - 1)) - 1);
  8764:     }
  8765: 
  8766:     return result;
  8767: }

  8912: // The imaginary suffix of a floating literal. C's suffixes are `f`/`l` and
  8913: // GNU adds `i`/`j` for an imaginary constant, in either order and either
  8914: // case, so the run of trailing letters is scanned rather than just the last
  8915: // one. Reports the spelling with the imaginary letter removed, which is an
  8916: // ordinary real literal the parser below already understands; `arena` is only
  8917: // touched when that letter is not the last one.
  8918: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_number_imaginary_spelling(Arena* arena, String8 spelling, String8* real_out)
  8919: {
  8920:     u64 suffix_start = spelling.length;
  8921:     u64 imaginary_index = spelling.length;
  8922:     while (suffix_start)
  8923:     {
  8924:         u8 byte = (u8)spelling.pointer[suffix_start - 1];
  8925:         if (byte == 'i' || byte == 'I' || byte == 'j' || byte == 'J')
  8926:         {
  8927:             // Two imaginary letters is not a literal any compiler accepts;
  8928:             // leave it alone and let the real parser refuse the spelling.
  8929:             if (imaginary_index != spelling.length)
  8930:             {
  8931:                 return false;
  8932:             }
  8933:             imaginary_index = suffix_start - 1;
  8934:         }
  8935:         else if (byte != 'f' && byte != 'F' && byte != 'l' && byte != 'L')
  8936:         {
  8937:             break;
  8938:         }
  8939:         suffix_start -= 1;
  8940:     }
  8941:     if (imaginary_index == spelling.length || !suffix_start)
  8942:     {
  8943:         return false;
  8944:     }
  8945:     if (imaginary_index == spelling.length - 1)
  8946:     {
  8947:         *real_out = (String8){.pointer = spelling.pointer, .length = spelling.length - 1};
  8948:         return true;
  8949:     }
  8950:     char8* copy = arena_allocate(arena, char8, spelling.length - 1);
  8951:     memcpy(copy, spelling.pointer, imaginary_index);
  8952:     memcpy(copy + imaginary_index, spelling.pointer + imaginary_index + 1, spelling.length - imaginary_index - 1);
  8953:     *real_out = (String8){.pointer = copy, .length = spelling.length - 1};
  8954:     return true;
  8955: }
  8956: 
  8957: // The suffix of a floating constant: how many trailing bytes it occupies and
  8958: // which type it names, reported as one code. C's suffixes are `f`/`F` for
  8959: // float and `l`/`L` for long double, and C23 adds `f16`/`F16` for `_Float16`
  8960: // -- the only one longer than a letter, so reading the last byte alone cannot
  8961: // recognize it. The half suffix reports as 'h', a letter C does not use as a
  8962: // suffix, so a caller comparing against 'f' or 'l' cannot confuse the two.
  8963: // Every spelling-to-value path shares this so that the type a literal is
  8964: // given and the digits that are parsed for it cannot disagree.
  8965: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL u32 c_ir_float_suffix(String8 spelling, char8* code_out)
  8966: {
  8967:     // In a hexadecimal spelling `f` and `F` are digits, and only a `p`
  8968:     // exponent makes such a spelling a floating constant at all: `0x2f16` is
  8969:     // the integer 12054 and `0x2f` the integer 47, where `0x1p4f` really does
  8970:     // carry the float suffix. Asking for the exponent is what keeps a
  8971:     // float-typed initializer written with a hexadecimal integer from losing
  8972:     // its last digits to a suffix that is not there.
  8973:     bool hexadecimal = spelling.length >= 2 && spelling.pointer[0] == '0' && (spelling.pointer[1] == 'x' || spelling.pointer[1] == 'X');
  8974:     bool suffixable = !hexadecimal;
  8975:     for (u64 index = 2; !suffixable && index < spelling.length; index += 1)
  8976:     {
  8977:         suffixable = spelling.pointer[index] == 'p' || spelling.pointer[index] == 'P';
  8978:     }
  8979:     char8 code = 0;
  8980:     u32 length = 0;
  8981:     if (suffixable && spelling.length >= 3 && (spelling.pointer[spelling.length - 3] == 'f' || spelling.pointer[spelling.length - 3] == 'F') &&
  8982:         spelling.pointer[spelling.length - 2] == '1' && spelling.pointer[spelling.length - 1] == '6')
  8983:     {
  8984:         code = 'h';
  8985:         length = 3;
  8986:     }
  8987:     else if (suffixable && spelling.length)
  8988:     {
  8989:         char8 last = spelling.pointer[spelling.length - 1];
  8990:         if (last == 'f' || last == 'F' || last == 'l' || last == 'L')
  8991:         {
  8992:             code = last;
  8993:             length = 1;
  8994:         }
  8995:     }
  8996:     *code_out = code;
  8997: 
  8998:     return length;
  8999: }

 10403: // One operand in the common real type the usual arithmetic conversions pick.
 10404: // Only an integer operand can lose anything here -- a float widens into a
 10405: // double exactly and every encoded value is already exact in the x87 format --

 10426: // The IEEE special cases, which answer before the rational core sees anything.
 10427: // The invalid combinations among them -- inf minus inf, inf times zero, inf
 10428: // over inf, zero over zero -- have to give the same answer as
 10429: // c_ir_fold_float_invalid_operation gives an in-function constant, because
 10430: // the sign IEEE-754 leaves unspecified is a compatibility choice and the two
 10431: // paths would otherwise print `nan` and `-nan` for one spelling.  They also
 10432: // do not care where the operation would round: the NaN is the same value at
 10433: // every precision and widens exactly.
 10434: //
 10435: // A NaN operand wins outright and keeps its own sign, the left one first; the
 10436: // sign flip a subtraction applies to its right operand happens only after
 10437: // that, which is why `1.0L - -nan` is still negative.  Everything else is the
 10438: // ordinary infinity and division-by-zero algebra, with the invalid
 10439: // combinations -- inf minus inf, inf times zero, inf over inf, zero over zero
 10440: // -- becoming the default NaN.  A finite operation returns false and the
 10441: // caller folds it as a rational instead.

 10623: // The usual arithmetic conversions decide where an operation rounds: both

 10648: // One numeric token as the long double value it converts to.  The three cases
 10649: // are the literal's own type: an L-suffixed spelling is already this format, a

 10651: // exactly, and an integer spelling converts from its own integer type, where a
 10652: // leading minus on an unsigned literal wraps before the widening.

 12051: // What a string-literal token range shares across its fragments: the
 12052: // encoding its prefixes agree on and the element width and kind that
 12053: // encoding means for `target`. `start` and `end` come back trimmed of the
 12054: // redundant parentheses the decoders accept (c_ir_string_literal_range_trim),
 12055: // and `shape_out` carries only those three fields. Both range entry points
 12056: // below open with this and differ only in what they do with the fragments.
 12057: // Inlined by force: left to the host compiler's judgement it stayed out of
 12058: // line with two callers, and the call layer -- a 128-byte CPreprocessResult
 12059: // and the trimmed bounds travelling through it -- cost about 60 instructions
 12060: // per literal on the stage-1 corpus, where most literals are a few bytes.
 12061: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL BUSTER_INLINE bool c_ir_string_literal_range_shape(CPreprocessResult const* preprocess, Target target, u32* start, u32* end,
 12062:                                                         CIrDecodedString* shape_out)
 12063: {

 12065:     bool result = c_ir_tokens_are_string_literals(*preprocess, *start, *end);
 12066:     CIrStringEncoding encoding = C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_ORDINARY;
 12067:     bool has_encoding = false;
 12068:     for (u32 index = *start; result && index < *end; index += 1)
 12069:     {
 12070:         CIrStringEncoding fragment_encoding = C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_ORDINARY;
 12071:         result = c_ir_string_encoding(c_token_spelling(preprocess->spelling_base, preprocess->tokens[index]), &fragment_encoding);
 12072:         if (result && fragment_encoding != C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_ORDINARY)
 12073:         {
 12074:             result = !has_encoding || fragment_encoding == encoding;
 12075:             encoding = fragment_encoding;
 12076:             has_encoding = true;
 12077:         }
 12078:     }
 12079:     u32 width = 1;
 12080:     CTypeKind element_kind = C_TYPE_CHAR;
 12081:     if (encoding == C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_UTF8)
 12082:     {
 12083:         element_kind = preprocess->dialect == C_PREPROCESS_DIALECT_GNU23 || preprocess->dialect == C_PREPROCESS_DIALECT_C23 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR : C_TYPE_CHAR;
 12084:     }
 12085:     else if (encoding == C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_UTF16)
 12086:     {
 12087:         width = 2;
 12088:         element_kind = C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT;
 12089:     }
 12090:     else if (encoding == C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_UTF32)
 12091:     {
 12092:         width = 4;
 12093:         element_kind = C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT;
 12094:     }
 12095:     else if (encoding == C_IR_STRING_ENCODING_WIDE)
 12096:     {
 12097:         bool short_wchar = target_uses_16_bit_wchar(target);
 12098:         width = short_wchar ? 2 : 4;
 12099:         element_kind = short_wchar ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT :
 12100:                        target_uses_unsigned_wchar(target) ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : C_TYPE_INT;
 12101:     }
 12102:     *shape_out = (CIrDecodedString){
 12103:         .element_width = width,
 12104:         .element_kind = element_kind,
 12105:         .encoding = encoding,
 12106:     };
 12107:     return result;
 12108: }

 14610: // A call to abort-like entry points terminates an ordinary body, but GNU
 14611: // statement expressions still need to hand their value/control back to the
 14612: // enclosing expression walker.  Keep the context query local to lowering so
 14613: // the call emitter can avoid inserting an early unreachable terminator in
 14614: // those nested bodies (the body walker already knows how to close them).
 14615: /* Whether something enclosing the call being lowered resumes after it, which
 14616:    is what decides that a noreturn callee may not end its block. A GNU
 14617:    statement expression is resumed by the enclosing expression frame; every
 14618:    branching expression -- `? :`, `&&`, `||`, and a lowered branch condition --
 14619:    created a merge block its arm is expected to reach. Buster's own
 14620:    BUSTER_CHECK puts a noreturn call in a conditional operand, so this is not
 14621:    a hypothetical shape. */
 14622: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_lowering_resumes_after_call(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder)
 14623: {
 14624:     bool result = false;
 14625:     for (u32 index = 0; index < builder->lower_machine.frame_count && !result; index += 1)
 14626:     {
 14627:         CIrLowerFrame* frame = &builder->lower_machine.frames[index];
 14628:         switch (frame->kind)
 14629:         {
 14630:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_LOGICAL_VALUE:
 14631:             // Every expression is lowered through one of these, and it only
 14632:             // branches once it has found a root `&&`/`||`; the stage says
 14633:             // which, because the frame that merely forwards to the expression
 14634:             // core sets LOGICAL_CORE before pushing anything.
 14635:             result = frame->stage != (u8)C_IR_LOWER_STAGE_LOGICAL_CORE;
 14636:             break;
 14637:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_STATEMENT_EXPRESSION:
 14638:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_CONDITION:
 14639:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_CONDITION_LEAF:
 14640:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_CONDITIONAL_VALUE:
 14641:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_ARITHMETIC_CONDITIONAL_LEFT:
 14642:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_ARITHMETIC_CONDITIONAL_COMPLETION:
 14643:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_ARITHMETIC_CONDITIONAL_FALSE_COMPLETION:
 14644:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_SELECTION_EXPRESSION:
 14645:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_SELECTION_CONTINUE:
 14646:             result = true;
 14647:             break;
 14648:         case C_IR_LOWER_FRAME_BODY:
 14649:             result = frame->as.body.state && frame->as.body.state->statement_expression_mode;
 14650:             break;
 14651:         default:
 14652:             break;
 14653:         }
 14654:     }
 14655: 
 14656:     return result;
 14657: }

 14662:    type.  GNU statement expressions and branching operands are the exception,
 14663:    because their nested body is resumed by the enclosing expression frame,

 15330: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_signbit_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, IrValueId value)
 15331: {
 15332:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15333:     IrTypeId value_type = value.value < builder->function->value_count ? builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
 15334:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, value_type);
 15335:     if (type && type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT && (type->bit_width == 32 || type->bit_width == 64 || type->bit_width == 80 || type->bit_width == 128))
 15336:     {

 15338:         u32 width = type->bit_width;
 15339:         CTypeKind bits_kind = width == 32 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : width == 80 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT : C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG;
 15340:         IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, bits_kind);
 15341:         IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, value_type, source);
 15342:         if (bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && slot.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
 15343:             c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, value_type, value, source))
 15344:         {
 15345:             IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
 15346:             IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, value_type, source);
 15347:             IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
 15348:                                          ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15349:             IrValueId bits_place = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15350:             if (bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 15351:             {
 15352:                 // The supported formats are little-endian. The wide sign field
 15353:                 // starts at byte eight: the x87 sign/exponent or binary128 high limb.
 15354:                 if (width > 64)
 15355:                 {
 15356:                     IrValueId index = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width == 80 ? 4u : 1u, false, token, builder->s32_type);
 15357:                     if (index.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 15358:                     {
 15359:                         bits_place = c_ir_emit_index_place(builder, bits_address, index, source);
 15360:                     }
 15361:                 }
 15362:                 else
 15363:                 {
 15364:                     bits_place = c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source);
 15365:                 }
 15366:             }
 15367:             IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15368:             IrValueId shift = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width == 32 ? 31u : width == 80 ? 15u : 63u, false, token, bits_type);
 15369:             if (bits.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && shift.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 15370:             {
 15371:                 IrValueId sign = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, shift, bits_type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
 15372:                 if (sign.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 15373:                 {
 15374:                     result = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, sign, builder->s32_type, source);
 15375:                 }
 15376:             }
 15377:         }
 15378:     }
 15379:     return result;
 15380: }

 15617: // Which arithmetic each operator gets is Clang's, checked against
 15618: // `clang -O0 -S -emit-llvm` for every combination rather than derived:
 15619: //   * `+` and `-` are componentwise, and a real operand touches only the real
 15620: //     half (the imaginary half of the promoted real operand is a positive
 15621: //     zero, and Clang carries the other operand's imaginary part through
 15622: //     unchanged rather than adding it).
 15623: //   * `*` and `/` with a real operand scale or divide both halves.
 15624: //   * `*` and `/` with two complex operands call the compiler runtime --
 15625: //     __mulsc3/__muldc3/__multc3 and __divsc3/__divdc3/__divtc3 -- which is
 15626: //     what Clang emits without -ffast-math or -fcx-limited-range. Those
 15627: //     helpers implement the overflow- and NaN-recovering forms from C11
 15628: //     Annex G, and calling them rather than inlining Smith's algorithm is the
 15629: //     choice made here: it is bit-for-bit what a Clang-built object does, and
 15630: //     the alternative would be a second, subtly different implementation of
 15631: //     the same numerics living in this file.
 15632: //   * `real / complex` also goes to the runtime, with the numerator's
 15633: //     imaginary part passed as a positive zero, again matching Clang.
 15634: //   * `==` and `!=` compare both halves.
 15635: //
 15636: // System V x86-64 returns a `long double _Complex` in ST(0)/ST(1) (the psABI's
 15637: // COMPLEX_X87 class) where the equivalent struct is returned in memory. That
 15638: // is the one place the aggregate model is not the ABI, and it is the only
 15639: // thing the backends had to learn about complex: the classifier gives that
 15640: // result four X87/X87_UP eightbyte parts, the canonical x86-64 emitter pushes
 15641: // the imaginary half and then the real one before its RET and pops them in
 15642: // that order after a call, and every other position -- the argument, the
 15643: // loads, the stores, the copies -- is the two-field aggregate unchanged.

 15941: // signbit builtin uses, because there is no absolute-value opcode and calling
 15942: // libm would make complex division depend on a library.
 15943: //
 15944: // The 80-bit x87 spelling has no integer of its own width, so it is punned
 15945: // one halfword at a time: the sign bit is bit 15 of the sixteen-bit
 15946: // sign/exponent field at byte eight, which is exactly the `se` member of
 15947: // musl's `union ldshape`, and the ten-byte significand below it is left
 15948: // alone.
 15949: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_float_magnitude(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId type_id, IrSourceRange source)
 15950: {
 15951:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
 15952:     if (!type || type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT || (type->bit_width != 32 && type->bit_width != 64 && type->bit_width != 80))
 15953:     {
 15954:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15955:     }
 15956:     u32 bit_width = type->bit_width;
 15957:     CTypeKind bits_kind = bit_width == 32 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : bit_width == 64 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG : C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT;
 15958:     IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, bits_kind);
 15959:     IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, type_id, source);
 15960:     if (bits_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || slot.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ||
 15961:         !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, type_id, value, source))
 15962:     {
 15963:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15964:     }
 15965:     IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
 15966:     IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
 15967:     IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
 15968:                                  ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source)
 15969:                                  : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15970:     IrValueId bits_place = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15971:     if (bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 15972:     {
 15973:         if (bit_width == 80)
 15974:         {
 15975:             // The fifth halfword of the sixteen-byte slot: byte eight, where
 15976:             // the x87 format keeps the sign and the exponent.
 15977:             IrValueId halfword_index = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, (CToken){0}, builder->s32_type);
 15978:             bits_place = halfword_index.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_index_place(builder, bits_address, halfword_index, source)
 15979:                                                                          : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15980:         }
 15981:         else
 15982:         {
 15983:             bits_place = c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source);
 15984:         }
 15985:     }
 15986:     IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15987:     IrValueId mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder,
 15988:                                                    bit_width == 32   ? UINT64_C(0x7fffffff)
 15989:                                                    : bit_width == 64 ? UINT64_C(0x7fffffffffffffff)
 15990:                                                                      : UINT64_C(0x7fff),
 15991:                                                    false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
 15992:     if (bits.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || mask.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 15993:     {
 15994:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 15995:     }
 15996:     IrValueId cleared = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, mask, bits_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
 15997:     if (cleared.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, bits_place, bits_type, cleared, source))
 15998:     {
 15999:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 16000:     }
 16001:     return c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
 16002: }

 18155: // The one vector type the 512-bit vocabulary speaks in: 64 bytes of u8. Every
 18156: // builtin that returns a vector returns this, and `Simd512` in
 18157: // <buster/lib/simd.h> is declared to match, so no conversion ever appears at a
 18158: // call site. The layout matches what the `vector_size` attribute produces for
 18159: // the same spelling, so the two are the same IR type and not two that happen to
 18160: // agree.
 18161: // __builtin_popcount is one instruction where the target has POPCNT and the
 18162: // classic SWAR sequence where it does not, decided here rather than in the
 18163: // backends: an IR expansion is the same handful of ordinary instructions every
 18164: // backend already emits, and it keeps AArch64 from needing a NEON round trip
 18165: // for a scalar operation the compiler itself barely uses.
 18166: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_population_count(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, CToken token, IrSourceRange source)
 18167: {
 18168:     IrType* integer = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
 18169:     if (!integer || integer->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
 18170:     {
 18171:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18172:     }
 18173:     if (target_cpu_feature_has(builder->target, TARGET_CPU_FEATURE_X86_POPCNT))
 18174:     {
 18175:         IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);
 18176:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_UNARY, type);
 18177:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
 18178:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
 18179:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
 18180:         instruction.unary_operation = IR_UNARY_INTEGER_POPULATION_COUNT;
 18181:         instruction.result = result;
 18182:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
 18183:         return result;
 18184:     }
 18185:     // The classic SWAR sequence: subtract the odd bits to make two-bit sums,
 18186:     // add the pairs into four-bit sums, fold to bytes, then let one multiply
 18187:     // gather every byte sum into the top byte.
 18188:     u32 width = integer->bit_width;
 18189:     u64 mask = width >= 64 ? UINT64_MAX : (((u64)1 << width) - 1);
 18190:     IrValueId one = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 1, false, token, type);
 18191:     IrValueId odd_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x5555555555555555) & mask, false, token, type);
 18192:     IrValueId shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, one, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
 18193:     IrValueId high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, odd_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);

 18212: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_simd_vector_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder)
 18213: {
 18214:     IrTypeId element = builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR];

 18216:     if (!element_type || element_type->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER || element_type->bit_width != 8)
 18217:     {
 18218:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
 18219:     }
 18220:     for (u32 type_index = 0; type_index < builder->program->types.count; type_index += 1)
 18221:     {
 18222:         IrType* candidate = builder->program->types.types + type_index;
 18223:         if (candidate->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR && candidate->element_type.value == element.value && candidate->element_count == 64 &&
 18224:             candidate->layout.size == 64)
 18225:         {
 18226:             return candidate->id;
 18227:         }
 18228:     }
 18229:     return ir_program_add_type(builder->program, (IrType){
 18230:                                                      .name = S8("GNU vector"),
 18231:                                                      .element_type = element,
 18232:                                                      .return_type = IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
 18233:                                                      .layout =
 18234:                                                          {
 18235:                                                              .size = 64,
 18236:                                                              .alignment = 64,
 18237:                                                              .resolved = true,
 18238:                                                          },
 18239:                                                      .kind = IR_TYPE_VECTOR,
 18240:                                                      .element_count = 64,
 18241:                                                      .bit_width = 512,
 18242:                                                  });
 18243: }

 18370: // Aggregate exchanges compare the promoted object's representation. Keep the
 18371: // atomic instruction integer-typed: two pointer views name the same object,
 18372: // and private scalar storage carries values between the record and its bits.
 18373: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_atomic_aggregate_bits_place(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId object_type,
 18374:                                                             IrTypeId bits_type, IrSourceRange source)
 18375: {
 18376:     IrType* object = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, object_type);
 18377:     IrType* bits = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, bits_type);
 18378:     // GNU's generic forms name an ordinary object, while C11 aggregate
 18379:     // exchange/CAS name an atomic-qualified one. In both cases the integer
 18380:     // view must cover exactly the storage the caller supplied.
 18381:     bool valid = object && bits && object->layout.resolved && bits->layout.resolved &&
 18382:                  object->layout.size == bits->layout.size && bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
 18383:     IrTypeId atomic_bits = valid ? c_ir_add_qualified_type(builder->program, bits_type, true, object->is_volatile) : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
 18384:     IrTypeId pointer_type = valid ? c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, atomic_bits) : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
 18385:     IrValueId address = valid ? c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, place, object_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18386:     IrValueId cast = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18387:     IrValueId result = cast.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, cast, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18388:     return result;
 18389: }
 18390: 
 18391: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_atomic_aggregate_bits_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId record_type,
 18392:                                                             IrTypeId bits_type, bool to_bits, IrSourceRange source)
 18393: {
 18394:     IrType* record = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, record_type);
 18395:     IrType* bits = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, bits_type);
 18396:     bool valid = record && bits && record->layout.resolved && bits->layout.resolved && record->layout.size <= bits->layout.size &&
 18397:                  value.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
 18398:     IrValueId slot = valid ? c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18399:     IrTypeId pointer_type = valid ? c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, record_type) : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
 18400:     IrValueId address = valid ? c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18401:     IrValueId cast = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18402:     IrValueId record_place = cast.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, cast, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18403:     valid = valid && record_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
 18404:     if (valid && to_bits)
 18405:     {
 18406:         // A three-byte record uses a four-byte atomic object. Initialize the
 18407:         // promoted tail before writing the record, matching aggregate stores.
 18408:         IrValueId zero = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
 18409:         valid = zero.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, bits_type, zero, source) &&
 18410:                 c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, record_place, record_type, value, source);
 18411:     }
 18412:     else if (valid)
 18413:     {
 18414:         valid = c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, bits_type, value, source);
 18415:     }
 18416:     IrValueId result = valid ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, to_bits ? slot : record_place, to_bits ? bits_type : record_type, source)
 18417:                             : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 18418:     return result;
 18419: }

 23757: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_increment(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId type, IrValueId previous, CToken token, bool prefix)
 23758: {
 23759:     IrValueId one = c_ir_emit_integer_value(builder, 1, false, token);
 23760:     IrType* place_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
 23761:     if (place_type && place_type->is_atomic)
 23762:     {
 23763:         IrValueId atomic_previous = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 23764:         IrValueId atomic_result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 23765:         if (!c_ir_emit_compound_assignment(builder, place, type,
 23766:                                            c_token_is_punctuator(&token, C_PUNCTUATOR_PLUS_PLUS) ? C_CONDITIONAL_ADD : C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT, one,
 23767:                                            c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token), &atomic_previous, &atomic_result))
 23768:         {
 23769:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 23770:         }
 23771:         return prefix ? atomic_result : atomic_previous;
 23772:     }
 23773:     IrValueId values[2] = {
 23774:         previous,
 23775:         one,
 23776:     };
 23777:     u32 value_count = 2;
 23778:     IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
 23779:     if (!c_ir_apply_operation(builder, c_token_is_punctuator(&token, C_PUNCTUATOR_PLUS_PLUS) ? C_CONDITIONAL_ADD : C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT, values, &value_count,
 23780:                               source, IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID) ||
 23781:         value_count != 1 || !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, place, type, values[0], source))
 23782:     {
 23783:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 23784:     }
 23785:     if (prefix && values[0].value < builder->function->value_count && builder->function->values[values[0].value].canonical_type.value != type.value)
 23786:     {
 23787:         // `++E` has the value E holds after the store, which is the value in
 23788:         // E's own type: the addition ran in the promoted type, so a narrower
 23789:         // object's result has to come back down before anything reads it.
 23790:         // SQLite carries its page-header cell count into the high byte with
 23791:         // `if( (++data[hdr+4])==0 ) data[hdr+3]++;`, and that carry is lost
 23792:         // when the comparison sees 256 instead of 0.
 23793:         values[0] = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[0], type, source);
 23794:     }
 23795:     return prefix ? c_ir_bit_field_assignment_value(builder, place, values[0], source) : c_ir_vla_pointer_rvalue(builder, previous, source);
 23796: }

 23804: // Aggregate operands are captured values, while volatile qualifiers belong to
 23805: // their destination places. If a conversion retained the unqualified value,
 23806: // initialize explicit storage through the ordinary qualified STORE contract.
 23807: // Keep exact constructor typing and evaluate each initializer only once.
 23808: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_initializer_capture(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId type_id, IrValueId* operands,
 23809:                                                         u64* fields, u32 count, IrSourceRange source)
 23810: {
 23811:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
 23812:     bool array = type->kind == IR_TYPE_ARRAY || type->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR;
 23813:     bool storage = false;
 23814:     for (u32 index = 0; index < count && !storage; index += 1)
 23815:     {
 23816:         IrTypeId field_type = array ? type->element_type : type->fields[fields[index]].type;
 23817:         IrTypeId operand_type = builder->function->values[operands[index].value].canonical_type;
 23818:         storage = operand_type.value != field_type.value &&
 23819:                   ir_types_differ_only_in_volatile(&builder->program->types, operand_type, field_type);
 23820:     }
 23821:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 23822:     if (storage)
 23823:     {
 23824:         IrValueId place = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, type_id, source);
 23825:         bool valid = place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
 23826:         for (u32 index = 0; index < count && valid; index += 1)
 23827:         {
 23828:             IrValueId field;
 23829:             if (array)
 23830:             {
 23831:                 IrValueId offset = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, index, false, (CToken){0}, builder->size_type);
 23832:                 field = offset.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_index_place(builder, place, offset, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
 23833:             }
 23834:             else
 23835:             {
 23836:                 field = c_ir_emit_field_index_place(builder, place, (u32)fields[index], source);
 23837:             }
 23838:             IrTypeId field_type = array ? type->element_type : type->fields[fields[index]].type;
 23839:             valid = field.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, field, field_type, operands[index], source);
 23840:         }
 23841:         if (valid)
 23842:         {
 23843:             result = c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, place, type_id, source);
 23844:         }
 23845:     }
 23846:     else
 23847:     {
 23848:         result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type_id);
 23849:         if (result.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
 23850:         {
 23851:             IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(array ? IR_OPCODE_ARRAY : IR_OPCODE_AGGREGATE, type_id);
 23852:             instruction.operands = operands;
 23853:             instruction.operand_count = count;
 23854:             instruction.immediates = fields;
 23855:             instruction.immediate_count = array ? 0 : (u16)count;
 23856:             instruction.result = result;
 23857:             IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
 23858:             builder->function->values[result.value].definition = id;
 23859:         }
 23860:     }
 23861:     return result;
 23862: }

 23866: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_zero_storage_compatible(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId root)
 23867: {
 23868:     IrType* root_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, root);
 23869:     bool compatible = root_type && root_type->layout.resolved && root_type->layout.size >= C_IR_BOUNDED_ZERO_STORAGE_MIN_BYTES &&
 23870:                       (root_type->kind == IR_TYPE_ARRAY || root_type->kind == IR_TYPE_STRUCT || root_type->kind == IR_TYPE_UNION);
 23871:     if (compatible)
 23872:     {
 23873:         u32 capacity = builder->program->types.count;
 23874:         IrTypeId* pending = arena_allocate(builder->temporary_arena, IrTypeId, capacity);
 23875:         u8* seen = arena_allocate(builder->temporary_arena, u8, capacity);
 23876:         memset(seen, 0, capacity);
 23877:         u32 count = 1;
 23878:         pending[0] = root;
 23879:         seen[root.value] = 1;
 23880:         for (u32 index = 0; compatible && index < count; index += 1)
 23881:         {
 23882:             IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, pending[index]);
 23883:             compatible = type && type->layout.resolved && !type->is_atomic && !type->is_volatile;
 23884:             if (compatible)
 23885:             {
 23886:                 bool array = type->kind == IR_TYPE_ARRAY || type->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR;
 23887:                 bool record = type->kind == IR_TYPE_STRUCT || type->kind == IR_TYPE_UNION;
 23888:                 compatible = array || record || type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER || type->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN ||
 23889:                              type->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER || type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT;
 23890:                 u32 children = array ? 1 : record ? type->field_count : 0;
 23891:                 for (u32 child = 0; compatible && child < children; child += 1)
 23892:                 {
 23893:                     IrTypeId id = array ? type->element_type : type->fields[child].type;
 23894:                     compatible = id.value < capacity;
 23895:                     if (compatible && !seen[id.value])
 23896:                     {
 23897:                         seen[id.value] = 1;
 23898:                         pending[count++] = id;
 23899:                     }
 23900:                 }
 23901:             }
 23902:         }
 23903:     }
 23904:     return compatible;
 23905: }
