   288: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool link_x86_emit(LinkX86InstructionBuilder* builder, String8 mnemonic,
   289:                                        BusterX86MetadataPhysicalOperand const* operands, u32 operand_count)
   290: {
   291:     if (!builder || builder->count > builder->capacity || (operand_count && !operands) || operand_count > 16) return false;
   292:     BusterX86MetadataEmitResult result = buster_x86_metadata_encode((BusterX86MetadataEncodeQuery){
   293:         .physical = {
   294:             .mnemonic = mnemonic,
   295:             .operands = operands,
   296:             .operand_count = operand_count,
   297:             .features = {.names = 0, .count = 0},
   298:             .address_size = 64,
   299:             .execution_mode = BUSTER_X86_METADATA_EXECUTION_MODE_64,
   300:             .include_privileged = true,
   301:             .include_not64 = false,
   302:             .include_implicit = false,
   303:             .source_semantics = false,
   304:         },
   305:         .output = builder->bytes + builder->count,
   306:         .output_capacity = builder->capacity - builder->count,
   307:     });
   308:     if (result.status != BUSTER_X86_METADATA_ENCODE_SUCCESS || result.byte_count > builder->capacity - builder->count)
   309:         return false;
   310:     builder->count += result.byte_count;
   311:     return true;
   312: }

   319: // ELF PLT entries reserve a five-byte PUSH for the import index.  The generic
   320: // physical selector intentionally shortens numeric immediates when they fit
   321: // (for example, PUSH 0 -> 6a 00), which is correct for ordinary instructions
   322: // but changes the fixed 16-byte PLT entry layout.  Enumerate the PUSH metadata
   323: // candidates locally and exact-emit the candidate whose schema carries an
   324: // imm32 field; no form ID or raw instruction bytes are part of this adapter.
   325: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL bool link_x86_emit_push_imm32(LinkX86InstructionBuilder* builder,
   326:                                                   BusterX86MetadataPhysicalOperand const* immediate)
   327: {
   328:     if (builder && builder->count <= builder->capacity && immediate && immediate->kind == BUSTER_X86_METADATA_PHYSICAL_OPERAND_IMMEDIATE &&
   329:         immediate->width == 32 && builder->capacity - builder->count >= 5)
   330:     {
   331:         BusterX86MetadataPhysicalQuery physical = {
   332:             .mnemonic = S8("PUSH"),
   333:             .operands = immediate,
   334:             .operand_count = 1,
   335:             .features = {.names = 0, .count = 0},
   336:             .address_size = 64,
   337:             .execution_mode = BUSTER_X86_METADATA_EXECUTION_MODE_64,
   338:             .include_privileged = true,
   339:             .include_not64 = false,
   340:             .include_implicit = false,
   341:             .source_semantics = false,
   342:         };
   343:         BusterX86MetadataCandidateRange candidates = buster_x86_metadata_lookup_mnemonic(S8("PUSH"));
   344:         BusterX86MetadataCandidateIterator iterator = buster_x86_metadata_filter(candidates, (BusterX86MetadataFilter){
   345:                                                                                                   .require_64_bit = true,
   346:                                                                                                   .exclude_not64 = true,
   347:                                                                                               });
   348:         u32 form_id = UINT32_MAX;
   349:         while (buster_x86_metadata_candidate_next(&iterator, &form_id))
   350:         {
   351:             BusterX86MetadataForm form = {0};
   352:             if (!buster_x86_metadata_form(form_id, &form) || form.immediate_width != 4) continue;
   353:             bool has_imm32_operand = false;
   354:             for (u32 operand_index = 0; operand_index < form.operand_count; operand_index += 1)
   355:             {
   356:                 BusterX86MetadataOperand operand = {0};
   357:                 if (!buster_x86_metadata_operand(form_id, operand_index, &operand))
   358:                 {
   359:                     has_imm32_operand = false;
   360:                     break;
   361:                 }
   362:                 if (operand.kind == BUSTER_X86_METADATA_OPERAND_IMMEDIATE &&
   363:                     (operand.physical_width_flags & BUSTER_X86_METADATA_PHYSICAL_WIDTH_32))
   364:                 {
   365:                     has_imm32_operand = true;
   366:                 }
   367:             }

  1003:             // The shared model cannot express Clang's f128 union merging.
  1004:             // Keep these signatures explicit until that rule is represented.
  1005:             valid &= !(quad && task.in_union);
  1006:         }
  1007:     }
  1008:     if (!valid || !occupied || occupied == 2)
  1009:     {
  1010:         llvm_bc_fail(context, LLVM_BITCODE_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE,
  1011:                      llvm_bc_s8("unsupported LLVM SysV aggregate register layout"), 0, 0, 0, IR_SYMBOL_ID_INVALID);
  1012:     }
  1013:     else if (occupied == 1)
  1014:     {
  1015:         // NO_CLASS tail padding consumes no register. Keep canonical storage
  1016:         // size for coercion temporaries, but omit its synthetic INTEGER part.
  1017:         abi->part_count = 1;
  1018:     }
  1019:     else if (upper_register && !independent_upper && abi->part_count == 2 &&
  1020:              abi->parts[0].abi_class == IR_ABI_CLASS_FLOAT && abi->parts[1].abi_class == IR_ABI_CLASS_FLOAT)
  1021:     {
  1022:         // SSEUP uses the upper half of the first XMM register. A floating
  1023:         // field in the upper eightbyte would instead require a second XMM.
  1024:         abi->part_count = 1;
  1025:         abi->parts[0] = (IrAbiPart){.abi_class = IR_ABI_CLASS_VECTOR, .size = 16};
  1026:     }
  1027:     scratch_end(temporary);
  1028: }

  2248: {
  2249:     if (!instruction->operand_count)
  2250:     {
  2251:         wasm64_fail(emitter->context, WASM64_ERROR_IR_VALIDATION, wasm64_s8("Wasm64 call has no callee"), emitter->function, 0, instruction,
  2252:                     instruction->symbol);
  2253:         return;
  2254:     }
  2255:     IrValue* callee_value = emitter->function->values + instruction->operands[0].value;
  2256:     IrType* callee_type = wasm64_type(emitter->context, callee_value->canonical_type);
  2257:     bool indirect = callee_type && callee_type->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER;
  2258:     if (indirect)
  2259:     {
  2260:         wasm64_fail(emitter->context, WASM64_ERROR_INDIRECT_CALL, wasm64_s8("indirect calls are unsupported by Wasm64"), emitter->function, 0,
  2261:                     instruction, instruction->symbol);
  2262:         return;
  2263:     }
  2264:     Wasm64FunctionRecord* record = wasm64_function_record_for_symbol(emitter->context, instruction->symbol);
  2265:     if (!record)
  2266:     {
  2267:         wasm64_fail(emitter->context, WASM64_ERROR_UNRESOLVED_SYMBOL, wasm64_s8("unresolved direct Wasm64 call"), emitter->function, 0, instruction,
  2268:                     instruction->symbol);
  2269:         return;
  2270:     }
  2271:     // Wasm types every call by the callee's own declared signature, so a call
  2272:     // that carries a signature of its own cannot be encoded: that is what a
  2273:     // pre-C23 `()` declaration produces, since it names no parameters and each
  2274:     // call site supplies them (see IrType.is_unprototyped).
  2275:     if (instruction->operand_count - 1 != record->signature.param_count)
  2276:     {
  2277:         wasm64_fail(emitter->context, WASM64_ERROR_VARIADIC,
  2278:                     wasm64_s8("a call whose arguments the callee's declaration does not describe is unsupported by Wasm64"), emitter->function, 0,
  2279:                     instruction, instruction->symbol);
  2280:         return;
  2281:     }
  2282:     for (u32 argument_index = 1; argument_index < instruction->operand_count; argument_index += 1)
  2283:     {
  2284:         wasm64_fe_emit_value(emitter, instruction->operands[argument_index]);
  2285:     }

  2289:     {
  2290:         wasm64_fe_local_set(emitter, emitter->value_locals[instruction->result.value]);
  2291:     }
  2292: }

    18: // A Windows ARM64 va_list is a pointer into the homed x-register area
    19: // followed by the caller's stack arguments. Clang advances that pointer
    20: // linearly, but the ABI moves a multi-slot argument wholly to the stack
    21: // when it cannot fit in the remaining x registers. Preserve Clang's
    22: // native va_arg lowering for every load; only move the list pointer over
    23: // the unused tail of the register area at that discontinuity.

    31:     BUSTER_CHECK(BUSTER_IS_POWER_OF_TWO(alignment) && alignment <= 2 * sizeof(u64));

    34:     {

    45:         // starts on an even x-register, and an argument that does not fit in
    46:         // the remaining x-register slots moves wholly to the stack.

   457: 
   458: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL u64 string_format_u128_parts_divide(StringFormatU128Parts* value, u64 divisor)
   459: {
   460:     BUSTER_CHECK(divisor >= 2 && divisor <= 16);
   461: 
   462:     u64 remainder;
   463:     if (!value->high)
   464:     {
   465:         // A value that fits in the low half divides without the bit loop.
   466:         remainder = value->low % divisor;
   467:         value->low /= divisor;
   468:     }
   469:     else
   470:     {
   471:         StringFormatU128Parts quotient = {0};
   472:         remainder = 0;
   473: 
   474:         // Long division from the most significant bit keeps the implementation
   475:         // independent of a compiler-provided 128-bit integer type.
   476:         for (u64 bit_index = 128; bit_index != 0; bit_index -= 1)
   477:         {
   478:             u64 shift = bit_index - 1;
   479:             u64 bit = shift >= 64 ? (value->high >> (shift - 64)) & 1u : (value->low >> shift) & 1u;
   480:             remainder = remainder * 2 + bit;
   481: 
   482:             if (remainder >= divisor)
   483:             {
   484:                 remainder -= divisor;
   485:                 if (shift >= 64)
   486:                 {
   487:                     quotient.high |= (u64)1 << (shift - 64);
   488:                 }
   489:                 else
   490:                 {
   491:                     quotient.low |= (u64)1 << shift;
   492:                 }
   493:             }
   494:         }
   495: 
   496:         *value = quotient;
   497:     }
   498: 
   499:     return remainder;
   500: }

  8046:     // Stage-9 scheduling. Thirty-two independent products all combined at
  8047:     // the end hold every intermediate live to the combine in source order —
  8048:     // more than the x86-64 register file — and sinking each product to its
  8049:     // first use removes the excess. The pass must keep the block partition
  8050:     // and the SSA def-before-use order, its output must satisfy the
  8051:     // structural verifier, and on this shape the scheduled FAST placement
  8052:     // must model strictly cheaper — that modeled improvement is the
  8053:     // acceptance discipline's whole basis for keeping a schedule. The

 11591:     // The 128-bit binary subset both machine selectors carry (#811). The x86-64
 11592:     // one refused every operation in it -- add, subtract, the bitwise trio, two
 11593:     // of the three shift directions, the i128-typed constants and the ordered
 11594:     // comparisons -- while the AArch64 one selected them all, so the fixture is
 11595:     // built for both targets and run on both: natively here, and under
 11596:     // qemu-aarch64 where that is installed.
 11597:     //
 11598:     // The multiply came later, on the x86-64 side only, and it lives in a
 11599:     // function of its own in the fixture so the AArch64 lane can still pin
 11600:     // everything else at zero -- see the per-target expectation below.
 11601:     //
 11602:     // The fallback count is pinned because running alone proves nothing: the
 11603:     // canonical emitter answers identically, and a selector that stopped
 11604:     // firing would silently retire the coverage.
 11605:     String8 i128_binary_allocators[] = {
 11606:         S8("none"),
 11607:         S8("mir-stack"),
 11608:         S8("fast"),
 11609:         S8("quality"),

 11618:         {
 11619:             TemporalArena i128_binary_temporary = scratch_begin(&arguments->arena, 1);
 11620:             String8 i128_binary_path = buster_test_temporary_path(
 11621:                 i128_binary_temporary.arena, S8("buster-c-i128-binary"),
 11622:                 string_format(i128_binary_temporary.arena, S8("-{u32}-{S8}.elf"), target_index, i128_binary_allocators[allocator_index]));
 11623:             String8 i128_binary_command_line[] = {
 11624:                 S8("-target"),
 11625:                 i128_binary_targets[target_index],
 11626:                 string_format(i128_binary_temporary.arena, S8("-fregister-allocator={S8}"), i128_binary_allocators[allocator_index]),
 11627:                 S8("-o"),
 11628:                 i128_binary_path,

 11630:             };

 11634:             BUSTER_TEST(arguments, i128_binary.error == COMPILER_DRIVER_ERROR_NONE);

 11636:             bool native_x64 = target_index == 0 && BUSTER_LINUX && BUSTER_CPU_ARCH_X86_64;
 11637:             bool emulated_a64 = target_index == 1 && aarch64_i128_qemu_available;
 11638:             if (i128_binary.error == COMPILER_DRIVER_ERROR_NONE && (native_x64 || emulated_a64))
 11639:             {

 11645:                     os_process_spawn(run_arguments, (SliceString8){0}, (SliceString8){0}, (ProcessSpawnOptions){.use_process_environment = true});
 11646:                 BUSTER_TEST(arguments, i128_binary_run.handle != 0);
 11647:                 if (i128_binary_run.handle)
 11648:                 {
 11649:                     BUSTER_TEST(arguments, os_process_wait_sync(i128_binary_temporary.arena, i128_binary_run).result == PROCESS_RESULT_SUCCESS);
 11650:                 }
 11651:             }
 11652:             scratch_end(i128_binary_temporary);
 11653:         }

 11655:     // Two of the machine census's small-class tail (#813), which happen to be

 11728:     // The System V x86-64 side of the same stack boundary: a sixteen-aligned
 11729:     // argument's stack home is rounded up to a sixteen-aligned offset, and
 11730:     // the machine placement must count the same padding eightbytes the
 11731:     // canonical emitter and clang do — its callee used to read a stacked
 11732:     // __int128 one eightbyte early. The fixture's callees stay inside the
 11733:     // machine subset by forwarding their halves to the one checker that owns
 11734:     // the __int128 shifts, and the census pin below fails if lowering changes
 11735:     // ever push them to the canonical fallback, which would silently retire
 11736:     // this coverage. On an x86-64 Linux host each image also runs.

  2255: // [[noreturn]] is the one C23 attribute buster acts on, and the reason the

  9393: // The function type the first call in `name` takes its callee from: the type
  9394: // of the IR_OPCODE_FUNCTION reference for a direct call, and the pointee of
  9395: // the callee pointer for an indirect one.
  9396: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL IrType* c_test_first_call_callee_type(IrProgram* program, IrModule* module, String8 name)
  9397: {
  9398:     IrType* result = 0;
  9399:     for (u32 function_index = 0; function_index < module->function_count && !result; function_index += 1)
  9400:     {
  9401:         IrFunction* function = module->functions + function_index;
  9402:         if (!string_equal(function->name, name))
  9403:         {
  9404:             continue;
  9405:         }
  9406:         for (u32 instruction_index = 0; instruction_index < function->instruction_count && !result; instruction_index += 1)
  9407:         {
  9408:             IrInstruction* instruction = function->instructions + instruction_index;
  9409:             if (instruction->opcode != IR_OPCODE_CALL || !instruction->operand_count ||
  9410:                 instruction->operands[0].value >= function->value_count)
  9411:             {
  9412:                 continue;
  9413:             }
  9414:             IrType* callee = ir_type_from_id(&program->types, function->values[instruction->operands[0].value].canonical_type);
  9415:             result = callee && callee->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER ? ir_type_from_id(&program->types, callee->element_type) : callee;
  9416:         }
  9417:     }
  9418: 
  9419:     return result;
  9420: }

  9435: /* Before C23 a function declared `()` has no parameter list, so a call to it
  9436:    supplies one: the arguments take the default argument promotions and the
  9437:    call site -- not the declaration -- says where they go. The IR shows that
  9438:    directly, because the reference the call takes to the symbol carries the
  9439:    call's own signature (see IrType.is_unprototyped) with the `...` that makes
  9440:    a System V caller set the AL vector count for a callee that turns out to be
  9441:    variadic. These calls used to be refused outright as "could not prepare C
  9442:    calls" whenever no later prototype in the same unit happened to replace the
  9443:    declaration; that refusal now survives only where the callee really does
  9444:    have a parameter list to overrun, and says so. */

 18056: // A leaf query must not acquire storage proportional to unrelated types. Dirty
 18057: // high-water marks observe even allocations rewound before the query returns.
 18058: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL UnitTestResult c_test_constexpr_leaf_storage(UnitTestArguments* arguments)
 18059: {
 18060:     UnitTestResult result = {0};
 18061:     TemporalArena temporary = scratch_begin(0, 0);
 18062:     CPreprocessResult tokens = c_preprocess(temporary.arena,
 18063:         S8("constexpr int first = 7;\n"
 18064:            "constexpr double fraction = 1.5;\n"
 18065:            "constexpr int *nothing = nullptr;\n"
 18066:            "constexpr unsigned char octet = 23;\n"),
 18067:         (CPreprocessOptions){.dialect = C_PREPROCESS_DIALECT_C23, .source_path = S8("constexpr-leaf-storage.c")});
 18068:     CParseResult parse = c_parse(temporary.arena, tokens);
 18069:     BUSTER_TEST(arguments, tokens.diagnostic_count == 0);
 18070:     BUSTER_TEST(arguments, parse.diagnostic_count == 0);
 18071:     BUSTER_TEST(arguments, parse.declaration_count == 4);
 18072:     if (!parse.diagnostic_count && parse.declaration_count == 4)
 18073:     {
 18074:         u32 original_count = parse.type_count;
 18075:         u32 unrelated_counts[] = {0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 1024, 65536, 0};
 18076:         CType* types = arena_allocate_zeroed(temporary.arena, CType, original_count + 65536);
 18077:         memcpy(types, parse.types, sizeof(*types) * original_count);
 18078:         parse.types = types;
 18079:         parse.type_capacity = original_count + 65536;
 18080:         bool census = os_get_environment_variable(S8("BUSTER_CONSTEXPR_CENSUS")).length != 0;
 18081:         for (u32 count_index = 0; count_index < BUSTER_ARRAY_LENGTH(unrelated_counts); count_index += 1)
 18082:         {
 18083:             parse.type_count = original_count + unrelated_counts[count_index];
 18084:             for (u32 declaration_index = 0; declaration_index < parse.declaration_count; declaration_index += 1)
 18085:             {
 18086:                 TemporalArena probe = scratch_begin(&temporary.arena, 1);
 18087:                 // Move through the public allocator to the previous high-water
 18088:                 // mark, so a reused dirty arena cannot hide another allocation.
 18089:                 u64 dirty = arena_dirty_position(probe.arena);
 18090:                 if (dirty > probe.arena->position)
 18091:                 {
 18092:                     arena_allocate(probe.arena, u8, dirty - probe.arena->position);
 18093:                 }

 18096:                                                                       &parse.declarations[declaration_index]);
 18097:                 u64 growth = arena_dirty_position(probe.arena) - before;
 18098:                 if (census)
 18099:                 {
 18100:                     string_print(S8("CONSTEXPR_LEAF_CENSUS types={u32} declaration={u32} scratch_growth={u64}\n"),
 18101:                                  parse.type_count, declaration_index, growth);
 18102:                 }
 18103:                 BUSTER_TEST(arguments, valid);
 18104:                 BUSTER_TEST(arguments, parse.diagnostic_count == 0);
 18105:                 BUSTER_TEST(arguments, probe.arena->position == before);
 18106:                 BUSTER_TEST(arguments, growth == 0);
 18107:                 scratch_end(probe);
 18108:             }
 18109:         }
 18110:         parse.type_count = original_count;

     2: // i128 arithmetic. Keep this fixture strict on AArch64; Win64 x86-64 i128 ABI
     3: // exclusions are unrelated. The structural machine tests cover retry paths.

     5: typedef unsigned __int128 Wide;
     6: typedef __int128 SignedWide;
     7: typedef struct Pair Pair;
     8: struct Pair
     9: {
    10:     Limb low;
    11:     Limb high;
    12: };
    13: 
    14: static volatile Limb runtime_seed = 0x13579bdf2468ace0ULL;
    15: 
    16: static Wide pair_bits(Pair value)
    17: {
    18:     return (Wide)value.low | ((Wide)value.high << 64);
    19: }
    20: 
    21: static int pair_matches(Wide value, Pair expected)
    22: {
    23:     return (Limb)value == expected.low && (Limb)(value >> 64) == expected.high;
    24: }

    26: static void reference_update(Pair* value, Pair operand, int operation)
    27: {
    28:     Limb old_low = value->low;
    29:     switch (operation)
    30:     {
    31:         case 0:
    32:             value->low = old_low + operand.low;
    33:             value->high += operand.high + (value->low < old_low);
    34:             break;
    35:         case 1:
    36:             value->low = old_low - operand.low;
    37:             value->high -= operand.high + (old_low < operand.low);
    38:             break;
    39:         case 2:
    40:             value->low &= operand.low;
    41:             value->high &= operand.high;
    42:             break;
    43:         case 3:
    44:             value->low |= operand.low;
    45:             value->high |= operand.high;
    46:             break;
    47:         case 4:

===== tests/basic_c_aarch64_float_to_i128.c =====

     1: /* Finite, representable float-to-i128 conversions. The reference decodes
     2:    IEEE significands using integer operations; it performs no floating cast.
     3:    Both limbs of prefilled output storage must be replaced. */
     4: typedef unsigned long long U64;
     5: typedef unsigned int U32;
     6: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     7: typedef __int128 S128;
     8: 
     9: static void double_to_unsigned(double value, U128 *output)
    10: {
    11:     *output = (U128)value;
    12: }
    13: 
    14: static void double_to_signed(double value, S128 *output)
    15: {
    16:     *output = (S128)value;
    17: }
    18: 
    19: static void float_to_unsigned(float value, U128 *output)
    20: {
    21:     *output = (U128)value;
    22: }
    23: 
    24: static void float_to_signed(float value, S128 *output)
    25: {
    26:     *output = (S128)value;
    27: }
    28: 
    29: static void decoded_magnitude(U64 fraction, unsigned exponent, unsigned fraction_bits, unsigned bias, U128 *output)
    30: {
    31:     *output = 0;
    32:     if (exponent >= bias)
    33:     {
    34:         U128 significand = ((U128)1 << fraction_bits) | fraction;
    35:         unsigned integer_exponent = exponent - bias;
    36:         if (integer_exponent >= fraction_bits)
    37:         {
    38:             *output = significand << (integer_exponent - fraction_bits);
    39:         }
    40:         else
    41:         {
    42:             *output = significand >> (fraction_bits - integer_exponent);
    43:         }
    44:     }
    45: }
    46: 
    47: static int check_double(U64 bits)
    48: {
    49:     union { U64 bits; double value; } input = {bits};
    50:     unsigned exponent = (unsigned)(bits >> 52) & 2047;
    51:     U64 fraction = bits & 0x000fffffffffffffULL;
    52:     U128 magnitude;
    53:     decoded_magnitude(fraction, exponent, 52, 1023, &magnitude);
    54:     U128 sign_limit = (U128)1 << 127;
    55:     U128 unsigned_output = ~(U128)0;
    56:     S128 signed_output = -1;
    57:     int result = 0;
    58:     if (!(bits >> 63) || exponent < 1023)
    59:     {
    60:         double_to_unsigned(input.value, &unsigned_output);
    61:         if (unsigned_output != magnitude)
    62:         {
    63:             result = 1;
    64:         }
    65:     }
    66:     if (magnitude < sign_limit || ((bits >> 63) && magnitude == sign_limit))
    67:     {
    68:         U128 sign_mask = (U128)0 - (bits >> 63);
    69:         U128 expected = (magnitude ^ sign_mask) - sign_mask;
    70:         double_to_signed(input.value, &signed_output);
    71:         if ((U128)signed_output != expected)
    72:         {
    73:             result = 2;
    74:         }
    75:     }
    76:     return result;
    77: }
    78: 
    79: static int check_float(U32 bits)
    80: {
    81:     union { U32 bits; float value; } input = {bits};
    82:     unsigned exponent = (bits >> 23) & 255;
    83:     U32 fraction = bits & 0x007fffffU;
    84:     U128 magnitude;
    85:     decoded_magnitude(fraction, exponent, 23, 127, &magnitude);
    86:     U128 sign_limit = (U128)1 << 127;
    87:     U128 unsigned_output = ~(U128)0;
    88:     S128 signed_output = -1;
    89:     int result = 0;
    90:     if (!(bits >> 31) || exponent < 127)
    91:     {
    92:         float_to_unsigned(input.value, &unsigned_output);
    93:         if (unsigned_output != magnitude)
    94:         {
    95:             result = 3;
    96:         }
    97:     }
    98:     if (magnitude < sign_limit || ((bits >> 31) && magnitude == sign_limit))
    99:     {
   100:         U128 sign_mask = (U128)0 - (bits >> 31);
   101:         U128 expected = (magnitude ^ sign_mask) - sign_mask;
   102:         float_to_signed(input.value, &signed_output);
   103:         if ((U128)signed_output != expected)
   104:         {
   105:             result = 4;
   106:         }
   107:     }
   108:     return result;
   109: }
   110: 
   111: int main(void)
   112: {
   113:     /* All finite exponents below 2^128, including subnormals, signed zero,
   114:        fractions on either side of one, and both sides of every limb boundary.
   115:        Negative unsigned inputs are confined to (-1, 0], where truncation is
   116:        representable. Positive 2^127 and larger are only converted unsigned. */
   117:     U64 double_fractions[] = {0, 1, 0x0007ffffffffffffULL, 0x0008000000000000ULL,
   118:                              0x000aaaaaaaaaaaaaULL, 0x000ffffffffffffeULL, 0x000fffffffffffffULL};
   119:     U32 float_fractions[] = {0, 1, 0x003fffffU, 0x00400000U, 0x00555555U, 0x007ffffeU, 0x007fffffU};
   120:     int result = 0;
   121:     for (unsigned exponent = 0; exponent <= 1150 && !result; exponent += 1)
   122:     {
   123:         for (unsigned fraction = 0; fraction < sizeof(double_fractions) / sizeof(double_fractions[0]) && !result; fraction += 1)
   124:         {
   125:             U64 bits = ((U64)exponent << 52) | double_fractions[fraction];
   126:             result = check_double(bits);
   127:             if (!result)
   128:             {
   129:                 result = check_double(bits | 0x8000000000000000ULL);
   130:             }
   131:         }
   132:     }
   133:     for (unsigned exponent = 0; exponent <= 254 && !result; exponent += 1)
   134:     {
   135:         for (unsigned fraction = 0; fraction < sizeof(float_fractions) / sizeof(float_fractions[0]) && !result; fraction += 1)
   136:         {
   137:             U32 bits = (exponent << 23) | float_fractions[fraction];
   138:             result = check_float(bits);
   139:             if (!result)
   140:             {
   141:                 result = check_float(bits | 0x80000000U);
   142:             }
   143:         }
   144:     }
   145:     return result;
   146: }

     1: /*
     2:  * AArch64 canonical i128 arithmetic fixture.
     3:  *
     4:  * The helpers write through pointers deliberately.  The current AArch64
     5:  * caller path does not promise a direct i128 return shape yet; storing both
     6:  * halves still exercises the canonical operation and makes stale high-half
     7:  * results visible to a runtime oracle when this fixture is linked under
     8:  * qemu-aarch64 (or on an AArch64 host).
     9:  */

    18:     *remainder = dividend % divisor;
    19: }

    32:        oracle for this extension. */

    99: /* The machine selector's direct i128 subset: pair signatures over slot-backed
   100:    halves, carry/borrow add and subtract, per-half bitwise, constant-amount
   101:    shifts, and the whole comparison ladder.  Each function is small enough to
   102:    select whole, so the register-allocator lanes run the machine rows here
   103:    while the divide and multiply helpers above keep the canonical fallback. */
   104: static U128 add_pair(U128 left, U128 right) { return left + right; }
   105: static U128 subtract_pair(U128 left, U128 right) { return left - right; }
   106: static U128 and_pair(U128 left, U128 right) { return left & right; }
   107: static U128 or_pair(U128 left, U128 right) { return left | right; }
   108: static U128 xor_pair(U128 left, U128 right) { return left ^ right; }
   109: static U128 shift_left_1(U128 value) { return value << 1; }
   110: static U128 shift_left_64(U128 value) { return value << 64; }
   111: static U128 shift_left_65(U128 value) { return value << 65; }
   112: static U128 shift_right_1(U128 value) { return value >> 1; }
   113: static U128 shift_right_64(U128 value) { return value >> 64; }
   114: static U128 shift_right_127(U128 value) { return value >> 127; }
   115: static S128 arithmetic_shift_right_1(S128 value) { return value >> 1; }
   116: static S128 arithmetic_shift_right_65(S128 value) { return value >> 65; }
   117: static S128 arithmetic_shift_right_127(S128 value) { return value >> 127; }
   118: static int less_unsigned(U128 left, U128 right) { return left < right; }
   119: static int less_equal_unsigned(U128 left, U128 right) { return left <= right; }
   120: static int greater_unsigned(U128 left, U128 right) { return left > right; }
   121: static int greater_equal_unsigned(U128 left, U128 right) { return left >= right; }
   122: static int less_signed(S128 left, S128 right) { return left < right; }
   123: static int less_equal_signed(S128 left, S128 right) { return left <= right; }
   124: static int greater_signed(S128 left, S128 right) { return left > right; }
   125: static int greater_equal_signed(S128 left, S128 right) { return left >= right; }

   127: int main(void)
   128: {
   129:     U128 quotient = 0;
   130:     U128 remainder = 0;
   131: 
   132:     /* q=0 and q=1 exercise the compare branches before/at subtraction. */
   133:     U128 small = ((U128)0x123456789abcdef0ULL << 64) | 0x1111222233334444ULL;
   134:     unsigned_divide(small, small + 1, &quotient, &remainder);
   135:     if (!equal_unsigned(quotient, 0) || !equal_unsigned(remainder, small))
   136:         return 1;
   137:     unsigned_divide(small, small, &quotient, &remainder);
   138:     if (!equal_unsigned(quotient, 1) || !equal_unsigned(remainder, 0))
   139:         return 2;
   140: 
   141:     /* A high-only divisor and a carry from the low half into the high half. */
   142:     U128 high_divisor = (U128)1 << 64;
   143:     U128 high_dividend = high_divisor * 3 + 7;
   144:     unsigned_divide(high_dividend, high_divisor, &quotient, &remainder);
   145:     if (!equal_unsigned(quotient, 3) || !equal_unsigned(remainder, 7))
   146:         return 3;
   147:     U128 carry_dividend = ((U128)0xdeadbeefcafebabeULL << 64) | 0xffffffffffffffffULL;
   148:     carry_dividend += 1;
   149:     unsigned_divide(carry_dividend, 0x123456789ULL, &quotient, &remainder);
   150:     if (!equal_unsigned(quotient * 0x123456789ULL + remainder, carry_dividend))
   151:         return 4;
   152: 
   153:     /* Signed combinations, including INT128_MIN divided by a defined value.
   154:        Zero divisors and INT128_MIN/-1 remain outside the fixture because the
   155:        C frontend treats those signed-division cases as undefined behavior. */
   156:     S128 positive = (S128)(((U128)0x123456789abcdef0ULL << 64) | 0x1111222233334444ULL);
   157:     S128 negative = -positive;
   158:     S128 minimum = -((S128)1 << 126) - ((S128)1 << 126);
   159:     S128 signed_quotient = 0;
   160:     S128 signed_remainder = 0;
   161:     signed_divide(negative, positive, &signed_quotient, &signed_remainder);
   162:     if (!equal_signed(signed_quotient, -1) || !equal_signed(signed_remainder, 0))
   163:         return 5;
   164:     signed_divide(positive, negative, &signed_quotient, &signed_remainder);
   165:     if (!equal_signed(signed_quotient, -1) || !equal_signed(signed_remainder, 0))
   166:         return 6;
   167:     signed_divide(negative, negative, &signed_quotient, &signed_remainder);
   168:     if (!equal_signed(signed_quotient, 1) || !equal_signed(signed_remainder, 0))
   169:         return 7;
   170:     signed_divide(minimum, (S128)3, &signed_quotient, &signed_remainder);
   171:     if (!equal_signed(signed_quotient * 3 + signed_remainder, minimum) || signed_remainder >= 0)
   172:         return 8;
   173:     signed_divide((S128)23, (S128)-5, &signed_quotient, &signed_remainder);
   174:     if (!equal_signed(signed_quotient, -4) || !equal_signed(signed_remainder, 3))
   175:         return 9;
   176:     signed_divide((S128)-23, (S128)-5, &signed_quotient, &signed_remainder);
   177:     if (!equal_signed(signed_quotient, 4) || !equal_signed(signed_remainder, -3))
   178:         return 10;
   179: 
   180:     /* Both halves of the count result are checked, not merely a u64 cast. */
   181:     U128 leading = 0;
   182:     U128 trailing = 0;
   183:     count_bits((U128)1 << 127, &leading, &trailing);
   184:     if (!equal_unsigned(leading, 0) || !equal_unsigned(trailing, 127))
   185:         return 11;
   186:     count_bits((U128)1, &leading, &trailing);
   187:     if (!equal_unsigned(leading, 127) || !equal_unsigned(trailing, 0))
   188:         return 12;
   189:     /* Float boundaries stay inside the C conversion-defined ranges. */
   190:     double converted = 0.0;
   191:     signed_to_double((S128)3, &converted);
   192:     if (converted != 3.0)
   193:         return 13;
   194:     signed_to_double(-((S128)1 << 100), &converted);
   195:     if (converted != -(double)((S128)1 << 100))
   196:         return 14;
   197:     unsigned_to_double((U128)1 << 127, &converted);
   198:     if (converted != 0x1p127)
   199:         return 15;
   200:     /* Integer-to-double ties retain the discarded low-half sticky bit. */
   201:     U128 double_tie = ((U128)1 << 127) + ((U128)1 << 74);
   202:     unsigned_to_double(double_tie - 1, &converted);
   203:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0x47e0000000000000ULL)
   204:         return 16;
   205:     unsigned_to_double(double_tie, &converted);
   206:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0x47e0000000000000ULL)
   207:         return 17;
   208:     unsigned_to_double(double_tie + 1, &converted);
   209:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0x47e0000000000001ULL)
   210:         return 18;
   211:     S128 signed_double_tie = ((S128)1 << 126) + ((S128)1 << 73);
   212:     signed_to_double(signed_double_tie - 1, &converted);
   213:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0x47d0000000000000ULL)
   214:         return 19;
   215:     signed_to_double(signed_double_tie, &converted);
   216:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0x47d0000000000000ULL)
   217:         return 20;
   218:     signed_to_double(signed_double_tie + 1, &converted);
   219:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0x47d0000000000001ULL)
   220:         return 21;
   221:     signed_to_double(-(signed_double_tie - 1), &converted);
   222:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0xc7d0000000000000ULL)

   224:     signed_to_double(-signed_double_tie, &converted);
   225:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0xc7d0000000000000ULL)
   226:         return 23;

   228:     if (double_bits(converted) != 0xc7d0000000000001ULL)
   229:         return 24;
   230:     /* The same tie probes at binary32 precision, with a signed pair too. */
   231:     U128 float_tie = ((U128)1 << 127) + ((U128)1 << 103);
   232:     float float_converted = 0.0f;
   233:     unsigned_to_float(float_tie - 1, &float_converted);
   234:     if (float_bits(float_converted) != 0x7f000000U)
   235:         return 25;
   236:     unsigned_to_float(float_tie, &float_converted);
   237:     if (float_bits(float_converted) != 0x7f000000U)
   238:         return 26;
   239:     unsigned_to_float(float_tie + 1, &float_converted);

   243:     signed_to_float(signed_float_tie - 1, &float_converted);

   250:     if (float_bits(float_converted) != 0x7e800001U)

   253:     U128 unsigned_value = 0;

   255:     if (!equal_signed(signed_value, minimum))
   256:         return 31;
   257:     double_to_signed(0x1p126, &signed_value);

   261:     if (!equal_unsigned(unsigned_value, (U128)1 << 127))

   264:     if (!equal_signed(signed_value, minimum))

   270:     if (!equal_unsigned(unsigned_value, (U128)1 << 127))
   271:         return 36;
   272: 
   273:     /* The machine subset: a carry that crosses the half boundary and its
   274:        inverse borrow, then a doubling checked against the shift row. */
   275:     U128 all_low = ((U128)0x0123456789abcdefULL << 64) | 0xffffffffffffffffULL;
   276:     if (!equal_unsigned(add_pair(all_low, 1), (U128)0x0123456789abcdf0ULL << 64))
   277:         return 37;
   278:     if (!equal_unsigned(subtract_pair((U128)0x0123456789abcdf0ULL << 64, 1), all_low))
   279:         return 38;
   280:     if (!equal_unsigned(add_pair(small, small), shift_left_1(small)))
   281:         return 39;
   282:     /* Per-half bitwise over byte-alternating patterns. */
   283:     U128 pattern_a = ((U128)0xf0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0ULL << 64) | 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffULL;
   284:     U128 pattern_b = ((U128)0x0ff00ff00ff00ff0ULL << 64) | 0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0fULL;
   285:     if (!equal_unsigned(and_pair(pattern_a, pattern_b), ((U128)0x00f000f000f000f0ULL << 64) | 0x000f000f000f000fULL))
   286:         return 40;
   287:     if (!equal_unsigned(or_pair(pattern_a, pattern_b), ((U128)0xfff0fff0fff0fff0ULL << 64) | 0x0fff0fff0fff0fffULL))
   288:         return 41;
   289:     if (!equal_unsigned(xor_pair(pattern_a, pattern_b), ((U128)0xff00ff00ff00ff00ULL << 64) | 0x0ff00ff00ff00ff0ULL))
   290:         return 42;
   291:     /* Constant shifts across the amount boundaries: cross bits below 64,
   292:        the identity move at exactly 64, and the sign fill above it. */
   293:     U128 wide_bits = ((U128)0x8000000000000001ULL << 64) | 0x8000000000000001ULL;
   294:     if (!equal_unsigned(shift_left_1(wide_bits), ((U128)0x0000000000000003ULL << 64) | 0x0000000000000002ULL))
   295:         return 43;
   296:     if (!equal_unsigned(shift_left_64(wide_bits), (U128)0x8000000000000001ULL << 64))
   297:         return 44;
   298:     if (!equal_unsigned(shift_left_65(wide_bits), (U128)0x0000000000000002ULL << 64))
   299:         return 45;
   300:     if (!equal_unsigned(shift_right_1(wide_bits), ((U128)0x4000000000000000ULL << 64) | 0xC000000000000000ULL))
   301:         return 46;
   302:     if (!equal_unsigned(shift_right_64(wide_bits), (U128)0x8000000000000001ULL))
   303:         return 47;
   304:     if (!equal_unsigned(shift_right_127(wide_bits), (U128)1))
   305:         return 48;
   306:     if (!equal_signed(arithmetic_shift_right_1((S128)wide_bits), (S128)(((U128)0xC000000000000000ULL << 64) | 0xC000000000000000ULL)))
   307:         return 49;
   308:     if (!equal_signed(arithmetic_shift_right_65((S128)wide_bits), (S128)(((U128)0xffffffffffffffffULL << 64) | 0xC000000000000000ULL)))
   309:         return 50;
   310:     if (!equal_signed(arithmetic_shift_right_127((S128)wide_bits), (S128)-1))
   311:         return 51;
   312:     /* Every ordering, on both sides of the high-half tie. */
   313:     U128 same_high_small = ((U128)5 << 64) | 10;
   314:     U128 same_high_large = ((U128)5 << 64) | 20;
   315:     U128 higher = ((U128)6 << 64) | 1;
   316:     if (!less_unsigned(same_high_small, same_high_large) || less_unsigned(same_high_large, same_high_small) ||
   317:         !less_unsigned(same_high_large, higher) || less_unsigned(higher, same_high_large) || less_unsigned(higher, higher))
   318:         return 52;
   319:     if (!less_equal_unsigned(same_high_small, same_high_small) || !less_equal_unsigned(same_high_small, same_high_large) ||
   320:         less_equal_unsigned(higher, same_high_large))
   321:         return 53;
   322:     if (!greater_unsigned(higher, same_high_large) || greater_unsigned(same_high_small, same_high_large) || greater_unsigned(higher, higher))
   323:         return 54;
   324:     if (!greater_equal_unsigned(higher, higher) || !greater_equal_unsigned(same_high_large, same_high_small) ||
   325:         greater_equal_unsigned(same_high_small, same_high_large))
   326:         return 55;
   327:     S128 negative_deep = -(S128)(((U128)1 << 64) | 5);
   328:     S128 negative_tiny = -(S128)5;
   329:     S128 positive_tiny = (S128)5;
   330:     if (!less_signed(negative_deep, negative_tiny) || !less_signed(negative_tiny, positive_tiny) ||
   331:         less_signed(positive_tiny, negative_tiny) || less_signed(positive_tiny, positive_tiny))
   332:         return 56;
   333:     if (!less_equal_signed(positive_tiny, positive_tiny) || !less_equal_signed(negative_deep, negative_tiny) ||
   334:         less_equal_signed(positive_tiny, negative_tiny))
   335:         return 57;
   336:     if (!greater_signed(positive_tiny, negative_tiny) || !greater_signed(negative_tiny, negative_deep) ||
   337:         greater_signed(negative_deep, negative_tiny))
   338:         return 58;
   339:     if (!greater_equal_signed(negative_tiny, negative_tiny) || !greater_equal_signed(positive_tiny, negative_deep) ||
   340:         greater_equal_signed(negative_deep, positive_tiny))
   341:         return 59;
   342:     /* Two negatives sharing a high half defer to the unsigned low halves. */
   343:     S128 deep_negative_a = -(S128)(((U128)1 << 64) | 5);
   344:     S128 deep_negative_b = -(S128)(((U128)1 << 64) | 4);
   345:     if (!less_signed(deep_negative_a, deep_negative_b) || less_signed(deep_negative_b, deep_negative_a))
   346:         return 60;
   347:     return 0;
   348: }
===== tests/basic_c_aarch64_i128_abi.c =====

     1: // Focused AAPCS64 __int128 boundary fixture.  The pair in a bare integer-128
     2: // value is an INTEGER pair, but the pair itself has sixteen-byte alignment:
     3: // after an odd X-register cursor it rounds to the next even register, and
     4: // after the register file closes its stack image starts at an even eightbyte.
     5: // The functions are deliberately call boundaries rather than only arithmetic
     6: // bodies so a caller/callee disagreement cannot hide in one compiler's frame
     7: // representation.  This file has no hosted dependencies and therefore also
     8: // runs as a static AArch64 image under qemu-aarch64 when the emulator exists.
     9: typedef unsigned char u8;
    10: typedef unsigned long long u64;
    11: 
    12: typedef struct
    13: {
    14:     __int128 value;
    15: } I128Wrapper;
    16: 
    17: static int check_i128(__int128 value, u64 low, u64 high)
    18: {
    19:     return (u64)value == low && (u64)(value >> 64) == high;
    20: }
    21: 
    22: // One consumed GPR leaves x1, so C.8 rounds the pair to x2:x3.  The trailing
    23: // scalar catches a callee that starts the pair at x1 or fails to advance two
    24: // registers after it.
    25: static int after_one(int tag, __int128 value, int tail)
    26: {
    27:     return tag == 11 && check_i128(value, 0x0123456789abcdefULL, 0x1122334455667788ULL) && tail == 22;
    28: }
    29: 
    30: // Six consumed GPRs leave x6, already even, so the pair fits exactly in
    31: // x6:x7.  This is the non-rounding register-pair case.
    32: static int after_six(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, __int128 value)
    33: {
    34:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && check_i128(value, 7, 8);
    35: }
    36: 
    37: // Seven consumed GPRs leave only x7.  The pair spills at the stack base and
    38: // closes the X file, so the following scalar must also be stacked.
    39: static int after_seven(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, __int128 value, int tail)
    40: {
    41:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && g == 7 && check_i128(value, 9, 10) && tail == 11;
    42: }
    43: 
    44: // The ninth scalar occupies stack eightbyte zero.  A sixteen-byte pair that
    45: // follows it must skip eightbyte one and begin at NSAA+16.
    46: static int after_stacked_scalar(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, int h, int i, __int128 value)
    47: {
    48:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && g == 7 && h == 8 && i == 9 && check_i128(value, 12, 13);
    49: }
    50: 
    51: static __int128 make_i128(void)
    52: {
    53:     return ((__int128)0x8899aabbccddeeffULL << 64) | (__int128)0x0123456789abcdefULL;
    54: }
    55: 
    56: static I128Wrapper wrapper_after_one(int tag, I128Wrapper value, int tail)
    57: {
    58:     if (tag != 31 || tail != 32 || !check_i128(value.value, 33, 34))
    59:     {
    60:         return (I128Wrapper){0};
    61:     }
    62:     return value;
    63: }
    64: 
    65: int main(void)
    66: {
    67:     __int128 value = ((__int128)0x1122334455667788ULL << 64) | (__int128)0x0123456789abcdefULL;
    68:     if (!after_one(11, value, 22))
    69:     {
    70:         return 1;
    71:     }
    72:     if (!after_six(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ((__int128)8 << 64) | 7))
    73:     {
    74:         return 2;
    75:     }
    76:     if (!after_seven(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, ((__int128)10 << 64) | 9, 11))
    77:     {
    78:         return 3;
    79:     }
    80:     if (!after_stacked_scalar(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, ((__int128)13 << 64) | 12))
    81:     {
    82:         return 4;
    83:     }
    84:     if (!check_i128(make_i128(), 0x0123456789abcdefULL, 0x8899aabbccddeeffULL))
    85:     {
    86:         return 5;
    87:     }
    88:     I128Wrapper wrapped = {.value = ((__int128)34 << 64) | 33};
    89:     I128Wrapper wrapped_result = wrapper_after_one(31, wrapped, 32);
    90:     if (!check_i128(wrapped_result.value, 33, 34))
    91:     {
    92:         return 6;
    93:     }
    94:     return 0;
    95: }

===== tests/basic_c_aarch64_i128_divide.c =====
--- lines 1-200 ---
     1: /* AArch64 i128 division: exact quotients/remainders, independent shifted-
     2:    divisor reference, and canonical control flow around split MIR blocks. */
     3: typedef unsigned long long U64;
     4: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     5: typedef __int128 S128;
     6: 
     7: static void unsigned_divide(U128 n, U128 d, U128 *q, U128 *r)
     8: {
     9:     *q = n / d;
    10:     *r = n % d;
    11: }
    12: 
    13: static void signed_divide(S128 n, S128 d, S128 *q, S128 *r)
    14: {
    15:     *q = n / d;
    16:     *r = n % d;
    17: }
    18: 
    19: /* Align the divisor upward and subtract downward. This does not use either
    20:    C division or the dividend-prefix loop selected for the operations above. */
    21: static void reference(U128 n, U128 d, U128 *q, U128 *r)
    22: {
    23:     U64 low = (U64)n;
    24:     U64 high = (U64)(n >> 64);
    25:     U64 divisor_low = (U64)d;
    26:     U64 divisor_high = (U64)(d >> 64);
    27:     U64 bit_low = 1;
    28:     U64 bit_high = 0;
    29:     U64 quotient_low = 0;
    30:     U64 quotient_high = 0;
    31:     U64 half_low = (low >> 1) | (high << 63);
    32:     U64 half_high = high >> 1;
    33:     while (divisor_high < half_high || (divisor_high == half_high && divisor_low <= half_low))
    34:     {
    35:         divisor_high = (divisor_high << 1) | (divisor_low >> 63);
    36:         divisor_low <<= 1;
    37:         bit_high = (bit_high << 1) | (bit_low >> 63);
    38:         bit_low <<= 1;
    39:     }
    40:     while (bit_low || bit_high)
    41:     {
    42:         if (high > divisor_high || (high == divisor_high && low >= divisor_low))
    43:         {
    44:             U64 borrow = low < divisor_low;
    45:             low -= divisor_low;
    46:             high -= divisor_high;
    47:             high -= borrow;
    48:             quotient_low |= bit_low;
    49:             quotient_high |= bit_high;
    50:         }
    51:         divisor_low = (divisor_low >> 1) | (divisor_high << 63);
    52:         divisor_high >>= 1;
    53:         bit_low = (bit_low >> 1) | (bit_high << 63);
    54:         bit_high >>= 1;
    55:     }
    56:     *q = ((U128)quotient_high << 64) | quotient_low;
    57:     *r = ((U128)high << 64) | low;
    58: }
    59: 
    60: static int check(U128 n, U128 d)
    61: {
    62:     U128 expected_q;
    63:     U128 expected_r;
    64:     reference(n, d, &expected_q, &expected_r);
    65:     U128 q = ~(U128)0;
    66:     U128 r = ~(U128)0;
    67:     unsigned_divide(n, d, &q, &r);
    68:     int result = q != expected_q || r != expected_r;
    69:     U128 limit = (U128)1 << 127;
    70:     for (unsigned signs = 0; signs < 4 && !result; signs += 1)
    71:     {
    72:         unsigned negative_n = signs & 1;
    73:         unsigned negative_d = (signs >> 1) & 1;
    74:         if (n <= limit - !negative_n && d <= limit - !negative_d &&
    75:             !(n == limit && negative_n && d == 1 && negative_d))
    76:         {
    77:             U128 n_mask = (U128)0 - negative_n;
    78:             U128 d_mask = (U128)0 - negative_d;
    79:             U128 q_mask = (U128)0 - (negative_n != negative_d);
    80:             U128 n_bits = (n ^ n_mask) - n_mask;
    81:             U128 d_bits = (d ^ d_mask) - d_mask;
    82:             U128 q_bits = (expected_q ^ q_mask) - q_mask;
    83:             U128 r_bits = (expected_r ^ n_mask) - n_mask;
    84:             S128 signed_q = -1;
    85:             S128 signed_r = -1;
    86:             signed_divide((S128)n_bits, (S128)d_bits, &signed_q, &signed_r);
    87:             result = (U128)signed_q != q_bits || (U128)signed_r != r_bits;
    88:         }
    89:     }
    90:     return result;
    91: }
    92: 
    93: /* Several divisions in one block, scalar edge copies out of that block,
    94:    a canonical back edge, and a switch whose targets follow split blocks. */
    95: static U64 control_flow(U128 n, U128 d, unsigned choice)
    96: {
    97:     U64 result = 17;
    98:     for (unsigned index = 0; index < 4; index += 1)
    99:     {
   100:         if ((choice + index) & 1)
   101:         {
   102:             result += (U64)(n / d);
   103:             result ^= (U64)(n % d);
   104:         }
   105:         else
   106:         {
   107:             result ^= (U64)(n / d);
   108:             result += (U64)(n % d);
   109:         }
   110:         switch ((choice + index) & 3)
   111:         {
   112:         case 0: result += 3; break;
   113:         case 1: result ^= 5; break;
   114:         case 2: result += 7; break;
   115:         default: result ^= 11; break;
   116:         }
   117:     }
   118:     return result;
   119: }
   120: 
   121: /* A label address captured before a division must still name the entry of
   122:    its expanded canonical block when consumed by a computed branch. */
   123: static U64 computed_flow(U128 n, U128 d, unsigned choice)
   124: {
   125:     void *targets[] = {&&quotient, &&remainder};
   126:     U64 result = (U64)(n / d);
   127:     goto *targets[choice & 1];
   128: quotient:
   129:     result += 3;
   130: remainder:
   131:     result += 5;
   132:     return result;
   133: }
   134: 
   135: static U64 control_reference(U64 q, U64 r, unsigned choice)
   136: {
   137:     U64 result = 17;
   138:     for (unsigned index = 0; index < 4; index += 1)
   139:     {
   140:         if ((choice + index) & 1)
   141:         {
   142:             result += q;
   143:             result ^= r;
   144:         }
   145:         else
   146:         {
   147:             result ^= q;
   148:             result += r;
   149:         }
   150:         switch ((choice + index) & 3)
   151:         {
   152:         case 0: result += 3; break;
   153:         case 1: result ^= 5; break;
   154:         case 2: result += 7; break;
   155:         default: result ^= 11; break;
   156:         }
   157:     }
   158:     return result;
   159: }
   160: 
   161: int main(void)
   162: {
   163:     int result = 0;
   164:     U128 maximum = ~(U128)0;
   165:     for (unsigned bit = 0; bit < 128 && !result; bit += 1)
   166:     {
   167:         U128 power = (U128)1 << bit;
   168:         U128 values[] = {0, 1, power - 1, power, power + 1, maximum,
   169:                          ((U128)0xdeadbeefcafebabeULL << 64) | 0xfedcba9876543210ULL};
   170:         U128 divisors[] = {1, 3, power, power + (bit != 0), maximum,
   171:                            ((U128)1 << 64) - 1, ((U128)1 << 64) + 1};
   172:         for (unsigned n = 0; n < 7 && !result; n += 1)
   173:         {
   174:             for (unsigned d = 0; d < 7 && !result; d += 1)
   175:             {
   176:                 result = check(values[n], divisors[d]);
   177:             }
   178:         }
   179:     }
   180:     U64 random = 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
   181:     for (unsigned index = 0; index < 256 && !result; index += 1)
   182:     {
   183:         random ^= random << 13;
   184:         random ^= random >> 7;
   185:         random ^= random << 17;
   186:         U128 n = ((U128)random << 64) | (random ^ 0xa5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5ULL);
   187:         random ^= random << 13;
   188:         random ^= random >> 7;
   189:         random ^= random << 17;
   190:         U128 d = (((U128)random << 64) | (random >> 1) | 1) >> (index & 127);
   191:         d |= 1;
   192:         result = check(n, d);
   193:         U128 q;
   194:         U128 r;
   195:         reference(n, d, &q, &r);
   196:         if (!result && control_flow(n, d, index) != control_reference((U64)q, (U64)r, index)) result = 2;
   197:         if (!result && computed_flow(n, d, index) != (U64)q + 5 + ((index & 1) ? 0 : 3)) result = 3;
   198:     }
   199:     return result;
   200: }

     1: /* Integer-to-float nearest-even boundaries. The integer reference constructs
     2:    the expected IEEE image directly, without any integer-to-floating cast. */
     3: typedef unsigned long long U64;
     4: typedef unsigned int U32;
     5: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     6: typedef __int128 S128;
     7: 
     8: static void unsigned_to_double(U128 value, double *output)
     9: {
    10:     *output = (double)value;
    11: }
    12: 
    13: static void signed_to_double(S128 value, double *output)
    14: {
    15:     *output = (double)value;
    16: }
    17: 
    18: static void unsigned_to_float(U128 value, float *output)
    19: {
    20:     *output = (float)value;
    21: }
    22: 
    23: static void signed_to_float(S128 value, float *output)
    24: {
    25:     *output = (float)value;
    26: }

    28: static U64 expected_bits(U128 magnitude, unsigned precision, unsigned bias)
    29: {
    30:     U64 result = 0;
    31:     if (magnitude)
    32:     {
    33:         U64 upper = (U64)(magnitude >> 64);
    34:         unsigned exponent = upper ? 64 : 0;
    35:         U64 remaining = upper ? upper : (U64)magnitude;
    36:         while (remaining > 1)
    37:         {
    38:             remaining >>= 1;
    39:             exponent += 1;
    40:         }
    41:         U64 significand;
    42:         if (exponent < precision)
    43:         {
    44:             significand = (U64)(magnitude << (precision - 1 - exponent));
    45:         }
    46:         else
    47:         {
    48:             unsigned discarded = exponent - (precision - 1);
    49:             U128 unit = (U128)1 << discarded;
    50:             U128 remainder = magnitude & (unit - 1);
    51:             significand = (U64)(magnitude >> discarded);
    52:             if (remainder > (unit >> 1) || (remainder == (unit >> 1) && (significand & 1)))
    53:             {
    54:                 significand += 1;
    55:             }
    56:             if (significand == ((U64)1 << precision))
    57:             {
    58:                 significand >>= 1;
    59:                 exponent += 1;
    60:             }
    61:         }
    62:         U64 fraction_mask = ((U64)1 << (precision - 1)) - 1;
    63:         result = ((U64)(exponent + bias) << (precision - 1)) | ((U64)significand & fraction_mask);
    64:     }
    65:     return result;
    66: }
    67: 
    68: static int check_unsigned(U128 value)
    69: {
    70:     union { U64 bits; double value; } wide = {0x7ff8000000000001ULL};
    71:     union { U32 bits; float value; } narrow = {0x7fc00001U};
    72:     unsigned_to_double(value, &wide.value);
    73:     int result = wide.bits != expected_bits(value, 53, 1023) ? 1 : 0;
    74:     /* Larger unsigned integers exceed FLT_MAX and are outside C's defined
    75:        conversion range. All unsigned values fit in the double range. */
    76:     U128 float_maximum = (U128)0xffffff << 104;
    77:     if (value <= float_maximum)
    78:     {
    79:         unsigned_to_float(value, &narrow.value);
    80:         if (narrow.bits != (U32)expected_bits(value, 24, 127))
    81:         {
    82:             result = 2;
    83:         }
    84:     }
    85:     return result;
    86: }
    87: 
    88: static int check_signed(U128 magnitude, int negative)
    89: {
    90:     union { U64 bits; double value; } wide = {0x7ff8000000000001ULL};
    91:     union { U32 bits; float value; } narrow = {0x7fc00001U};
    92:     U128 sign_mask = (U128)0 - (unsigned)negative;
    93:     S128 value = (S128)((magnitude ^ sign_mask) - sign_mask);
    94:     signed_to_double(value, &wide.value);
    95:     signed_to_float(value, &narrow.value);
    96:     U64 sign64 = negative && magnitude ? 0x8000000000000000ULL : 0;
    97:     U32 sign32 = negative && magnitude ? 0x80000000U : 0;
    98:     int result = wide.bits != (expected_bits(magnitude, 53, 1023) | sign64) ? 3 : 0;
    99:     if (narrow.bits != ((U32)expected_bits(magnitude, 24, 127) | sign32))
   100:     {
   101:         result = 4;
   102:     }
   103:     return result;
   104: }
   105: 
   106: static int check_magnitude(U128 value)
   107: {
   108:     int result = check_unsigned(value);
   109:     U128 minimum_magnitude = (U128)1 << 127;
   110:     if (!result && value < minimum_magnitude)
   111:     {
   112:         result = check_signed(value, 0);
   113:     }
   114:     if (!result && value <= minimum_magnitude)
   115:     {
   116:         result = check_signed(value, 1);
   117:     }
   118:     return result;
   119: }
   120: 
   121: int main(void)
   122: {
   123:     int result = check_magnitude(0);
   124:     for (unsigned exponent = 0; exponent < 128 && !result; exponent += 1)
   125:     {
   126:         U128 power = (U128)1 << exponent;
   127:         U128 edges[] = {power - 1, power, power + 1, power | 0x5555555555555555ULL,
   128:                        power | ((U128)0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaULL << 64), ~(U128)0};
   129:         for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(edges) / sizeof(edges[0]) && !result; i += 1)
   130:         {
   131:             result = check_magnitude(edges[i]);
   132:         }
   133:         unsigned precisions[] = {24, 53};
   134:         for (unsigned p = 0; p < 2 && !result; p += 1)
   135:         {
   136:             if (exponent >= precisions[p])
   137:             {
   138:                 U128 unit = (U128)1 << (exponent - precisions[p] + 1);
   139:                 U128 half = unit >> 1;
   140:                 /* Even and odd ties, their neighbors, and a significand
   141:                    carry. The exponent sweep crosses the 64-bit boundary. */
   142:                 U128 ties[] = {power + half - 1, power + half, power + half + 1,
   143:                                power + unit + half - 1, power + unit + half, power + unit + half + 1,
   144:                                power - half - 1, power - half, power - half + 1};
   145:                 for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(ties) / sizeof(ties[0]) && !result; i += 1)
   146:                 {
   147:                     result = check_magnitude(ties[i]);
   148:                 }
   149:             }
   150:         }
   151:     }
   152:     return result;
   153: }

     1: // Windows ARM64 variadic arguments occupy an imaginary stack whose first
     2: // eight slots travel in X0-X7. An eight-aligned pair can straddle X7 and SP;
     3: // a bare __int128 instead rounds its address to sixteen-byte alignment.
     4: // Clang 18 disagrees with itself at these boundaries, so the optional assembly
     5: // companion is an independent producer/consumer oracle for the ABI layout.
     6: #ifndef BUSTER_PLATFORM_VA_ABI_PROBE
     7: #define BUSTER_PLATFORM_VA_ABI_PROBE 0
     8: #endif
     9: 
    10: typedef __builtin_va_list WindowsBoundaryVaList;
    11: struct WindowsBoundaryPair { long long low; long long high; };
    12: 
    13: int windows_va_split(int count, ...)
    14: {
    15:     WindowsBoundaryVaList arguments;
    16:     __builtin_va_start(arguments, count);
    17:     int good = count == 6;
    18:     for (int index = 0; index < count; index += 1)
    19:     {
    20:         good &= __builtin_va_arg(arguments, long long) == 11 * (index + 1ll);
    21:     }
    22:     struct WindowsBoundaryPair pair = __builtin_va_arg(arguments, struct WindowsBoundaryPair);
    23:     long long tail = __builtin_va_arg(arguments, long long);
    24:     __builtin_va_end(arguments);
    25:     return good && pair.low == 71 && pair.high == 83 && tail == 97;
    26: }
    27: 
    28: int windows_va_i128(int count, ...)
    29: {
    30:     WindowsBoundaryVaList arguments;
    31:     __builtin_va_start(arguments, count);
    32:     int good = count == 0 || count == 6 || count == 8;
    33:     for (int index = 0; index < count; index += 1)
    34:     {
    35:         good &= __builtin_va_arg(arguments, long long) == 11 * (index + 1ll);
    36:     }
    37:     __int128 value = __builtin_va_arg(arguments, __int128);
    38:     long long tail = __builtin_va_arg(arguments, long long);
    39:     __builtin_va_end(arguments);
    40:     return good && (long long)value == 71 && (long long)(value >> 64) == 83 && tail == 97;
    41: }

     1: /* Scalar and slot-backed i128 zero counts. The wide builtin spelling is a
     2:  * Buster extension: external compilers use two defined 64-bit calls instead
     3:  * of silently truncating an i128 argument to __builtin_clzll/__builtin_ctzll.
     4:  * Expected answers below are independent bit-position and literal controls.
     5:  */
     6: typedef unsigned int U32;
     7: typedef unsigned long long U64;
     8: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     9: 
    10: static U32 leading32(U32 value) { return (U32)__builtin_clz(value); }
    11: static U32 trailing32(U32 value) { return (U32)__builtin_ctz(value); }
    12: static U32 leading64(U64 value) { return (U32)__builtin_clzll(value); }
    13: static U32 trailing64(U64 value) { return (U32)__builtin_ctzll(value); }
    14: 
    15: static void counts128(U128 value, U128 *leading, U128 *trailing)
    16: {
    17: #ifdef __BUSTER__
    18:     *leading = __builtin_clzll(value);
    19:     *trailing = __builtin_ctzll(value);
    20: #else
    21:     U64 low = (U64)value;
    22:     U64 high = (U64)(value >> 64);
    23:     *leading = high ? (U32)__builtin_clzll(high) : low ? 64u + (U32)__builtin_clzll(low) : 128u;
    24:     *trailing = low ? (U32)__builtin_ctzll(low) : high ? 64u + (U32)__builtin_ctzll(high) : 128u;
    25: #endif
    26: }
    27: 
    28: static int check128(U64 low, U64 high, U32 expected_leading, U32 expected_trailing)
    29: {
    30:     U128 value = ((U128)high << 64) | low;
    31:     U128 leading = ~(U128)0;
    32:     U128 trailing = ~(U128)0;
    33:     counts128(value, &leading, &trailing);
    34:     int failed = leading != (U128)expected_leading || trailing != (U128)expected_trailing;
    35:     return failed;
    36: }
    37: 
    38: int main(void)
    39: {
    40:     int failed = 0;
    41:     for (U32 bit = 0; bit < 32; bit += 1)
    42:     {
    43:         U32 value = (U32)1 << bit;
    44:         failed |= leading32(value) != 31u - bit;
    45:         failed |= trailing32(value) != bit;
    46:         failed |= leading32(value | 1u) != 31u - bit;
    47:         failed |= trailing32(value | 0x80000000u) != bit;
    48:     }
    49:     for (U32 bit = 0; bit < 64; bit += 1)
    50:     {
    51:         U64 value = (U64)1 << bit;
    52:         failed |= leading64(value) != 63u - bit;
    53:         failed |= trailing64(value) != bit;
    54:         failed |= leading64(value | 1ull) != 63u - bit;
    55:         failed |= trailing64(value | 0x8000000000000000ull) != bit;
    56:     }
    57:     for (U32 bit = 0; bit < 128; bit += 1)
    58:     {
    59:         U64 low = 0;
    60:         U64 high = 0;
    61:         if (bit < 64)
    62:         {
    63:             low = (U64)1 << bit;
    64:         }
    65:         else
    66:         {
    67:             high = (U64)1 << (bit - 64);
    68:         }
    69:         failed |= check128(low, high, 127u - bit, bit);
    70:         failed |= check128(low | 1ull, high, 127u - bit, 0);
    71:         failed |= check128(low, high | 0x8000000000000000ull, 0, bit);
    72:     }
    73:     failed |= check128(~0ull, ~0ull, 0, 0);
    74:     failed |= check128(~0ull, 0, 64, 0);
    75:     failed |= check128(0, ~0ull, 0, 64);
    76:     failed |= check128(0x0000000100000000ull, 0x0000000080000000ull, 32, 32);
    77:     failed |= check128(0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaull, 0x5555555555555555ull, 1, 1);
    78:     /* The existing AArch64 direct oracle defines the all-zero pair as 128.
    79:        External controls guard both limbs, never call a zero-input builtin. */

     1: // Exercise asm-goto edge remapping after native wide division splits a block.
     2: #if defined(__aarch64__) || defined(_M_ARM64)

     1: // The one C23 attribute buster acts on.  basic_c_c23_attributes.c proves the
     2: // rest are parsed and discarded; this one proves [[noreturn]] is read, and it
     3: // is written as a pair so the proof discriminates: die_marked and die_plain
     4: // differ in nothing but the attribute, so a compiler that ignored it would
     5: // lower the two callers identically.
     6: //
     7: // c_ir_noreturn_marker_in_range has had a [[ branch since it was written, but
     8: // it was unreachable dead code -- an attributed declaration failed to parse
     9: // long before the lowering could ask about it -- so the driver test checks the
    10: // generated assembly rather than only that this runs: a call to a noreturn
    11: // callee ends control flow, and the caller's fallthrough is replaced by a trap
    12: // instead of an ordinary return sequence.
    13: //
    14: // Declared rather than included: the driver test compiles this without an
    15: // -isysroot, the same way basic_c_noreturn_call.c declares exit.
    16: __attribute__((noreturn)) void exit(int status);
    17: 
    18: // The marked callee.  Both the plain C23 spelling and the reserved scoped one
    19: // have to be read; glibc-style headers use the reserved spellings so a user
    20: // macro named `noreturn` cannot capture them.

    45: // declaration, which is the shape the issue reported failing with an
    46: // "undeclared identifier" on the parameter itself.

    49:     exit(status);
    50: }

    44:     // Exact to a 64-bit significand and not representable in a double, so a
    45:     // half that quietly moved through an f64 fails here.
    46:     long double pi = 3.14159265358979323846264338327950288L;
    47:     ldc z = ldc_compose(pi, -pi);
    48:     if (!check(z, pi, -pi)) return 1;

    50:     real_shape.f = __real__ z;
    51:     if (real_shape.i.m != 0xc90fdaa22168c235UL || real_shape.i.se != 0x4000) return 2;
    52:     union ldshape imaginary_shape;
    53:     imaginary_shape.f = __imag__ z;
    54:     if (imaginary_shape.i.m != 0xc90fdaa22168c235UL || imaginary_shape.i.se != 0xc000) return 3;
    55: 
    56:     // Which half is which: a swapped pair passes every test whose two halves
    57:     // are the same magnitude, so nothing here uses one.
    58:     ldc asymmetric = ldc_compose(3.5L, -1.25L);
    59:     if (!check(asymmetric, 3.5L, -1.25L)) return 4;
    60:     if (ldc_real(asymmetric) != 3.5L) return 5;
    61:     if (ldc_imaginary(asymmetric) != -1.25L) return 6;
    62:     if (!check(ldc_conjugate(asymmetric), 3.5L, 1.25L)) return 7;
    63:     if (!check(ldc_relay(asymmetric), 3.5L, 1.25L)) return 8;

    65: 
    66:     // A subnormal keeps a clear integer bit and a zero exponent field, which
    67:     // a round trip through anything narrower would flush away.
    68:     union ldshape tiny;
    69:     tiny.f = __real__ ldc_compose(0x1p-16400L, 1.0L);

    78:     if (!check(ldc_sum(asymmetric, other), 7.5L, 2.75L)) return 11;

    80:     // A negative zero compares equal to a positive one, so the sign comes
    81:     // back through the field view.

     1: // QuickJS builds its property tables with `JS_PROP_DOUBLE_DEF("NaN", NAN, 0)`
     2: // and `JS_PROP_DOUBLE_DEF("Infinity", 1.0 / 0.0, 0)`.  Hosted <math.h> spells
     3: // NAN as `(__builtin_nanf(""))` and INFINITY as `(__builtin_inff())`, so a
     4: // static initializer holding either is a constant expression the constant
     5: // evaluator has to fold -- and an IEEE divide by zero is a value, not the
     6: // "unknown" an integer divide by zero has to answer.  The spellings are
     7: // written out here rather than included so the fixture needs no SDK.
     8: static const double constants[] = {
     9:     (__builtin_nanf("")),
    10:     (__builtin_inff()),
    11:     -(__builtin_inff()),
    12:     __builtin_huge_val(),

    14:     -1.0 / 0.0,
    15:     0.0 / 0.0,
    16:     1.5,
    17: };

    27: };

    30:     {"NaN", .value = {.number = (__builtin_nanf(""))}},
    31:     {"Infinity", .value = {.number = 1.0 / 0.0}},
    32:     {"answer", .value = {.integer = 42}},
    33: };
    34: 
    35: static int is_nan(double value)
    36: {
    37:     return value != value;
    38: }
    39: 
    40: // Distinct rounding points: unsigned and wide integer conversion, integer
    41: // ties/sticky bits, f32 arithmetic, and a subsequent widening conversion.
    42: static const double rounded[] = {
    43:     (double)0x8000000000000000ULL,
    44:     (double)0xffffffffffffffffULL,
    45:     (double)((unsigned __int128)1 << 100),
    46:     (double)(-((__int128)1 << 100)),
    47:     (double)(((unsigned __int128)1 << 100) | 0xffffffffffffffffULL),
    48:     (double)(float)0x8000008000000001ULL,
    49:     (double)(float)(((unsigned __int128)1 << 100) + ((unsigned __int128)1 << 76) + 1),
    50:     (double)(16777216.0f + 1.0f),
    51:     (double)((16777216.0f + 1.0f) - 16777216.0f),
    52:     (double)(1.0f / 3.0f),
    53:     (double)((1.0f + 0x1p-24f) * 2.0f),
    54:     (double)((1.0f + 0x1p-23f) * (1.0f + 0x1p-23f)),
    55: };
    56: static const double *observed_rounded = rounded;
    57: static int check_constant_rounding(void)
    58: {
    59:     int failures = 0;
    60:     const double expected[] = {
    61:         0x1p63, 0x1p64, 0x1p100, -0x1p100,
    62:         0x1.000000001p100, 0x1.000002p63, 0x1.000002p100,
    63:         16777216.0, 0.0, 0x1.555556p-2, 2.0, 0x1.000004p0,
    64:     };
    65:     for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(expected) / sizeof(expected[0]); ++i)
    66:         failures += observed_rounded[i] != expected[i];
    67:     return failures;
    68: }
    69: 
    70: int main(void)
    71: {
    72:     if (check_constant_rounding()) return 14;
    73:     if (!is_nan(constants[0])) return 1;
    74:     if (constants[1] <= 1.0e308 || is_nan(constants[1])) return 2;
    75:     if (constants[2] >= -1.0e308 || is_nan(constants[2])) return 3;
    76:     if (constants[3] != constants[1]) return 4;
    77:     if (constants[4] != constants[1]) return 5;
    78:     if (constants[5] != constants[2]) return 6;
    79:     if (!is_nan(constants[6])) return 7;
    80:     if (constants[7] != 1.5) return 8;
    81:     if (!is_nan(table[0].value.number)) return 9;
    82:     if (table[1].value.number != constants[1]) return 10;
    83:     if (table[2].value.integer != 42) return 11;
    84:     // The created NaN's sign is canonical, so a folded 0.0/0.0 has the same
    85:     // bytes the reference compiler writes.
    86:     if (__builtin_signbit(constants[6])) return 12;
    87:     if (__builtin_signbit(constants[0])) return 13;
    88:     return 0;
    89: }

===== tests/basic_c_i128_block_parameters.c =====
--- lines 1-113 ---
     1: /* Preserve both limbs through canonical joins, mixed loop parameters,
     2:    parallel swap/rotation cycles, repeated switch targets and computed gotos.
     3:    Pointer signatures keep this independent of platform i128 call ABIs. */
     4: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     5: typedef __int128 I128;
     6: 
     7: void wide_choose(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
     8: {
     9:     *out = n ? in[0] : in[1];
    10: }
    11: 
    12: void wide_signed(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
    13: {
    14:     I128 value = n ? (I128)in[0] : (I128)in[1];
    15:     *out = (U128)value;
    16: }
    17: 
    18: void wide_nested(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
    19: {
    20:     *out = (n & 1) ? ((n & 2) ? in[0] : in[1]) : ((n & 2) ? in[2] : in[3]);
    21: }
    22: 
    23: void wide_swap(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
    24: {
    25:     U128 a = in[0];
    26:     U128 b = in[1];
    27:     while (n > 0)
    28:     {
    29:         U128 temporary = a;
    30:         a = b;
    31:         b = temporary;
    32:         n -= 1;
    33:     }
    34:     out[0] = a;
    35:     out[1] = b;
    36: }
    37: 
    38: void wide_rotate(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
    39: {
    40:     U128 a = in[0];
    41:     U128 b = in[1];
    42:     U128 c = in[2];
    43:     int count = 0;
    44:     while (count < n)
    45:     {
    46:         U128 temporary = a;
    47:         a = b;
    48:         b = c;
    49:         c = temporary;
    50:         count += 1;
    51:     }
    52:     out[0] = a;
    53:     out[1] = b;
    54:     out[2] = c;
    55:     out[3] = (U128)count;
    56: }
    57: 
    58: void wide_switch(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
    59: {
    60:     U128 value = in[0];
    61:     switch (n)
    62:     {
    63:     case 0:
    64:     case 2: value = in[1]; break;
    65:     case 1:
    66:     case 3: value = in[2]; break;
    67:     default: break;
    68:     }
    69:     *out = value;
    70: }
    71: 
    72: void wide_indirect(U128* out, U128 const* in, int n)
    73: {
    74:     U128 value = in[0];
    75:     void* destination = n ? &&replace : &&done;
    76:     goto *destination;
    77: replace:
    78:     value = in[1];
    79: done:
    80:     /* Exercise a conditional value after the indirect branch. */
    81:     *out = (n & 2) ? value : in[2];
    82: }
    83: 
    84: int main(void)
    85: {
    86:     U128 in[4];
    87:     in[0] = ((U128)0x123456789abcdef0ULL << 64) | 0xfedcba9876543210ULL;
    88:     in[1] = ((U128)0x8070605040302010ULL << 64) | 0x0102030405060708ULL;
    89:     in[2] = (U128)1 << 127;
    90:     in[3] = ((U128)0xffffffffffffffffULL << 64) | 0xffffffffffffffffULL;
    91:     U128 out[4];
    92:     int failed = 0;
    93:     for (int n = 0; n < 18; n += 1)
    94:     {
    95:         wide_choose(out, in, n);
    96:         failed |= out[0] != in[n ? 0 : 1];
    97:         wide_signed(out, in, n);
    98:         failed |= out[0] != in[n ? 0 : 1];
    99:         wide_nested(out, in, n);
   100:         int selected = (n & 1) ? ((n & 2) ? 0 : 1) : ((n & 2) ? 2 : 3);
   101:         failed |= out[0] != in[selected];
   102:         wide_swap(out, in, n);
   103:         failed |= out[0] != in[n & 1] || out[1] != in[(n & 1) ^ 1];
   104:         wide_rotate(out, in, n);
   105:         failed |= out[0] != in[n % 3] || out[1] != in[(n + 1) % 3] || out[2] != in[(n + 2) % 3];
   106:         failed |= out[3] != (U128)n;
   107:         wide_switch(out, in, n);
   108:         failed |= out[0] != in[n < 4 ? 1 + (n & 1) : 0];
   109:         wide_indirect(out, in, n);
   110:         failed |= out[0] != in[(n & 2) ? (n ? 1 : 0) : 2];
   111:     }
   112:     return failed;
   113: }
===== tests/basic_c_i128_divide_oracle_edges.c =====

     1: /* Preserve the direct native emitter's bit results outside defined C divide
     2:    inputs. These are an implementation oracle, never a Clang differential:
     3:    zero divisors produce an all-ones magnitude quotient and the dividend as
     4:    remainder; the signed minimum divided by -1 wraps to the minimum. */
     5: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     6: typedef __int128 S128;
     7: 
     8: static volatile U128 numerator = ((U128)0x923456789abcdef0ULL << 64) | 0xfedcba9876543210ULL;
     9: static volatile U128 zero = 0;
    10: static volatile S128 minimum = (S128)((U128)1 << 127);
    11: static volatile S128 minus_one = -1;
    12: 
    13: int main(void)
    14: {
    15:     U128 n = numerator;
    16:     U128 d = zero;
    17:     int result = n / d != ~(U128)0 || n % d != n;
    18:     S128 sn = (S128)n;
    19:     S128 sd = (S128)d;
    20:     result |= sn / sd != 1 || sn % sd != sn;
    21:     sn = (S128)(n >> 1);
    22:     result |= sn / sd != -1 || sn % sd != sn;
    23:     sn = minimum;
    24:     sd = minus_one;
    25:     result |= sn / sd != sn || sn % sd != 0;
    26:     return result;
    27: }
