===== tests/basic_c_invalid_bit_field_width.c =====
--- lines 1-38 ---
     1: // C requires the width of a *named* bit-field to be at least one bit
     2: // (C23 6.7.3.2p4).  Zero is reserved for the unnamed `int : 0;`, which
     3: // declares no member and only moves the next one to its type's boundary, and
     4: // both reference compilers refuse the named spelling: "named bit-field 'b' has
     5: // zero width" (Clang), "zero width for bit-field 'b'" (GCC).  Accepted, the
     6: // member was laid out as the zero-width member it is not allowed to be -- the
     7: // struct below measured 4/4 -- and `v.b = 0;` followed by a read of `v.b`
     8: // compiled and answered zero.
     9: //

   156: int main(void)
   157: {
   158:     // 3.14159265358979323846264338327950288L is exact to a 64-bit
   159:     // significand and is not representable in a double, so a lowering that
   160:     // quietly copied through an f64 fails the mantissa checks below.
   161:     long double pi = 3.14159265358979323846264338327950288L;
   162:     union ldshape shape = shape_of(pi);
   163:     if (shape.i.m != 0xc90fdaa22168c235UL) return 1;
   164:     if (shape.i.se != 0x4000) return 2;
   165:     if (shape_mantissa(shape) != 0xc90fdaa22168c235UL) return 3;
   166:     if (shape_sign_exponent(shape) != 0x4000) return 4;
   167:     if (shape_value(11, shape, 22) != pi) return 5;
   168: 
   169:     union ldshape bumped = shape_bump(11, shape, 22);
   170:     if (bumped.i.m != 0xc90fdaa22168c235UL + 33UL) return 6;
   171:     if (bumped.i.se != 0x4000) return 7;
   172: 
   173:     // The sign bit and the biased exponent, read the way __signbitl and
   174:     // __fpclassifyl read them.
   175:     union ldshape negative = shape_of(-1.0L);
   176:     if ((negative.i.se >> 15) != 1) return 8;
   177:     if ((negative.i.se & 0x7fff) != 0x3fff) return 9;
   178:     if (negative.i.m != 0x8000000000000000UL) return 10;
   179: 
   180:     // A subnormal: the explicit integer bit is clear and the exponent field
   181:     // is zero, which is exactly what an f64 round trip would flush away.
   182:     union ldshape tiny = shape_of(0x1p-16400L);
   183:     if (tiny.i.se != 0) return 11;
   184:     if (tiny.i.m != 0x0000200000000000UL) return 12;
   185: 
   186:     // Negative zero survives, and the union sees the sign an equality
   187:     // comparison cannot.
   188:     union ldshape minus_zero = shape_of(-0.0L);
   189:     if (minus_zero.i.se != 0x8000) return 13;
   190:     if (minus_zero.i.m != 0) return 14;
   191: 
   192:     union ldmixed mixed;
   193:     mixed.f = -1.5L;
   194:     union ldmixed mixed_back = mixed_round_trip(11, mixed, 22);
   195:     if (mixed_back.f != -1.5L) return 15;
   196:     if (mixed_back.m != mixed.m) return 16;
   197: 
   198:     union ldfloating floating;
   199:     floating.f = 1.0L + 0x1p-63L;
   200:     union ldfloating floating_back = floating_round_trip(11, floating, 22);
   201:     if (floating_back.f != floating.f) return 17;
   202:     if (floating_back.f == 1.0L) return 18;
   203: 
   204:     struct ldpair pair;
   205:     pair.v[0] = 1.25L;
   206:     pair.v[1] = -2.5L;
   207:     struct ldpair pair_back = pair_round_trip(11, pair, 22);
   208:     if (pair_back.v[0] != 1.25L || pair_back.v[1] != -2.5L) return 19;
   209: 
   210:     struct ldlarge large;
   211:     large.f = 0x1p16000L;
   212:     large.tail = 41;
   213:     struct ldlarge large_back = large_round_trip(11, large, 22);
   214:     if (large_back.f != 0x1p16000L || large_back.tail != 42) return 20;
   215:     union ldshape large_shape = shape_of(large_back.f);

     1: // Scalar float function bodies on the machine path: the f32/f64
     2: // arithmetic, comparison, negation, and conversion shapes the AArch64
     3: // FARITH/FCMP port covers, each computed from runtime operands so nothing
     4: // folds before selection. Comparisons cover the NaN row of every operator
     5: // because the unordered-false conditions are the part a wrong condition
     6: // table would miscompile. Every function is self-checking through main's
     7: // exit status, so the register-allocator-mode differential (NONE as the
     8: // oracle) needs only the exit codes to agree.
     9:

    11: {
    12:     double x = a;
    13:     double y = b;
    14:     double z = (x + y) * 0.5 - x / (y + 3.0);
    15:     return (int)(z * 4.0);
    16: }
    17: 
    18: static int f32_arith(int a)
    19: {
    20:     float x = (float)a;

    23: }

===== tests/basic_c_negative_constant_widening.c =====
--- lines 1-77 ---
     1: // A constant carries only the bits its own type is wide, so a negative one
     2: // that initializes a wider object has to replay its sign bit.  Every
     3: // initializer below spells its value in a type narrower than the object it
     4: // initializes; before the constant cast sign-extended, each stored the
     5: // unsigned reading of the narrow bits -- `(long long)-1` became 4294967295 --
     6: // while an explicitly `LL`-suffixed literal was already wide and stayed
     7: // correct.
     8: 
     9: struct fields
    10: {
    11:     long long wide;
    12:     unsigned long long unsigned_wide;
    13: };
    14: 
    15: static const long long plain[] = {-1};
    16: static const long long converted[] = {(long long)-1};
    17: static const long long suffixed[] = {-1LL};
    18: static long long writable[] = {-1};
    19: static const long long scalar = -1;
    20: static const unsigned long long unsigned_scalar = -1;
    21: // The unsigned source is the control: converting it widens by zero extension,
    22: // so this one must keep the value the sign-extending path would destroy.
    23: static const long long from_unsigned = (unsigned)-1;
    24: static const signed char narrowed = -1;
    25: static const struct fields grouped = {-1, -1};
    26: static const long long nested[2][2] = {{-1, 2}, {-3, 4}};
    27: static const __int128 wide_pair = -1;
    28: 
    29: // Read the images through pointers stored in writable globals.  A direct read
    30: // of a `const` object can be folded back into its initializer expression,
    31: // which would check the constant evaluator twice and never look at the bytes
    32: // the object writer emitted.
    33: static const long long *observed_plain = plain;
    34: static const long long *observed_scalar = &scalar;
    35: static const struct fields *observed_grouped = &grouped;
    36: static const __int128 *observed_wide_pair = &wide_pair;
    37: 
    38: // Constant operators must perform the same integer promotions as runtime
    39: // operators. Inspect stored images so this is not merely re-folding a const.
    40: static const long long promoted[] = {
    41:     +(signed char)-1, -(signed char)-1, ~(unsigned char)0,
    42:     +(short)-2, -(short)-2, ~(unsigned short)0,
    43:     (-4 >> 1U), ((signed char)-4 >> 1ULL), ((short)-8 >> 2U),
    44:     (1U << 31ULL),
    45: };
    46: static const long long *observed_promoted = promoted;
    47: static const _Bool truth[] = {
    48:     (_Bool)2, (_Bool)256, (_Bool)-2, (_Bool)0.5, (_Bool)-0.5,
    49:     (_Bool)((unsigned __int128)1 << 100), (_Bool)&scalar,
    50:     (_Bool)0, (_Bool)0.0, (_Bool)-0.0, (_Bool)(void *)0,
    51: };
    52: static const _Bool *observed_truth = truth;
    53: 
    54: static int check_constant_promotions(void)
    55: {
    56:     int failures = 0;
    57:     const long long expected[] = {-1, 1, -1, -2, 2, -1, -2, -2, -2, 2147483648LL};
    58:     for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(expected) / sizeof(expected[0]); ++i)
    59:         failures += observed_promoted[i] != expected[i];
    60:     for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(truth) / sizeof(truth[0]); ++i)
    61:         failures += observed_truth[i] != (i < 7);
    62:     return failures;
    63: }
    64: 
    65: int main(void)
    66: {
    67:     if (check_constant_promotions()) return 10;
    68:     if (plain[0] != -1 || converted[0] != -1 || suffixed[0] != -1 || writable[0] != -1) return 1;
    69:     if (scalar != -1 || unsigned_scalar != 0xffffffffffffffffull) return 2;
    70:     if (from_unsigned != 4294967295LL || narrowed != -1) return 3;
    71:     if (grouped.wide != -1 || grouped.unsigned_wide != 0xffffffffffffffffull) return 4;
    72:     if (nested[0][0] != -1 || nested[0][1] != 2 || nested[1][0] != -3 || nested[1][1] != 4) return 5;
    73:     if ((long long)wide_pair != -1 || (long long)(wide_pair >> 64) != -1) return 6;
    74:     if (observed_plain[0] != -1 || *observed_scalar != -1) return 7;
    75:     if (observed_grouped->wide != -1 || observed_grouped->unsigned_wide != 0xffffffffffffffffull) return 8;
    76:     return (long long)*observed_wide_pair == -1 && (long long)(*observed_wide_pair >> 64) == -1 ? 0 : 9;
    77: }

     1: // A braced string literal is the contents of a character array but one
     2: // element of an array of pointers.  SQLite lists the shared-library suffixes
     3: // to try as `static const char *azEndings[] = { "so" };`, which sizes the

     5: // integer spellings below are the names Clang and GCC predefine for the
     6: // keyword; SQLite's decimal extension uses them directly.

    13: static unsigned long string_length(const char *text)
    14: {
    15:     unsigned long length = 0;
    16:     while (text[length]) length += 1;
    17:     return length;
    18: }
    19: 
    20: int main(void)
    21: {
    22:     __int128_t wide = 0;
    23:     __uint128_t unsigned_wide = 0;
    24:     unsigned long long low;
    25: 
    26:     if (sizeof endings / sizeof endings[0] != 1) return 1;
    27:     if (string_length(endings[0]) != 2 || endings[0][0] != 's') return 2;
    28:     if (sizeof many / sizeof many[0] != 3) return 3;
    29:     if (string_length(many[2]) != 3) return 4;
    30:     if (sizeof letters != 4 || letters[2] != 'c') return 5;
    31:     if (sizeof plain != 5) return 6;
    32:     if (sizeof qualified / sizeof qualified[0] != 1) return 7;
    33: 
    34:     wide = (__int128_t)1 << 100;
    35:     unsigned_wide = (__uint128_t)wide + 1;
    36:     low = (unsigned long long)(unsigned_wide >> 64);
    37:     if (sizeof(__int128_t) != 16 || sizeof(__uint128_t) != 16) return 8;
    38:     if (low != (1ull << 36)) return 9;
    39:     if ((unsigned long long)(unsigned_wide & 0xffffffffffffffffull) != 1ull) return 10;
    40:     return 0;

===== tests/basic_c_typeof_declaration.c =====
--- lines 1-52 ---
     1: // Three shapes musl's `weak_alias` needs, each of which failed on its own.
     2: //
     3: //   #define weak_alias(old, new) \
     4: //           extern __typeof(old) new __attribute__((__weak__, __alias__(#old)))
     5: //
     6: // 1. The spelling is `__typeof`. GCC and Clang accept `typeof`, `__typeof`
     7: //    and `__typeof__`; only the first (in GNU/C23 dialects) and the last were
     8: //    recognized here, so every `weak_alias` in a translation unit compiled
     9: //    under -std=c99 declared nothing at all and the name failed as
    10: //    "use of undeclared identifier" at its first use.
    11: // 2. A declarator with no parameter list still declares a function when the
    12: //    specifiers give it a function type (C11 6.7.6.3): `extern __typeof(f) g;`
    13: //    declares the function `g`. It was classified as an object with a
    14: //    function type, which has no storage and no call target.
    15: // 3. C11 6.2.7p3 makes an unprototyped `long f();` compatible with a
    16: //    non-variadic prototype for the same function, which is how
    17: //    `src/thread/pthread_cancel.c` declares `__syscall_cp_asm` twice.
    18: //
    19: // The results are read at run time: a declaration that resolves to the wrong
    20: // entity still links, and only calling it says which function ran.
    21: 
    22: static int base(int x)
    23: {
    24:     return x * 3;
    25: }
    26: 
    27: // The typeof-derived function declaration, in all three spellings.

    29: extern __typeof__(base) via_underscore_typeof_underscore;
    30: 
    31: int via_underscore_typeof(int x)
    32: {
    33:     return x + 1;
    34: }
    35: 
    36: int via_underscore_typeof_underscore(int x)
    37: {
    38:     return x + 2;

===== tests/basic_c_win64_narrow_abi.c =====
--- lines 1-60 ---
     1: // The Win64 call shapes that clang picks for values narrower than one vector
     2: // register, crossing real call boundaries in both directions. MSVC has no
     3: // generic vector extension and no __int128, so clang's answers are the
     4: // de-facto ABI here; each was measured against clang 22 with
     5: // --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc before being implemented:
     6: //
     7: //   - A single-lane vector travels exactly like its scalar element: integer
     8: //     lanes ride the positional GPR and come back in RAX, float lanes ride
     9: //     the positional XMM register and come back in XMM0. Buster used to pass
    10: //     every Win64 vector by reference, so these four families disagreed with
    11: //     clang in both directions.
    12: //   - A multi-lane vector under eight bytes is an indirect argument and a
    13: //     direct XMM0 result. The result half is what buster used to refuse: it
    14: //     returned anything narrower than eight bytes by reference.
    15: //   - __int128 is an indirect argument and an XMM0 result. Buster used to
    16: //     return it through the caller's hidden pointer.
    17: //
    18: // The fixture is deliberately callee-in-another-function: a round trip
    19: // through one identity function cannot tell an argument-side disagreement
    20: // from a return-side one, so every family checks the two halves separately.
    21: // tests/c_abi_* pairs the same shapes against clang objects for real; this
    22: // fixture is the in-tree regression that runs on every platform.
    23: typedef unsigned char u8;
    24: typedef unsigned short u16;
    25: typedef unsigned int u32;
    26: typedef unsigned long long u64;
    27: 
    28: typedef u8 Vector1U8 __attribute__((vector_size(1)));
    29: typedef u16 Vector1U16 __attribute__((vector_size(2)));

    31: typedef u64 Vector1U64 __attribute__((vector_size(8)));
    32: typedef float Vector1F32 __attribute__((vector_size(4)));
    33: typedef double Vector1F64 __attribute__((vector_size(8)));
    34: typedef u8 Vector2U8 __attribute__((vector_size(2)));

     1: // The 128-bit binary subset the machine selectors carry, written so both
     2: // targets run it: the AArch64 selector reached this subset first and the x86-64
     3: // one refused all of it (issue #811), which is why tests/basic_c_aarch64_i128.c
     4: // -- the fixture that had the coverage -- is an AArch64 file. That one also
     5: // exercises the divides and the i128 GNU bit builtins, which no machine path
     6: // selects and which the x86-64 canonical emitter does not carry at all, so this
     7: // is a separate file rather than a second lane over it.
     8: //
     9: // Every operation here has to *select*: the driver test pins the fallback count
    10: // as well as running the program, because the canonical emitter would produce
    11: // the same answers and hide a selector that stopped firing.
    12: //
    13: // The values are chosen to cross the halfway boundary in both directions --
    14: // carries out of the low half, borrows into it, shift amounts below, at and
    15: // above 64, and comparisons that the high halves decide against ones only the
    16: // low halves can.

===== tests/basic_c_x86_64_i128_complement.c =====

     1: /* Runtime i128 complements checked against independent 64-bit limb operations.
     2:    Pointer signatures also exercise Windows without requiring a bare-i128 ABI. */
     3: typedef unsigned long long U64;
     4: typedef unsigned __int128 U128;
     5: typedef __int128 I128;
     6: 
     7: static void complement_unsigned(U128* out, U128 const* in)
     8: {
     9:     *out = ~*in;
    10: }
    11: 
    12: static void complement_signed(I128* out, I128 const* in)
    13: {
    14:     *out = ~*in;
    15: }
    16: 
    17: static void complement_twice(U128* out, U128 const* in)
    18: {
    19:     U128 first = ~*in;
    20:     *out = ~first;
    21: }
    22: 
    23: static void complement_mix(U128* out, U128 const* in, U128 const* mask)
    24: {
    25:     U128 first = ~*in;
    26:     *out = first ^ *mask;
    27: }
    28: 
    29: static int check(U64 low, U64 high)
    30: {
    31:     U128 value = ((U128)high << 64) | low;
    32:     U128 output = ((U128)0x0123456789abcdefULL << 64) | 0xfedcba9876543210ULL;
    33:     complement_unsigned(&output, &value);
    34:     int failed = (U64)output != ~low || (U64)(output >> 64) != ~high;
    35:     complement_signed((I128*)&output, (I128 const*)&value);
    36:     failed |= (U64)output != ~low || (U64)(output >> 64) != ~high;
    37:     complement_twice(&output, &value);
    38:     failed |= (U64)output != low || (U64)(output >> 64) != high;
    39:     U128 mask = ((U128)0x8070605040302010ULL << 64) | 0x0102030405060708ULL;
    40:     complement_mix(&output, &value, &mask);
    41:     failed |= (U64)output != (~low ^ 0x0102030405060708ULL) || (U64)(output >> 64) != (~high ^ 0x8070605040302010ULL);
    42:     complement_unsigned(&value, &value);
    43:     failed |= (U64)value != ~low || (U64)(value >> 64) != ~high;
    44:     return failed;
    45: }
    46: 
    47: int main(void)
    48: {
    49:     int failed = check(0, 0);
    50:     failed |= check(~(U64)0, ~(U64)0);
    51:     failed |= check(0, ~(U64)0);
    52:     failed |= check(~(U64)0, 0);
    53:     failed |= check(0x123456789abcdef0ULL, 0xfedcba9876543210ULL);
    54:     failed |= check(0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaULL, 0x5555555555555555ULL);
    55:     for (unsigned bit = 0; bit < 128; bit += 1)
    56:     {
    57:         U64 low = 0;
    58:         U64 high = 0;
    59:         if (bit < 64) low = (U64)1 << bit;
    60:         else high = (U64)1 << (bit - 64);
    61:         failed |= check(low, high);
    62:         failed |= check(~low, ~high);
    63:     }
    64:     return failed;
    65: }
===== tests/basic_c_x86_64_i128_stack_abi.c =====
--- lines 1-82 ---
     1: // System V x86-64 places a sixteen-byte-aligned stack argument at a
     2: // sixteen-aligned offset in the argument area, not immediately after the
     3: // eightbyte before it.  The machine placement used to pack the cursor tight,
     4: // so a machine-selected callee read a stacked __int128 one eightbyte early
     5: // while the canonical caller (and clang) had padded — a disagreement only a
     6: // run can see, and only when the callee itself stays inside the machine
     7: // subset.  Every callee here therefore forwards its halves to the one
     8: // checker that owns the __int128 shifts: the shifts are what push a function
     9: // to the canonical fallback, and a callee that fell back would silently stop
    10: // covering the machine placement.  basic_c_x86_64_i128_stack_abi in
    11: // driver_test.c pins that census.  This file has no hosted dependencies and
    12: // the same shapes hold on AArch64, whose placement rounds by C.8/C.12.
    13: typedef unsigned long long u64;
    14: 
    15: typedef struct I128Box
    16: {
    17:     __int128 value;
    18: } I128Box;
    19: 
    20: typedef struct AlignedPair
    21: {
    22:     _Alignas(16) long low;
    23:     long high;
    24: } AlignedPair;
    25: 
    26: static int check_halves(__int128 value, u64 low, u64 high)
    27: {
    28:     return (u64)value == low && (u64)(value >> 64) == high;
    29: }
    30: 
    31: // Seven integer arguments leave an odd stack cursor: g takes eightbyte zero,
    32: // so the sixteen-aligned pair must skip eightbyte one and start at sixteen.
    33: // The trailing scalar catches a callee that never counted the padding.
    34: static int bare_after_seven(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, __int128 value, int tail)
    35: {
    36:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && g == 7 && check_halves(value, 9, 10) && tail == 11;
    37: }
    38: 
    39: // Eight integer arguments leave an even cursor: g and h take eightbytes zero
    40: // and one, the pair starts at sixteen with no padding to insert.  This is the
    41: // tight case, and the caller must not invent a gap where none belongs.
    42: static int bare_after_eight(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, int h, __int128 value, int tail)
    43: {
    44:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && g == 7 && h == 8 && check_halves(value, 12, 13) && tail == 14;
    45: }
    46: 
    47: // The same rounding through the aggregate shape: a one-member wrapper keeps
    48: // the sixteen-byte alignment of the pair it carries.
    49: static int boxed_after_seven(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, I128Box box, int tail)
    50: {
    51:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && g == 7 && check_halves(box.value, 15, 16) && tail == 17;
    52: }
    53: 
    54: // A sixteen-aligned aggregate with no __int128 inside: _Alignas raises the
    55: // slot alignment the same way the pair's own type does.
    56: static int aligned_after_seven(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f, int g, AlignedPair pair, int tail)
    57: {
    58:     return a == 1 && b == 2 && c == 3 && d == 4 && e == 5 && f == 6 && g == 7 && pair.low == 18 && pair.high == 19 && tail == 20;
    59: }
    60: 
    61: int main(void)
    62: {
    63:     if (!bare_after_seven(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, ((__int128)10 << 64) | 9, 11))
    64:     {
    65:         return 1;
    66:     }
    67:     if (!bare_after_eight(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, ((__int128)13 << 64) | 12, 14))
    68:     {
    69:         return 2;
    70:     }
    71:     I128Box box = {.value = ((__int128)16 << 64) | 15};
    72:     if (!boxed_after_seven(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, box, 17))
    73:     {
    74:         return 3;
    75:     }
    76:     AlignedPair pair = {.low = 18, .high = 19};
    77:     if (!aligned_after_seven(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, pair, 20))
    78:     {
    79:         return 4;
    80:     }
    81:     return 0;
    82: }
===== tests/c_abi.h =====
--- lines 1-88 ---
     1: // Shared prelude for the C ABI interop suite ported from Zig's test/c_abi
     2: // (ziglang/zig @ 3c46da14db, test/c_abi/{main.zig,cfuncs.c}). The suite is a
     3: // pair of translation units that pass every ABI-relevant shape across the
     4: // boundary in both directions: c_abi_cfuncs.c keeps the upstream C side nearly
     5: // verbatim, c_abi_main.c and c_abi_main_generated.c are the C translation of
     6: // main.zig (the Zig side), so the upstream `zig_` symbol prefix survives to
     7: // keep the pair diffable against upstream. The driver test compiles all three
     8: // with the compiler under test and runs the result; compiling the two sides
     9: // with different compilers (one of them clang) turns the same fixtures into a
    10: // cross-compiler conformance harness.
    11: //
    12: // This header replaces upstream's hosted includes (<inttypes.h>, <stdbool.h>,
    13: // <stdalign.h>, <complex.h>, ...) because the fixtures must also cross-compile
    14: // for targets whose system headers are absent; everything the suite needs is
    15: // declared freestanding below.
    16: #ifndef C_ABI_H
    17: #define C_ABI_H
    18: 
    19: // Capability gates. Upstream already keys optional families off ZIG_NO_*
    20: // macros per target; the port extends the same scheme with the shapes the
    21: // compiler under test cannot build yet. Both translation units include this
    22: // header, so the two sides always agree on which families exist — that must
    23: // hold even when the sides are compiled by different compilers, which is why
    24: // the gates are unconditional rather than keyed off __BUSTER__. Compile with
    25: // -DC_ABI_FULL (clang on both sides) to run the complete upstream suite.
    26: // Bool vectors are excluded from the port itself, not just gated for the
    27: // compiler under test: they need clang's ext_vector_type on both sides, and
    28: // upstream only exercises them on a handful of targets anyway.
    29: #define ZIG_NO_BOOL_VECTORS
    30: 
    31: // ZIG_NO_VECTORS strips the whole integer/float vector matrix. Since the
    32: // System V single-lane-double fix (<1 x double> arguments are MEMORY class
    33: // like GCC's and clang's, bare returns stay in XMM0) and the Win64 narrow
    34: // fix below, the gated matrix passes cross-compiler against clang in both
    35: // directions, so pairings no longer need it; it remains available for
    36: // targets whose vector ABI is still being brought up.
    37: //
    38: // Win64 needed its own answers for everything narrower than one vector
    39: // register, because MSVC has no generic vector extension and clang's choices
    40: // are therefore the de-facto ABI: a single-lane vector travels like its
    41: // scalar element (integer lanes in the positional GPR, float lanes in the
    42: // positional XMM register), and a multi-lane vector under eight bytes is an
    43: // indirect argument with a direct XMM0 result. __int128 answers the same way
    44: // -- indirect argument, XMM0 result. Buster passed all of these by reference
    45: // in both directions before, which agreed with itself and with nothing else.
    46: 
    47: #ifndef C_ABI_FULL
    48: // Non-power-of-two lane counts are rejected as function parameter and return
    49: // types.
    50: #define ZIG_NO_NON_POW2_VECTORS
    51: // Vectors wider than 64 bytes cross the boundary on Win64 x86-64 only:
    52: // that convention legalizes them the way clang and MSVC do (one indirect
    53: // reference per register-sized piece for an argument, up to four direct
    54: // registers or the hidden pointer for a result), while every other
    55: // convention still rejects the signature types. Target-keyed like the
    56: // F128/INT128_SHIFTS gates below, so both sides agree whichever compiler
    57: // builds them.
    58: #if !(defined(_WIN32) && defined(__x86_64__))
    59: #define ZIG_NO_WIDE_VECTORS
    60: #endif
    61: // long double supports transport only; comparisons count as the unsupported
    62: // wide floating-point arithmetic.
    63: #define ZIG_NO_LONG_DOUBLE
    64: // __fp16 is not parsed (upstream's ZIG_NO_RAW_F16 only skips bare f16 on
    65: // targets where the struct form still works).
    66: #define ZIG_NO_F16
    67: #define ZIG_NO_F80
    68: #define ZIG_NO_F128
    69: // _Complex is parsed and its ABI is the psABI's, but the upstream complex
    70: // tests read the halves back with creal/cimag, which Clang folds to builtins
    71: // and Buster emits as libm calls; the c_abi link line carries libc only, so
    72: // enabling them here would fail the link rather than test the ABI.
    73: // tests/basic_c_complex_arithmetic.c covers the same argument and result
    74: // shapes at real call boundaries without the dependency.
    75: #define ZIG_NO_COMPLEX
    76: // Calling-convention attributes (ms_abi, sysv_abi, preserve_none) are
    77: // silently skipped, so testing them would test nothing and break the
    78: // cross-compiler pairing.
    79: #define ZIG_NO_CC_ATTRIBUTES
    80: #endif
    81: 
    82: // Target-derived gates that upstream cfuncs.c sets in its own prelude;
    83: // mirrored here so both translation units always agree on the family set.
    84: #if defined(__APPLE__) || defined(_MSC_VER)
    85: #ifndef ZIG_NO_F128
    86: #define ZIG_NO_F128
    87: #endif
    88: #endif

   138: 
   139: int native_va_list_read(void* storage, int scenario)
   140: {
   141:     va_list* ap = (va_list*)storage;
   142:     struct NativeVaPublicLayout image;
   143:     unsigned char* bytes = (unsigned char*)&image;
   144:     unsigned char* source = (unsigned char*)storage;
   145:     for (unsigned long index = 0; index < sizeof(image); index += 1) { bytes[index] = source[index]; }
   146:     int named_stack = scenario & 256;
   147:     int named_vector = scenario & 512;
   148:     int bad = sizeof(va_list) != 32 || _Alignof(va_list) != 8;
   149:     bad |= (unsigned long)image.stack < 4096 || ((unsigned long)image.stack & 7) != 0;
   150:     if (!named_stack) { bad |= (unsigned long)image.gr_top < 4096 || ((unsigned long)image.gr_top & 7) != 0; }
   151:     if (!named_stack && !named_vector) { bad |= (unsigned long)image.vr_top < 4096 || ((unsigned long)image.vr_top & 15) != 0; }
   152:     bad |= image.gr_offs != (named_stack ? 0 : -48) || image.vr_offs != (named_stack || named_vector ? 0 : -128);
   153:     scenario &= 255;
   154:     if (!bad)
   155:     {
   156:         if (scenario == 0)
   157:         {
   158:             for (int index = 1; index <= 12; index += 1)
   159:             {
   160:                 bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != index;
   161:                 bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != index + 0.5;
   162:                 if (index == 5)
   163:                 {
   164:                     va_list copy;
   165:                     __builtin_va_copy(copy, *ap);
   166:                     bad |= __builtin_va_arg(copy, long long) != 6;
   167:                     bad |= __builtin_va_arg(copy, double) != 6.5;
   168:                     __builtin_va_end(copy);
   169:                 }
   170:             }
   171:         }
   172:         else if (scenario == 1)
   173:         {
   174:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 1;
   175:             struct NativeVaHfa4 a = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHfa4);
   176:             struct NativeVaHfa2 b = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHfa2);
   177:             bad |= a.a != 1 || a.b != 2 || a.c != 3 || a.d != 4 || b.a != 5 || b.b != 6;
   178:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != 7.5;
   179:         }
   180:         else if (scenario == 2)
   181:         {
   182:             for (int index = 1; index <= 7; index += 1) { bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != index; }
   183:             unsigned __int128 pair = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, unsigned __int128);
   184:             bad |= (unsigned long long)pair != 0x123456789abcdef0ull || (unsigned long long)(pair >> 64) != 0xfedcba9876543210ull;
   185:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 8;
   186:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != 9.5;
   187:         }
   188:         else if (scenario == 3)
   189:         {
   190:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 1;
   191:             for (int index = 1; index <= 7; index += 1) { bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != index + 0.5; }
   192:             struct NativeVaHfa4 a = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHfa4);
   193:             bad |= a.a != 1 || a.b != 2 || a.c != 3 || a.d != 4;
   194:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != 8.5;
   195:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 8;
   196:         }
   197:         else if (scenario == 4)
   198:         {
   199:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 1;
   200:             unsigned __int128 first = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, unsigned __int128);
   201:             bad |= (unsigned long long)first != 0x123456789abcdef0ull || (unsigned long long)(first >> 64) != 0xfedcba9876543210ull;
   202:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 3;
   203:             unsigned __int128 second = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, unsigned __int128);
   204:             bad |= (unsigned long long)second != 0x9876543210abcdefull || (unsigned long long)(second >> 64) != 0x1122334455667788ull;
   205:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 8;
   206:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != 9.5;
   207:         }
   208:         else if (scenario == 5)
   209:         {
   210:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != 1;
   211:             struct NativeVaHfa3d a = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHfa3d);
   212:             struct NativeVaHfa4d b = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHfa4d);
   213:             struct NativeVaHfa3d c = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHfa3d);
   214:             bad |= a.a != 2 || a.b != 3 || a.c != 4;
   215:             bad |= b.a != 5 || b.b != 6 || b.c != 7 || b.d != 8;
   216:             bad |= c.a != 2 || c.b != 3 || c.c != 4;
   217:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != 9.5;
   218:         }

   223:             bad |= a.a != 17 || a.b != 18 || a.c != 19;
   224:             for (int index = 2; index <= 6; index += 1) { bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, long long) != index; }
   225:             struct NativeVaOdd odd = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaOdd);
   226:             struct NativeVaAligned aligned = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaAligned);
   227:             bad |= odd.bytes[0] != 31 || odd.bytes[16] != 47;

   238:             bad |= a[0] != 2 || a[1] != 3;
   239:             bad |= b[0] != 4 || b[1] != 5 || b[2] != 6 || b[3] != 7;
   240:             bad |= c.a[0] != 4 || c.a[3] != 7 || c.b[0] != 8 || c.b[3] != 11;
   241:             bad |= d.a[0] != 2 || d.a[1] != 3 || d.b[0] != 12 || d.b[1] != 13;
   242:             bad |= d.c[0] != 14 || d.c[1] != 15 || d.d[0] != 16 || d.d[1] != 17;
   243:             bad |= __builtin_va_arg(*ap, double) != 9.5;
   244:             struct NativeVaHva2 spill = __builtin_va_arg(*ap, struct NativeVaHva2);
   245:             bad |= spill.a[0] != 4 || spill.a[3] != 7 || spill.b[0] != 8 || spill.b[3] != 11;

===== tools/bench_service/README.md =====
--- lines 154-244 ---
   154: service account. The configured cgroup root must remain root/service-owned and
   155: non-writable by other users. Dot components and symlink aliases fail closed.
   156: 
   157: The durable `worker-JOB` intent binds `{job, token, request digest, boot_id,
   158: unit_name}` before launch. Before the helper is continued, an immutable
   159: `worker-instance-JOB` record additionally binds the manager invocation ID,
   160: validated cgroup path and descriptor-observed device/inode identities for the
   161: configured root, service slice and leaf. Every signal and final absence proof
   162: revalidates that instance; same-name or slice replacement is quarantined. On restart a
   163: different boot ID is interrupted only if no terminal outcome was durable. An
   164: already-durable success/failure/cancellation is preserved while cleanup is
   165: completed. On the same boot the exact instance is terminated, never adopted as
   166: successful work. A missing record, foreign unit/cgroup identity, or failed
   167: populated-descendant cleanup leaves the active job reconciliation-required.
   168: OOM, runtime timeout, ordinary execution failure and cancellation retain
   169: distinct evidence/outcomes.
   170: 
   171: The production systemd path is Linux-only. Windows and macOS return
   172: `unsupported`; those builds still compile the bounded codec and portable
   173: manifest record. Injected tests cover fixed argv/resource/sandbox propagation,
   174: ancestor verification, lease ordering, restart identity, reboot interruption,
   175: distinct terminal causes, retained outcome evidence, full bundle replay, a
   176: live `setsid` descendant that forces TERM/KILL cleanup, and a sibling stage
   177: that survives parent TERM/KILL until it is directly killed. On Linux the
   178: service self-test additionally drives a materializer-to-recipe bridge: a real
   179: `bq_materialize` workspace and result root feed the real
   180: `bench_service_recipe` build-graph entry, with only the external build and
   181: throughput executables replaced by temporary scripts, and the published
   182: bundle is validated by the worker's exhaustive validator. They do not replace a
   183: privileged live-systemd qualification; if systemd is unavailable, command
   184: construction and seams are the only validation and deployment remains explicit
   185: operator work. Reference deployment files are under `deploy/`; nothing in the
   186: build installs, enables or mutates them.
   187: 
   188: ## Build and registered tests
   189: 
   190: The existing native `build.c` driver owns compilation and execution:
   191: 
   192: ```sh
   193: ./build.sh bench_service capabilities
   194: ./build.sh bench_service self-test
   195: ./build.sh bench_service self-test --sanitize
   196: ./build.sh bench_service_recipe_self_test
   197: ```
   198: 
   199: `test_all_combinations` runs the normal service self-test beside the existing
   200: throughput self-test on each desktop lane, and also runs its AddressSanitizer
   201: and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer variant on POSIX hosts. Existing compiler,
   202: throughput, sanitizer and workflow gates are retained. `shared.c` is the same
   203: foundation linkage used by the throughput tool. There is no new dependency,
   204: measurement loop or general-purpose testing framework.
   205: 
   206: Linux supervisor deadline coverage lives in `worker_deadline_tests.c`. Timed
   207: commands use explicit `exec` so the test retains an owned direct child rather
   208: than depending on PID 1 to reap an orphaned shell descendant. The observed
   209: `fork` PID identifies the group even when timeout precedes all output; a
   210: stopped-before-exec control covers that case. Separate owned live/zombie group
   211: members must prevent cleanup success until explicitly reaped. Failure
   212: diagnostics retain individual results, elapsed time, PID/group identity and
   213: process state before bounded cleanup. The 20 ms command deadline, 1,000 ms
   214: test bound and production cleanup policy are unchanged, including treating
   215: unreaped zombies as present group members.
   216: 
   217: The normal native executable is `build/bench-service-tools/service` (`.exe` on
   218: Windows). The fixed-recipe self-test is a Linux build-driver command; it uses
   219: private disposable workspaces and short-lived local fixture helpers, while the
   220: service tests exercise the installed-path manifest contract and replay
   221: validator. A passing disposable test is not a live qualification of the
   222: operator-installed compiler or throughput binary. Tests use private,
   223: disposable directories with deterministic source manifests;
   224: no sleeps, timing assertions, external workers or network access are involved.
   225: Windows validates the portable codec and rejects durable queue opening as
   226: unsupported. **Journal durability and fake execution are POSIX-only in this
   227: slice**; native Linux/macOS test evidence must not be described as Windows
   228: storage support.
   229: 
   230: The optional materializer additionally takes two absolute, bounded paths from
   231: the trusted local worker/operator interface, never from a submitted job:
   232: 
   233: * `INSTALLED_ROOT` is an operator-provisioned, mode-read-only tree. The selected
   234:   recipe, source directories, manifests, and source files must have no write bits.
   235:   Every absolute-path component is opened relative to its verified parent with
   236:   symbolic-link following disabled.
   237: * `WORKSPACE_ROOT` is an already provisioned private local directory owned by
   238:   the service account. Every attempt uses an exclusive deterministic child and
   239:   refuses an existing child rather than deleting or reusing it.
   240: 
   241: These paths configure installed policy and job storage. They do not add
   242: request-controlled commands, flags, source paths, or executable paths. The
   243: eventual worker unit must pin them; this unauthenticated local interface must
   244: not be exposed to untrusted callers.

   140: BUSTER_GLOBAL_LOCAL String8 clang_analyze_module(String8 file)
   141: {
   142:     // A source basename is the stable module key; its paired *_test TU follows
   143:     // the same owner. No filesystem discovery or reconstructed compile flags.
   144:     u64 start = 0;
   145:     for (u64 i = 0; i < file.length; i += 1)
   146:     {
   147:         if (file.pointer[i] == '/' || file.pointer[i] == '\\')
   148:         {
   149:             start = i + 1;
   150:         }
   151:     }
   152:     String8 result = string_slice(file, start, file.length - 2);
   153:     if (string_ends_with_sequence(result, S8("_test")))
   154:     {
   155:         result.length -= 5;
   156:     }
   157:     return result;

   161: {
   162:     // Fixed byte-order-independent FNV-1a, unaffected by database enumeration.

   167:     }

   195: }

===== tools/throughput/DEDICATED.md =====

    99: must be an owner-matched private regular file with one link. The harness
   100: reasserts a nonblocking exclusive `flock` on that same open file description;
   101: it never unlocks or substitutes another description during handoff. A closed
   102: descriptor, directory, final symlink, replaced path, different inode, separate
   103: open description, shared permissions or extra link is rejected before host
   104: capture or result creation.
   105: 
   106: After admission, the harness marks its descriptor close-on-exec before any
   107: compiler child. The service's descriptor is in a different process and is not
   108: changed. The harness copy stays open across preparation, warmups, measurements,
   109: diagnostic replays, fixed-point checks, sealing and evidence finalization, and
   110: is closed only on the CLI exit path. The service must retain its own copy for
   111: the whole supervised job and must not unlink or replace the path. Ordinary
   112: `--lock-file` acquisition remains inheritable and otherwise unchanged.
   113: 
   114: For `run`, the lease spans input preparation, warmups, measurements, diagnostic
   115: replays, fixed-point checks and comparison. It is acquired before any result
   116: directory is created and released on all normal CLI exits. Default runs without
   117: these options take no lease. Offline `compare` takes no lease and should be run
   118: away from an active measurement session.
   119: 
   120: ## Frozen-source A/A, then A/B
   121: 
   122: Prepare absolute paths for `IDE`, `FROZEN_ROOT` and `FROZEN_GENERATED`, an exact
   123: compiler revision label `SHA`, and a fresh `RESULTS` directory. Use the same
   124: immutable compiler for both A/A subjects:
   125: 
   126: ```sh
   127: "$BENCH" run \
   128:   --baseline "$IDE" --candidate "$IDE" \
   129:   --baseline-id "$SHA" --candidate-id "$SHA" \
   130:   --cpu "$CPU" --machine-id "$ENV_ID" --lock-file "$LOCK" \
   131:   --output "$RESULTS" --profile ci --mode all --pairs 30 --warmups 2 \
   132:   --self-host-root "$FROZEN_ROOT" \
   133:   --self-host-generated "$FROZEN_GENERATED" \
   134:   --require-identical-output
   135: 
   136: "$BENCH" compare --output "$RESULTS"
   137: ```
   138: 
   139: Then repeat with immutable baseline/candidate compilers against exactly the
   140: same frozen inputs, header environment, flags and target. Change revision labels
   141: accordingly. Never reuse an output directory or compare different work as a
   142: compiler speedup. Cross-variant byte identity is required for implementation
   143: refactors; intentional output changes need a declared semantic/ABI oracle while
   144: retaining within-variant determinism. Canonical own-source `test_self_host`
   145: remains a separate correctness gate. Frozen self-host jobs currently use FAST;
   146: `--mode all` does not expand them to all allocators.
   147: 
   148: Add `--require-pmu` only after verifying the existing generic counter workflow
   149: on the real host. Counters remain separate diagnostic replays; qualification
   150: itself does not probe PMU access. Missing counters are not zero. This does not
   151: supply model-specific Zen 5 events or validate physical Zen 4 behavior.
   152: 
   153: The current two-round guard remains 15% **and** 2 ms for wall time, 20% **and**
   154: 16 MiB for RSS. Thirty pairs do not tighten those margins. Exit 0 means no
   155: confirmed substantial regression, not equivalence, a speedup or a qualified
   156: noise floor. #426 owns the subsequent empirical A/A calibration and any opt-in
   157: statistical policy. Retain inconclusive and failed experiments, not just wins.
   158: 
   159: ## Evidence and limits
   160: 
   161: Opt-in run metadata contains `host_qualification` schema 1 inside the existing
   162: sealed `metadata.json`. It records the operator label, lock path, selected CPU,
   163: and bounded pre-run procfs/sysfs observations. Governor/driver/SMT topology
   164: paths refer to the **selected CPU**, not necessarily CPU 0. The older standalone
   165: convenience snapshots remain unchanged; do not treat their cpu0 policy files as
   166: the selected-core qualification evidence.
   167: 
   168: Every observation includes its path, errno, truncation flag and value. A
   169: successfully read empty file is an empty string; an unreadable/error-containing
   170: file is null. Each value is limited to 4095 bytes, with explicit truncation;
   171: `/proc/cpuinfo` can therefore contain only a prefix, not every processor. Raw
   172: bytes are JSON-escaped, including high bytes. Counts and labels do not establish
   173: bare metal, stable identity or idle hardware. The record explicitly leaves
   174: physical isolation, SMT idleness and effective cgroup limits unverified.
   175: `/proc/self/cgroup` records membership, not a parsed effective resource limit.
   176: 
   177: The snapshot is taken once, before preparation/timing. It is not an automatic
   178: before/after drift detector. `/proc/meminfo`, boot identity, process IDs and
   179: frequency observations can vary legitimately. Hashing this record is evidence
   180: integrity, not a stable machine fingerprint or an authenticity signature.
   181: 
   182: Native tests cover lock contention, failure/exit cleanup, inherited holder
   183: lifetime across exec, missing/empty/truncated/NUL-containing observations,
   184: CPU selection, optional-platform refusal and sealed metadata corruption. These
   185: are infrastructure tests, not compiler or physical-host performance results.
   186: Physical 9700X A/A and native platform CI must be reported separately when run.
   187: 
   188: Further workload coverage stays under #346/#423; multicore CPU-set experiments
   189: under #424. Do not use this single-CPU admission path to claim multicore scaling.
===== tools/throughput/README.md =====

     1: # Reproducible compiler-throughput experiments
     2: 
     3: This measures **Buster's implementation**, not the running time of its output.
     4: The harness is native C with no third-party dependencies. `build.c` owns tool
     5: and compiler construction; the standalone utility owns experimental design,
     6: process measurement, deterministic inputs, raw data and statistical replay.
     7: The existing compiler correctness matrix and canonical `test_self_host` gate
     8: are unchanged. A timing result is not a substitute for either.
     9: 
    10: Dedicated Linux acceptance hosts: see [qualification and exclusive runs](DEDICATED.md)
    11: for the opt-in machine observations, shared lease, frozen-source A/A procedure
    12: and the distinction between software validation and physical-host acceptance.
    13: 
    14: ## Start here
    15: 
    16: From the repository root, after building two uninstrumented Release compilers:
    17: 
    18: ```sh
    19: ./build.sh bench_throughput self-test
    20: ./build.sh bench_throughput run --baseline /absolute/base/ide --candidate /absolute/candidate/ide --output build/throughput-comparison --baseline-id BASE_COMMIT --candidate-id HEAD_COMMIT
    21: ./build.sh bench_throughput compare --output build/throughput-comparison
    22: ```
    23: 
    24: On GitHub-hosted machines, bootstrap `build/build` with the image's Clang as
    25: `.github/workflows/compiler-throughput.yml` does, then use `./build/build` in
    26: place of `./build.sh`. Canonical local bootstrapping still uses TCC. On Windows
    27: use `build.ps1` from a configured native developer shell.
    28: The tool itself supports Linux, macOS and Windows; native harness tests run on
    29: all three. Hardware counters currently have a Linux implementation only.
    30: 
    31: `bench_throughput self-test --sanitize` builds and runs the same native suite
    32: with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Sanitizer construction
    33: is also owned by `build.c`, including the Linux CI invocation.
    34: 
    35: `bench_throughput self-test` runs both the statistical/hash tests and native
    36: integration tests, including fixed-seed corpus hashes, rejected sample paths,
    37: deliberately invalid result bundles and timed-out children. Their expected error
    38: diagnostics are not compiler failures.
    39: 
    40: A direct standalone build is useful when diagnosing the harness:
    41: 
    42: ```sh
    43: clang -Isrc -DBUSTER_SINGLE_THREADED=1 -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fwrapv -fno-strict-aliasing -funsigned-char tools/throughput/throughput.c tools/throughput/shared.c -lm -o build/throughput
    44: ```
    45: 
    46: On Windows, replace `-lm` with `-lws2_32` and add
    47: `-Wno-microsoft-enum-forward-reference`; Psapi uses its source-level import
    48: pragma. Compile `tests.c` in place of `throughput.c` for the native test runner. No compiler is built inside a timed observation.
    49: Do not build, test, profile or run another benchmark concurrently on the
    50: measurement host. Use a new output directory for every run; existing results
    51: are not silently overwritten. Comparison never downloads historical numbers
    52: from a different runner and never automatically updates a golden baseline.
--- lines 431-521 ---
   431: These share the existing saturation, calling-thread and failed-attempt rules.
   432: They do not add timers, histograms, per-function storage or a reporting switch.
   433: Explicit clear bytes exclude ordinary map writes and allocator-internal clears.
   434: 
   435: The `validation_*` and `preparation_*` fields attribute the canonical boundary.
   436: `validation_calls` counts complete module-verifier entries. The ownership fields
   437: count the preliminary function scan, published-CFG checks, lowered functions,
   438: blocks, instruction-chain steps and owner-map clear bytes. The remaining fields
   439: count globals/relocations and their overlap pairs, aliases, initializers, value
   440: and provenance visits, block parameters and incoming values, instruction,
   441: operand, target and result checks, opcode-operation checks, conversions,
   442: calls/fixed arguments, provenance-bearing opcodes and terminator checks.
   443: `preparation_*_validations` separates the four verifier call sites: uncertified
   444: input, changed promotion output, certified FAST input, and changed FAST output.
   445: The other preparation fields count lowered functions offered to promotion,
   446: FAST, and dense-CFG publication. Successful validation therefore normally
   447: visits each instruction once for ownership and once for opcode semantics; those
   448: visits prove different invariants and are not a measured redundancy. Counters
   449: record work reached before the first validation error, so compare successful
   450: inputs when using totals as complete populations.
   451: 
   452: Initial estimates and finish populations cover different failure boundaries;
   453: do not subtract them blindly on invalid sources. Counts do not measure
   454: append latency, phase times, retained arena memory, or all-consumer cost.
   455: Reuse per-site allocation diagnostics and uninstrumented paired experiments.
   456: A smaller count is not a speedup. Normal builds preprocess recording calls
   457: away and retain neither counter storage nor reporting API. Row layout,
   458: IDs, source/label provenance, and arena lifetimes are unchanged.
   459: 
   460: ## Frozen-source self-host stages
   461: 
   462: ```sh
   463: ./build.sh bench_throughput run --baseline /base/ide --candidate /candidate/ide --output build/throughput-self-host --profile full --self-host-root /frozen/buster --self-host-generated /frozen/buster/build/generated
   464: ```
   465: 
   466: Configure a frozen worktree once to obtain generated headers. Both compilers
   467: compile **the same frozen unity source and headers**, not their respective
   468: moving source trees. Stage 1 measures each trusted host compiler. Stage 2 uses
   469: the stage-1 outputs as compilers and is a separate series. Full source/header
   470: trees are hashed before/after; symlinks and special files are refused. System
   471: headers/SDKs must also remain fixed and their build provenance must be retained.
   472: 
   473: A frozen source tree may differ from either original compiler revision. The
   474: appropriate executable fixed point is then **stage 2 == stage 3**, checked for
   475: each variant after measurements. This is deliberately distinct from Buster's
   476: canonical own-source `test_self_host`; the latter remains unchanged and required
   477: for compiler changes. Repeated outputs within every series must be identical.
   478: `--require-identical-output` additionally requires A/B byte equality; leave this
   479: off for intentional generated-code changes and run correctness tests separately.
   480: 
   481: With allocation probes, the harness also builds a separately instrumented
   482: frozen stage-1 compiler outside timing trials, then uses it to measure stage-2
   483: allocation requests. Instrumentation is not inferred from the parent compiler.
   484: The instrumented frozen source must contain the hook. Unix self-host commands
   485: include `-lm`; macOS SDK/framework and Windows system-include arguments must be
   486: supplied to match the canonical platform command in `docs/agents/build.md`.
   487: 
   488: ## Statistical comparison and the CI guard
   489: 
   490: Each of two **predeclared rounds** contains at least 20 adjacent A/B pairs per
   491: workload/mode. Within two-pair blocks, one pair is AB and the other BA, with the
   492: first order chosen by the recorded seed. Workload order is also shuffled. Two
   493: warmups per variant/case precede timing. All raw observations remain; no
   494: best-of-N selection, outlier trimming, selective cancellation or rerun-until-green.
   495: 
   496: The exact one-sided paired sign test asks whether a majority of pairs crosses
   497: **both** a relative and an absolute practical margin:
   498: 
   499: * Wall time: candidate exceeds baseline by 15% **and** 2 milliseconds.
   500: * Peak RSS: candidate exceeds baseline by 20% **and** 16 MiB.
   501: 
   502: Bonferroni corrects the nominal family alpha of 1% over every workload/mode and
   503: both guarded metrics. The same metric/case must be significant in **both rounds**
   504: to fail. Medians, median paired ratios, relative median absolute deviations and
   505: conservative distribution-free median-ratio confidence intervals are retained.
   506: The sign-test error model assumes independent pairs; shared-host contention and
   507: serial correlation can violate that model. These nominal levels are not a
   508: universal false-positive guarantee. Run A/A experiments on the intended runner
   509: before tightening thresholds or adjudicating small changes.
   510: 
   511: A broad interval or a one-round-only signal is **inconclusive**, reported as a
   512: warning rather than equivalence or a hard CI failure. `--no-guard` explicitly
   513: marks small smoke experiments as diagnostic. Standalone utility exit statuses: 0 = no confirmed
   514: regression (inspect warnings), 1 = confirmed substantial regression, 2 = invalid
   515: or incomplete experiment. A missing/failed compiler, timeout, stale artifact,
   516: missing metrics, nondeterminism, changing inputs, or corrupted result bundle can
   517: never be discarded into a passing timing result.
   518: 
   519: CI builds both immutable PR revisions on one runner, sequentially, using the
   520: same Clang/build-driver policy and generated workload. It runs all 24 synthetic
   521: case/mode combinations with two 20-pair rounds. It does not cache compilers,

   651: static int tp_workload_absolute_path_syntax(char const* path, int windows)
   652: {
   653:     int ok = path && path[0];
   654:     if (ok && windows)
   655:     {
   656:         int drive = ((path[0] >= 'A' && path[0] <= 'Z') || (path[0] >= 'a' && path[0] <= 'z')) &&
   657:                     path[1] == ':' && tp_workload_path_separator(path[2]);
   658:         int unc = tp_workload_path_separator(path[0]) && tp_workload_path_separator(path[1]);
   659:         char const* server = unc ? path + 2 : NULL;
   660:         char const* share = server;
   661:         while (share && *share && !tp_workload_path_separator(*share)) ++share;
   662:         int server_present = share && share > server;
   663:         if (share && *share) ++share; else share = NULL;
   664:         unc = unc && server_present && share && *share && !tp_workload_path_separator(*share);
   665:         ok = drive || unc;
   666:     }
   667:     else if (ok) ok = path[0] == '/';
   668:     return ok;
   669: }
